News.title: Christa Pike’s lawyers to appear in court for 1st time in evidence fight suggesting she could SUE over failed execution
News.content:
Next

CHRISTA Pike’s lawyers will appear in court for the first time since her botched execution today in a fight over crucial evidence that could lay the groundwork for a lawsuit against Tennessee.

The 50-year-old death row inmate is now conscious and speaking after surviving two rounds of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital on September 30.



Pike spent days unconscious and on a ventilator after the execution attempt left her with severe burns and blisters to her arms, and her lawyers say she remains hospitalized receiving critical medical care.

Her legal team said she remains handcuffed and shackled to her hospital bed despite the injuries to her arms and warned that her prognosis remains unclear.



Attorneys for Pike are due before Chancellor I’Ashea Myles in Davidson County Chancery Court at noon ET Wednesday after filing an emergency motion less than two days after the execution attempt.

The motion asks Myles to order the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve physical, written and electronic evidence that could help establish exactly what happened inside the execution chamber.



According to the filing, Pike’s attorneys want evidence including needles, syringes, remaining pentobarbital, execution logs and communications concerning the protocol used that night preserved.

Her lawyers first emailed the state about its duty to preserve evidence at 1.09am the morning after the failed execution and sent officials a detailed list of items the following afternoon, the filing states.

The evidence battle could lay the groundwork for a potential federal civil-rights lawsuit over Pike’s treatment during the unprecedented execution attempt.

Knoxville attorney Marcos Garza, who is not involved in Pike’s case but reviewed the filing for WVLT, said he could see her lawyers eventually bringing a Section 1983 action alleging a violation of her constitutional rights.



Garza said the preservation request appeared designed to “set up the playing field” by securing evidence of what Pike’s attorneys allege was negligence or recklessness by the state, although no such lawsuit has yet been filed.



Dr. Joel Zivot, an anesthesiologist who has advised Pike’s legal team, told The U.S. Sun Wednesday that she is now off the ventilator and breathing on her own.

“She’s breathing on her own, I think she’s on some supplemental oxygen, but not what she required initially,” he said.

Zivot separately told the BBC that Pike knows her name but thought it was still September when asked the date after regaining consciousness.

“She has some memories of being in the hospital but no memory, I believe, of the execution attempt,” he said.

Pike remains in intensive care, with Zivot warning that despite her progress she is not yet free from the risk of serious complications.



Pike survived after Tennessee officials administered two lethal doses of pentobarbital during the execution attempt at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.

According to the emergency motion, members of the execution team used at least seven needles while attempting to establish IV access and one was bent at a 90-degree angle when it was removed.

The filing alleges officials failed to recognize that the IV lines were incorrectly placed and that pentobarbital was leaking into Pike’s surrounding tissue before administering the second dose.

Her attorneys have said Pike’s right arm turned purple and began blistering after the drugs were administered, while witnesses described the haunting sounds of her choking and struggling to breathe.

Pike’s lawyers had warned before the execution that her small veins and blood disorder, essential thrombocytosis, could make establishing and maintaining IV access more difficult.



Her attorneys now argue that the failed execution subjected Pike to “cruel and unusual punishment” in violation of the Eighth Amendment and have called on Governor Bill Lee to commute her death sentence to life without parole.

The Tennessee Attorney General’s Office is opposing the need for a separate preservation order, arguing that the Department of Correction is already required to retain evidence connected to what happened.

The state has maintained that officials followed Tennessee’s established execution protocol, despite Pike surviving.

Lee has since described what happened as “deeply disturbing,” ordered an independent investigation and halted further executions in Tennessee for the remainder of 2026.

Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada has also announced his resignation in the aftermath of the failed execution.



Pike remains sentenced to death for the 1995 torture and murder of 19-year-old fellow Knoxville Job Corps student Colleen Slemmer, whose mother has now spoken about Pike regaining consciousness.

May Martinez said she had suspected Pike would survive and does not believe Tennessee will attempt to execute her daughter’s killer for a second time.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Asked what she would prefer to happen next, Martinez said: “It doesn’t matter what I think. They’re going to do what they’re going to do.”

Myles is expected to hear arguments from both sides before Pike’s attorneys hold a press conference following the hearing.

News.title: Girl, 13, took her own life 45mins after telling a nurse she was suicidal – her mum was told ‘that’s just how she is’
News.content:
AGONY FOR ELLA Girl, 13, took her own life 45mins after telling a nurse she was suicidal – her mum was told ‘that’s just how she is’







Next

ELLA Murray had her whole life ahead of her.

A formidable rugby player, with a wicked sense of humour and the ability to turn her hand to almost anything, the world was at her feet.



But after a series of tragic incidents, including the death of a close school friend, the 13-year-old, from Sheerness, Kent, found herself spiralling into a darker and darker place.

After making desperate pleas to medical professionals, the teen heartbreakingly took her own life.



She attempted suicide at home just 45 minutes after a visit from a nurse – and died the next day at King’s College Hospital on November 15, 2023.

Now, her devastated mum Natalie James, 39, is fighting for change in Ella’s name – so no other parent will have to face her agony.





The mum-of-six is campaigning for the government to make suicide risk assessments a mandatory requirement if a young person says they want to kill themselves.

The petition, put together by Ella’s friend Daisy Sunley, has already garnered nearly 15,000 signatures. It closes on October 10.

“Ella did all the right things, everything we tell young people to do,” said Natalie, who is a part-time student.

“What would she have had to do? What would it have taken to get their attention? Hold a knife to her throat?”

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

A four-day inquest held in December 2024 in Maidstone revealed the tragically preventable circumstances leading up to Ella’s death.



The Year 9 student at Highsted Grammar School in Sittingbourne – who had begun to show signs of deteriorating mental health – told teaching staff she wanted to end her own life.

The school filed reports to Medway Maritime Hospital in November 2023, where she was seen by a pediatric nurse.

She was later referred to the Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) and seen by a mental health nurse, who deemed her “medium risk”.



Ella was discharged with a home treatment plan and seen by another nurse the next day at her home in Sheerness, Kent.

Natalie recalled Ella becoming agitated in the intervening period, as her mood dramatically shifted.

When the nurse dropped by the following day, Natalie asked her to go on a walk with Ella, hoping she would feel more confident speaking in private.

But when the pair returned just 30 minutes later, the nurse dismissed Ella’s claims about hearing voices and said she did not qualify for a hospital admission.

“She told us she couldn’t wave a magic wand and make the voices in Ella’s head go away,” said Natalie.



For help and support, call the Samaritans for free from a UK phone, completely anonymously, on 116 123 or go to samaritans.org.

“That was just the way Ella was, that’s what she told us.”

It was only at the inquest that the family heard exactly what Ella had revealed during her brief walk with the nurse.

“She had told the nurse I’ve given up, I’ve tried everything,” said Natalie.

“I can’t do this anymore. You need to take me away.



“Or else I am going to hurt myself or someone else.”

The inquest heard that she told the nurse she would “hurt herself or others” if she stayed at home, was feeling suicidal and wanted to go to the hospital.

However, it was deemed she did not meet the criteria to be admitted.

The coroner – Catherine Wood – said at the 2024 inquest that it was “incredible” a risk assessment was not completed after this admission

She added: “I simply cannot accept it is reasonable to leave her at home even with a plan to see her the following day. There was a clear failure here to keep Ella safe.



“This was a child crying out for help, and I find she should have been risk-assessed. Had she been, she would have been high risk.”

After returning home, Ella checked in on her brother, whom she was very close to, handing him a tablet to play with so he wouldn’t follow her.

She then went upstairs and took her own life – less than 45 minutes after the nurse’s visit.

Nearly three years on from her death, Natalie continues to fight for answers and accountability.

“At the time, I had very little understanding of mental health,” said Natalie.



“I thought it may have just been down to teenage years, social media and friendships.”

“But I assumed when a young person said they were going to end their life, they should automatically be given a suicide assessment.

“Obviously in Ella’s case, there was no such thing.”

Natalie said the family continue to keep Ella’s memory alive by laying flowers at her grave every week.

And while she hopes to bring about positive change through the petition and save other parents from the agony of losing a child to suicide, daily life remains a constant battle.



“I feel like I’m living in a parallel universe,” said Natalie.

“It’s as though this has happened to someone else. Not to me.”

In the Prevention of Future Death report coroner Catherine Wood for Mid Kent and Medway concluded that there had been a “failure to undertake adequate, or any, risk assessment” on the day Ella died.

She added that had steps been taken to share information between her school, social services and the mental health providers when she went to A&E, Ella “may still be alive today”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Medway Maritime Hospital and Kent’s Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services have been approached for comment.



Click here to sign Natalie’s petition on the government website.

News.title: Woman in her 40s found dead & man in hospital after late-night ‘axe attack’ in seaside town as murder suspect arrested
News.content:
'MURDER' PROBE Woman in her 40s found dead & man in hospital after late-night ‘axe attack’ in seaside town as murder suspect arrested







Next

A WOMAN has been found dead after reports of an axe attack at a historic seaside town last night.

Emergency services scrambled to a house in Dartmouth, Devon, at around 9.20pm, where a woman in her 40s was found dead.



A man in his 40s was rushed to hospital with facial injuries which are not believed to be life-changing.

A local man – who cops confirmed is a British national – in his 30s was arrested at the scene on suspicion of murder.



Devon and Cornwall Police said it is not looking for any other suspects at the moment.

Detective Inspector Guy Biggar from the Major Crime Investigation Team said: “We appreciate the concern this distressing incident may have caused with the local community but there is nothing to indicate a wider threat to the public.

“We would ask people not to speculate, particularly on social media, while we work to ascertain exactly what has happened.

“Our enquiries are at a very early stage, therefore it is too soon in the investigation to speculate on motivation.



“Our thoughts are with the family and friends who have lost a loved-one in tragic circumstances, and we will continue to support them through this difficult time.”

Locals said “someone with an axe” had attacked people, adding that they had never seen such a large police response in the quiet town.

One neighbour said: “It was mayhem last night. Paramedics and police doing a fab job and thoughts and prayers with the victims.

“I’m shocked. I have never heard of anything like this in Dartmouth. My thoughts are with anyone caught up in this.”

Another local added: “I saw the helicopter and the fire engines coming out from the ferry.



“There were about five or more fire engines. It looked fairly unusual.”

One neighbour said: “It looked huge from the Kingswear side.

“I saw several ambulances, four fire engines and seven police cars plus the air ambulance between about 9.30 and 11, all racing along the embankment.



“I didn’t think we had so many resources.”

The Sun has contacted South Western Ambulance Service and Devon and Somerset Fire and Rescue Service for comment.

News.title: Influencer ‘shot boyfriend & her three kids before turning gun on herself’ after chilling message about ‘nasty side’
News.content:
MURDER-SUICIDE HORROR Influencer ‘shot boyfriend & her three kids before turning gun on herself’ after chilling message about ‘nasty side’







Next

AN INFLUENCER allegedly shot her boyfriend and three children dead before turning the gun on herself.

Cindy Tamez, 33, shared a chilling social media post just hours before the bodies were discovered in which she said “not everyone knows my nasty side”.



Now investigators believe that Cindy shot her partner and her two eldest kids before she fled their home in northern Mexico with her two-year-old son.

She is then believed to have shot the toddler before taking her own life, officials said.





The mum and her youngest son, Gustavo, were found dead inside a Jeep with a .38-calibre automatic pistol.

Her two other sons Bruno, 10, and Christian, 11, and her partner Leodegario Moya Garza were found dead inside the family home.



Before the tragedy was uncovered, Cindy posted a clip from inside a moving car with the caption: “Not everyone knows my nasty side.”

“I’d burn down my own house just to watch my neighbour’s go up in flames, even knowing I’d get f**ked over too.”

It’s been reported that Leodegario was asleep when he was shot.



The two boys were found downstairs behind a sofa.

Investigators believe the boys may have hidden there after hearing Tamez shoot their dad.

Local media reports suggest that an extramarital affair may have been a factor in the horror killings.

“Several extramarital relationships involving the murdered man have come to light,” reporter Raymundo Elizalde said.

“So the investigation may be heading towards a crime of passion.”



The horrifying events unfolded after a gathering with family and friends the previous night.

Evidence of alcohol consumption was found at the home, officials said.

Prosecutors believe that the couple argued before the killings.

Cindy, whose full name was Cinthya Abigail Tamez Rivera, was reportedly involved in money lending and informal savings schemes.

She is also reported to have bought, sold and raffled items including vehicles, chains, watches and mobile phones.



The influencer had tens of thousands of followers on social media, through which she projected an image of affluence and success.

Some of her posts focused on themes of revenge.

Another said: “I’m probably just as much of a piece of sh*t as you, or even worse, but I never screw someone over unless they’ve screwed me over first.”

News.title: Sadistic murderer butchered housemate & displayed cling-film wrapped body parts before posing as victim in cruel twist
News.content:
Next

A CONCRETE bunker in Kersal Dale nature reserve in Salford is a popular place for walkers to take shelter in rain or stop to have a cigarette.

But a gruesome find here triggered one of the most complex and challenging murder investigations that Greater Manchester Police have ever faced.



Wrapped in clingfilm and propped against the wall was the blooded torso of a man, in plain sight.

Police were called, but with no head, legs or arms, identifying him was an immediate problem.



It gradually became apparent that the sadistic murderer was depositing his victim’s various body parts, carried in bags, all across Greater Manchester.

“It was a harrowing case, not dissimilar to some of the things you would see in a horror film,” says Detective Chief Superintendent Lewis Hughes who led the investigation for Greater Manchester Police, in an exclusive interview ahead of the TV documentary Murder Scene: The Incident Room.



“I’ve been in GMP over 23 years now and I’ve dealt with terrible, terrible jobs.

“But this, in many ways, was one of the most complex and certainly one of the most gruesome.



“It’s rare somebody would go to the lengths seen here to brutally kill someone and dismember and dispose of them.

“The number of crime scenes, body parts, the spread of evidence, made it a fascinating and complicated case.

“There was all manner of things within the bunker with which the killer could have concealed the remains.

“But he seemingly chose not to do so.



“He had left them on display in the middle of the bunker.

“It struck me that this might not be somebody who had made a mistake but somebody goading the police, leaving the body part, leaving the clue, and seeing what happened next.”

With access to the spot only accessible by foot, detectives began scouring hours of CCTV to see if there was footage of anyone entering the woodland with a heavy bag and exiting without it.

DNA on the torso indicated he was a male, possibly in his 60s or 70s, and the remains were estimated to have been in the woodlands for two or three days after they were found on 4 April 2024.



But Kersal is a busy area.

“It was like looking for a needle in a haystack,” says DCI Hughes of the two-week trawl.



“There were loads of people on CCTV but it was very clear in my mind that we had to look for a heavy bag carrier.

“As soon as we saw a man with such a bag, resting, swapping hands, going into the woodlands near the site and coming out with an empty bag, I was very clear that was the murderer.

“Then we had to track him backwards and see what his journeys were.

“We knew he would eventually be seen going to a car, a house, an associate – some way that would enable us to identify him.”



Further CCTV footage was discovered of him making his way back from Kersal Dale and boarding a bus.

Detectives approached Transport for Greater Manchester to see if they had any onboard CCTV of him but, agonisingly, the request came a day too late.

The retention period for it is 14 days.

But the QR ticket he purchased showed that he had got on at Worsley on 2 April.

Quite by chance, detectives were scouring the area for CCTV locations when they saw the man they believed was in their footage.



After almost three weeks of searching, could this be the cold-blooded killer they have been looking for?

Officers raced to the scene and stopped a bus he was travelling on and arrested him.

He had long black hair and was wearing the same beanie hat.

He was identified as Marcin Majerkiewicz, a 42-year-old Polish national who had lived in the Manchester area for a long time and worked in various fast-food establishments.

At the time of the murder, he was unemployed, had split from his partner and children and was renting a room from 67-year-old Stuart Everett, the man who had taught him English years earlier when he first arrived in the UK.



Stuart was born Roman Ziemacki, to Polish parents who moved to Derby in the 1950s.

He had changed his name to Stuart Everett and worked in the NHS but was now retired.

He was unmarried, had no children and had an older brother, Richard.

Police visited Stuart’s house in Worsley Road, Manchester and there was no sign of him.

Neighbours said that they had heard he was unwell and had left the area.



The house seemed quite bare and tidy but, in the bedroom, where Majerkiewicz slept, specks of blood were found on floorboards and scraps of carpet outside in the bin that the suspect had cut away.

This blood was a DNA match to that on the human remains found in Kersal Dale.

Majerkiewicz was charged with murder.



He remained calm and denied he had killed and disposed of anyone.

He said that he had last seen Stuart at Easter when he was going to his brother’s.

No additional body parts were found at Kersal Dale so the search area was widened.

CCTV once again proved vital in assisting the hunt.

By looking at footage from a camera close to Majerkiewicz’s home in the days before and after the 2 April, police made a breakthrough.



On 28 March he walked along a road with a large bag that seemed full and heavy.

For eight minutes he disappeared from camera before returning with nothing in the bag.

Detectives then went to the location and walked along the route knowing that he had walked four minutes to somewhere and then returned four minutes later.

They got to a point on Chesterfield Close and started looking in the alleyway.

There they recovered some black bin bags that had been thrown over some high fencing.



Inside were more of Stuart’s remains.

Richard Ziemacki had last seen his brother in March 2024 when he was going to Cheltenham Races.

“He stayed with us for four or five days and went back on the Saturday after the racing festival had finished,” he says.

“I dropped him off at the railway station and that was the last time I saw him.”

When detectives first contacted Richard to tell him that Stuart had gone missing but some body remains had been found, he replied that he did not think it was his brother as Stuart had been in touch with him in the last few days and had sent him a birthday card.



It wasn’t until Richard supplied police with DNA that it was confirmed that Stuart was the victim.

Majerkiewicz had assumed his identity, unsuspected, for four weeks, accessing his bank account to draw cash and even to send money to Stuart’s family on their birthdays, along with cards and WhatsApp messages.

“He had gone to great lengths to put up the charade that Stuart was very much safe and well so that his family had no reason to report him missing,” says DCS Hughes.

It was a particularly cruel façade for the family.

“I would say that was probably more horrific than anything else, to try and pull the wool over my eyes, that my brother was still alive when he had been murdered weeks earlier,” says Richard.



Majerkiewicz was some £30,000 in debt with loans from various places.

“He had a financial motive for murder but his fascination with horror movies, gore and torture, was a big factor too,” says DCS Hughes.

“He downloaded a lot of such movies on his phone and his body was covered in horror tattoos.

“We think he killed Stuart Everett and started to dismember him at the same time he was searching on the internet for horror films that involved chopping people up.”

Stuart’s mobile phone, that Majerkiewicz had taken control of, was tracked as having been in Blackleach Reservoir on 3 April.



CCTV footage showed Majerkiewicz heading there, carrying a red plastic bag.

It was here that a police diving team found a hacksaw under the water.

Despite being submerged, it contained Stuart Everett’s DNA.

They also found an ear, some hair and part of Stuart’s head underwater.

A reconstruction was made of Stuart’s skull in plastic which indicated he had been hit on the head with a blunt implement that had killed him.



“Through an extensive examination of Marcin Majerkiewicz’s phone, we were able to establish that he had been in contact with a white van man, someone who could be hired to take waste and dispose of it from the property,” says DCS Hughes.

“We tracked down the driver and he said he had been asked by Majerkiewicz to do a house clearing.”

At a lock-up on an industrial estate police found a fridge freezer which had Stuart’s hairs inside.

After Majerkiewicz had dismembered him, he had stored him in the fridge in between depositing his body parts all over Greater Manchester.

Only around 35 to 40 per cent of Stuart’s body has ever been found.



A sofa bed contained a large blood stain that suggested Stuart was sitting there when he had been fatally struck on the head, likely with a hammer.

At his trial in March 2025, Marcin Majerkiewicz showed no remorse and made no admission of guilt.

He was found guilty of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 34 years.

“There was huge sense of relief that justice had been done,” says Richard.

“My brother and I were very close and his life was taken away from him.



“It was a pointless, needless murder of a vulnerable old man.”

“Marcin Majerkiewicz had tried to hide in plain sight, taking what looked like everyday bus trips with shopping bags and, for the most part, it didn’t look in any way suspicious,” says DCS Hughes.

“If he’d gone in the dead of night and he was the only person on the street, that would look more suspicious.

“But he had not disguised his face and he reckoned without the value of CCTV.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“And that brought about his downfall.”

News.title: Boy, 16, has fingers blown off by grenade in French riots as nearly 90 teachers wounded in violence & 6,000 arrested
News.content:
Next

A TEENAGE boy has had his fingers blown off by a grenade as violent riots over school conditions continue to sweep across France.

More than a quarter of a million people took to the streets on Tuesday with over 1,000 injured and more than 6,600 people arrested so far.



Protesters have torched classrooms and pelted police with rocks and bottles in clashes across Paris, Marseille and Strasbourg.

Police have responded by firing tear gas and launching stun grenades.



The violent clashes have seen at least 1,065 people wounded including 761 police officers.

Earlier this morning a 16-year-old boy suffered a self-inflicted injury while protesting outside Couffignal high school in Strasbourg.

The teenager had two fingers torn off “with his own mortar fire” according to police.

He was rushed to hospital in a state of “absolute emergency” – the latest casualty of a spiralling protest movement.



Since the start of the crisis more than half of the nation’s schools have been shut down and dozens of teachers targeted.

Education minister Édouard Geffray said that 24 schools were so badly burned they will not be able to reopen for several weeks.

He added that 89 teachers have been injured in the horrifying wave of protests with many of them being “deliberately targeted”.



Dozens of police officers and pupils have also been wounded.

Earlier this week a teenage boy had his hand blown off by a stun grenade fired by police in Lens, northern France.

The 15-year-old pupil’s hand had to be amputated following the horror injury on Monday.

His devastated mum told BFMTV: “His future is ruined.”

She added: “What happened to my son is horrible, we’re still in shock.”



“A lot of lies are circulating; my son didn’t pick up the grenade from the ground.

“He was hit with a weapon of war; it’s not normal to use that against young people.”

Desperate to curb the violence between pupils and police, the French government today suspended the use of stun grenades.

One senior minister said that “the police response was too harsh and lacking empathy”.

He added that the officer who fired the grenade has been suspended.



A further 18 cops are under investigation for using excessive violence against rioters.

One video shows a teenager’s jaw being broken and his upper teeth smashed out with a police baton.

But in other clips, hooded teens can be seen chasing down a policewoman and kicking her to the ground or firing flares at officers over barricades.

It comes after a total of 6,629 people have been arrested – of which a majority are minors.

News.title: Teaching assistant, 34, ‘showed boy, 15, her sex toys after grooming him with KFC and treat-or-treating’
News.content:
'PAEDO' MISS Teaching assistant, 34, ‘showed boy, 15, her sex toys after grooming him with KFC and treat-or-treating’







Next

A TEACHING assistant took a schoolboy home where she paraded in hot pants and showed him a drawer full of sex toys, a court heard.

Melanie Rock, 34, allegedly groomed the 15-year-old pupil on Instagram before meeting him outside school at KFC and Domino’s.

She was a teaching assistant at Medina College on the Isle of Wight at the time of the alleged offences between October and November 2023.

Prosecuting, Tim Devlin, said she began chatting to the boy on social media after her initial attempts to obtain his phone number were rebuffed.





He told the Isle of Wight Crown Court that the boy visited Rock’s home address in Cowes several times.

On one occasion he was shown a drawer in her bedroom “filled with sex toys” and watched the teaching assistant “parade around” in a pair of hot pants, it is alleged.

Rock is also accused of giving him money and vapes, as well as buying him a pair of designer Trapstar tracksuits worth more than £350.

On one occasion, she allegedly slipped £20 into his pocket, telling him “this is your Christmas money”.



They then went to Rock’s home, ate Domino’s pizza and went trick-or-treating, jurors were told.

During interview, the boy said Rock had “taken him under her wing” at school and admitted he was surprised when she messaged him because she was a teacher.

He claimed she hugged him from behind and pressed her body against his with her legs around him in a “koala hug”.

The boy also told police Rock invited him to “enjoy her room” before she “directed him” towards a drawer containing a blue bag, handcuffs and black see-through lingerie.



He added that the incident involving the sex toys had left him feeling that the whole situation was “weird”.

The court heard a fellow staff member saw Rock with the teen at Pizza Hut and the authorities and police were informed.

When questioned by police, Rock claimed she had only met the boy by chance and that he had visited her home on just a single occasion.

But Mr Devlin told the court that CCTV footage showed Rock and the boy together at various locations on numerous days.

It is understood that Rock is no longer employed at Medina College.



She has denied meeting a child following sexual grooming and sexual activity with a child by a person in a position of trust.

The trial, which is expected to last around 4 days, continues.

News.title: Christa Pike could still be executed under 80-year-old ruling - what happens next for death row killer
News.content:
Christa Pike could face another execution attempt under 80-year-old ruling - what happens next for killer

Willie Francis was just 17 when he survived America's attempt to execute him in 1946. A supreme court ruling in his case from 80 years ago could now become significant to what happens to Christa Pike

View 4 Images Pike's lawyers are pushing for her execution to be commuted to life without parole (Image: J. Miles Cary, Knoxville News Sentinel)

Christa Pike’s fate is yet to be confirmed - but under one historic ruling the convicted murderer could face another execution attempt.

‌



‌



Pike has woken up after the horror attempt to execute her by lethal injection failed. She was given two doses of the drug - the maximum allowed under Tennessee’s protocol - but the death row inmate survived. She is now conscious, speaking and continuing to receive critical medical care, her lawyers confirmed.

‌



But questions are now circulating over whether she could face another execution attempt. US constitutional law prohibits the execution of a prisoner who is legally incompetent. The protection has been established through a series of cases including Ford v Wainwright, Panetti v Quarterman and Madison v Alabama.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Pike remains under medical care after surviving Tennessee's attempt to execute her (Image: Tennessee Department of Correction/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Texas killer to be executed with pentobarbital exactly one week after Christa Pike botched lethal injection READ MORE :

Tennessee courts have also recognised that a person cannot be executed if they lack the mental capacity required to understand the punishment they are about to face. If Pike survives but is left with profound cognitive impairment, doctors and courts would have to assess whether she is capable of understanding that she has been sentenced to death and why the state intends to execute her.

But at present, experts have described her recovery as unprecedented. Authorities are yet to say whether they will try to execute Pike again, while executions in the state have been paused for the rest of the year. If she is ultimately deemed legally competent, an almost 80-year-old ruling involving death row inmate Willie Francis could become significant.

Francis, 17, survived a botched execution in the electric chair on May 3, 1946. The execution failed after the portable electric chair was improperly set up. When the switch was flipped, electricity surged through him, causing him to scream, but the current was not enough to kill him.

‌



The execution was halted and he was returned to his cell. His lawyer, Bertrand DeBlanc, fought the case all the way to the US Supreme Court, arguing that a second attempt to execute Francis would violate the Constitution’s Fifth Amendment protection against double jeopardy and Eighth Amendment protection against cruel and unusual punishment.

View 4 Images Francis's lawyers took his case to the US Supreme Court in a bid to prevent a second execution attempt (Image: Wikimedia Commons)

The Supreme Court ruled against Francis. The majority concluded that the Constitution protects against intentional cruelty, but because the first failure was considered an “unforeseeable accident” caused by a mechanical malfunction, the state was legally allowed to try again.

‌



He returned to the electric chair just over a year later, on May 9, 1947, when his execution was successfully carried out. But whether the ruling could clear the way for Tennessee to try to execute Pike again may depend on the circumstances surrounding her failed execution.

The Supreme Court’s decision rested in part on Francis’s failed execution being considered an unforeseeable accident, rather than the intentional infliction of unnecessary pain. Pike’s lawyers could argue her case is different, as they had raised concerns before her execution, including difficulties accessing her veins.

View 4 Images Governor Bill Lee has ordered an independent review into what happened during Pike's execution (Image: Jae S. Lee / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

‌



Governor Bill Lee said he had ordered a “comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred”. He added: “A lawfully imposed sentence is among the State’s most serious responsibilities, and the people of Tennessee expect it to be done in a manner that is not only legal and constitutional, but is effective.”

Pike’s lawyers are now pushing for the death penalty to be taken off the table altogether by asking Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to commute her sentence to life in prison without the possibility of parole. Attorney Stephen Ferrell said: “The least that could happen now is that we at least take death of the table and start looking for what the future could be for her.”

Ferrell added that he and the rest of Pike’s legal team were “certainly willing to discuss that with the governor, with whoever could make that decision.” Governor Bill Lee has yet to publicly grant their renewed request.

Article continues below

He previously rejected Pike’s bid before the failed execution, saying: “My responsibility is to uphold the sentences that Tennessee juries have handed down, even when it’s difficult, and that is exactly what we intend to do in the days ahead.”

News.title: Boots to be bought by billionaire Weston family's company for £6.7 billion
News.content:
Boots to be bought by billionaire Weston family's company for £6.7 billion

Chemist chain Boots, one of the best known names on Britain's high streets, is changing hands again in a big money deal

View 2 Images Boots the Chemist is set to be sold to a Canadian family with a retail empire

High street chain Boots has been bought by the Canadian branch of the mega-wealthy Weston family for £6.7billion.

‌



‌



Wittington Investments, the Weston's holding company, will buy the business from majority owner, private equity firm Sycamore Partners, and the Pessina family.

‌



It comes only a year after Sycamore took over Boots through the acquisition of parent firm Walgreens Boots Alliance, before splitting the business into divisions.

‌



The takeover deal will see Wittington acquire Boots' retail and pharmacy operations in the UK and Ireland, Boots Opticians, the No7 Beauty Company, and its Thailand and franchise businesses.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Boots has faced challenges from competition in the pharmacy and beauty market (Image: martinrlee via Getty Images)

‌



Galen Weston, chairman of Wittington, who will become chairman of Boots, said: "Boots is one of Britain's most enduring businesses, with a rich heritage, a trusted name and a vital role in everyday life across the UK and Ireland.

"We see a meaningful opportunity to make a great business even better through stable long-term ownership, further capital investment, and the renewed operating focus required to serve customers with excellence for generations to come."

The deal marks a return to the UK high street for the branch of the Weston family, coming five years after they sold department store Selfridges for £4billion.

‌



The British side of the Weston family is the largest shareholder in Associated British Foods, the parent company of budget fashion chain Primark.

The Canadian Weston family, which owns the grocery chain Loblaws and pharmacy business Shoppers Drug Mart in Canada through Wittington, first held talks to buy Boots earlier this year after it was put up for sale. The whole Weston family was ranked fifth on this year's Sunday Times Rich List with a combined fortune of almost £19 billion.

Wittington said it is partnering with Toronto-based Fairfax Financial Holdings on the deal, with Wittington having operational control. Fairfax's investments include Sleep Country, Canada's largest mattress retailer and the owner of Simba Sleep in the UK.

Article continues below

The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027 and is subject to regulatory approvals.

News.title: Monzo launches new feature with £9k tax-free limit from Wednesday
News.content:
Monzo launches new feature with £9k tax-free limit from Wednesday

The digital bank has announced a new feature which is operated through the app

View 3 Images Parents and legal guardians, also called a 'Registered Contact' can open and manage the account within their app (Image: Monzo)

Digital bank Monzo has announced a new feature which comes with a £9,000 tax-free limit. The app-based bank opened the savings option on Wednesday.

‌



‌



It means parents who want to start putting money aside for their child’s future have a new option to consider, after the bank unveiled a Junior Stocks & Shares ISA, designed to make it simpler for parents and legal guardians to invest directly in their child’s future. All transactions will be done through the Monzo app.

‌



Parents and legal guardians, also called a ' Registered Contact', can open and manage the account within their app, while grandparents, relatives and friends can chip in via a shared gifting link. It boasts a £9,000 tax-free allowance, meaning families can contribute up to this amount each tax year across all Junior ISAs held by the child, allowing extended networks to work together towards a single future fund.

‌



The Junior ISA is available for 0 to 16-year-olds. Funds legally belong to the child from day one and are strictly locked until the child turns 18.

View 3 Images Monzo announced the launch today, October 7

Monzo, founded in 2015, confirms that children aged 16 and 17 will not have account management access at launch. The Junior ISA automatically converts into an adult Stocks & Shares ISA on the child’s 18th birthday, following identity verification.

‌



The bank says it does not charge any platform fees, meaning more of the money stays invested for the child’s future. Customers will still pay a fund management charge, depending on which investment they choose.

The ability to create a shared gifting link for the Junior Stocks will be gradually rolled out to customers over the coming weeks, Monzo confirms. Monzo currently serves more than 16 million customers, including more than 1 million businesses.

It says the launch reflects how children and teenagers are using digital tools to build good saving habits. It also boasts more than one million young customers, with one in seven young savers now having more than one Savings Pot.

‌



Over half (55%) give their Pots goal-based names. More than 26,000 children have a Pot called “Future”, while others are saving for longer-term goals like “House”, “Investment” and “Charity”. Some are less sure, using names such as “IDK” and “Things”.

Jo Phillips, General Manager of Wealth at Monzo, said: “With more than one million young customers already using Monzo, we know how important it is for families to build strong financial habits early. From weekly allowance top-ups to tax-free long-term investments all in one place, bringing the Junior Stocks & Shares ISA into the app takes our wealth ecosystem for families one step further."

View 3 Images Monzo's Junior Stocks & Shares ISA (Image: Monzo)

‌



Jo Phillips, General Manager of Wealth at Monzo, shares her top tips for talking to children about savings:

Break the money taboo at the dinner table: Money shouldn't be a secret topic that kids only learn about when they get their first job. As a mum myself, I think it's so important to talk openly about saving, budgeting, and even how investing works early on. Involve them in simple everyday chats about household budgets or show them how their savings pots grow. Breaking the money stigma at home gives kids massive confidence with cash before they step out into the real world .

News.title: Clashes erupt at pro-Palestine march on anniversary of Hamas attacks
News.content:
Clashes have erupted during a pro-Palestine march through central London

Students had marched through central London in a pro-Palestine demonstration marking three years since Hamas’s October 7 attacks.

Clashes erupt at pro-Palestine march on anniversary of Hamas attacks

Clashes had erupted during a pro-Palestine march through central London on the third anniversary of Hamas’s October 7 attacks.

Students from the University of London Coalition marched from King’s College London in the Strand towards University College London in Holborn.

Groups of protesters clashed near Russell Square, where counter-protesters carrying Israeli flags gathered and shouted at those taking part in the march.

Counter-demonstrators later made their way through the gardens in Russell Square after officers blocked them from following the pro-Palestine protesters. They gathered behind the garden gates chanting: “Shame on you.”

Police blocked the garden exit closest to where the pro-Palestine demonstrators had gathered as the march continued through central London.

A number of people were arrested as a result of the demonstrations.

News.title: Urgent warning to drivers ahead of October 25 as UK-wide change coming
News.content:
Urgent warning to drivers ahead of October 25 as UK-wide change coming

UK drivers are being made aware of the issues they may face as a result of the change

View 3 Images Motoring experts have warned drivers to be extra vigilant (Image: Getty)

An urgent warning has been issued to drivers ahead of October 25, when a major change will take place across the UK. Motoring specialists are urging drivers to be extra vigilant ahead of dark nights and adverse weather.

‌



‌



When clocks go back an hour on Sunday, October 25, Brits will see the sun setting around 4.50pm, meaning that many commuters will be driving home in the dark. Driving in the dark can be tricky because reduced natural light narrows your field of vision, slows your reaction time, and makes your eyes struggle with contrast and glare.

‌



Ahead of October 25, Blackcircles.com are reminding drivers what to check when navigating darker roads. James Harding, a motoring specialist with 16 years of experience at Blackcircles.com, warned: "Unlit roads can be more dangerous, especially to cars with less powerful headlights. Reduced visibility often means that sharp bends, debris and standing water can appear much later than they usually would.

‌



"You may also not notice loose gravel, mud, potholes or broken edges until you are close." He added: "Before you set off, you must also check that your tyres have the correct pressure and adequate tread. Having a good grip is especially important when you are unable to see road surfaces."

View 3 Images Data shows shows that accidents between 4pm and 7pm increase (Image: Getty)

Why can the clocks going back be a problem for drivers?

According to car experts, the clocks going back significantly affects drivers by shifting daylight hours, which causes a sharp spike in road accidents and evening driving risks. When the transition from British Summer Time (BST) to Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) takes place, peak evening rush hours are suddenly plunged into darkness.

‌



This leads to a documented increase in traffic accidents and injury claims of 11% to over 20% in the following weeks. Vehicle collisions rise by about 11% in the fortnight following the autumn clock change, according to the AA. Data from Zurich Insurance shows that accidents between 4pm and 7pm jump from 25% to 30% after the shift.

Drivers must contend with reduced visibility, a low-lying autumn sun that can cause severe glare, and poorer weather conditions like rain, fog, and slippery fallen leaves. These hazards make vulnerable road users, such as pedestrians, cyclists, and horse riders, much harder to spot, creating a particularly dangerous environment for young, new, or business fleet drivers who are statistically at a higher risk of crashing during this seasonal shift.

View 3 Images Vehicle collisions rise by about 11% in the fortnight following the autumn clock change

‌



How to drive safely in the dark:

Look well ahead, not just directly in front of the car. Scan for bends, pedestrians, cyclists, animals, road debris and changes in the road surface.

Expect potholes and road-edge hazards. If you can't clearly see the road surface, reduce speed rather than suddenly swerving at the last moment. If you see a pothole, brake before it if you have enough distance, rather than braking hard while you're already going over it. Keep the steering controlled and don't make a dangerous last-second swerve.

Leave more space. A larger following distance gives you additional time to react if the vehicle ahead brakes or encounters something.

‌



Be particularly careful on bends. You may not be able to see an approaching vehicle, cyclist, pedestrian or obstruction around the corner. Slow down before reaching any bends in the road.

Slow down when visibility is limited. It is important to drive slowly, at a speed where you can safely stop if you notice hazards in the road.

Article continues below

Use headlights correctly. On an unlit road, use full beam when appropriate, but dip it for oncoming traffic and when following another vehicle to avoid dazzling the driver.

Watch for pedestrians and cyclists. Pedestrians and cyclists can be surprisingly difficult to see on dark roads, particularly if they're wearing dark clothing. Be sure to keep an eye out for anyone walking or cycling, and give them plenty of passing space.

James continued: "If you've recently driven down a particularly rough, dark road and notice vibrations, a steering pull, or loss of tyre pressure, it is important to check your tyres promptly."

News.title: Christa Pike execution farce in full - from bungled lethal injection to coming round in hospital
News.content:
Christa Pike execution farce in full - from bungled lethal injection to coming round in hospital

While she is now conscious and speaking, her lawyers have said, death row inmate Christa Pike's future remains unclear as investigators probe her botched execution

View 15 Images Christa Pike is conscious and speaking, her lawyers have said (Image: J. Miles Cary, Knoxville News Sentinel)

Christa Pike has regained consciousness after a bungled attempted execution left her hospitalised with extensive injuries last week, and is now awaiting a decision on her future after the long ordeal.

‌



‌



The death row inmate, 50, is "conscious and speaking", her lawyers have said, despite having been twice dosed with deadly chemical pentobarbital during a scheduled lethal injection on September 30 in Tennessee, the US. Medics have cleared her body of the substance, which is said to have left her with extensive burns, and she is "handcuffed and shackled to the bed" in hospital.

‌



Experts have said her recovery is unprecedented, and authorities are now probing the events leading up to the execution attempt as she faces an uncertain future, with a hearing on the incident due to take place today at 11am CDT (5pm BST) at Tennessee's Davidson County Chancery Court.

‌



Massive interest in Pike's history and sentence have also developed over the last week, so we've explored the grim crimes leading to her death row sentence - and looked in depth at the botched execution.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Texas killer to be executed with pentobarbital exactly one week after Christa Pike botched lethal injection READ MORE :

View 15 Images Pike brutally murdered Colleen Slemmer (Image: WVLT 8)

‌



The twisted murder of Colleen Slemmer

On January 12, 1995, 18-year-old Pike, along with her 17-year-old boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and 18-year-old friend Shadolla Peterson, brutally tortured and killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. All four were students living at a Job Corps training centre in Knoxville, Tennessee.

Pike believed that Colleen was trying to "steal" her boyfriend, Shipp, and claimed Ms Slemmer had been "running her mouth" about her.

Pike and Peterson lured Colleen into the woods near an abandoned boiler house on the University of Tennessee's agricultural campus, convincing her to sign out of their dormitory with them under the pretence of "making peace" and offering her cannabis.

‌



Once they reached the remote spot, the pair brutally beat, kicked, and slashed their victim using a box cutter and a miniature meat cleaver, with the ordeal lasting between 30 minutes and one hour.

View 15 Images A pentagram was sliced into Ms Slemmer's body (Image: May Martinez via AP)

The murder's Satanic overtones

Ms Slemmer's murder attracted heightened attention due to its brutal nature, with Pike and Shipp having carved a pentagram into their victim's body.

‌



The death came at the height of the "Satanic panic" of the 1980s and 1990s, stoking fears of devil worship, with Shipp eventually admitting he had carved the symbol.

Shipp had as a teenager had kept a satanic altar in his room, and was known by the nickname "Baby Satan" among his fellow Jobs Corps members.

View 15 Images Pike was sentenced to death row in 1996 (Image: WBIR-TV via AP)

‌



The trial and sentencing of Christa Pike

Pike and her boyfriend were arrested three days after they killed Ms Slemmer, with the killer's early testimony about the horror act caught in police tapes.

She told investigators during an interview that she had only intended to scare Slemmer, not kill her. During the trial, police played a taped confession in which Pike described a 30-to-45-minute "torture session".

A jury found her guilty of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder in 1996, and she was sentenced to death aged 20, making her the youngest woman on death row in the entire US at the time.

‌



View 15 Images Tadaryl Shipp was sentenced to life in jail without parole

The fate of Tadaryl Shipp

Pike was 18 when she murdered Ms Slemmer, and her boyfriend 17, but due to the severity of their crime both were tried as adults when they were brought before the court in 1995.

Shipp, however, did not meet age requirements to receive the death penalty like his girlfriend, and when he was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit first-degree murder, was sentenced to life in prison without eligibility for parole.

‌



He is now 49, and has been serving his life sentence at Tennessee's Northwest Correctional Complex, although the conditions of his imprisonment have somewhat relaxed in recent years.

Shipp has since become eligible for parole, and had his first hearing in October 2025. He was flatly denied by the Tennessee Board of Parole at the time due to the "heinous and heartless nature of the crime". His next review is due in October 2031.

View 15 Images Shadolla Peterson accepted a plea deal and was given a lesser sentence (Image: WBIR10/YouTube)

‌



The fate of Shadolla Peterson

As Pike and Shipp went through the courts charged with the murder of Ms Slemmer, Peterson, the former's best friend, escaped with a lesser charge and ultimately lighter far lighter punishment.

District Public Defender Mark Stephens maintained that, while his client was present when the murder took place, she was unaware Pike and Shipp had planned to murder the 19-year-old.

She agreed to accept a plea deal for a lesser accessory to murder charge in exchange for testifying against her two friends, and was kept behind bars until this was finalised.

‌



After around 460 days behind bars, Peterson ultimately went on to serve six years of probation, and in the years since has maintained a private life.

View 15 Images Pike spent decades on death row

Pike on death row

Pike has spent more than 30 years awaiting her death, all of which time has been in solitary confinement at the Debra K Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Nashville.

‌



Her time awaiting her sentence wasn't spent in deep reflection, as she would go on to also commit crimes while behind bars. In 2001, just five years into her sentence, Pike choked fellow inmate Patricia Jones with a shoestring.

She was convicted of attempted first-degree murder for the attack three years later. In March 2012, it was reported that Pike had made escape plans with two alleged accomplices, one of whom was a corrections officer.

She was rumbled before she had the opportunity to carry it out, however, and the Tennessee Department of Corrections has not disclosed what she had planned. Pike was not charged for the conspiracy, but one of her co-conspirators received a seven-year prison sentence.

‌



View 15 Images Pike killed a fellow inmate while in prison (Image: WVLT 8)

Execution date set

Tennessee's Supreme Court officially set an execution date for Pike last year, which was met with several appeals from her legal team, who launched a bid to prevent this from ultimately being carried out.

Her lawyers argue that carrying out the execution by lethal injection would violate her constitutional rights against cruel and unusual punishment, as she suffers from blood clots and obesity.

‌



They also said she was a victim of sexual abuse as a child, a claim that received backing from experts at the UN Human Rights commission, who warned earlier this month that her execution would break international law.

The Tennessee Supreme Court ultimately denied Pike's request for a stay of execution after finding that she was not at "substantial risk" of severe pain or needless suffering on September 25, and it was allowed to go ahead at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, Tennessee on September 30.

View 15 Images Pike's execution was scheduled for September 30 (Image: Tennessee Department of Correction/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Pike's final request

Pike's attorneys revealed that the convicted murderer requested no men be involved in administering the lethal drug. She made the request due to her history of suffering sexual abuse, fearing being put to death by a man would be needlessly traumatic.

“That was her biggest fear as the victim of sexual abuse, that she would be pinned down, prodded, poked, cut,” one of her lawyers, Stephen Ferrell, said.

“What I saw was consistent with that,” another of her lawyers, Randy Spivey, said in response to a question about whether the execution team had been staffed entirely by women.

‌



View 15 Images Pike's execution was scheduled for September 30 (Image: WKRN News)

Pike's 'last' words

Pike was allowed to deliver a final statement before her death, saying she would leave the world "with love" after saying this was how she had lived her life.

She said: "I just want to say that I'm going to leave this world the way I spent most of my life, and that is with love." Pike added that she loved her supporters, and those who hated her.

‌



She then saiid: "I'm at peace and I'm ready to go." Afterwards, continuing in the theme of her statement, the convicted murderer sang "I Love You So Much" with her spiritual adviser.

View 15 Images Reporters walk from the attempted execution of Christa Pike (Image: AP Photo/George Walker IV)

The execution

Pike was strapped to a gurney in the viewing gallery before the execution was carried out, with curtains opening for a gallery of gathered journalists and family members of her victims at 6.30pm on September 30.

‌



Media witnesses said the events transpired as followed:

7.34pm: As the pentobarbital was administered, Pike said: "The vein in my arm feels like it's about to bust."

7.39pm: Pike kicked off the sheet that covered her

‌



7:41 pm: A "small white rock" appeared in a window, believed to be a " signal that a round of deadly drugs has been pushed through the IV lines."

7:46 pm: The blinds closed

After 7:46pm: The blinds reopened, but Pike was still moving

‌



8:05/8:06 pm: The blinds were drawn a second time

8:53 pm: Media witnesses were escorted out of the building, they claimed Pike was "snoring" at the time

9pm: An ambulance arrived at the facility, and Pike was rushed to Vanderbilt University Medical Center

‌



View 15 Images Emergency vehicles arrive at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution after the failed execution of Christa Pike (Image: AP Photo/George Walker IV)

The aftermath

Pike's lawyers said that, the day following her intended execution, she was in critical condition, unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator.

They said her arms were left swollen, blistered and burned by the pentobarbital administration, and that she had up to seven pricks from attempted IV line insertion.

‌



She awoke on October 6, with the lawyers saying she was speaking. They branded her recovery "medically unprecedented". "Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care," they said.

"Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed. Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery."

Her attorneys said they are grateful for the first responders and the medical team at the hospital "who treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her". The hearing at Davidson County Chancery Court will explore what happened wrong during the execution attempt.

‌



View 15 Images May Martinez said officials 'f***** up' (Image: AP Photo/George Walker IV)

What victims' families said

The mum of twisted Pike's victim has come out swinging against state officials, saying "they f***** up" after she was let in the dark about the state of the execution.

Speaking to US outlet NBC news, May Martinez, the mum of Colleen Slemmer, said she wanted the execution to be carried out. But, she added: "They went to try to execute her, and she didn’t die." She was left furious with the state's Republican governor Bill Lee, its Department of Correction and attorney general after her daughter's murderer was rushed to hospital.

‌



The mum said the killer had never expressed remorse during the attempted execution on Wednesday, and since the twin attempts has received little communication from officials. She said: "They didn’t say anything, and then, all of a sudden, they asked all the victims to leave. And we left."

“We didn’t know anything until we got up to the office and saw the commissioner. And he said that it didn’t work ... and she’s on her way to the hospital.” When asked what her message to the governor and attorney general was by NBC, furious Martinez replied: "They f***** up."

Immediately after the botched execution, Ms Martinez said of Pike: "If I could have gotten in that room, I would have taken the box cutter and cut her up like she did Colleen."

‌



View 15 Images Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has indefinitely postponed Pike's execution (Image: AP)

What happens next?

It is currently unclear as to what will happen next, but inquiries have been launched by Tennessee officials, with its governor, Bill Lee, has ordered a moratorium on upcoming executions.

The last remaining execution, of Gary Wayne Sutton, will not go ahead, and Mr Lee said he had ordered a "comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred".

‌



He added: "A lawfully imposed sentence is among that State's most serious responsibilities, and the people of Tennessee expect it to be done in a manner that is not only legal and constitutional, but is effective."

View 15 Images Witness Catherine Sweeney with WPLN, recounts the planned execution of Christa Pike at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution (Image: DENNY SIMMONS / THE TENNESSEAN / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

Experts weigh-in on second execution attempt

Among the options being considered is whether Pike should be subject to a second attempted execution, with questions lingering as to whether she is mentally competent to understand why she is being put to death.

‌



Pike has strong arguments that it would be cruel and unusual to try again, and that it would violate the prohibition on double jeopardy, trying or punishing someone twice for the same offense, said Deborah Denno, a Fordham Law professor who has studied execution methods for 36 years.

“She has satisfied this very, very high standard for cruel and unusual punishment,” Denno said. “She also has a very good double-jeopardy argument. They carried out every aspect of the execution. She didn’t die, but every process they intended, they did it.”

Seattle University Law Professor Michael Russo, who handled capital cases as a public defender in Los Angeles, called the failed execution horrible, but said he doubted whether the Supreme Court would stop the state from trying again on double-jeopardy grounds, should it decide to do so.

Article continues below

“There’s nobody else in the history of the death penalty in this country who has gone through what she’s been through,” Russo said. But, he added, “I think what this Supreme Court would say is, her sentence was to die — to be executed — not to suffer an attempt at execution.”

News.title: All UK drivers told to tap on bonnet and check under their car before driving off
News.content:
All UK drivers told to tap on bonnet and check under their car before driving off

As mornings turn colder and darker, the one small habit before setting off can help reduce the risk of harm

View 4 Images Doing a quick visual check and tapping the nonnet could wake them up and give them time to scramble out safely (Image: Getty)

Drivers across the country are being urged to do a quick check every time they're about to drive off. It comes as the weather is turning cooler and the mornings are getting darker.

‌



‌



Autumn mornings are starting to feel very different. There's a chill in the air windscreens are misting up, and the light is arriving later every day. On October 1, the sun won't rise in London until just after 7am, and by October 24, the day before the clocks go back, it won't be up until around 7.40am.

‌



That means plenty of drivers heading off to work or on the school run will be setting out in low light, from cars that have been parked outside all night. And for a cat looking for somewhere dry and sheltered, the space underneath a car, inside a wheel arch or tucked into the engine bay can be very hard to resist.

‌



Natalie Surtees, COO and co-founder of Tedaisy Insurance Group, the company behind Perfect Pet , said: "As the nights get colder, cats naturally look for somewhere warm and out of the weather. A parked car ticks every box. It keeps off the wind and rain, and there are lots of snug little gaps a cat can squeeze into.

"Most drivers never give it a second thought. But that's exactly why it's worth making a quick check part of your morning routine at this time of year."

View 4 Images Cats frequently look for shelter under and inside cars

‌



Does the same apply to EV drivers?

It's a familiar risk with petrol and diesel cars, where the engine stays warm long after the car has been parked. With more than two million zero-emission cars now licensed in the UK, according to Department for Transport figures for the second quarter of 2026, Natalie said many EV drivers wrongly assume the problem doesn't apply to them.

She added: "It's easy to think that because there's no hot engine, cats won't bother with an electric car. But a car doesn't need to be warm to be appealing. Shelter is often what a cat is really after.

"Electric cars are also much quieter than petrol or diesel when they pull away, so a cat dozing underneath gets far less warning than it would from an engine starting up."

‌



View 4 Images Cats are drawn to the residual heat from a recently parked engine block, warm tires, and insulated wheel wells

How can you reduce the risk of harm?

However, there are a few simple steps drivers can take to avoid putting cats at risk. Natalie also says: "Give the bonnet a firm tap, have a look around the wheels and tyres, and then wait a few seconds before you drive off. That gives any cat plenty of time to hop out."

Cat owners can help from their side as well. Natalie said: "If your cat likes to be out at night, a cosy bed indoors or in a sheltered spot at home can make a parked car far less tempting when the temperature drops.

‌



It's also a good time to check your cat's microchip details are up to date. A cat that gets a fright can bolt and end up a long way from home, and an accurate microchip is often how lost cats are reunited with their owners.

View 4 Images Cars can help shield them from rain, wind, and snow (Image: Getty)

Since June 2024, it has been a legal requirement in England for pet cats to be microchipped by 20 weeks old, and owners must keep their contact details on the microchip database up to date. If a cat is found without a microchip, the owner has 21 days to get one fitted or could face a fine of up to £500.

Article continues below

Natalie said: "None of this means worrying every time you get in the car. A tap on the bonnet and a quick look round the wheels is all it takes, and it soon becomes second nature, whatever you drive."

News.title: Boots sold in £7bn deal to Canadian billionaire family
News.content:
Boots, the High Street pharmacy and retail chain, has been sold in an $8.9bn (Â£6.7bn) deal to the holding company of Canada's billionaire Weston family.

Wittington Investments confirmed it had agreed to buy Boots on Wednesday from US private equity firm Sycamore Partners.

Sycamore had only owned the retailer for 18 months after taking over the retailer's previous owner.

The deal covers Boots' retail operations in the UK and Ireland, Boots Opticians, No7 Beauty Company and its Thailand and franchised businesses.

Galen Weston, chairman of Wittington, said the firm played "a vital role in everyday life across the UK and Ireland".

The deal is expected to be completed early next year.

Boots has faced challenges in recent years with growing debt and changing shopping habits resulting in more people buying cheaper products online.

It has closed hundreds of branches across the UK, leaving it with about 1,800 currently and 51,000 employees.

But Weston, who will become chairman of Boots, signalled the new owners had fresh plans for the chain.

"We see a meaningful opportunity to make a great business even better through stable long-term ownership, further capital investment, and the renewed operating focus required to serve customers with excellence for generations to come," he said.

The Weston family owns the Canadian grocery chain Loblaws, pharmacy business Shoppers Drug Mart, and previously owned the London department store Selfridges, which it sold in 2022 for $4bn.

The family is also the majority owner of Associated British Foods, the parent firm of Primark.

The Westons were ranked fifth on this year's Sunday Times Rich List with a combined fortune of almost Â£19bn.

News.title: How did Christa Pike survive two lethal injections - and what happens now?
News.content:
Convicted murderer Christa Pike has woken up and begun speaking from her hospital bed almost a week after authorities in the US state of Tennessee botched her execution, her lawyers said.

Pike, 50, was sent to hospital after surviving two attempts to execute her via lethal injection for the 1995 murder of a 19-year-old she met at a summer camp for troubled teens.

An independent review of what went wrong in the Nashville execution chamber on 30 September has been ordered by Tennessee Governor Bill Lee.

He has also halted executions in the state for the rest of the year.
