Sports.title: Ally McCoist ‘concerned’ by Scotland just two months into Sebastien Pocognoli tenure
Sports.content:
Ally McCoist ‘concerned’ by Scotland just two months into Sebastien Pocognoli tenure

Sebastien Pocognoli is already under pressure to prove himself just four games into his spell as Scotland manager.

That's the view of ex-Scotland star Ally McCoist, who has admitted he is 'concerned' following the 2-1 defeat to Slovenia on Tuesday night.



3 Pocognoli has overseen back-to-back Scotland home defeats for the first time since 2019 Credit: AFP

It's been a nightmare start to Pocognoli's spell in charge at Hampden Park - losing two and winning just one of his first four matches.

Sitting third in Nations League Group B1, any chance of sealing a promotion spot already looks unlikely.

How has Pocognoli fared at Scotland so far?

It was only last week which saw Pocognoli oversee an unwanted 55-year first following Scotland's 3-0 home defeat to Switzerland.



Having failed to win in his opening two games - becoming the first Scotland manager to do so since 2008 - he has now added more unwanted records to his name.

Scotland, who have lost to Slovenia for the first time in their history, have now been defeated in back-to-back games at Hampden Park for the first time in seven years.



They had led 1-0 at the break courtesy of Ryan Christie's 31st minute strike, only for Aljosa Matko and Danijel Sturm to compound another miserable night for the Tartan Army.

And for McCoist, who scored 19 times in 61 games for Scotland between 1986-1998, he declared the future doesn't look bright under their Belgian boss.



What has McCoist said about Scotland?

Speaking on the Sports Breakfast show, McCoist was asked by co-host and fellow ex-Scotland international Alan Brazil as to whether they can beat North Macedonia in their first game in November's international break.

To which he suggested that Pocognoli could already be packing his bags in the near future.

He said: "Yes [Scotland can win], but I think the jury is out longer term, I think Macedonia are probably the worst team in the group."

3 Scotland look set to remain in Group B of the Nations League having won just one of their four matches so far Credit: Getty



McCoist then continued: "Listen, it's still very early days in his tenure, clearly, we will give him time and so we should.

"I was encouraged with the second half [0-0 draw away at Slovenia], I was encouraged watching the comfortable victory against North Macedonia away.

"But the two home games, particularly last night, because whether we want it or not, you probably got a wee excuse/reason for the Switzerland game where there was a sending off for [Jack] Hendry early on in the game.

"But I was more concerned about last night.

"Because the signs... even when we went 1-0 up, I wouldn't say it was against the run of play, but they certainly looked [more] livelier in forward areas than we did."



What did Pocognoli say after Scotland's defeat to Slovenia?

Pocognoli - Scotland's second-ever foreign boss - declared his side deserved nothing against Slovenia as he stated they lacked bravery and were second best in every department.

3 A defeat against North Macedonia next up for Scotland would see them lose three home games in a row for the first time in their history Credit: Getty

He told BBC Scotland: "We didn't deserve to get the win, that's the reality.

"We didn't deliver a great game, on the ball and off the ball we were below the level we expect.



"We were not proactive enough, on and off the ball. Probably the structure off the ball needs to be more proactive, front-footed to push the line higher.

"On the ball we were not clever enough. We were far from strong enough in the duels.

"It's a process about being brave, trying to defend forward and we were not compact in our defensive shape.

"The reality is each game teaches us some information. We will try to go through the process we want and learn from this one and do better in the next one."

Sports.title: Alan Brazil reveals sources have told him what Man City’s punishment will be
Sports.content:
Alan Brazil reveals sources have told him what Man City’s punishment will be

Alan Brazil has claimed two different sources have revealed Manchester City's potential Financial Fair Play (FFP) punishment to him.

The Premier League giants have been found guilty of all charges against them, it was announced last week.



5 City are facing unprecedented sanctions unless they can get the verdict overturned Credit: Getty

However, City have since appealed against the ruling, delaying the start of the sanction hearing.

Amid the wait for any possible punishments, legendary talkSPORT host Brazil has hinted he could know what is to come.

Brazil 'reveals' City sanctions

According to the former Scotland forward, Enzo Maresca's side are in line for a sizeable points deduction.



Brazil admits he has no idea when the alleged sanction could be handed out, though.

Discussing City's predicament with Ally McCoist on Wednesday's Breakfast show, Brazil revealed: "I’m hearing a 60-point deduction, which will please people and still give City a chance of surviving.



"I don’t know whether it’s this season. I can’t see how that can be this season because of the timing, when they get it through it’ll be too late.

"Is it next season? But they are talking about a 60-point deduction."

In a potential boost to City fans, though, Brazil added that it could simply be 'nonsense' that he has been told.



Meanwhile, McCoist is doubtful a 60-point penalty would be a strong enough sanction for City's offences.

He replied: "I think a lot of people wouldn’t think that’s enough. Obviously we’ll have to wait and see how this appeal goes.

5 City could be set for a 60-point deduction, according to Brazil's 'sources' Credit: Getty

"If they didn’t win the appeal, I think people would be looking for a stronger punishment than that."



As for whether a 60-point deduction would guarantee relegation, McCoist added: "I'm not sure it would guarantee (relegation).

"You'd have to say it probably would (mean City were relegated). If you're staying up with maybe 37, 38, 39 points, it would make it a challenge, put it that way."

What sanctions could City actually face?

Any potential punishment for City remains months away following their appeal against the ruling.

Premier League rules require the appeal hearing to take place within 12 weeks.



It must last a maximum of five days, with the decision to be given within 30 days.

5 City fans are anxiously awaiting the outcome of their sanction hearing Credit: Getty

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire listed the potential punishments which could be in store for City earlier this month.

He told talkSPORT: "As far as the outcome is concerned, I think we've got to look at precedent.



"Chelsea were given significant fines from both the Football Association (and remember, the Football Association might take this up later) and from the Premier League for around £20m over their financial misdemeanours, not registering payments to unauthorised agents and so on.

"So you would expect that to be quite significant. Also, it was noticeable in the Chelsea claim that the club agreed to pay the Premier League legal costs, which were quite substantial. These are going to be far bigger.

"So we're probably talking about £50m-£60m in all probability, plus a substantial fine.

"Then, of course, we've got the precedent of Nottingham Forest, Everton, and Leicester City, all of whom breached the PSR limits and were given points deductions.



5 City's appeal against the Premier League's ruling has delayed any potential punishments Credit: Getty

"Now, the logic behind that is that if you spend more money on players, it gives you an advantage on the pitch, and that advantage on the pitch should be punished with a punishment on the pitch in the form of a points deduction.

"Given that the Man City offences took place over a longer period of time, therefore it's multiple offences over multiple years, you would expect a multiple of the points deductions that we've seen.

"We don't know by how much Man City exceeded the PSR limits, and we're now working on the basis of reading some of the former reports that it works out as a three-point deduction to kick off with, plus one extra point per extra £6.5m over the limit. So that will form a rough basis.



"And then there's a further issue, have you assisted with the investigation? We'll suggest they probably haven't.

"So that's called an aggravating factor, and the panel could subsequently give an additional points deduction on top of that.

"If all of those are proven post-appeal, my gut reaction is we would be looking for somewhere in the region of perhaps 50 to 60 points. If it's more than 70 points, they're effectively relegated.

5 City fans could be waiting around four months to discover their fate Credit: Getty



"From a drama point of view, and I appreciate the commission's not interested in the drama, you give Man City a 50-point deduction, they go to minus 35, there are 33 matches left to play for, you've actually got a fantastic story because they could try and stay up.

“They could just about stay up and I think the attitude of the players and everything would be fascinating, but that's a Hollywood story, rather than, is that appropriate?"

Sports.title: The Coldplay Kiss-Cam meets football! Female fan separates herself from 'boyfriend' in excruciating moment when cameras turned to them at Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell
Sports.content:
A female football fan was seen separating herself from her boyfriend after the couple were caught on camera during Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell.

The couple were among over 80,000 spectators present at the Estadio Monumental as Argentina paid tribute to the legendary star in a friendly against Benin.

Cameras picked out the couple during the pre-match build-up, with footage shared on social media showing the female fan realising they were being shown on the big screens.

The fan was then seen awkwardly removing her boyfriend's hand from her shoulder.

She then began adjusting her hair while glancing in his direction and exchanging words.

Football fans were quick to begin speculating about the moment on social media, with some joking it was 'Argentina's Coldplay moment'.

A female football fan was seen separating herself from her boyfriend after the couple were caught on camera during Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell

Fans joked on social media that it was Argentina's 'Coldplay moment', referencing the infamous kiss-cam which caught a a CEO and his co-worker embracing last year

Others gave a more sympathetic view of the clip, suggesting the female fan had merely wanted to adjust their hair

The comments referenced the infamous kiss-cam at a Coldplay gig last year that caught a CEO and his co-worker embracing.

'Coldplay Kiss Cam moment at Lionel Messi farewell,' one fan joked.

'It feels like she deliberately put some distance between herself and the camera once she noticed it,' another wrote.

'I feel that pain bro,' a third added.

Others, however, offered a more sympathetic view of the clip with one fan saying: 'Am I being naive to theorize that she might have just wanted his arm off her so she could fix her hair?'

The match itself proved an emotional occasion as Messi said farewell to Argentina's national team.

The 39-year-old capped his 208th and final appearance for his country with a goal and two assists as Argentina waved goodbye to its hero with a 3-0 win.

Following the game, tributes to Messi continued with an emotional musical performance before Messi took the microphone himself.

Lionel Messi played his final match for Argentina in an emotional affair in Buenos Aires

Fireworks were launched into the night sky above the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires

At the national anthem, Messi's sons - Thiago, Mateo and Ciro - joined their father

Messi scored his final goal for Argentina from the penalty spot as they earned a 3-0 win over Benin

'My dad is the first person I think about tonight,' he began, remembering his father, Jorge, who died aged 68 back in August.

'I can only thank you all. It has been a huge pride to defend this shirt for over 20 years. We never stopped fighting, never stopped giving everything. Playing for Argentina is the most beautiful thing.'

Messi's speech left supporters and players such as Enzo Fernandez struggling to contain their emotions.

'I want to thank all of my teammates. You made all of my dreams come true... I was surrounded by warriors. I'm going to miss this,' he continued.

'This may be the saddest day of my career, leaving the national team. I don't want to leave this place. I don't want to leave the field... I love all of you, and I will miss all of you. I am proud to be Argentinian.'

Sports.title: Formula One is less stressful without Christian Horner, claims Max Verstappen - as former Red Bull boss targets comeback
Sports.content:
Formula One is less stressful without Christian Horner, claims Max Verstappen - as former Red Bull boss targets comeback

Max Verstappen has claimed the Formula One paddock is ‘less stressful’ without Christian Horner - as his former Red Bull boss eyes a return to the sport.

Horner left Red Bull, where he led Verstappen to all four of his four drivers’ titles, last year and the 52-year-old recently declared he had ‘unfinished business’ and spoke of his ‘dream’ to lead Ferrari.

Despite the Tifosi since declaring confidence in team principal Fred Vasseur, Horner’s potential return remains on the hottest topics on the grid.

Horner’s sparring with Mercedes counterparts Toto Wolff and McLaren’s Zak Brown shaped F1 for much of the past decade.

But Verstappen, who won his first victory of the season in Malaysia last weekend, insisted a potential Horner comeback is not required to reignite a paddock once compared to a ‘Piranha Club’ because of its ferocity.

Max Verstappen won four drivers' championships under Christian Horner at Red Bull

Verstappen said: ‘To be honest, I like to see that people get on. It is not nice when you constantly have tension between people. Of course, from the outside, people like it, but honestly between the teams, it is better when you have just a friendly relationship.

‘It is not as spicy, but I obviously quite like how things are going at the moment, with everyone’s behaviour, let’s put it like that.

‘It is less stressful. We are all leading a stressful life and, when you can take a bit of stress out of it at times, it is good.

‘He has shown he did a good job. Of course, people spread a lot of rumours (about Horner’s return), and I don’t know how much of that is true.

‘I don’t want to sound rude, but it is also not my problem or concern. He wants to come back, and if there is a good opportunity, I am sure he will do it, but I don’t know where that is going to be.’

Sports.title: British cyclist who was brutally wiped out by rival claims he has received NO apology and is lucky to be walking after crash ended his Commonwealth Games dream
Sports.content:
Team England cyclist Matthew Richardson says he has received no apology and is 'lucky' to be walking after being wiped out by a rival before the Commonwealth Games.

Richardson was slammed off the track by Japanese cyclist Kento Suzuki while competing in the Keirin World Series in July, leaving the velodrome in an ambulance.

The 27-year-old won gold for Australia in 2022, before 'defecting' to England, claiming it was like ‘Hogwarts’ compared to ‘High School’.

He was favourite to retain his gold in Glasgow but never got to take part after the horrifying crash, which the Aussies made fun of.

Richardson was unable to walk for four days after coming away with a broken scapula and a heavily bruised hip.

'If I’d landed in a slightly different way, I might not be walking,' he told The Times.

Team England cyclist Matt Richardson says he is lucky to be walking after being wiped out by a rival (Instagram: matty__richo)

Richardson's hopes of competing at the Commonwealth Games were ended in Japan in July

'I was just stuck to the floor, my whole right side just felt like it was on fire. But it could have been a lot worse. Given how the crash happened, coming away with the injuries I had was probably pretty lucky.

'I was whisked off in an ambulance, I was gone. I haven’t spoken to him, I don’t intend to speak to him, that’s that.

'A line was crossed that day, for sure. We understood the risk, as the international racers coming in to race Japanese keirin, we knew it was argy-bargy. But there’s a difference between argy-bargy and intentionally taking a wider line to hit someone off their bike.

'It’s pretty disappointing that that can happen in keirin racing, that a rider has decided to put another rider’s safety at risk like that. We do understand the risks, but that was definitely a step too far.

'The rehab’s been all right, the hip recovered pretty quickly. The shoulder has taken a bit longer, given how much I use it sprinting on my bike. This is the first time I’ve broken anything.

'I’ve been quite lucky, when I have crashed I’ve seemed to be able to roll out of it or crash in a good way, potentially stemming from my gymnastics background [he was a promising junior gymnast in Australia before switching to cycling as a teenager]. This was definitely the worst crash I’ve ever had.'

Australia's representatives were unsympathetic at the time.

'I think maybe he got his Hogwarts invitation left in the mail,’ joked cyclist Leigh Hoffman.

Richardson is in a relationship with fellow British cycling star Emma Finucane (Instagram: matty__richo)

The pair were previously team-mates Down Under.

‘It was horrible, I’ve seen video of the crash, it’s pretty serious,’ added Hoffman. ‘I would have loved for him to come here and race and see how Danny [teammate Danny Barber] and I stack up. It would have been great if he stayed in Australia, but his heart was obviously never always in it – so good riddance.’

Fellow Australian Ryan Elliott added: ‘We checked his passport for his lineage, so he’s good. It [the rivalry with the British] has definitely grown a lot since the … defection. Definitely it’s there with the defector himself. This one is sweet.’

Richardson had been due to compete in the team sprint, keirin, and the sprint in Scotland.

He won two silver medals for Australia at the Paris Games in 2024, but controversially switched his allegiance to Team GB just days later.

Sports.title: Revealed: How Portugal boss Jorge Jesus defied Cristiano Ronaldo's eight-point apology script - as he slaps down sulking star's 1,996-word statement by insisting his focus is on the 'team'
Sports.content:
Jorge Jesus refused to follow Cristiano Ronaldo's planned eight-point script at a press conference as the Portugal boss, leading to the legendary forward's claim he had 'broken promises'. The eight points were included in an extraordinary 1,996 word statement made by the 41-year-old on Tuesday night. When questioned about Ronaldo's comments on Wednesday, Jesus responded: 'I read the statement, and now, as I do every day, I'm going to the federation to work, to think about the team and the national team.' Ronaldo, who abandoned his country after a spat over being an unused substitute, made the statement having promised he would tell his side of the story. The statement included notes he expected Jesus to address at a press conference before their Nations League match against Denmark. Ronaldo's notes followed a meeting with Jesus and Simao Coutinho, the sporting director of Al-Nassr, who has worked with both at the Saudi Arabian club. Jorge Jesus deviated from eight-points Cristiano Ronaldo expected the Portugal boss to address at a press conference last week Jesus' comments ultimately led to Ronaldo walking out of the Portugal national team camp THE EIGHT-POINT APOLOGY RONALDO WANTED 1. I myself, and no one else, proposed to Cristiano a plan for him this sporting season with the National Team. It was a long and very good conversation. 2. I know how much he lives and loves the national team and the weight he has in the world, and even more the weight and the positive influence he has had on the national team for 24 consecutive years. 3. The plan I proposed to Cristiano was accepted. 4. He never questioned my options. He was exemplary, loyal and professional. 5. The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed. 6. I made a mistake by putting someone of the stature of Pelé or Maradona on to warm up and then not putting him in the game. If it were today I would not do it. 7. To close the subject: I want Cristiano in the National Team. In fact I do not want him a little, I want him a lot. Fortunately he also believes in me. He believed at Al Nassr and he does here as well. 8. About not greeting the fans. We have already spoken about that. Someone who has played more than 230 matches for the national team does not receive lessons from me on love for Portugal. It was a moment of frustration that erases nothing. He is the player who gives the most autographs, takes the most selfies, and shows the most affection to the fans. Let us not invent problems where they do not exist. When we are not happy we react. The forward claims an agreement was reached for Jesus to clarify Ronaldo's situation at a press conference, explaining that the Portugal boss had initially changed his plans. Ronaldo claimed Jesus had told him he would play the final 30 minutes against Norway but was instead left on the bench despite warming up. Jesus appeared to follow some of Ronaldo's requests, but the coach stopped short of following all of the demands as he continued to assert his authority. Ronaldo expected that Jesus would confirm the 'plan I proposed to Cristiano was accepted'. 'The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.' While Jesus acknowledged there were discussions over his role for the match, the coach stressed he remained in charge of the final decisions. 'The status doesn't give players preferential treatment. The status is about respect for their careers. Like I do with Cris. 'I always put the issue first, the plan, which is drawn up with the player, and I'm the one who decides. They know, even the presidents know. The president is in charge at the club, I'm in charge at the team.' Jesus had conceded it was a mistake to make Ronaldo warm-up without bringing him on due to his status, but then insisted he would take decisions he believes are required during matches Another of Ronaldo's requests was for Jesus to say: 'I made a mistake by putting someone of the stature of Pelé or Maradona on to warm up and then not putting him in the game. If it were today I would not do it.' The Portugal boss appeared to have followed some of the request, even referencing legends Pele and Maradona during his press conference as he acknowledged he had made a mistake with his handling of Ronaldo. Jesus, however, had continued by again stressing that he can promise players 'whatever I want' but he would not change his mind on decisions regardless of the status of the player. 'I told Cris that he wasn't going to play these two games,' Jesus said. 'I thought during the game, maybe I'll need him and he'll warm up. And then I didn't put him in the game. 'Any player, when we're warming up for 20 or 30 minutes, and then they don't come on. No one is happy about that. Much less Cris. Much less Pele, Maradona, that's the status. 'When the game started, I told him to warm up at the 45th minute, I didn't know what I was going to do. That's what I did wrong, I should have had him warm up about 15 minutes later.' Jesus, however, added: 'The game dictates what I'm going to do. I thought I had even discussed it with him, but maybe until I needed him in the final minutes. 'But the game dictated other things and I didn't put him in. 'I can promise whatever I want. I'm a coach, I told the player he wasn't going to play, but I'll put you on the bench. 'Since I saw the game my way, he didn't come on. There will never be a player who will change my mind. Never, zero.' Ronaldo's future with the Portuguese national team is in doubt following his walkout and explosive statement Another of Ronaldo's requests was for Jesus to confirm his desire for him to be part of the Portugal squad by saying 'I want Cristiano in the National Team. In fact I do not want him a little, I want him a lot.' The request was not touched upon by Jesus in his comments to the media, as well as highlighting Ronaldo's love of the national team. Jesus, however, had previously referred to Ronaldo as being a 'symbol of Portugal' in a joint press conference at the start of the international break. Ronaldo's extraordinary statement and requests have cast further doubt over his future with the national team. Ronaldo has accepted he may be punished and insists he is still available to play if called upon. The striker also reveals that he offered to retire if that's what the coach and head of Portuguese FA wanted, only for them to reiterate their desire to have him. Whether it is possible for Jesus and Ronaldo to reconcile remains to be seen but with his 42nd birthday approaching in February, the explosive row could well be the end of the five-time Ballon d'Or winner's future in competitive international football. Jesus remains magnanimous and two days ago insisted Ronaldo returning to the fold is a live possibility. He explained: 'It's up to Cris to decide his own life. In the next call-up, if Cris is playing and wants to be in the national team, why not? 'Resentment? Nothing, it was a misunderstanding. In my opinion, it's easy to resolve. When will I resolve it? I don't know. The game is over, and only afterwards will we know how things will turn out. 'It's not up to me. To reach an agreement with two people, both people need to talk and agree. That's not up to me. 'Just because it was him, and perhaps rightly so because he's a symbol, this whole problem of him coming on, warming up, not coming on. How many players warmed up today and didn't come on? Will there be a problem? No. 'With Cris it's different, he's a symbol. But is it a problem? For me it wasn't a problem. If Cris wants to and is playing for Al-Nassr, he'll be in the next squad. We talked before this squad and we can talk before the next one. It's Cris who will decide.'

Sports.title: Arise, Sir Kevin! Rugby league legend Sinfield is knighted by Prince William after raising £13m for MND in honour of team-mate Rob Burrow
Sports.content:
Arise, Sir Kevin! Rugby league legend Sinfield is knighted by Prince William after raising £13m for MND in honour of team-mate Rob Burrow

Rugby league legend and motor neurone disease campaigner Kevin Sinfield has been knighted by Prince William in recognition of his charity fundraising in honour of ex-team-mate Rob Burrow.

Sinfield has completed seven running challenges inspired by former Leeds Rhinos star Burrow, who died in 2024 after living with MND for four and a half years.

The grueling ultramarathons ran by Sinfield saw him cover over 27.9 miles per day, with the 45-year-old launching his first annual challenge six years ago in 2020.

Sinfield was awarded the honour by Prince William on Wednesday at Windsor Castle.

The Prince of Wales previously made a surprise trip to visit the former rugby league star on the third day of his endurance challenge with his wife Catherine.

'What you're doing is so inspiring - the unity that you're building,' the Princess of Wales told Sinfield in Wakefield.

Sir Kevin Sinfield was knighted by Prince William on Wednesday after raising more than £13m for motor neurone disease charities

The former rugby league star began his challenges six years ago following the diagnosis of his close friend, the late Rob Burrow

Since beginning his campaign, Sinfield has raised over £13million for MND charities, but following the end of 'The 7 in 7: The Grande Finale week', he confirmed that he would be changing his fundraising in a bid to give those who volunteer for him a break.

'The team, it was right we made this seven because seven felt right,' he said on BBC Breakfast earlier this week. 'The commitment from the team has been unbelievable.

'They're all volunteers. They all put so much time and effort into it. There's no events company or marketing company. It's 16 of us.

'I think I felt I needed to release, if that's the right word, disconnect, uncouple... I can't find the right term that has enough warmth for that group. Set them free... I'm not sure they want to be set free. We'll see. But I will be going again.'

'It has to look different and it has to feel different,' Sinfield continued when prompted on what his next challenge might look like. 'I made a commitment for life. I'm in this for life. There'll come a point where I can't run.

'The team didn't make this commitment. I'd like to go again. It has to look different. I'd like us to go Down Under. Since March this year, there's been a bit of a plan of going after Australia and New Zealand and doing a 7 in 7 there.

'Put the codes together - rugby league, rugby union, Aussie Rules. I've got a lot of friends over there who I think would be keen to support.

'MND is big over there, too. I think if we can go after this globally and pull countries together, we have a chance of curing it sooner.'

Prince William and his wife Catherine met with Sinfield in Wakefield midway through his run

The 46-year-old plans to complete more challenges but will change things up to give his volunteers a break

Sinfield previously ran the first Rob Burrow Leeds Marathon named for his friend with Burrow himself, pushing him around the circuit in 2023 in a specially adapted wheelchair.

Metres from the finish line, the duo sparked emotional scenes when Sinfield picked up Burrow to carry him across.

Burrow's wife Lindsey was among those awestruck by Sinfield's commitment to fundraising, but told BBC Radio 4 that it was 'bittersweet' that her late husband could not also share pride in person at his friend's achievements.

'It's bittersweet that Rob's not here today to see Kevin finish his final challenge but Rob will be with us in spirit and it's just testimony to Kevin that he's so humbled to do this not just for Rob but for the whole MND community,' she said. 'It's just incredible.

'I am in complete awe of the efforts of Kevin and his team over the last seven days, and not just over the last seven days but over the last seven years,' she added.

Sports.title: Formula One star Valtteri Bottas completes 419KM 'commute' to Singapore after snubbing private jets for epic journey from Malaysia
Sports.content:
Formula One star Valtteri Bottas completes 419KM 'commute' to Singapore after snubbing private jets for epic journey from Malaysia

Formula One star Valtteri Bottas has completed his remarkable 419km cycle to the Singapore Grand Prix this weekend.

The majority of drivers tend to travel to races on private jets, but Bottas, 37, snubbed that option to take his own route across Asia.

The Finnish driver crashed out of Sunday's chaotic Bahrain Grand Prix, which was held in Malaysia due to security concerns in the Middle East, and he had to cover 419km (260 miles) to get to Singapore.

Bottas began his odyssey shortly after the race finished in Malaysia, and he documented it on social media.

The 37-year-old shared several videos and snaps, and on Wednesday afternoon he posted a selfie of himself on his bike with the caption: '419.67km commute,' alongside the tick emoji.

Bottas also shared a photo of his 'certificate of completion' after achieving the feat.

Yea I’m riding to Singapore 🚲



On the gravel roads less travelled with my new @canyon_bikes Grail CFR.



See you there 🇸🇬 pic.twitter.com/jFKZCM6Vnq — Valtteri Bottas (@ValtteriBottas) October 5, 2026

F1 star Valtteri Bottas has completed his incredible 419km journey from Malaysia to Singapore

Bottas began the remarkable odyssey shortly after Sunday's Grand Prix in Malaysia ended

Some of his earlier posts had included one which was captioned: 'Taking the path less travelled (and maybe a bit longer).'

In another post on X, Bottas shared a video of him cycling at night and added: 'Yea I'm riding to Singapore.

'On the gravel roads less travelled with my new @canyon_bikes Grail CFR. See you there.'

Bottas travelled alongside his partner Tiffany Cromwell, who is a professional cyclist from Australia, and needed to make it there by Thursday to fulfil his media commitments ahead of this weekend's race.

The journey was off-road and on gravel, and on Monday, during the second day of Bottas' cycle, he covered 161.91km across nearly six hours, before he made up 161 km on Tuesday.

It is an unusual way to travel to a race for an F1 driver, yet it is perhaps no surprise that Bottas is undertaking it given he has a history of completing cycling-related endeavours, often with Cromwell.

This included him qualifying for the Gravel World Championships after coming fifth in an off-road qualifying event in the Czech Republic during the summer.

However, given that event comes this weekend, he will be unable to compete.

In the past, he has also taken part in other gravel races, while he is known to be involved with FNLD GRVL, a yearly race in his native Finland.

Bottas has ten wins in his F1 career, but he has endured a difficult 2026 season with Cadillac after spending last year as Mercedes' reserve driver.

After 16 races, the 37-year-old is yet to score a point and he has failed to finish eight of those.

Sports.title: Coco Gauff sparks health fears as she is dumped out of China Open in the wake of 'cheating' storm and racist abuse: 'I feel like I'm going to pass out'
Sports.content:
Coco Gauff sparks health fears as she is dumped out of China Open in the wake of 'cheating' storm and racist abuse: 'I feel like I'm going to pass out'

Coco Gauff was knocked out of China Open amid concerns over her health one day after the American star highlighted the vile racism she had encountered after being mixed up in a 'cheating' storm against 16-year-old Sun Xinran.

The two-time Grand Slam champion had been 5-4 down in her third-round tie in Beijing when she patted a straightforward volley over the net, which Sun charged up the court to send back for a winner.

But Gauff had thrown up her arms in complaint as the forehand sailed over her head, telling the chair umpire that she had been distracted by a sponsor change on the electronic advertising boards on both sides of the court.

With the point replayed, Gauff wrenched momentum from her opponent and booked her spot in the fourth round - only to struggle from the early stages against world No19 Elise Mertens.

Level on serve at 4-3, Gauff's game unravelled to lose the next six games, with the US star telling her camp with some concern at 4-1 in the second set that she didn't know why she was so low on fighting spirit.

'I have no energy. I'm trying, I have no energy. I can't see the ball, I feel like I'm going to pass out,' she told the team in her player's box. 'I'm going to just try to finish the match.'

Coco Gauff sparked health concerns after revealing she was going to 'pass out' during her defeat by Elise Mertens in China

In the build-up to the match the US star had to contend with vile racism on social media after she requested a replayed point in her third-round match against Sun Xinran

Gauff eventually lost 6-3, 6-3, downed in straight sets for the first time since February.

The 22-year-old's preparations will have been marred somewhat in the build-up as she struggled in the face of racist abuse on social media in the wake of her controversial point against Sun.

Sharing a statement to clarify when she had stopped the match as she had done, Gauff sought to set the record straight after being accused that she had only protested due to her low-quality volley.

Gauff cited a flicker at the beginning of the point which she admitted she wasn't sure 'if that is what I actually saw'.

Continuing, the former US Open champion wrote: 'We are told before the matches we are allowed to continue to finish play so KEEP IT [in] MIND I am thinking about all this while I'm playing the point.

'Anything can be challenged after the point is over (as in most sports you can review a call after the play is over, I personally think this is the correct rule). If I would've lost the point my opponent is also free to do the same thing and ask for a replay and she would've been completely in her right to do so.

'When it flickered again I raised my hands before she hit her shot because this is when I was sure I saw the light flicker and it wasn't my mind doing tricks lol (which again doesn't matter because anything can be challenged after the point).

'It was an unfortunate situation but it is out of my control, the think pieces and calling me unfair is ridiculous when those are the rules. I did not make them, I think it's weird I'm getting hate for following the rules.

Gauff told reporters of the toll the cheating storm had taken on her after her defeat

'Xinran is [an] incredible talent and player, I apologized for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood. I did not like to see her so emotional as I've been there and I really understand what it is like but this is just the beginning of an incredible career.

'It was an honor to share the court in front of her home crowd.'

She also highlighted the level of racism she is subject to on social media, with her reply coming to a commenter who had written 'f*** you' to her and called her the n-word.

'Hey everyone,' Gauff replied, amplifying the comment. 'You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist.

'The amount of racist comments/dms I’ve received in the last few hours is insane. Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief.'

Gauff received an outpouring of support from fans in the wake of the racist abuse on social media, which was later limited after violating X's rules against hateful conduct.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi brutally SNUBS Benin star's attempted selfie in awkward post-match exchange - as legend's Argentina farewell is tainted by Malvinas controversy
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's farewell celebration was marred by criticisms on social media of his apparent brutal snubbing of a Benin player keen to take a picture with the retiring superstar.

The 39-year-old's retirement has been in the works since his country's ultimately heartbreaking run to the World Cup final and defeat to Spain.

The diminutive Argentine received a well-planned hero's send-off in Buenos Aires in a friendly against Benin - a nation whose team is ranked 93rd in FIFA's ranking - hoping to provide his final win.

But while the goodbye left his team-mates, family, and fans in the stands in tears as he paid tribute to his country and his late father Jorge, those online highlighted the superstar seeming to bypass a member of the opposition during the post-match festivities.

The player put his arm around Messi as he looked to take a picture with the football icon but the 39-year-old appeared to blank him.

He then continued doggedly to attempt to capture the special meeting, following Messi until his team-mate Amiro Amadou eventually intervened to suggest that he give up.

Lionel Messi was approached for a selfie by a Benin player but appeared to snub his rival

After the superstar's farewell match against the West African nation, the retiring legend was criticised on social media for appearing in no mood for pleasantries

Messi attracted widespread criticism for the perceived gesture, with one fan saying: 'There’s nothing to laugh or cry about here!! Messi totally ignored all the Benin Players that wanted a selfie!

'The easiest thing to do! Will take just seconds! What a shame! Nonsense!!'

Another added: 'I felt bad for that Benin player that was trying to take a selfie with Messi (weeping emoji).'

A third stated: 'Bro only wanted a selfie but Messi treated him like trash (heartbreak emoji).'

But others were quick to suggest that Messi was merely overwhelmed by the moment, as he was set to give a touching speech which brought his team-mates to tears and took in the recent death of his father Jorge.

After thanking his team-mates, Messi mused: 'This may be the saddest day of my career, leaving the national team. But I'll be here supporting whoever comes next. When we are united we are stronger than anyone else.'

He ended his speech with gratitude: 'I don't want to leave this place. I don't want to leave the field. I love all of you, and I will miss all of you. I am proud to be Argentinian.'

Also causing controversy on the emotional night was the return of Argentina's incendiary World Cup banner claiming their national sovereignty over the Falkland Islands.

Eyebrows were raised by the singer of the Argentine national anthem, Falklands War veteran Fabio Santana, who stood beside the same flag which was thrown down from the crowds after Argentina defeated England in their World Cup semi-final meeting.

Argentina also courted controversy with the return of the World Cup 'Malvinas' banner, which the federation were previously fined over

Santana then wrapped himself in the flag and embraced Messi, displaying the banner's 'Malvinas' message which translates to 'the Falklands are ours'.

The Argentina football federation was fined a staggering £237,000 after players displayed the banner after victory Stateside and sang anti-English songs.

The message was painted on a hotel bedsheet and smuggled into the stadium before the incendiary clash, with a member of the Argentina national team set-up confirming with a picture on social media that the banner was taken back to the team's hotel after the final whistle.

Before the grudge match, tensions had been inflamed by Argentine ministers and journalists reasserting the country's claim to the islands, and after the banner was displayed, the backlash in the United Kingdom was fierce.

UK Secretary of State for Business and Trade Peter Kyle said it was 'entirely inappropriate' to wave the banner, praising England for acting with dignity in ‘real contrast with what we saw with the Argentina team’.

Sports.title: Ex-Tottenham defender Ramon Vega steps forward to challenge Gianni Infantino and save FIFA
Sports.content:
Ramon Vega is stepping forward to serve as the next president of FIFA.

Former Switzerland international Vega says he has strong support to challenge Gianni Infantino at the election next March. And he has now launched an 11-page manifesto explaining why he is the right man to become the new chief of world football.

Vega, 55, is a compelling candidate because he brings together two worlds rarely combined at the highest level of football leadership: elite professional football and international finance and governance.

He says: “Football is woven into the very fabric of my being. I’m standing because my life prepared me to serve the game.”

‌



The ex-Tottenham League Cup winner and Celtic domestic treble-winning defender says he will put fans and players at the centre of his vision after claiming the game has been left “facing a serious crisis of trust and identity.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“I was a defender on the field. I am ready to defend the game — its integrity, its people and its future.”

‌



Vega, who has been preparing to seek the FIFA presidency since 2015, said the concerns he raised during previous attempts to stand — including his 2022 campaign, which ended under what he describes as “difficult and deeply questionable circumstances” — have become increasingly visible across world football.

“In 2022, I said that when the football community and wider society were ready for real reform, I would be ready to lead and coordinate that change,” Vega said. “Four years later, I am still here. My commitment has not changed, and the time has come.”

Vega said his candidacy would focus on restoring trust in FIFA, strengthening institutional governance, protecting the independence and dignity of its member associations, ensuring a fairer and more effective distribution of football’s financial resources, and creating a more transparent and inclusive decision-making system involving those directly affected by FIFA’s decisions.

“I am not standing to continue the war. I am standing to end it,” Vega said.

‌



View 7 Images Ramon Vega during his time with Tottenham

“Football needs dialogue, stability and unity. We may not agree on everything, but we must find common ground and put the interests of the game before individual interests.”

Vega says: “At the heart of my campaign is my Hungarian wife and First Lady, Claudia — my partner throughout this mission and a woman with her own remarkable history in football.

“More than 25 years ago, when very few women worked at the highest levels of the men’s professional game, she was already breaking barriers — working in technical and operational roles and sitting on the bench in men’s UEFA Champions League, UEFA Cup and international competition. Her experience extends from technical operations and the pitch to the boardroom and football diplomacy.

‌



“With studies in media, communications and psychology, 20 years of ballet training, and extensive international experience, she brings discipline, resilience, empathy and a deep understanding of both football and people.”

7 View 7 Images Ramon Vega alongside his wife Claudia 7 View 7 Images Claudia is playing a key role in her husband's bid to become FIFA president

Vega says: “Claudia was breaking barriers long before inclusion became a slogan. She earned her place on her own merit. Her journey represents a principle at the heart of our vision: competence, courage and leadership have no gender.”

‌



They both care passionately about the men’s and women’s game and all age groups. Vega speaks six different languages and has a degree in economics and finance.

For more than a decade, they have travelled the world together, listening to people across the game and learning from the different realities facing the global football family. Associations across different confederations have encouraged Vega to pursue this candidacy. That encouragement has continued to grow.

“Before the World Cup, I had already communicated my intention to stand for the FIFA presidency to one of FIFA’s vice presidents. This candidacy is therefore not a sudden decision. It is the result of years of preparation, dialogue and commitment.”

The former Swiss centre-half is well known in football boardrooms, within international football circles and among player unions, and he says the football calendar will be a key part of his manifesto.

‌



View 7 Images Ramon Vega will contest Gianni Infantino in next year's elections (Image: Tomasz Karczewski/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

There has not been one clear favourite to stand against Infantino, and there is a deadline of November 18 to stand as a candidate in the FIFA election next March. Any candidate must receive the backing of at least five federations, and Vega says he has that support to go up against Infantino, who has already confirmed he plans to stand again.

Vega has presented a passionate manifesto of clear aims and targets, and football has also been crying out for former players to take senior roles within the game.

Highly educated Vega, who also speaks six languages fluently, played for Cagliari in Italy during a career which also took him from Switzerland to England and Scotland. He said:

‌



“Football is the people’s game. It belongs to everyone — players, coaches, referees, volunteers, communities and the billions of fans who give the game its soul.

“For a long time, I have felt that it is our destiny to serve — to serve football, to serve its people and to leave a legacy for generations to come.

“Football taught me that the game is far more than a sport. It is a source of identity, unity and hope for billions of people.

“My journey did not end on the pitch. For the past 25 years, I have built a career in the financial industry in London and globally, working with businesses across different continents, languages and cultures.

‌



View 7 Images Gianni Infantino has come under fire since this summer's World Cup (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

“Football is facing a serious crisis of trust and credibility. The current leadership has demoralised the game. Dictatorship, intimidation and blackmail have divided member associations.

“We cannot allow battles of egos within football administration to damage the players, coaches, referees and billions of supporters who deserve better. Football is in the emergency room, on life support. We cannot wait any longer.

“Power-driven individuals must never again be allowed to govern our game. No individual or institution is greater than football itself. The President must serve FIFA — not control it.

‌



“I have come in the spirit of fair play — not merely to criticise, but to unite all those who work for the game, play the game and love the game.

“Football needs fundamental reform, restored trust and stability — not cosmetic adjustments. We cannot heal division through boycotts that only create more damage and deepen the divide.

“We must answer challenges with solutions, not confrontation. I have a duty and a social responsibility to protect and defend the game. I come from the game, I stand for the game, and I will fight for the game.”

Vega says the last World Cup — with sky-high ticket prices — was impossible for fans, while he is equally passionate about restructuring the global calendar, which is a huge issue for players.

‌



He added: “The game belongs to the people. The fans are being priced out. The game is losing its soul.

View 7 Images Ramon Vega along with Henrik Larsson celebrating winning the league title with Celtic in 2001

“Players’ welfare and safeguarding must be at the heart of the game. We need a responsible international calendar that protects their health and puts quality before quantity.”

Vega doesn’t see the FIFA Presidency as a position of personal power. Humility and dialogue are the philosophy of his leadership.

‌



“I am not standing for greed, ego or power. I have already achieved my professional career and built a second career in the global financial world. I am a fulfilled and balanced person.

"I do not need a position to define who I am, but I have an athlete’s DNA. I am always driven to improve, develop and make things better. That is why I am here — not to take from football, but to give back to it and inspire the next generation.

“My purpose is straightforward: to serve football and the people who give the game its life. I am standing to reunite the global football family, deliver genuine and lasting reforms, modernise FIFA for the 21st century, restore stability and credibility, and rebuild the trust that our game urgently needs.

“I offer every member association a neutral, independent and credible democratic alternative: a candidate rooted in the game who can bridge football and international business, bring cultures together and lead FIFA with competence, integrity and independence.

‌



“My integrity and my love for the game are unwavering. The game is ready for change, and I am ready to serve football!”

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Punishment agreement, UEFA consider action, HMRC investigation revealed
Sports.content:
Manchester City are still waiting to discover their punishment for being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules, though they have appealed the decision

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live blog on Wednesday, October 7, where we will bring you the latest after an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of breaking Premier League rules in a strongly-worded report released last week.

City were found to have inflated revenue by more than £830million over a nine-season period between 2009-10 and 2017-18. However, the Etihad club have since appealed against the decision and continue to deny any wrongdoing.

However, it is being reported that Premier League clubs believe City should be expelled from the top flight next season if their appeal against the financial charges fails. That’s according to Sky Sports, who are reporting that clubs in the top-flight believe a points deduction would not be sufficient if it resulted in City spending just one season outside the Premier League.

UEFA are also believed to be monitoring developments and will wait until the end of the Premier League's disciplinary process before deciding whether to take any potential action against City.

The Financial Times is reporting that HMRC probed City in 2018 over whether it used complex arrangements to underpay tax. The report claims a civil investigation into the club’s tax affairs followed the publication of leaked internal emails by Der Spiegel in 2018. The Financial Times says Man City and HMRC declined to comment.

And former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher believes City should face a multi-year punishment for their financial misdemeanours. There is still much discussion about potential outcomes, so stay right here for all of the latest...

Sports.title: Micah Richards leaps to Cristiano Ronaldo defence and fires shots at Alan Shearer's record
Sports.content:
Micah Richards leaps to Cristiano Ronaldo defence and fires shots at Alan Shearer's record

Micah Richards poked fun an Alan Shearer's goalscoring record with England, as he underlined the case for Cristiano Ronaldo to continue with Portugal amid criticism of the veteran forward

View 2 Images Micah Richards has launched a defence of Cristiano Ronaldo following criticism this week (Image: Getty)

Micah Richards has jumped to the defence of Cristiano Ronaldo, insisting he still has "a couple of years left" - and took aim at Alan Shearer's England record.

‌



‌



The Portuguese superstar chose to issue an apology on social media on Tuesday night after walking out of camp following a disagreement with Jorge Jesus over playing time and his role.

‌



Now 41, Ronaldo is in the twilight years of his career and many expected him to retire in the aftermath of the World Cup, but he's chosen to remain playing. Jorge Jesus' arrival has heralded a new era with Portugal, and his ideas have seemingly angered the five-time Ballon d'Or winner.

‌



Portugal won all four games during the international break and, after failing to surpass a quarter-final since their Euro 2016 victory, there is now a school of thought that as a team they are better without Ronaldo - and Shearer admits it is hard to accept your own decline.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said on The Rest is Football: "It's the hardest thing to accept that you perhaps aren't as good as you have been over the years."

Richards quipped back and said: "He's still got a couple of years left in him, come on guys, he can still score. I'm not having that he's done yet, he's still banging them in."

Ronaldo remains prolific in Saudi Arabia, albeit there's criticism of the quality of opposition he's facing. With Al-Nassr he's scored 132 times in 155 games and his Portugal exploits have seen him become the highest scorer in the history of international football.

‌



The former Manchester City defender was then reminded of Ronaldo's recent international record. He failed to score from open play at the World Cup in Qatar, went goalless at Euro 2024 and then scored just twice at this summer's World Cup - with those two strikes coming against minnows Uzbekistan.

View 2 Images Micah Richards mocked Alan Shearer's England goalscoring record (Image: PA)

It was then that Richards chose to take aim at Shearer and his 30 goals for the Three Lions, claiming that a host of those came against lesser outfits.

Article continues below

"Oh we're bringing teams into," he said. "Ask Al who he scored against? Gaz scored against top teams, Al scored against some terrible teams."

Whilst Shearer's only England hat-trick came against Luxembourg at Wembley, the Newcastle legend did come up with goals against leading nations, often at major tournaments. At Euro 96 he top scored, finding the net against Holland and Germany. At the World Cup two years later he scored in the last 16 loss to Argentina and his final international goal came in a 1-0 victory over Germany at Euro 2000.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua tickets prices revealed for mega-fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua tickets prices revealed for mega-fight

The two British heavyweight legends will clash in Cardiff on December 11 with more than 80,000 tickets set to go on sale on Friday

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua (Image: Getty Images for Netflix)

Boxing fans will have to stump up at least £75 to watch Tyson Fury take on Anthony Joshua.

‌



‌



The two British heavyweight legends will clash in Cardiff on December 11 with more than 80,000 tickets set to go on sale on Friday. And the cheapest seats, high up in the stands, will cost £75, with no prices yet released for seats closer to the ring. Fans can expect VIP tickets to cost well over £1,000.

‌



Meanwhile, Fury insists his grudge match with Joshua is perfectly timed as he predicts a classic to rival the ‘Thrilla in Manila’. Previous attempts to match the UK’s pre-eminent heavyweights of their generation have repeatedly fallen through, but Fury rejects the widely-held belief the bout has arrived too late.

‌



Tyson Fury to make Donald Trump offer for Anthony Joshua fight READ MORE :

Tyson Fury's uncle responds to claim he is helping Anthony Joshua READ MORE :

Instead, he has invoked the thrilling third meeting between Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier in 1975 as inspiration to deliver a spectacular night in the Welsh capital. “I don’t regret anything because it’s finally happening,” Fury said. “It probably makes more financial sense now and that’s what we’re in this sport for.

“It’s more money than it ever was before, plus the fact we’ve got the broadcasting giant Netflix streaming it and (Saudi Arabian boxing supremo) Turki Alalshikh has got an open chequebook. “There’s never been a better time to be the don of the division. And the fact it’s happening in Cardiff – even better.

‌



“You got Ali v Joe later on in their careers – it was a great fight and I believe this will be a great fight, too. I believe it will be one of the biggest fights the world ’s ever seen and it’ll live up to all the expectations.” Outside the respectful tone struck at Wednesday’s launch presser when he offered to share a pint of Guinness with Joshua after they had finished in the ring, Fury has been directing a verbal onslaught at his 36-year-old foe.

“I don’t know him as a man,” the ‘Gypsy King’ said. “I only know him as the fake facade we see on TV or when he’s doing interviews. I don’t know anything about him at all behind the mask. Sometimes that slips now and again, but I don’t know him as an individual, I don’t know him at all.

“For me, he was never any good. He would never beat me in a million years in any time. When I hit him with that right hand, he’s going to feel the full force of it, he’s going to fall over in a heap. Before the bell goes, he’ll be looking for a landing position on the floor somewhere.

Article continues below

“If he didn’t fight me, who would he fight next? He just got knocked down twice by Kristian Prenga, whoever the f*** he is. What happens if he fights a live opponent? Someone who’s not hand-picked and selected – a bum – to knock over? I don’t know anyone he could beat and he definitely ain’t beating me – that’s for sure!”

Sports.title: Narcissist Cristiano Ronaldo needs kicking to the kerb for 2,000 words of Portugal petulance
Sports.content:
Narcissist Cristiano Ronaldo needs kicking to the kerb for 2,000 words of Portugal petulance

Cristiano Ronaldo should be kicked out of the Portugal national team and never allowed to return - his selfish narcissism must not be tolerated anymore

View 4 Images Cristiano Ronaldo left the Portugal squad after a falling out with manager Jorge Jesus (Image: Octavio Passos/Getty Images)

There comes a point in every dictator's declining reign where the delusion completely swallows the man. For Cristiano Ronaldo, that moment arrived in a 2,000-word manifesto that reads like the fever dream of a disgraced monarch demanding his subjects bow down to his bygone glory.

‌



‌



In case you missed the latest instalment of the endless, suffocating Festival of Ronaldo, after being denied his mandatory red-carpet entry during Portugal's 2-1 win over Norway last month, the 41-year-old folded his monogrammed dressing gowns, bunged them in a suitcase, and flew home in a sulk.

‌



There was no applause for the plebs in the stands, nor any sweaty high-fives for his team-mates. Just a dark, thunderous march down the tunnel and up the stairs of his private jet, before spending the next week furiously drafting a wild list of demands, specifying the exact, mandatory compliments that Portugal boss Jorge Jesus was required to pay him at his next press conference.

‌



Let that settle in for a second. A five-time Ballon d'Or-winning multi-millionaire, a human monument carved out of abs and unyielding vanity, sat down to compose a compulsory script for his international manager.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo prove how different they are with farewell actions READ MORE :

Why Cristiano Ronaldo is furious with Jorge Jesus as scathing Portugal statement released READ MORE :

When Jesus refused to play the ventriloquist's dummy, Ronaldo's fragile, heavily moisturised ego couldn't take it. He said he felt "betrayed" - as though a sacred, divine covenant between deity and peasant had been brutally shattered by the mere application of tactical common sense.

‌



He bitterly lamented that Jesus had reneged on a solemn pledge to give him 30 minutes of pitch-time - as if international football were a school play where every student is guaranteed a speaking part.

But the real sting, the absolute core of his existential anguish, was that Jesus had omitted his pre-approved eight-point press conference script. A list of commandments, lest we forget, that explicitly told the manager to publicly rank him alongside Pele and Diego Maradona.

It is a level of unhinged, diamond-encrusted entitlement usually reserved for Roman emperors in their lead-poisoned twilight. A spectacle of such staggering, glorious narcissism that even the most extravagant opera director would reject it for being entirely too on the nose.

‌



What makes this absurd piece of theatre even more pathetic is the timing. Ronaldo didn't drop his epic announcement on a random Tuesday by accident. He dropped it on the exact day Lionel Messi was taking his final, glorious bow for Argentina.

View 4 Images Argentina fans gave Lionel Messi the send-off his talent - and personality - deserved (Image: 2026 Shutterstock Editorial)

While Messi was being borne aloft in Buenos Aires like a glowing, bearded fragment of human divinity - after scoring, carving out two goals, and bidding a dignified, emotional farewell to a weeping nation following a 3-0 win over Benin - Ronaldo was pacing the lonely marble halls of his mansion, wrapped in a cloud of nuclear-grade envy, unleashing a press release designed to violently drag the global camera lenses off his rival and back toward himself.

‌



That is insecurity on an intergalactic level. It's the footballing equivalent of a toddler throwing a tantrum at someone else's birthday party and smashing the cake to make everyone look at him.

The tragedy of Cristiano Ronaldo is that despite winning everything, earning hundreds of millions, and carving his name into footballing folklore, he remains the most profoundly unfulfilled athlete on earth. He cannot digest the simple, inescapable truth that he might not be the best, and that age comes for us all. He couldn't handle it when Real Madrid stopped treating him like a God, or at Manchester United when Erik ten Hag asked him to run around a bit more. Now, he's treating an unexpected half-hour on the bench for Portugal as if it were a national tragedy requiring a UN intervention.

For half-a-decade now, Ronaldo has been an anchor holding Portugal back. His hyper-vampiric edge faded years ago, yet he stubbornly refuses to step aside. When colleagues like Goncalo Ramos come into the side and actually score goals, Ronaldo doesn't celebrate the team's success - he scowls from the sidelines, genuinely affronted that the footballing cosmos has the audacity to continue expanding without someone passing to him.

‌



View 4 Images Cristiano Ronaldo's egotism has been dragging Portugal down for years (Image: Getty Images)

We witnessed this tragicomedy in full bloom at the Qatar World Cup, where he mounted a forensic global campaign to claim Bruno Fernandes' goal against Uruguay on the grounds that a single, heavily-gelled hair follicle had grazed the ball as it dropped into the net. If Portugal win 5-0 and Ronaldo doesn't get on the scoresheet, he looks like a man whose car has just packed up on the North Circular. That isn't - as some exasperatingly try to argue - elite drive or unmatched winning mentality. It's pure, toxic selfishness.

Everyone sees through the facade now. Even his most devoted admirers - with the inevitable exception of Piers Morgan, who no doubt will find a way to champion this latest royal foot-stomp - are out of excuses. A profound, bone-deep exhaustion has settled over the watching world. Portuguese football fans are simply spent, suffering from terminal, unremitting CR7 fatigue.

‌



There are those who believe Ronaldo deserves a grand, misty-eyed farewell match like the one Messi enjoyed in Buenos Aires. A warm, golden evening of soft-focus nostalgia, rhythmic applause, and a tearful guard of honour lining his exit into the sunset. But in truth, he deserves precisely none of that.

A player who treats his country's shirt as a mere marketing prop for his personal brand does not earn the right to a dignified curtain call. A player who abandons his team-mates in the middle of an international window because his ego took a dent does not get a standing ovation. Ronaldo has proven, over and over again, that the name on the back of the shirt will always mean infinitely more to him than the crest on the front.

View 4 Images Ronaldo does not deserve a glorious, heartfelt farewell (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Portugal need to finally grow a spine, change the locks on the dressing room, and make the decision Ronaldo is too arrogant to make himself. Boot him out. Strike his name from the squad list and lock the door behind him. No farewell friendly. No ceremonial subbing off in the 89th minute. No lap of honour through a twinkling sea of smartphone screens.

Cristiano Ronaldo desperately wanted to write his own immortal ending. Instead, he should go out in a blaze of self-inflicted humiliation, remembered in his final international chapter not as a heroic colossus, but as a narcissistic, insecure diva who couldn't bear to sit in the back seat for once.

The Festival of Ronaldo is officially over. Pack down the marquee. Unplug the speakers. Turn off the lights.

Sports.title: Three wonderkids dubbed 'English Messi' and what happened as real thing retires from Argentina
Sports.content:
Three wonderkids dubbed 'English Messi' and what happened as real thing retires from Argentina

Several English players have been burdened with the tag over the years

View 4 Images Numerous players have been compared to the great Lionel Messi down the years (Image: Getty Images)

With a low centre of gravity, an unmatched dribbling skill set and a wand of a left foot, Lionel Messi's profile is incredibly unique. After 208 caps, 126 goals and 67 assists, the Argentine international has retired from international football, leaving as arguably the sport's greatest ever player.

‌



‌



When a young English player comes through the ranks with a comparable playing style, they have at times been dubbed 'the English Messi.' Said players then understandably struggle to live up to the hype and eventually fall by the wayside, sometimes out of the game entirely.

‌



Mirror Football recalls three players who were compared to Messi in their youth, the teams they've played for and where they are now...

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Harvey Elliott

Standing at 1.7 metres with a silky left foot, Harvey Elliott was dubbed 'the English Messi' by the media after joining Liverpool from Fulham in 2019.

Harvey Elliott enduring second loan nightmare as Liverpool star branded 'overweight' READ MORE :

Following an impressive loan at Blackburn, he broke into Jurgen Klopp's starting line-up before a horrific ankle fracture in September 2021 cruelly halted his momentum. Though he recovered to make 53 appearances in 2023/24, his game time dropped under Arne Slot, prompting a loan to Aston Villa.

‌



After Villa opted against activating his purchase clause, Elliott endured a wasted season in the Second City. Still contracted to Liverpool, he is now looking to kickstart his career on loan at Valencia.

View 4 Images Harvey Elliott's career has stalled after such a bright start (Image: Nigel French/Allstar, Getty Images)

Marcus Edwards

Speaking in 2016, then Tottenham boss Mauricio Pochettino remarked that Marcus Edwards' movement, body shape and dribbling style reminded him "a little bit of the beginning of Messi." No pressure then!

‌



The 17-year-old had just made his Spurs debut against Gillingham in the League Cup, but the pressure proved difficult to bear. After failing to make the grade at Spurs, Edwards took a leap abroad, rebuilding his career in Portugal with Vitoria de Guimaraes.

His form for Vitoria earned him a move to Sporting CP, where the winger scored 24 goals in 120 appearances. In 2025, Edwards returned to England with Burnley, where the now-27-year-old features in the Championship.

View 4 Images Marcus Edwards is now playing for Burnley following a spell in Portugal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Callum Gribbin

Former Manchester United youngster Callum Gribbin announced his promise during Edwin van der Sar's 2011 testimonial, scoring twice, including dispossessing a young Matthijs de Ligt, before a packed Amsterdam Arena.

His cheek and flair drew interest from Liverpool and Manchester City, earning him comparisons to Messi. However, off-pitch issues hindered his progression just as he approached senior breakthroughs.

View 4 Images Callum Gribbin played alongside Marcus Rashford in the Manchester United youth ranks (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Article continues below

After leaving Old Trafford, Gribbin had short spells with Sheffield United, Barrow and Radcliffe across the Football League and non-league. He has been without a club since leaving Warrington Rylands in 2025.

Sports.title: Premier League injury news: Club by Club updates and potential return dates
Sports.content:
Few teams escape the international break without some kind of fitness issue, which can often lead to a sense of frustration as the Premier League prepares to resume this weekend.

And it's been no different this time around, particularly after the game's bosses decided on an international break which has crammed four fixtures in three weeks.

Alex Scott's injury whilst away with England has again ignited the club vs country row as teams lay the blame for their player's welfare with the national sides.

We've seen a spate of players withdrawing from international duty, Arsenal infamously doing so previously, as clubs look to protect their players. Cole Palmer's decision to miss this set of England games served as a major frustration to Thomas Tuchel.

‌



We're about as far from the business end of the season as you can get, which can make stomaching injuries that bit easier, but equally no manager wants to be without his best players for any period of time.
