JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

We've got some huge clashes this weekend, some having major subplots. Manchester United face Tottenham as two underfire managers square off whilst Manchester City play for the first time since their guilty verdict, against Liverpool of all teams. We cast our eye over all 20 clubs to see how their squad is looking.

‌



Arsenal

William Saliba's injury is well documented and has kept him out thus far, but Ezri Konsa, who can act as a replacement, withdrew from England duty with a muscle issue, casting doubt over his availability. Ben White and Cristhian Mosquera were unlucky to miss out on the Brighton loss, and should be available. Kai Havertz and Christos Tzolis both picked up injuries on international duty, but their diagnosis will see them miss weeks, not months.

View 8 Images Ezri Konsa had to pull out of England duty and is now an injury concern (Image: MARKO PERKOV/AFP via Getty Images)

Aston Villa

Unai Emery knows that Amadou Onana's ACL injury will keep him out long-term, new signing Leon Goretzka confirmed he would be out until after the international break. Ian Maatsen is out with Emery claiming he could be sidelined for "a long, long time." Pau Torres and Marco Bizot are both doubts.

Bournemouth

The Cherries are unhappy with the way they believe England handled Scott - which means he could be out for up to eight weeks. A thigh injury will keep him out, he felt the issue prior to the win over Croatia, but played 70 minutes in midfield before being substituted. Eli Junior Kroupi is set to be back by November at the latest. He's been recovering from surgery on a foot injury sustained during a pre-season training and is targeting a return before the international break next month. Julian Araujo, Justin Kluivert and Veljko Milosavljevic will all miss out this weekend.

‌



Brentford

Mikkel Damsgaard is out having picked up an ankle injury whilst on international duty. Kaye Furo will also be missing after undergoing an operation. Mathias Jensen is a doubt but could yet feature this weekend whilst Josh DaSilva has returned to full fitness.

View 8 Images Mikkel Damsgaard is a doubt for Brentford

Brighton

Summer signing Femi Azeez could finally make his Seagulls debut this weekend. He arrived carrying an injury and is yet to play, but the international break has afforded him the time to regain his fitness. Brighton hope to have Jack Hinshelwood available. The likes of Kaoru Mitoma, Stefanos Tzimas and Evan Ferguson are longer term injuries whilst Yankuba Minteh is touch and go.

Chelsea

Cole Palmer controversially pulled out of England duty to work on a foot injury, but is in contention to play on Saturday. Joao Pedro, who missed the loss at Brentford, is expected back this month even if he misses out this weekend. Moises Caicedo has played just 14 minutes this season but could run out this weekend, as could Reece James.

‌



View 8 Images Moises Caicedo has played just 14 minutes this season (Image: Getty Images)

Coventry

Frank Lampard is hoping to have Haji Wright back by the end of this month, with this weekend potentially coming too soon. However Kaine Kesler-Hayden and Luke Woolfenden are both in contention to play. Aurele Amenda's calf injury is significant.

Crystal Palace

The Eagles could welcome back a trio of injured players following the international break. Dean Henderson, Jean-Philippe Mateta and Takehiro Tomiyasu all look to have dealt with their respective issues and could play this weekend.

Everton

The treatment room is a relatively quiet place on the blue half of Merseyside as David Moyes ' hopes to have summer arrival Christian Norgaard back after a period out. Merlin Rohl was another targeting this weekend, but it remains to be seen whether he'll be deemed fit enough to play.

‌



View 8 Images David Moyes is enjoying a squad largely free from injuries (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Fulham

The west Londoners are set to have Kenny Tete back after he was dealing with concussion. Tom Cairney underwent surgery on his knee back in August and had always been targeting this set of fixtures as a return date, but its more likely he'll be in contention from next weekend.

Hull

The newly promoted side have endured a fast start but have a notable injury list. Eliot Matazo's ACL injury will keep him out until the New Year whilst Jack Butland is another more long-term injury. Darko Gyabi is eyeing a November return. The impressive Nobel Mendy as well as Matt Targett, Elliot Stroud and Hidemasa Morita could all play this weekend.

Ipswich

The Tractor Boys' only absentee in September was Jack Taylor but the midfielder is now back and pushing for game time on Saturday.

‌



View 8 Images Harry Wilson has endured a slow start to his Leeds career

Leeds

Harry Wilson's time out with a quad injury could end this weekend as the Welshman looks to click into gear after his summer move. A hamstring injury has sidelined Joe Rodon for almost two months and this weekend could come too soon whilst we won't see Mateo Joseph until the New Year.

Liverpool

Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley won't be seen before this month is out as Giovanni Leoni continues his long road back, but could play in 2026 having barely featured since signing for the Reds. Federico Chiesa and Alexander Isak could play against Manchester City on Sunday whilst Cody Gakpo withdrew from international duty recently with no diagnosis yet communicated. Jeremy Jacquet was left out of the squad for France's game against Belgium on Monday after he picked up a slight knock, but could still feature this weekend with the club still to assess him.

Man City

Nico O'Reilly withdrew from the England squad for their final two Nations League matches of the international break because of injury with the severity yet to be determined, but is the only major issue for Enzo Maresca.

‌



View 8 Images Nico O'Reilly was another who withdrew from England duty (Image: Getty)

Man Utd

Marcus Rashford, Amad and Benjamin Sesko have all been nursing knocks but could be in contention this weekend. Matthijs de Ligt has been a more long-term absentee but the defender is edging closer to his return. Patrick Dorgu had to leave Denmark camp during the international break and this Saturday could come too soon. Manuel Ugarte continues his recovery from a long-term injury.

Newcastle

Whilst the Magpies are keeping tabs on the fitness of a host of their first-team stars, very few are long-term concerns and several of them could play this weekend. Nico Gonzalez, Jacob Ramsey, Anthony Elanga and Matias Fernandez-Pardo are all in contention. Tino Livramento withdrew from England duty recently and there's no word on him as of yet.

View 8 Images Newcastle will hope to have Nico Gonzalez back this weekend (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Nottingham Forest

Nikola Milenkovic and Nicolo Savona had been the only two injury concerns at the City Ground but both men are in the mix to play this weekend.

Sunderland

Romaine Mundle has been sidelined since the start of the season and is eyeing a return come late December into early January. Brian Brobbey played for the Netherlands recently but was forced off with an injury. Habib Diarra is close to a return whilst Daniel Ballard is nursing a thigh issue.

Tottenham

ACL injuries will keep Wilson Odobert and Xavi Simons sidelined - the latter out until 2027 comes around. Micky van de Ven is set to return this weekend with Pedro Porro and Mykhailo Mudryk remain sidelined. Dejan Kulusevski has been a notable absentee but his issue is not major and a first outing of the season is nearing.

Sports.title: Arsenal fans should savour every minute of Mikel Arteta - this could be his last contract
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta is already the longest-serving manager in the Premier League.

And now his new deal will take him beyond ten years in charge, beyond Jurgen Klopp's tenure at Liverpool and hurtling past Pep Guardiola'sdecade at Manchester City.

But it is impossible to believe he will ever get close to the 20 years plus that both Arsene Wenger and Sir Alex Ferguson had at Arsenal and Manchester United.

Furthermore, I think this could be Arteta’s last deal at Arsenal. Over ten years would be some achievement.

‌



England have gone up a gear without Declan Rice - his place is now under serious threat READ MORE :

Arsene Wenger was right to be fuming about Man City - now football owes him an apology READ MORE :

But the reason I think it may be his last is that the manager’s job has changed so much, it is so demanding and so gruelling that it breaks lesser, mere mortals.

You have to be some sort of Superman to carry on - and succeed - for this long. Arteta is defying sleep, logic and reason.

Endless meetings, endless demands and endless planning. His diary is planned to the minute. Every department of the club wants a piece of him. The job is so different to what it was.

It is utterly draining and I just think Arsenal should savour every minute he is in charge.

‌



What a job he has done. Arteta took charge in December 2019 and inherited a club which was dear to his heart - and a club in an absolute mess.

View 3 Images Pep Guardiola managed a decade at Man City before standing down (Image: Getty)

Don't miss John Cross' exclusive newsletter every Friday - just for Mirror+ subscribers - CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP

The job he has done has been nothing short of remarkable. I genuinely think the biggest thing he has done - and it comes before the first title in 22 years - is reconnecting with the fan base. They had become disillusioned and were unhappy.

‌



Now, Arsenal fans are connected, engaged and they even sing that awful North London Forever. That’s how much they’ve bought into it.

Last week we had the City verdict and that showed the scale of the job Arteta and the rest - like Klopp and Co - have done up even compete. Naturally Arteta will face some questions over his time at City and what he knew. That will take some navigating.

But Arteta’s crowning glory is the first title in 22 years. That was sensational and shows just what a job he has done.

To rebuild a fractured squad and a broken club, to turn them into champions… they finished second and needed to find a way to win. Arteta cracked it.

‌



View 3 Images Arteta will now go all out to add the Champions League to the Premier League (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Another reason why I think this may be Arteta’s last contract is that he will go full out to win the Champions League.

Arteta was absolutely gutted after losing the final. It hurt him so much. Haunted him all summer. But he wants to go back and win it more than anything.

There was a summer after his first title push where Arteta talked about questioning whether he could stay and had enough to complete the job. PSG were keen at that time. He could have gone. But he stayed to finish the job.

‌



That is why I think Arteta will see the Champions League as his next target and he will not give up until he wins it. But I’m convinced he can do it within his next contract.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: Dana White labels Eddie Hearn a NEPO BABY as war of words escalates between the promoters over Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua showdown
Sports.content:
Dana White labels Eddie Hearn a NEPO BABY as war of words escalates between the promoters over Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua showdown

Dana White's war of words with Eddie Hearn has taken another turn after the UFC and Zuffa Boxing chief essentially branded his rival a nepo baby.

The duo have been at each other's throats over various topics this year, from Conor Benn's future to the £150million blockbuster fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

Things have escalated over the last month. White, who runs Zuffa Boxing alongside Saudi Arabia's boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh, has been billed as the main promoter for the heavyweight showdown and fought for the contest to take place in New York City.

Hearn, who successfully wrestled the fight back to Cardiff, has claimed that the contract Joshua signed stipulates that White cannot be involved in the contest and threatened crunch talks with broadcaster Netflix over White's attendance at Fury and Joshua's press conference on Wednesday in London.

And now, White has taken aim. He said on the Diary of a CEO podcast: 'Eddie's not the guy, Eddie's dad is the guy.

'And I'm not saying this to s*** on Eddie - I'm just being honest. I don't dislike Eddie. But he's not the guy; his dad's the guy.'

Dana White (left) has taken aim at Eddie Hearn (right) as their war of words continues - source: X - @danawhite

White branded Hearn a nep baby due to the sporting success of his father Barry (second left)

Barry Hearn, Eddie's father, has been a sports promoter since the 1970s and has had a huge influence on the likes of boxing, darts and snooker.

Eddie, though, now works in his own right though, according to White, is in his dad's shadow.

White continued: 'Frank Warren's the real guy. I just saw this interview with him; I was like, 'F***ing love it… all this f***ing talking and all this f***ing bulls***, let's f***ing fight.''

There had been doubt over whether the December 11 fight would in fact go ahead due to the involvement of White.

White, whose involvement has been criticised by sections of the British boxing public, was grilled by the media in a cagey press conference, where he labelled the bout a 's***show' while conceding he has 'no idea' if the contest will take place.

'I don't know. The guy who is supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight the entire time,' he said. 'He hasn't done the fight any favours. I don't know anybody who is more full of s*** than Eddie Hearn.'

When asked whether he would step aside to allow the fight to go ahead, White said: 'That's not up to me. I'm involved in the f***ing fight.

'If Eddie Hearn really cared about this f***ing fight — first of all the fight would've happened a f***ing long time ago, one. Number two, he could finance the thing himself.

'Listen, this whole thing's a s***show right now. We'll all know a lot more in the next three, four days, see how this thing plays out.'

The duo have been at a battle over who will promote the fight between Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua (right)

White had initially raised eyebrows when Benn left Hearn's Matchroom to join Zuffa.

It remains to be seen whether White will have any involvement.

Hearn said this weekend: 'At this point, (White's) completely cooked. What he actually said was, "We're doing the TV production". Which, again, in the contract, is prohibited.

'After that video (of White saying he was producing the fight), I spoke to Sela (the Saudi entertainment company listed as promoters of the event). I said, "Have you seen this video?" They said, in writing, "Yes, and it's completely untrue".

'(White) cannot do that under the contract. They want me to meet them in LA next week, which I probably will.'

Sports.title: From beauty to beast! Former 'Miss Germany' targets a BOXING career and is set for her professional debut
Sports.content:
From beauty to beast! Former 'Miss Germany' targets a BOXING career and is set for her professional debut

A former winner of Miss Germany has announced a surprise career switch - and will swap the catwalk for the boxing ring at the age of 33.

Tatjana Genrich was voted Germany's most beautiful woman in 2022 and has now announced she will make her professional boxing debut next month in Magdeburg, rekindling her childhood love of the sport.

Genrich was the Saxony-Anhalt state champion in the flyweight division for amateur boxers between 2007 and 2009. And she recently opened up on why she originally went into the sport, saying: 'At school I was often bullied and I wanted to find a way to defend myself. That's how it all started.'

This then led to her attending a sports school in Halle, Germany where she was picked up by boxing promoter Ulf Steinforth. Years later he reconnected with the model after her fame and stature had grown and suggested the former amateur champion try her hand in the professional ranks.

When asked about their talks, Genrich said: 'Since I sponsor the ring girls at his boxing events, he approached me one day and asked if I wouldn't like to get back in the ring. I finally agreed and am now about to make my professional debut.'

Only four years ago she was Miss Germany... now Tatjana Genrich has her sights set on a career in boxing

The supermodel turned boxer still posts regularly to her 44,500 Instagram followers and owns her own modelling agency

Genrich will be hoping to her journey will inspire a new generation of young women into different sports

View this post on Instagram

Promoter SES Boxing are backing Genrich to become the country's next big superstar, saying: 'Tatjana can follow in Regina Halmich's footsteps. She has all the necessary qualities, an incredible presence, and is extremely ambitious.'

Halmich won 54 of her 56 fights during a storied career between 1994 and 2017 which saw her become one of the most successful female boxers of all time, and also modelled for German magazines.

To prepare for her first fight on November 14, Genrich - who also runs her own modelling agency with 80 models under contract - has begun a rigorous training routine that sees her spending five full days a week in the gym.

In her corner she will have coach Dirk Dzemski, who guided Robert Stieglitz to world champion status in the 2010s.

Genrich also detailed another motivation to succeed in her new career, saying:' I want to be a role model for young women and show them that you can be successful in both your career and sports.

'I train in areas like posture, running and choreography. This prepares me for competitions as well as events like fashion shows.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury plans to invite 'old buddy' Donald Trump to be part of his ringwalk for £150m mega-fight with Anthony Joshua: 'I'll definitely make the offer!'
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury has suggested he will try and persuade United States president Donald Trump to join him for his ringwalk when he takes on Anthony Joshua in December.

Fury met the president at the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in June, joining Trump, First Lady Melania Trump and a host of MAGA royalty on the South Lawn.

He raised eyebrows with a cap, which featured a particularly bold message of support for Trump. 'Donald Trump for Prime Minister', it read alongside an embroidered British flag.

The slogan was a nod to Trump's signature red 'Make America Great Again' caps, which he sported throughout his election campaigns.

It was there Fury said he was keen to take on Joshua in the near future – and that fight has come to fruition, and will take place on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

And Fury is keen to have his friend there. He said: 'I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we'll see if he's available.

'Probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States.'

Tyson Fury (centre) has said he will ask Donald Trump (right) to join his ringwalk when he faces Anthony Joshua

Though Fury may want Trump in his corner, Joshua will literally have a Fury in his, with Tyson's uncle, Peter, part of Joshua's group of trainers.

Tyson shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years, but his father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives'.

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

Sports.title: John Fury hits out at brother Peter, calling him a 'cockroach' for joining Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of Cardiff showdown
Sports.content:
John Fury called out his brother Peter for being a 'cockroach' after his estranged brother joined Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of the Briton's showdown with his son Tyson in December.

The long-awaited Battle of Britain is set to take place in Cardiff after months of back-and-forth between the Fury and Joshua camps, but neither John nor Peter will be in the corner of the Gypsy King, after Joshua announced this week that Fury's uncle had helped with his preparations.

Eyebrows were raised due to Peter's family ties, but Fury shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years.

His father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives.'

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

John Fury called out his brother Peter (left) for potentially helping Tyson's rival Anthony Joshua ahead of their Cardiff showdown (pictured in 2015)

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

John may have been staunchly defensive of Fury in the context of Peter doing anything to sabotage him in the ring, but relations between father and son remain minimal after having been, in John's words, 'completely destroyed'.

The duo are at loggerheads over Fury Junior's career, with his father adamant that he should prioritise his health and wellbeing by retiring for good after two failed attempts.

Peter previously trained Fury between 2011 and 2017, but left the camp amid a schism with father and son.

The Gypsy King had previously sought to set the record straight on Peter's involvement with his rival on social media, deeming Joshua's comments 'categorically untrue'.

'Even if Peter Fury hated me, he’s still my family,' he said. 'That would mean he would be a Fredo, scorpion, snake, rat, b****** piece of s*** if he did that.'

Sports.title: Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh calls out Dua Lipa in bizarre rant about pop sensation during Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference
Sports.content:
Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh calls out Dua Lipa in bizarre rant about pop sensation during Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference

Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh has claimed that Dua Lipa has refused to perform at the Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua super-fight in a bizarre tirade against the pop sensation during the launch press conference.

On Wednesday evening, Britain's two most iconic boxers of the last two decades went face to face for the first time since their eagerly anticipated clash was announced last week.

Ahead of the press conference, Alalshikh, who was lauded by Fury, Joshua and many others during the evening for financing the fight, was invited to speak about how the 'Battle of Britain' came to be.

New York's Madison Square Garden and Wembley had previously been billed as potential venues for the 'super' heavyweight clash, but it has since been confirmed that the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, will host the contest.

During his explanation of how the venue was eventually decided, Alalshikh took a swipe at Dua Lipa in the process.

He said: 'I will be honest today, I know that London wouldn't give me the stadium until 2am, and I know that Dua Lipa will not perform in the stadium, because she doesn't like boxing, and maybe she doesn't like me.'

Turki Alalshikh went on a bizarre tirade during Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua press conference

The boxing chief claimed that Dua Lipa has turned down the chance to perform ahead of the long-awaited bout

Dua Lipa's representatives have been approached for comment by Daily Mail Sport.

Alalshikh went on to also explain the financial losses that staging the bout in Britain has led to.

He added: 'Nobody questioned me about UK. I love the British people, I try to deliver everything for them. Put yourself in my shoes; there's a situation to lose $70million (£52.8m); the best is to have it in a good time zone.

'I have two reasons, and I know London won't deliver it; they won't give me the stadium until 2am... Wales delivered it; it's still the UK, the town of Ryan Giggs, let's do it.'

Anthony Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been vocal about his and the two-time heavyweight world champion's desire to have the fight staged in the UK.

The chairman of Matchroom took his moment on stage at the British Airways ARC to thank the British boxing community for applying the 'pressure' to ensure the fight is played out on British soil.

Fury and Joshua faced off for the first time ahead of their super fight on Wednesday evening

'I'm excited,' Hearn said. 'Turki, I know we've fallen out, but I promise you this'll be the greatest night you've ever had in boxing.

'On a serious note, when we talked about this fight, you envisaged it for British boxing. This guy (Joshua) has changed boxing in this country. So has Tyson Fury. We are the envy of the boxing world.

'We can't stage it anywhere else. Thank you to the British public for putting the pressure on. We couldn't do it, we failed.'

Sports.title: Ricky Hatton left £30MILLION estate after his tragic death, new figures reveal, as son Campbell claims family are 'completely in the dark' amid dispute over late boxer's finances
Sports.content:
Ricky Hatton left £30MILLION estate after his tragic death, new figures reveal, as son Campbell claims family are 'completely in the dark' amid dispute over late boxer's finances

Ricky Hatton reportedly amassed a £30million fortune before his death last year, though uncertainty remains over how the boxing legend's estate will be distributed.

Hatton, who died aged 46 last September, won multiple world titles before using his fight earnings to build a business empire worth more than £20million, with at least another £10m tied up in property investments, according to The Sun.

Trustees were appointed to manage Hatton's estate after he took his own life in September last year.

However, sources close to the family claim communication with the trustees has since broken down, with one describing the situation as a 'complete mess', according to an earlier report in The Sun.

It was thought Hatton had intended for his fortune to pass to his three children, Campbell, 25, and daughters Millie, 14, and Fearne, 12. However, a year after his death, the family are still waiting to learn how and when the estate will be distributed.

Campbell told The Sun on Wednesday: 'My family is still completely in the dark. We’ve had no involvement in my dad’s finances for over 15 years.'

Hatton, who died aged 46 last September, won multiple world titles before using his fight earnings to build a business and property empire

It was thought Hatton had intended for his fortune to pass to his three children, Campbell, 25 (above), and daughters Millie, 14, and Fearne, 12

During his successful boxing career, Hatton used his fight earnings to finance a string of businesses, many of them linked to property investments in his hometown of Hyde, as well as in Leicestershire, London and Kent.

One source said Hatton was 'determined to ensure that he had a financial legacy from his incredible career'.

'Everyone who knew and loved Ricky would give anything to have him back. But during his life he's done a great job of providing for the people he loved the most, his children,' the source added.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail reported that Hatton's house had been sold for £1.5m this year after £350,000 was knocked off the original asking price.

The house, where Hatton was found in September last year, was put up for sale shortly before his death for £1.85million but was later taken off the market following his tragic death.

The mansion then went back on offer for £1.75million, then £1.65million before it was sold for £1.5million.

It was described by the estate agent as being a 'landmark modern residence offering luxury, space and unrivalled lifestyle features'.

It said that the five-bedroom six-bathroom property, which was built in 2010, had been 'impeccably designed'.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail reported that Hatton's house had been sold for £1.5m this year after £350,000 was knocked off the original asking price

One source said Hatton was 'determined to ensure that he had a financial legacy from his incredible career'

Hatton put his own stamp on the property, decorating it with personal touches including a traditional telephone box in the garden and an array of Manchester City memorabilia. Among its more unusual features are seats salvaged from the club's former Maine Road stadium.

It has extensive landscaped grounds with greenbelt views, plus a leisure suite with a heated indoor pool and jacuzzi.

A private gym and cinema room complement a games room and bar area, which is separated from the pool by a striking glass wall.

The principal bedroom suite features a walk-in dressing room, a luxurious en suite bathroom, a crushed-velvet chaise longue and dark patterned wallpaper.

Elsewhere, the property offers multiple reception rooms and expansive open-plan living areas centred around a high-specification, dark-panelled kitchen.

Situated in the sought-after area of Gee Cross in Greater Manchester, the estate is equipped with advanced security features, including CCTV.

The estate agents said: 'This is a rare opportunity to acquire a truly outstanding home in one of the North West's most prestigious and sought-after residential locations.'

For confidential support, call Samaritans on 116 123, visit samaritans.org or visit thecalmzone.net/get-support.
