Sports.title: Anthony Joshua reveals that Tyson Fury's estranged uncle has joined his camp ahead of £150m mega-fight as Gypsy King claims: 'I've not spoken to him for years'
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua reveals that Tyson Fury's estranged uncle has joined his camp ahead of £150m mega-fight as Gypsy King claims: 'I've not spoken to him for years'

Anthony Joshua made the startling revelation that he has joined forces with Tyson Fury's uncle, Peter, ahead of their eagerly-anticipated super-fight in Cardiff in December.

Never has the calling of a sporting press conference agitated as much, if not more, attention than the event itself.

Without putting Fury and Joshua into the same room in London on Wednesday evening there would have been no chance of them sharing a ring in Cardiff two months from now.

Never has a promo prompted so many startling revelations, either. We might never have known that Fury’s estranged uncle is advising AJ on how to prevent Tyson beating him. Traveller families are usually bonded by such fierce loyalties that we can only wonder about the tensions around the camp fire.

‘Not to worry,’ said the Gypsy King about the defection. ‘I haven’t spoken to him for years.’

Nor might we have learned that Joshua took a mind-blowing pay cut in order to haul the Battle of Britain back home from the clutches of New York.

Even though the ritual stare down was lengthy the chatter was amicable and ended in smiles

When they took to the stage there were very few of the histrionics which are the trademark of most of Tyson Fury’s ticket-selling appearances

How much of a purse deduction? ‘Twelve figures’ declared his promoter Eddie Hearn. That’s £10million at least.

AJ shrugged and cited another fringe benefit picked up during the maelstrom of doubt as to whether this fight between a pair of British world heavyweight champions would ever take place. He also added Fury’s former trainer Ben Davison to his team.

Joshua said: ‘Ben’s pinpointing details which will make the difference on the night.’

Fury replied: ‘Ben can’t put muscles on that suspect chin.’

He could not resist reminding everyone that Davison has just returned from Las Vegas where he presided over Conor Benn’s two-round devastation by America’s great Latin hope, Ryan Garcia.

When they took to the stage there were very few of the histrionics which are the trademark of most of Fury’s ticket-selling appearances.

Instead he advertised ‘probably the greatest fight boxing’s ever seen if you factor in the commercial aspect'.

Which includes the US$150million split equally between the two of them as they put an end to 12 years of public waiting for this fight.

Joshua said: ‘Both of us want to do British boxing proud.’

Even though the ritual stare down was lengthy the chatter was amicable and ended in smiles with Fury inviting Joshua to ‘a pint of Guinness as soon as the fight over, win lose or draw'.

Well, they are ten weeks away from them putting on their fight faces.

Sports.title: Inside Alonso's decision to contest the 2027 Dakar Rally with Aston Martin
Sports.content:
Great speculation has accompanied Fernando Alonso in recent months as he held back on confirming his future in Formula 1. Now it appears that not only has he been able to agree favourable terms with Aston Martin to stay on in F1 for 2027, but also persuaded the car manufacturer to back him in another assault on the Dakar Rally, Autosport understands.

The deal was agreed as far back as August but has only just been leaked via the Spanish media. During the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend, Alonso made some cryptic remarks about "surprises" that could emerge "in the next few weeks". This was assumed by many to mean some kind of GT racing entry with Max Verstappen, but in fact it is a return to a challenging event he has contested before with Toyota - finishing 13th in 2020.

During his second stint at McLaren in the mid-2010s, Alonso became so disenchanted with the Honda-powered team’s competitiveness that he negotiated permission to contest the Indianapolis 500. He then took a sabbatical from F1 between 2018 and 2021, competing in the Indy 500 again as well as winning the Le Mans 24 Hours outright with Toyota in 2018 and 2019.

"Yes, exactly, I had to stop. I had to switch off from Formula 1," said Alonso of those experiences.

"I had to experience different formulas and different series, and learn from the specialists in those series and become a more complete driver. That was very important for me and I still find those challenges appealing. I don't know when I will do it, but I will repeat those experiences.

"I love challenges. My way of understanding motorsport and my way of living is around racing cars. It has been all my life and I think my strength has been to adapt to different cars, different rules: V10, V8, V6, Bridgestone, Michelin, Pirelli, KERS, hybrid, ground-effect cars, all these different things. Plus different series: prototypes, Indy, Dakar.

Alonso has already contested the Dakar, with Toyota in 2020 Photo by: Getty Images

"I try to use that strength and maybe do things that were possible in the 1960s, '80s or '90s and now probably no one will try. Max is the only one trying to do some GT racing. But apart from that, I like that challenge.

"I tried these things in the past and I will continue doing that. So maybe, yeah, you have more surprises in the next few weeks. There are things that people probably think that are impossible, but I want to find the limits of what is possible."

The Dakar Rally is an infamously challenging annual fixture which began life as the Paris-Dakar Rally, but was forced to shift location owing to instability in North Africa. After several years in South America it is now hosted by Saudi Arabia.

Alonso will drive an Aston-Martin branded car prepared by Prodrive, and based on the Dacia Sandrider which won the most recent running of the event in the hands of Nasser Al-Attiyah and co-driver Fabian Lurquin. Shortly after that, Dacia announced it would end its programme in the World Rally-Raid Championship (W2RC) a year earlier than originally planned, at the end of 2026 rather than the end of 2027.

The Sandrider itself was a development of a project which started life as the Prodrive Hunter, but was re-engined and rebodied to resemble the Dacia Manifesto concept car. The base vehicle lends itself to relatively straightforward re-engineering of body and powertrain.

Autosport understands that one of the plans on the table is to badge the new car as the Dreadnought, based on the virtual Aston Martin concept vehicle from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and style the body along the same lines.

Prodrive has a long history with Aston Martin. Founder David Richards served as chairman of the British marque from 2007 to 2013, and Prodrive ran Aston Martin’s successful GT and prototype sportscar racing programme.

The first tests with the Dacia Sandrider that will form the basis of the Dakar Aston Martin are reportedly due to take place within the next few weeks. Marc Coma, who partnered Alonso in 2020, is expected to return as his co-driver. The fellow Spaniard is a Dakar legend in his own right, having won the motorcycle category five times with KTM between 2006 and 2015.

The Dakar is unfinished business for Alonso, who finished 13th in 2020 Photo by: Getty Images

Prodrive is apparently planning to field a full Dakar team based around the Sandrider project rather than just a single car for Alonso and Coma. According to the Spanish reports, Al-Attiyah and Sebastien Loeb are also being considered as drivers. There has, however, been no official confirmation of the programme so far.

There is also uncertainty over where the 2027 Dakar Rally will actually take place. Until 2007, during its classic era, the event ran for decades from Europe into West Africa, usually finishing in Dakar. The 2008 edition had to be cancelled because of security concerns in Mauritania. From 2009 to 2019, the event retained the Dakar name but was held in South America, before moving to Saudi Arabia in 2020.

Officially, the 2027 Dakar is still scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia from 1-15 January. Organiser ASO has already published a detailed route comprising 13 stages and a total of 5,320 kilometres of competitive running. The FIA also continues to list Saudi Arabia as the official host country.

However, there is currently considerable uncertainty because of the geopolitical security situation in the Middle East. According to recent reports, ASO is therefore working on a contingency plan in which would Morocco step in as an alternative host.

A significantly more compact event of around eight stages is reportedly under consideration, although no final decision to move the rally to Morocco has been made.

Sports.title: Mercedes confirms Russell's Singapore GP grid penalty following Sepang retirement
Sports.content:
Mercedes has now confirmed that George Russell will take a grid penalty at this weekend’s Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix following his retirement in Malaysia.

The Mercedes driver was running third under the safety car, but then suddenly pulled over at Turn 1 with five laps remaining due to a power unit failure at Sepang last weekend.

It was subsequently presumed that his Silver Arrow would need a new engine for Singapore and if so, a grid penalty would be the consequence as Russell has already used the permitted four in a season.

So as published by Autosport on Tuesday and now confirmed by the Silver Arrows, Russell will start towards the back at Marina Bay this Sunday - a track he won at last year.

Team boss Toto Wolff said in Mercedes’ Singapore preview: “George has the added challenge of a power unit penalty, which will mean starting from the back of the grid on Sunday, following the engine failure in Malaysia.

“That is particularly frustrating given the way he drove last weekend and the result he deserved to be fighting for.

“Unfortunately, these things are part of the sport and our focus now is on giving him the best possible car and opportunities to fight back through the field.

“We need to maximise this final sprint weekend of the year, keep learning, and score the strongest result we can with both cars. Singapore will be an important test of our understanding and our resilience as a team.”

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes, race start Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

This is particularly damning for Russell as he tries to claw back an 84-point deficit to his championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli with just seven rounds remaining.

It also means that he is now likely to miss out on the updated Mercedes engine under the Additional Development and Upgrades Opportunities system, which the team was planning to give him later in the season.

So Mercedes hopes now lay with Antonelli to get the team back to winning ways, after Red Bull’s Max Verstappen dominated from pole at Sepang with the Italian in second.

“Malaysia was obviously a very difficult weekend for us,” added Wolff. “We have spent the days since then working hard to understand why our performance was not where it should have been.

“We have identified several areas we need to investigate further, but F1 doesn’t offer simple answers and we need more evidence before drawing firm conclusions.

“Singapore gives us an immediate opportunity to continue that work. The characteristics of the circuit are very different and that will help us build a clearer picture of where we are.

“That is why we will evaluate both the latest update package and our previous specification across the weekend to ensure we fully understand the direction we need to take.”

Sports.title: Russell to take grid penalty in Singapore due to Sepang retirement
Sports.content:
George Russell is set to receive a grid penalty for this weekend’s Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix as a consequence of his retirement in Sepang last weekend.

The Mercedes driver was running third under the safety car with five laps remaining until he stopped at the Turn 1 entry due to a sudden failure in his power unit.

It means he needs a new engine for Marina Bay and, because he’s already churned through four power units in the 2026 season, any additional changes will incur a 10-place grid penalty.

That is what will happen this weekend, The Athletic has reported, and with the Singapore street circuit being notoriously difficult to overtake on, starting towards the back will make it incredibly difficult for Russell.

That does not do his title hopes any good because he heads into the weekend 84 points behind his championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who in September had a similar penalty at Monza.

But the 20-year-old sensation overcame that in the most impressive ways, by winning his home Italian Grand Prix from 19th on the grid - overtaking Russell on his way to victory.

It shows that churning through power units has been an issue for Mercedes amid an otherwise dominant year, with the Silver Arrows suffering unreliability on several occasions.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

Antonelli, for example, suffered an engine failure late in the Barcelona race, while a power unit problem forced Russell to retire from the lead in Montreal - similarly to Sepang.

So this forthcoming grid drop of his was long expected, but it is understood that Mercedes was hoping to do it later in the year - most likely Austin, the race after Singapore.

That’s because it has been granted one upgrade token under the new-for-2026 Additional Upgrades and Opportunities System (ADUO), which it is soon expected to fit.

Russell and Mercedes were therefore hoping to take the penalty on the weekend the ADUO engine gets fitted, but because that is no longer on the cards, he may miss out altogether.

This is something deputy team principal Bradley Lord confirmed could be the case following the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

“He came on the radio behind the safety car and said 'PU's starting to sound funny',” said Lord.

“We saw sensors then misbehaving and it was clear we had to pull the car over and we'd had a failure of some sort.

“Still need to understand what it means for his pool because he's not rich in low-mileage power units either. So that may mean we need to alter what had been our previous plan.”

Sports.title: What caused Mercedes' pace deficit at Sepang despite upgraded W17?
Sports.content:
Mercedes' performance at Formula 1's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will require further investigation as the conditions around the Sepang circuit made it difficult for the team to get a read on its latest update package.

The team introduced a revised floor and sidepod package for F1's first visit to Sepang in nine years, but it became apparent that the team was struggling to unlock its usual top-line pace throughout the weekend. Regardless, it was set to pick up a double podium finish before George Russell retired with a powertrain issue late on.

Through the weekend, the team declared itself happy with the performance of the update in higher-speed corners, but the W17 overall did not gel with the circuit - particularly around the slower corners.

In the team's usual post-race debrief circulated on its social media channels, deputy team principal Bradley Lord explained that the drivers were having to resort to slightly unusual inputs in those slower corners to get the car to bite.

"The combination potentially of update, track temperature and track surface caused an interaction and a set of behaviours that meant the car was not in its usual happy state, that the drivers were having to turn the car on the throttle in the slow corners," said Lord.

"That was further exacerbating the challenges with tyre temperature. So that's not an easy thing to unpick.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

"It's a bit of a 3D problem that we need to work through and then figure out exactly what steps we take going forward to make sure we've got the base understanding that we need to understand that the update is working well and that we're heading in the right direction in our development, not just for this year's car but for next year as well.

"So that's work that's going on at the moment back in the factory and also over in Singapore in order to establish exactly what the plan is for the coming days and the race weekend in Singapore."

Why Sepang's surface was a problem for more than just tyres

There are two particular threads that link the track surface to the car, the most obvious being the interaction between the road and the tyres. The roughness of the circuit was a key factor in excess tyre heat, as the contact between the tyre and the surface produced greater levels of strain on the tyre.

When the tyre makes contact with the road, it deforms elastically - meaning that the tyre would return to its natural state if the load was removed. This is exacerbated by the track surface; if, like Sepang, there are lots of gaps in the surface, the tyre will partly fill some of those gaps.

Although this produces grip through the mechanical movement of the tyre, the loading and unloading (known as hysteresis) of the contact patch will produce more heat as waste energy. Since the tyre deforms more to fill those pockets in the road surface, the heat generation on the tyre surface increases.

The second mechanism at play, which is of an aerodynamic nature, was one hinted at by McLaren team principal Andrea Stella. F1 cars not only use aero parts to generate load, but also to create certain flow patterns and even accelerate airflow to ensure the rest of the car works efficiently.

On a race track, the roughness of the track surface needs to be considered, as the airflow underneath the car can be affected by this. No circuit is completely smooth, and teams will likely have some idea of roughness to apply to their simulations.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

In a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation, the "domain" walls at the bottom will have a frictional coefficient applied to ensure the flow field is accurate. Wind tunnels may also use textured belts to produce a similar effect.

When you have such a unique track surface, however, it will cause a different interaction with the airflow under the car. If you imagine that this airflow under the car is being accelerated to help produce downforce, one can also assume that the surface texture will manipulate how this flow operates. The boundary layer – the theoretical immediate layer of a fluid around a surface – will change and may lead to effects like turbulence through separation.

Teams have much more data on Singapore, and thus the car's relative performance – from both a tyre and aerodynamic standpoint – should be much more easy to read. Lord also touched on Russell's power unit failure in Malaysia, noting that the Mercedes powerplant had suffered a mechanical failure but still required an investigation to determine the cause.

"Our investigation so far, we've got the car back, we've been able to do a first inspection. It's clearly a mechanical failure on the PU side," he said.

"Exactly what the root cause is, we still need to determine, but the consequence was clear for all to see. A devastating blow for the team and 15 points lost, but most especially, of course, for George, who was on for a very, very solid podium finish."

Sports.title: The dire consequence of Russell's Bahrain GP in Malaysia retirement
Sports.content:
George Russell’s retirement from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will have huge consequences on the rest of his 2026 Formula 1 campaign - especially in regards to ADUO.

The Mercedes driver was running third under the safety car with five laps remaining at Sepang on Sunday, until he pulled over at the Turn 1 entry with a power unit failure.

Minds immediately went to what impact it would have on the title race, as second for team-mate Kimi Antonelli stretched his championship lead to 84 points with seven rounds left.

But Mercedes is also now having to reassess its plan of when to give Russell a new engine, considering it will incur a grid penalty as he’s already used the allotted four in a season.

“He came on the radio behind the safety car and said PU's starting to sound funny,” said Mercedes’ deputy team principal Bradley Lord.

“We saw sensors then misbehaving and it was clear we had to pull the car over and we'd had a failure of some sort.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

“Still need to understand what it means for his pool because he's not rich in low mileage power units either. So that may mean we need to alter what had been our previous plan.”

The plan was for Russell’s next power unit to be the updated version under the Additional Development and Upgrades Opportunities system, which grants Mercedes one token.

It’s believed that the 28-year-old was set to take his penalty in Austin, but Sepang means he might need to do it beforehand - Singapore this weekend - and consequently miss out on the upgrade.

When asked if that’s the case, Lord confirmed: “Potentially so, yeah. That's what we need to understand. But yes, there may be a double whammy effect there, which for him after such a gut-wrenching blow today... it was devastating to see him have to pull off as he did.

"Yeah, there may be a sort of double whammy effect there that is just a really unfortunate consequence of that issue.”

Sepang continued what’s been a series of bad luck for the pre-season title favourite, who retired from the lead in Montreal with a power unit failure, as well as other misfortunes in 2026.

Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

But there’s also been issues on Antonelli’s side, such as his power unit failure late on at Barcelona, so unreliability is the one concern amid an otherwise dominant year for Mercedes.

“I’m so massively annoyed, I’m not in a happy place,” team boss Toto Wolff told Sky Sports after the Malaysian race.

“First of all, we didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will.

“Then the race literally went, if you consider the fight with Lewis [Hamilton] behind, went against us.

“We had such an advantage, one VSC, two safety cars, you couldn't be more unlucky. And to make things worse, PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

“So, as much as I love to be here when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences, to be honest.”

Mercedes is still on course for its first constructors’ title since 2021 as it leads second-placed Ferrari by 151 points, a gap that stood at 160 heading into Malaysia.

“This overarching topic, the DNFs, that could cost us dearly also for the remaining seven races,” added Wolff. “A championship is quickly turned around against you or for you if you have a DNF, and that's why that can't continue.”

Sports.title: Honda HRC to get new boss with Watanabe set to retire
Sports.content:
Koji Watanabe, the long-time boss of Honda's racing activities under HRC, will retire on 1 January 2027, with Keiichi Yasuda appointed as his successor.

A long-time Honda employee after first joining the Japanese marque in 1987, Watanabe became the head of Honda's racing division in 2022. In that time Watanabe oversaw the company's merger of its four-wheel and two-wheel divisions as well as its U-turn on the decision to leave F1, returning as a works partner of Aston Martin for the 2026 regulations.

But Honda has now announced Watanabe will retire on 1 January, with Keiichi Yasuda his successor as HRC CEO. Yasuda is the current Executive Vice President and Representative Director, and was previously head of HR at Honda's racing division.

"This executive change is part of a planned periodic personnel rotation designed to strengthen the management structure in response to global transformation and to accelerate business expansion for the next generation," Honda stated.

"It is my honour serving as a president of HRC with the wonderful colleagues,” Watanabe said.

“In 2022, I assumed the post of President of the new HRC, unifying both motorcycle and automobile motorsport activities. Since then, we decided on our return to F1, expanded our global motorsport structure by reorganising HPD in the U.S. into HRC US and establishing HRC UK, and worked on building HRC's global brand.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

"For the remaining three months of my presidency, I will continue to do my utmost, aiming for victory until the very end."

Speaking on his new role, Yasuda said: "I consider it my mission to firmly inherit the solid foundation built by Watanabe.

"Evolve it further, unite everyone's vector toward the single goal of winning in races, and make HRC even stronger.

"Leveraging my management experience as president of overseas local entities and my background in HR, I will focus on investing in people and strengthening our organisation toward victory."

Sports.title: How FIA software bug caused chaos in Bahrain GP in Malaysia – and the emergency fix that saved the race
Sports.content:
The start of the first wet-weather race of the 2026 Formula 1 season descended into chaos. Leader Max Verstappen was the first to suffer from a lack of power while driving slowly during the formation laps behind the safety car, after which Lewis Hamilton came to a standstill and several other cars followed.

Race control was forced to stop the formation lap with a red flag, after which there was a 40-minute delay before fans actually got to see some F1 action.

Read Also: Formula 1 FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay

FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis confirmed to media including Autosport that a bug in the software supplied by the FIA and developed together with the teams over the course of multiple years was responsible for the chaos.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked because there's been very little wet running this year. There was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said during an impromptu media session post-race.

“Basically, on the formation lap, some cars went very slowly and almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars and some cars almost stopped completely. That bug prevented then the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again.”

This is closely related to the reduction in electrical power to 250kW in wet conditions.

Although the software required for this was tested by several teams, including Red Bull and Racing Bulls, it was not tested in the conditions behind the safety car – and therefore not at these extremely low speeds.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

At the Sepang International Circuit, those low speeds were reached in certain minisectors, with all the consequences that followed.

“It was mainly in some sectors where the full power was reduced. I don't know exactly what speed that was, but some cars reaching this very low speed somehow entered into a loop, which meant they couldn't re-accelerate and then it looked as if they came to a stop.”

In practice, this left drivers feeling as though the throttle pedal was no longer responding, something Oliver Bearman told the media with some surprise.

“I've never seen or felt anything like that. I was shocked that… I didn't even know that the FIA could control our throttle pedal. That was quite scary, actually,” the Haas driver said.

“My throttle pedal just stopped working. It was like it was not connected and the engine was just idling. It was so weird, I mean, shocking.”

One of the questions is why the internal combustion engine was also affected, when that should not be the case at extremely low speeds. The FIA does not yet have a formal answer to that question, but the initial suggestion is that the bug caused all throttle input to go towards recharging the MGU-K, which explains why drivers felt there was no response from the throttle pedal at all.

At first glance, it appeared as though the Mercedes-powered cars were less affected by the issue than other manufacturers, but Tombazis explained that there is no technical reason for that. It was simply related to the speeds reached in certain minisectors.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Not all cars reached the same low speeds on the formation lap. There was a bit of a concertina effect. I think Max slowed down quite a lot, being at the front, and then some cars braked harder as they were surprised and so on. That caused some cars to experience the problem and some others to not experience it.”

How the FIA provided F1 teams with an emergency fix

The FIA then had to react quickly to get the race near Kuala Lumpur under way after all, as Tombazis explained when asked by Autosport.

“Fortunately, our guys understood the issue very, very quickly. I think the update was done very competently. It was obviously a rush job. The priority was to get running as quickly as possible again, so I think the reaction time was quite fast,” he said.

“It wasn't a perfect job and, clearly, we didn't test the updates, but I think it was the way to handle such a case.”

In practice, the update meant that the FIA lifted the energy limit constraint – the restrictions associated with the 250kW limit – for the minisectors in which the low speeds had triggered the bug. Logically, this is not a watertight solution going forward, but it was an emergency measure to ensure the race could go ahead.

“In some of the sectors, some of these reductions of power were overridden,” Tombazis confirmed. “Clearly, we didn't have five days to do the updates. We only had a few minutes, but fortunately, I think we managed to do it without compromising any safety, any racing or fairness.”

How could this happen in the first place?

After the FIA update, all the teams still had to install the modified software, which explains the delay before the restart. The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was saved as a result, but that still does not explain how the FIA could have missed this issue throughout all its preparations and why it only surfaced in round 16 of the championship.

“The software was tested. It just wasn't tested in those specific conditions,” Tombazis replied. “What caught us out was the fact that cars went in that very, very low speed, which was not normally contemplated.”

FIA Safety Car Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

During the tyre tests in which the software was tested, the extremely low speeds were understandably not reached. Nevertheless, there is a crucial counterargument to that: in the rain, the likelihood of a safety car – and therefore low speeds – is very high. Should the FIA not have anticipated that, and was that the governing body’s biggest mistake?

Asked that question by Autosport, Tombazis responded: “Well, any bug is a product of a mistake. I don't know of any software that doesn't have bugs and updates. Your computer probably gets updated every three days and those are all bugs.

“Of course, anticipating these things is what one hopes to do, but sometimes some very combination of events isn't properly anticipated and causes the problem. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Although the cause of this problem is now known and a temporary fix has been introduced, the FIA still has many questions to answer internally – also to ensure that it does not happen again.

“We would all like it to be simpler, but the fact is when you have as much electrical energy, it does make it more complicated. I think you appreciate that the race has now finished about one hour ago and we haven't done a full debrief of the situation to see how we can avoid such an issue.

“Every race, we have a long debrief afterwards where we identify criticalities. Obviously, that was a major criticality and we need to make sure we avoid it.

“But can I guarantee it will never happen again? This specific problem, yes. A problem, no. But we will do our best to avoid it, of course.”

Sports.title: The slick tyre gamble that hurt McLaren and Ferrari's chances in Bahrain GP in Malaysia
Sports.content:
When the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia eventually got going after an hour and 33 minutes of delays, it became apparent that the intermediate was the tyre to be on among the opening laps - even if the Sepang circuit had looked like it was drying out.

At the front of the field, Ferrari and McLaren chose to go all-in on the dry tyres for the restart; Ferrari opted for the soft compound, while McLaren went for the mediums. When the race got underway behind the safety car, both teams were left to rue their choices as the circuit was still too slippery.

McLaren bailed on the plan early, stopping before the standing start to ensure Oscar Piastri could get a set of intermediates back onto the car, but Lando Norris and the Ferraris stuck with their choices. Charles Leclerc duly fed into the pitlane at the end of the lap, as the slick-tyre runners were swamped and then left behind by those who'd stuck with the intermediate for the start.

Lewis Hamilton and Norris surmised that, since they'd made their beds, they'd lie in them. Hamilton was asked if he wanted to stop again, but the seven-time champion reasoned that Ferrari might as well stick with the gamble given that the team was well behind - and pitting would only cost more time.

By the end of the eighth lap, the slick times were now equal with the intermediate runners; Valtteri Bottas' subsequent off then presented the inter-shod drivers with the chance to switch to slicks.

Speaking about the decision, Norris stated that the idea of starting on the slick was "quite convincing" and that he was unsure of the performance of the inter; on his recon lap to the grid, the Briton reported that the green-walled tyre was already feeling the pain on Sepang's rough surface.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

"It felt maybe a little bit of a risk, because a slick on a wet track is always a bit of a risk," Norris said. "There was enough people on it that it was quite convincing at the time that it was possibly going to be the right decision.

"The laps to the grid on the inter when it was a similar kind of condition, they had so much grip and my Inter was completely shredded after one lap.

"I was convinced a slick tyre would work, but I think it was just the fact I've never really been on the inter before. Things just felt a lot better than they should have done in a way.

"If we would have had a read on an inter from a previous weekend, maybe I would have been able to understand it more. But that convinced us and it clearly convinced a lot of people.

"Oscar probably made the right decision in boxing and we got it wrong today, that's all."

Leclerc theorised that the roughness of the tarmac made it more difficult to read the track surface, as water pooled up in the gaps - and the drop in temperature that accompanied the rain ensured that the circuit took much longer to dry out than expected. Given the length of the downpour, any residual circuit temperature was swiftly extinguished.

Even though the Monegasque switched tyres, the time loss involved in pitting after the start kept him behind Hamilton, who ran longer on his set of soft tyres and quickly began to make up positions.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

Hamilton joked that he wasn't going to "go to the casino with the guys" after the team's gambles didn't pay off, although praised his team's strategy in keeping him out on the road. The Briton was ultimately less enamoured with the medium after making a stop on lap 31, but the late-race VSC (later a full safety car) presented a chance to return to the soft - which he put to use with a pass on Isack Hadjar for third.

"As we pulled out [of the pits], all the spray came out the back of Max’s car and I was like, 'okay, I’m done. My race is really in trouble,'" Hamilton recounted.

"We just had to stick with it. As everyone’s overtaken me, they [the engineers] were like, 'we stop.' I know we’ve already made another 26 seconds. What’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I was just, 'Let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.'

"And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great then after that. Really good pitstops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy. But for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. Of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.

"We’ll definitely have an open dialogue, and I’m really so proud of my team. The mechanics every weekend, just the work they’re putting in, the engineers that accompany here every weekend, the catering, everyone really, really comes and gives it their best.

"Their heart’s all in the right spot. We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that. So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting."

Sports.title: Monaco rules out making changes to its Formula 1 track layout | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The president of the Automobile Club de Monaco says it will not make changes to the layout of the famous circuit.

The 3.3 kilometre circuit is the shortest and narrowest on the calendar. It has frequently been criticised for producing processional races because Formula 1 cars find it so difficult to overtake.

Although the track’s configuration has been revised many times since its first grand prix in 1929, the limited space available in the Principality makes significant alterations and widening impossible. Monaco has reclaimed land from the sea for construction purposes, such as when the ‘Nouvelle’ chicane was built 40 years ago, but ACM president Michel Boeri denied they plan to do so in future.

“Very importantly, the circuit will not be changed, contrary to what I’ve heard many people suggest,” he told Nice-Matin. “Demolishing this or moving that would automatically trigger a fresh review of the circuit and require new FIA homologation.”

Formula 1 has extended its contract to race in Monaco twice in the last two years. Its current deal will keep it on the calendar until at least 2035.

Boeri said F1 promoters Liberty Media saw the value of keeping one of the most historic venues on the calendar.

“They’re not here out of charity,” he said. “They’re here to make money. And we’re here to give them as little as possible and make as much as possible ourselves. It’s a straightforward, fair contest in an open market.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Our American friends realised how responsive we could be. Unlike those who still call Monaco ‘the merry-go-round’ and would do well to update their thinking, we reached an understanding in principle that the grand prix is a major draw for Formula 1. We weren’t going to be constantly hassled over whether a kerb had two or three too many corners.”

However Boeri indicated Monaco may find a way to increase the space available in the pit lane. “The grand prix’s future is secured until 2035, but with this platform and the building that will be constructed on it, we might be able to rethink the grid area and perhaps even extend the contract further,” he said, “All of that remains to be defined.

“It’s no secret, for example, that the pit lane will be difficult to sustain much longer. Space is limited, and the garages aren’t wide enough. And when you don’t have width on the ground, you build upward.

“I can already hear all the non possumus [‘not possible’] objections that will come from this area, but eventually people will see reason. I’m no gardener, but there’s more than one kind of tree, for example.”

The difficulty of overtaking in Monaco led F1 to introduce a rules change last year forcing drivers to make two tyre changes. The result was an even more processional race in which several cars deliberately lapped very slowly, prompting criticism from drivers which led to the rule being dropped.

Monaco will hold a sprint race for the first time next year, a decision which surprised many due to the difficulty of overtaking at the track.

Sports.title: Russell’s penalty, Mercedes’ leap backwards and more Singapore GP talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell will take another power unit penalty this weekend. Here are eight talking points for the Singapore Grand Prix.

Russell’s penalty blow

Azerbaijan gave George Russell a glimmer of hope that he might get back into the championship fight. He took pole and withstood everything Max Verstappen could throw at him, taking a 15-point bite out of his team mate’s championship lead.

With a few more weekends like that he could seriously think about getting back into contention. But that hope died in Malaysia (or, if you’re a Sky commentator, ‘Bahrain’). Russell was already running behind Andrea Kimi Antonelli when his power unit died.

F1’s rules mean Russell takes a double blow from the retirement as he will need to fit a new power unit this weekend, as Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff confirmed. “George has the added challenge of a power unit penalty, which will mean starting from the back of the grid on Sunday, following the engine failure in Malaysia,” he said. “That is particularly frustrating given the way he drove last weekend and the result he deserved to be fighting for.”

Mercedes’ leap backwards?

Both Mercedes drivers had to contend with another problem last weekend: the team’s much-vaunted upgrade for its W17 did not produce the desired step forwards. Indeed, as Antonelli observed, it might have made them slower.

And getting to the bottom of their problems this weekend will be especially challenging as teams only have a single practice session.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Last sprint race

There were groans of disappointment when F1 increased the number of sprint races per season from three to six. Now get ready to long for the days of only six sprint races, as F1 will hold 10 in 2027.

Singapore will hold the last sprint race of the season this weekend. It’s a curious choice of venue given that F1 previously said it intended to hold sprint events at tracks where overtaking is less difficult. Few would argue that description applies to the Marina Bay circuit.

But as the grimly processional last sprint race in Zandvoort showed, whether the ‘racing’ is actually good is not a consideration: F1 has decided there will be more of them.

Verstappen’s overdue win

Briefly, Marina Bay in Singapore was the only venue on the Formula 1 calendar which Verstappen had never won at. That is no longer the case, but it remains the track where he has made the most starts without winning.

That could change this weekend thanks to Red Bull’s resurgence in form. Verstappen won in Sepang (not to be confused with BIC) and came close to victory in Baku. After three podiums and second places in the last two editions of this race, his 10th appearance could be his best chance yet to win it.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Red Bull to pass McLaren?

Red Bull’s remarkable progress in recent races has coincided with a slump in form for McLaren, the form team around the summer break. It leaves Red Bull well-placed to jump ahead of McLaren into third place in the standings: the gap between them has shrunk from 83 points to 18 in just three rounds, and as this is a sprint event each team can score up to 58 this weekend.

Are Red Bull now the greatest threat to Mercedes? Or is this merely their turn to play a temporary role as the championship leaders’ token opposition, only to fade later as Ferrari and McLaren did?

Air quality

Not for the first time in Singapore, attendees are being warned about poor air quality in the run-up to the race. As was also the case in 2019, the cause is smoke drifting across from wildfires in nearby Indonesia.

The particularly hot conditions in parts of the world this year due to the increased intensity of the El Nino weather system have contributed. Singapore’s National Environment Agency gave a 24-hour Pollution Standards Index forecast “in the High Moderate to Mid Unhealthy range.” on Tuesday.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Patch Sunday?

Formula 1 faced ridicule over the farcical scenes which preceded Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, when multiple drivers suffered a near-total loss of power due to an FIA systems problem. All the Ferrari-powered cars were affected as were both of the Audis and some of the Red Bull-Ford cars, including that of pole-winner Verstappen.

The FIA confirms the problem was caused by F1 cars encountering wet conditions. The series may have been incredibly fortunate the cars were already running behind the Safety Car, instead of encountering rain during racing conditions, when multiple cars stopping on-tack would have presented an obvious hazard.

Last race on this layout?

This will be the fourth Singapore Grand Prix on the current track layout which bypasses the former turns 16 to 19 – scene of the infamous ‘Crashgate’ episode. This was done due to the construction of the new NS Square facility on the waterfront (below).

That construction was originally supposed to be completed during 2025, but was delayed, and a new target date of 2027 set. F1 drivers may experience a new variant of the Singapore track when they return next year, though whether it changes the venue for the better remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Stats: Verstappen avoids first win-less season since 2015, Red Bull-Ford’s first win and more | 2026 Bahrain GP in Malaysia stats and facts
Sports.content:
Before the unusually-named Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia began, Max Verstappen made it clear he wanted to avoid ending the season without a victory.

He put that right on Sunday, ensuring he claimed a victory for the 11th season in a row. He only failed to win a grand prix in his debut season at Toro Rosso (now Racing Bulls) in 2015.

But Verstappen needs to keep winning every year until 2030 to equal Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton’s joint record of 15 consecutive winning seasons (from 1992 to 2006 and 2007 to 2021 respectively).

Verstappen claimed the first victory for car number three since his former team mate Daniel Ricciardo won the Italian Grand Prix for McLaren five years ago. Two other drivers on the grid today have won with that number: Fernando Alonso twice in 2013 at Ferrari and Hamilton three times for McLaren in 2011, both in seasons before the FIA introduced ‘career numbers’.

This was the 72nd victory of Verstappen’s career. It came in Malaysia’s first grand prix in nine years, which Verstappen also won, taking the second win of his career at that point.

The race carried the title ‘Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia’ as it took the place of April’s cancelled race in the Middle East. It is by no means unique for one country to hold an event named for another: San Marino, Luxembourg and Switzerland all gave their names to races in other nearby countries: Italy, Germany and France respectively.

But there were a few noteworthy differences. Those latter cases were all events held in addition to rounds which took place in those countries, while F1 is not racing in Bahrain at all this year as it was considered too unsafe due to the proximity to the conflict in Iran. Precisely because of that, the distance between the event and the country it was named after was much greater than those earlier cases, being some 6,000 kilometres.

So instead of the Bahrain International Circuit holding its 23rd race, the Sepang International Circuit held its 20th. In theory Bahrain will hold the first round on the 2027 F1 calendar, but watch this space.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Verstappen’s success vindicated Red Bull’s decision to build their own power unit, in conjunction with Ford. The latter last contributed to a grand prix victory in 2003, when Giancarlo Fisichella won the Brazilian Grand Prix for Jordan (now Aston Martin) powered by a Ford-Cosworth RS1.

The same power units ended Mercedes’ monopoly on pole positions this year. After 15 consecutive Mercedes-powered poles, Verstappen claimed the first for a (partly) Ford-badged engine since Rubens Barrichello put his Stewart at the front of the field for the 1999 French Grand Prix at Magny-Cours.

However a substantial amount of credit must also go to Red Bull, who had already committed to building their own power units before teaming up with Ford. Although they previously ran their Honda-designed units successfully, they deserve to be regarded as a new engine constructor in their own right, and those don’t appear very often.

If we accept this was the first victory for a new engine built by a new constructor, when was the last time this happened? Red Bull’s other wins since 2022 have been credited to ‘Red Bull Powertrains’ and Honda RBPT but all involved the same Honda-derived power units.

Other new names which appeared on the winners lists in previous years were often due to branding exercises. Red Bull previously won races with Renault engines badged as TAG Heuer. Engines produced by Honda and Porsche won races labelled as Mugen-Honda and TAG-Porsche respectively.

Using a strict definition, avoiding all rebranded engines and those related to previous designs by constructors who had already won races, Red Bull-Ford’s win is the first for a new F1 engine constructor since BMW in 1982. That win came courtesy of Brabham’s Nelson Piquet in the Canadian Grand Prix. In an extremely unusual result, his team mate Riccardo Patrese finished that race in second place powered by a different engine: his Brabham was powered by Ford.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The others manufactures on the grid today are either yet to win (Audi) or scored their first wins long ago: Ferrari in 1951, Mercedes in 1954 and Honda in 1965.

A week ago, George Russell grabbed the eighth win of his career, in Baku. Verstappen served notice of Red Bull’s potential there, chasing his rival across the line, the pair separated by just 0.196 seconds. This was the closest finish to a grand prix since the rigged conclusion to the 2002 United States Grand Prix, where Schumacher attempted to contrive a ‘dead heat’ with team mate Barrichello, but instead was beaten to the line by 0.011s.

Finally, Fernando Alonso took advantage of the conditions in Sepang to claim Aston Martin’s best finish of the season with eighth place. Those four points leave his team just five shy of Williams.

Over to you

Have you spotted any other interesting stats and facts from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia or Azerbaijan Grand Prix? Share them in the comments.

Sports.title: “That was a big mess”: How all 22 drivers saw F1’s formation lap fiasco in Sepang | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Confusion reigned when Formula 1 drivers headed out to begin yesterday’s grand prix.

A software glitch struck much of the grid, causing some cars to slow to a crawl and others to stop entirely. Some power units sprang back into life while others stubbornly refused to work again.

Eventually race control abandoned the attempt to start the race and summoned the field back into the pits so the FIA could issue a software update. The process took the best part of an hour.

The problem was widespread throughout the field and affected drivers in different ways. Here’s how several of them experienced the fault.

1st: Max Verstappen

Verstappen’s car almost came to a stop at the front of the field. However a switch change on his steering wheel solved the problem for him.

Verstappen Verstappen slows at turn 10

Well, this is fucked. I can’t accelerate. Lambiase OK, stand by. Verstappen Why doesn’t it work? Lambiase Stand by. Verstappen It’s not working, guys. Lambiase Yep stand by Max, we’re looking. Let’s have fail one fail please, Max. Fail one fail.

The car accelerates away Lambiase Looks like maybe Lewis has a similar problem to you. He’s still struggling between turn 11 and turn 12.

Expecting the start to go ahead, Verstappen was unhappy that the side of the grid he was due to start from was wetter than the opposite side.

The fault struck Hamilton’s car at the same time as Verstappen’s. As a result, he appeared not to realise the Red Bull driver was suffering from the same problem as him. Ferrari had more difficulty finding a solution for Hamilton.

Sports.title: Callum Smith Signs Contract for Dmitry Bivol Fight
Sports.content:
Callum Smith has signed the documents for a title fight against Dmitry Bivol, according to RCC Boxing, with December 12 as the planned date in Yekaterinburg, Russia. The promoter’s announcement moves the matchup forward, although the date should still be treated as provisional.

RCC Boxing CEO German Titov told the organization’s press service that negotiations with Smith’s team had concluded, according to RBC Sport.

“Today we completed lengthy negotiations with Callum Smith’s team,” Titov said, translated from Russian.

Titov added that the necessary documents had been signed and RCC would organize the championship bout in Yekaterinburg. His wording on December 12 was “the planned date,” leaving room for further confirmation before fans make travel arrangements.

Smith is Bivol’s WBO mandatory challenger and holds the organization’s interim light heavyweight title. The British fighter’s route gives Bivol another title obligation to handle while a third meeting with Artur Beterbiev remains an attractive option.

The contract announcement is progress, but it comes from the company organizing the event. It supports reporting that RCC says Smith has signed. It does not justify turning a planned December date into an unconditional promise that the fight will happen that night.

For Smith, the opportunity would bring another attempt to win a full world title at light heavyweight after his defeat to Beterbiev. Bivol presents a different challenge: Smith would have to find ways to land his heavier punches against an opponent whose movement and combinations can leave challengers chasing rounds.

Smith cannot afford to spend long stretches following Bivol without throwing. Letting the champion dictate the distance would make it difficult to bring his power into the fight, particularly if Bivol establishes an early lead.

Bivol would also be putting another bout between himself and the Beterbiev trilogy. Smith’s mandatory position explains the matchup, but beating him would still leave the question of when Bivol and Beterbiev meet again.

The next step is firmer confirmation of the event details. RCC has announced signed documents; December 12 remains its stated target.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Uses Dana White to Build American Profile
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn admits his exchanges with Dana White are raising his profile in America. That gives him a reason to keep provoking the UFC boss during the Fury–Joshua promotion, but getting noticed is only the first step. Hearn still needs to give those American viewers a reason to follow his boxing shows.

“Don’t forget, my profile in America is nowhere near where it is in the UK, and that’s starting to change a lot because of the battle with Dana,” Hearn told Ariel Helwani. “Every time he speaks, he’s talking about me. It’s been really good for me and fun. Obviously, even more fun when you’re winning, but it’s a battle, isn’t it? It’s only the first of many in this process.”

Hearn’s admission helps explain the repeated comments about White’s role in Fury–Joshua. An irritated response puts the Matchroom promoter in front of White’s audience again. Hearn can benefit from that exposure regardless of whether the viewers agree with him.

The harder work comes afterward. American fans recognizing Hearn doesn’t necessarily mean they will watch his cards or buy tickets. His UK events being available through DAZN gives them access, but he needs fighters and matchups that make them want to tune in.

Joshua’s popularity in Britain cannot be treated as a guarantee of the same response in America. Fury–Joshua may draw attention as an individual event, but Hearn needs attractions that can support an ongoing U.S. schedule.

A promoter with P.T. Barnum’s instinct for exploiting publicity would move quickly to give that new audience something to buy. Alternating between American and British shows would let Hearn build interest while maintaining his established business at home.

That would require accepting smaller American ticket sales as part of the investment. Expecting British-sized crowds immediately could discourage the very shows needed to develop an audience. Repeat appearances, sensible venues, and more American fighters would give fans a chance to form an attachment.

Signing those fighters is only part of the job. Keeping them long enough to build their following is equally important.

Hearn calls the exchanges with White a win. The attention may be useful, but its commercial value remains unproven. If he doesn’t follow it with U.S. events people want to attend, his increased profile could fade when White stops responding.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Pushes Floyd Mayweather for Professional Fight
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia has set his sights on Floyd Mayweather for a fully sanctioned professional bout, insisting the retired legend reached out to him first. Ryan shut down any talk of an exhibition, making it clear he only wants a clash if Mayweather puts his 50-0 record on the line.

The Ring’s post on X detailing the challenge blew up instantly. Fans are definitely curious, though convincing Mayweather to risk his pristine ledger just before his 50th birthday is a massive hurdle.

“Okay Floyd let’s see how much you love that ‘0,’” Ryan posted on X. “And no I wouldn’t do an exhibition I want his 0 on the fucking line. How much does he actually think he got left. I’m ready Floyd, remember you made this call. I’m just returning the favor. Offer is on the table. Accept or not, if not I move foward as I have been.”

Ryan’s public callout does not mean Floyd agreed to step into a real ring. Nothing is signed, and no date exists.

Mayweather turns 50 this February. He has not fought professionally since beating Conor McGregor in 2017, and his last appearances against elite pugilists were his 2015 victories over Manny Pacquiao and Andre Berto.

Stepping into a real fight against a prime competitor after nearly a decade away is an entirely different reality. Mayweather still possesses unmatched ring IQ, yet reflex speed fades with time. Garcia’s explosive hand speed and blistering left hook could punish sluggish reactions if Floyd struggles to keep his legs under him as the rounds tick by. A decision win for Ryan seems likely, with a late stoppage well within reach if Mayweather cannot dodge incoming combinations.

Recent reports detailing Floyd’s financial headaches suggest a monster check would tempt him. Protecting that flawless record remains his primary concern. An exhibition gives him a lucrative payday with zero official consequences, but Garcia refuses to entertain that route.

Ryan also risks major blowback for targeting a man nearing 50. Floyd’s legendary status guarantees huge box office numbers, yet defeating an aged icon proves very little against the current elite at welterweight. Going after this spectacle suggests Ryan is chasing pure dollar signs, even if it hands him the historic bragging right of tarnishing Mayweather’s undefeated legacy.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Targets Vito Mielnicki Against Xander Zayas
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn wants Vito Mielnicki Jr. to face Xander Zayas in New York next summer, with both fighters taking another bout first under his preferred plan.

Vito beat Ammo Williams in his last fight, while Xander lost to Jaron Ennis. If Zayas decides against taking a fight first, he’ll be coming straight off that defeat to face Mielnicki.

“I want him to fight Xander Zayas. It’s a massive fight for New York,” Hearn said to iFL TV. “We’re promoting Xander Zayas’s next fight in February, it looks like. It won’t be that fight, but I’d like to see him come back and then fight Vito. Vito will have a fight as well around the same time, and then those two fight in the summer.”

Hearn favors that route, yet no deal exists for a bout between Mielnicki and Zayas. His proposal for February grants Xander a chance to get back in the ring before taking on Vito, even if the date and opponent stay unconfirmed.

The choice is more important to Zayas than Mielnicki. Vito comes into his next fight riding the win over Ammo Williams. Xander must prove his response after the loss to Ennis, so an interim contest allows him to test adjustments prior to taking on a rival with momentum.

Stepping directly into the ring with Mielnicki makes the comeback far tougher. Vito has every incentive to pursue the fight while the Williams victory remains fresh, as a win over Zayas hands him another prominent scalp to elevate his standing.

Hearn aiming for New York establishes a sharp promotional focus for the contest. Instead of feeding either fighter back to Ennis immediately, he seeks to pit them against one another so the victor earns a clear path back to the division’s biggest stages.

Locking down their upcoming bouts comes first. Hearn intends to get both fighters into the ring around February, securing ample preparation time for a summer clash rather than letting the plan fade away.

Sports.title: Dana White Spends Hours Working on Shakur Stevenson Fight
Sports.content:
Dana White is actively attempting to lock down Shakur Stevenson’s next bout, confirming on October 6 that he spent several hours that afternoon working on fight logistics. White’s brief update provides concrete evidence of ongoing negotiations behind the scenes, though an opponent, venue, and official date remain unconfirmed.

“Yeah, we’re working on the Shakur fight right now. Literally today, a couple hours of my day today was spent on Shakur,” White said during his post-Contender Series press conference.

Reporters pressed White for details, specifically referencing his prior remarks that Stevenson would return to action before the close of the year. White declined to reaffirm that original timeline, and he chose not to disclose which specific opponent he is targeting for the promotional launch.

That leaves the next announcement particularly important. Time spent discussing a fight is encouraging, but Shakur needs an agreement that gets him back in the ring.

Shakur pointed to money as the primary roadblock stalling bouts with Gary Antuanne Russell and Raymond Muratalla. Stevenson posted publicly on X claiming both fighters demanded three million dollars apiece to step in the ring with him, urging Zuffa Boxing to pay the price.

The figures nevertheless help explain why choosing an opponent and securing one can be very different tasks. Shakur wants meaningful fights, while the other side has its own price for accepting a difficult matchup.

White did not say whether he was working on a fight with Russell, Muratalla, or someone else. He gave no indication that a deal was close or an announcement was coming soon.

Shakur and Devin Haney have been going back and forth on X over weight. Haney has offered to come down to 145 pounds without a rehydration clause. Shakur has repeatedly asked for 144, along with a 10-pound limit on how much Haney can regain after the weigh-in.

Whether 145 is low enough for Shakur remains unclear. He is asking Haney to make two concessions: fight below the welterweight limit and restrict his weight gain afterward by 10 pounds. Haney’s offer brings them closer on the catchweight, but the rehydration clause remains a point of disagreement.

Sports.title: Emanuel Navarrete Targets Three Belts Against O’Shaquie Foster
Sports.content:
Naoya Inoue has what most world champions are still chasing: all four major belts in his division. Emanuel Navarrete can move a step closer to that position on October 24, when he faces O’Shaquie Foster in a three-belt super featherweight unification fight in San Antonio.

That gives boxing’s title picture something more useful than another list of belt holders. The Navarrete–Foster winner will leave with the IBF, WBO and WBC championships, reducing the number of separate champions at 130 pounds and putting an undisputed fight within reach. Top Rank has confirmed those three titles will be at stake.

Inoue, 33-0 with 27 knockouts, holds the WBA, WBC, IBF and WBO titles at super bantamweight. He retained the collection by defeating Junto Nakatani in May. His position gives challengers a clear target: they must beat him to take any of the four major championships at 122 pounds.

Elsewhere, winning a world title can leave a fighter with considerable unfinished business. Holding two belts makes someone a unified champion. Holding all four makes him undisputed. Adding the IBO championship does not replace a missing WBA, WBC, IBF or WBO belt.

Navarrete’s fight with Foster offers a practical example of that difference. Navarrete, 40-2-1 with 33 knockouts, brings the IBF and WBO titles. Foster brings the WBC belt. Even with victory, either man would still need the WBA championship to complete the set.

The benefit for supporters is a stronger answer to who leads the division. Separate champions can build separate careers, each defending a belt without facing the other titleholders. Unification forces at least two of those claims to be tested against each other.

Collecting belts should lead to better fights. Inoue has already completed that process at super bantamweight. Navarrete and Foster are taking another step toward it, and their October 24 meeting gives fans a fight that can settle something beyond another successful title defense.

Sports.title: Conor Wallace Questions Referee After Ben Whittaker Loss
Sports.content:
Conor Wallace believes the referee made it harder for him to finish Ben Whittaker last Saturday, allowing him to hold while hurt and declining to count falls that Wallace felt deserved knockdowns.

The late trouble also gives Eddie Hearn a reason to think carefully about a rematch. Neither Hearn nor Whittaker has committed to facing Wallace again, and the promoter has mentioned other possible opponents.

“I do definitely feel like the referee didn’t do me any favors,” Wallace told talkSPORT’s White and Jordan show on Tuesday morning. “I definitely feel like one or possibly two of them should have been knockdowns, and he was holding on for dear life. “You need to be given a chance to get going, and I was trying to get the action going. Yes, I did smother myself a little bit. Maybe I was trying too hard to put him away. I should have shortened those shots when I look back at it, but hindsight is a wonderful thing.”

Wallace puts his complaint at one or possibly two knockdowns. There is a case for examining all three falls, along with Whittaker’s repeated holding. Counting those falls and deducting points could have changed the result. Enforcing the rules on holding could also have forced Whittaker to keep fighting when he was struggling to survive.

Wallace accepts that he contributed to the missed opportunity by crowding his punches. Shorter shots and a little more room could make him harder to contain if he gets Whittaker hurt again.

He also wants to start faster, having conceded the early rounds. That requires care against Whittaker’s counter right, but Wallace now has twelve rounds of experience against him and knows he can cause trouble late.

Hearn has talked about Whittaker as a generational talent. Putting him straight back in with someone who came close to stopping him would put that description to a serious test. Wallace may have his number, particularly if he improves his opening rounds and finishes more patiently.

Choosing another opponent would be understandable from Hearn’s side. Whittaker already has his IBF mandatory position, and another Wallace fight brings considerable risk. Wallace’s confidence alone will not get the rematch made; Hearn and Whittaker still have to decide whether they want to take that chance.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Welcomes Christian Mbilli Unification Despite Shared Trainer
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias is willing to fight Christian Mbilli even if Marc Ramsey chooses the other corner, removing a potential obstacle to a super middleweight unification should both champions win their upcoming defenses.

The two fighters share Ramsey, but Iglesias will not allow that arrangement to prevent him from facing the WBC champion.

“Whoever’s in my corner is in my corner, but there are no excuses with me,” Iglesias told The Ring.

Iglesias defends his IBF title against Oliver Zaren this Thursday, October 8, in Quebec City on DAZN. Mbilli is scheduled to defend against Canelo Alvarez on October 31 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Iglesias views that fight as a 50-50 contest.

If both retain their titles, promoter Camille Estephan would have two champions at 168 pounds and an opportunity to arrange a unification. Iglesias has made clear that sharing a trainer would not be his reason for declining it.

The bigger obstacle could be business. If Mbilli beats Canelo, his next fight could attract considerably more attention. Matching him immediately against a dangerous puncher from the same stable would risk that opportunity.

Iglesias would have more to gain in recognition. Beating the man who had just defeated Canelo could transform his career, while Mbilli might have better-paying options. Having both champions under one promoter makes negotiations easier, but it does not guarantee Estephan wants the matchup.

Ramsey would also have a choice to make. If he stayed with Mbilli, his knowledge of Iglesias’s habits could help with preparation, although Iglesias only began working with him less than three months ago.

Inside the ring, Mbilli’s pressure could give Iglesias the exchanges he wants. Coming forward against a powerful southpaw creates opportunities for straight left hands and short counters.

That danger runs both ways. Iglesias would need to land enough to interrupt Mbilli’s attacks. If Mbilli takes his punches and keeps forcing exchanges, Iglesias would have to maintain his effectiveness through a demanding twelve rounds.

Iglesias must beat Zaren first. Beyond Thursday, his willingness puts the question to his promoter: would Eye of the Tiger match its champions if Mbilli returns from Riyadh with a victory over Canelo?

Ghana News.title: Eduwatch calls for urgent resolution of teachers’ strike and reforms
Ghana News.content:
Education policy think tank Africa Education Watch (Eduwatch) has called for an urgent resolution to the nationwide strike by Ghana’s pre-tertiary teacher unions, warning that continued disruption of classes is denying pupils valuable instructional time and could affect learning outcomes.

The strike, which began on September 25, 2026, has entered its 12th day, with teachers demanding action on a number of outstanding issues, including the placement of promoted teachers on their appropriate salary scales, payment of related arrears, the conclusion of negotiations on a new Collective Agreement and the implementation of the Deprived Area Allowance.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, October 7, Eduwatch said the continued industrial action was having implications not only for teaching and learning but also for the well-being of vulnerable children who rely on schools for services such as school feeding.

“Every additional day of disruption reduces instructional time and compromises children’s right to education,” the organisation said.

It warned that the effects could be particularly serious for children from low-income households who depend heavily on public schools for both education and social support.

Eduwatch has urged the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC), Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, Ghana Education Service (GES), Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD) and the teacher unions to intensify negotiations and reach a time-bound agreement to end the strike.

The organisation said the interests of learners should remain central to the discussions.

It also called on the CAGD and GES to act immediately to ensure that teachers who have been promoted receive the salaries and other compensation due to them.

Eduwatch said the current dispute also raised questions about how collective bargaining in the education sector was being managed.

According to the organisation, the existing Collective Agreement was due to expire in June 2026, while the teacher unions had indicated that proposals for its review were submitted several months before the expiry date.

“This raises legitimate concerns regarding why meaningful negotiations were not concluded ahead of expiry, with industrial action becoming the trigger for greater urgency at the negotiating table,” Eduwatch said.

It argued that negotiations on collective agreements should begin well before existing agreements expire, with clear timelines and milestones for reaching a settlement.

“Collective bargaining should be managed proactively, with negotiations commencing sufficiently ahead of the expiry of existing agreements, guided by clear milestones for conclusion,” the organisation said.

Eduwatch said delays that eventually result in industrial action ultimately impose the greatest cost on learners through lost classroom time.

“Stronger institutional accountability is therefore required to ensure that avoidable administrative and negotiation delays do not repeatedly translate into disruption of teaching and learning,” it added.

Beyond the immediate dispute, Eduwatch said the recurring problems surrounding teacher promotions, payroll placement, payment of arrears and incentives pointed to wider weaknesses in the management of the teaching workforce.

It therefore proposed a series of reforms aimed at making the system more efficient, predictable and transparent.

One of its key recommendations is the digitisation of processes between the GES and CAGD.

Eduwatch is also calling for greater decentralisation of the teacher promotion process.

It said the highly centralised system creates bottlenecks, particularly when large numbers of teachers have to be processed through the same administrative channels.

The organisation proposed that Regional Education Directorates should take greater responsibility for the assessment, verification and routine processing of promotions, while the GES Council maintains national oversight and approves recommendations.

Eduwatch said resolving the current strike should go beyond reaching an agreement that brings teachers back to the classroom.

It called for the immediate payment of outstanding promotion allowances, the conclusion of negotiations on the new Collective Agreement and measures to restore lost instructional time.

It also urged the government and education sector institutions to implement reforms that would prevent similar disputes from recurring.

“Protecting instructional time and the right to education requires not only resolving the present strike, but also building efficient, predictable, transparent and accountable systems for managing Ghana’s teaching workforce,” Eduwatch said.

Ghana News.title: Media worker, journalist remanded over alleged GH¢800k fraud
Ghana News.content:
An Accra Circuit Court has remanded two men into police custody over an alleged GH¢800,000 fraud involving a Ghanaian resident in the United States.

Bilyaminu Ibrahim, a media worker, is alleged to have collected the money from the complainant under the pretext of helping to avert spiritual attacks.

Ibrahim and Mohammed Musah, a journalist, have been charged with conspiracy to commit crime, namely defrauding by false pretence, defrauding by false pretence and harbouring a criminal, respectively.

Chief Inspector Ramata Asumah, prosecuting, told the court that Fawuziya Issaka was the complainant and younger sister of the alleged victim, Tourwana Katakarauo, who resides in the United States.

The court heard that in 2021, Katakaraou Jabiru, Ibrahim’s alleged accomplice, learnt that Tourwana was facing challenges in the United States and allegedly planned with Ibrahim to obtain money from her under false pretences.

The prosecution said Jabiru told Fawuziya that he knew a spiritualist who could help resolve the challenges, after which Ibrahim allegedly posed as the spiritualist.

The two allegedly collected GH¢800,000 from Tourwana in instalments, claiming they needed the money for sacrifices and other spiritual activities to avert attacks against her and her mother.

The prosecution said they later told Tourwana that her late father was indebted to an unknown man who planned to haunt her spiritually, prompting further payments purportedly for Quran recitals and other spiritual activities.

The court heard that in 2023, Jabiru learnt that Tourwana’s mother had suffered a stroke and allegedly told Ibrahim that someone was trying to inflict a similar attack.

They allegedly collected additional money to provide spiritual protection and redirect the attack to the “sender”, after which they received further payments as appreciation.

The prosecution said the matter was reported to family elders but could not be resolved, leading to a Police complaint.

During investigations, Ibrahim allegedly admitted posing as a spiritualist, while the Police recovered GH¢49,000 from him.

The prosecution said Jabiru fled to Togo after learning of Ibrahim’s arrest but returned to Dodowa in September 2026, where he stayed with Ibrahim and Musah.

On October 1, Police officers who went to Jabiru’s residence met Musah, who allegedly told them that Jabiru had gone out.

Musah subsequently sent Jabiru a text message stating: “Don’t come to the House.”

The prosecution said Musah admitted in his statement that he sent the message because he did not want Jabiru to be arrested.

Jabiru is currently at large.

Ibrahim and Musah are expected to reappear before the court, presided over by Mr Joseph Kunsong, on October 20, 2026.

Musah has denied the charge of harbouring a criminal.
