This is why this is a national emergency, not just a tech trend.

What Nigeria Must Do: A 3-Point Agenda

We cannot afford to be spectators in Nigeria while the future is coded in San Francisco.

Build AI-Native Talent, Not Certificate Holders: We must stop training people to compete with AI on raw knowledge. At Bildup AI, our Workforce Readiness Program in Lagos, Abuja, and Enugu is built on this principle: train humans with AI-native intelligence who can command a fleet of AI agents. That is the only workforce that survives RSI. Create a National RSI Observatory: We need a joint task force of NITDA, private labs like Bildup AI, and universities to monitor RSI signals and audit models deployed in critical sectors like finance and health. Invest in Sovereign Infrastructure: We need compute and data infrastructure that ensures Nigerian context is not an afterthought. If AI is to improve itself for us, it must be trained on us.

Conclusion

The race is no longer about who builds the best AI. The race is about who builds the AI that builds the best AI. Recursion has started. The loop is slow now, but loops compound. Nigeria has two choices: understand RSI and shape it, or ignore it and be shaped by it. At Bildup AI, we have chosen to understand it, teach it, and build for it.

*Chibuike Aguene is the CEO of Bildup AI, which builds AI-native workforce infrastructure used by tens of thousands of businesses annually. He leads the Bildup AI Workforce Readiness Program across Lagos, Abuja, and Enugu.

World.title: Lagos Honours 435 Retired Education Workers, Urges Them to Prioritise Health, Retirement Planning
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

The Lagos State Government has honoured 435 retired and retiring teachers, as well as non-teaching staff for their years of service and contributions to the development of the state’s education sector.

Speaking at the 2026 retirees senth-forth ceremony, the Executive Chairman of the State Universal Basic Education Board (LASUBEB), Dr. Hakeem Babatunde Shittu, urged the retiring education personnel to pay close attention to their health and embrace retirement as a natural phase of life.

He described retirement as an inevitable stage that every worker should prepare for from the beginning of their career.

According to him, workers should be grateful to God for the opportunity to serve and contribute to the development of the education sector, noting that retirement should be viewed as a milestone rather than an end to meaningful engagement.

He said: “It’s a living phenomenon. You have to retire one day. The moment you get your appointment letter, you know where you are going.”

The chairman noted that many workers who started their careers together would eventually reach retirement at different times, stressing the importance of appreciating the opportunity to complete one’s years of service.

He encouraged the retirees to remain connected with their colleagues and continue to communicate with people they had worked with, despite leaving active service.

Shittu also advised retirees to pay greater attention to their wellbeing, particularly as they advance in age.

“I always like to ask those that already retired, please always listen to your body and obey. Because when you get to 60, definitely your body has to be talking to you, and you have to listen,” he stated.

A permanent board member, Babatunde Williams, described the occasion as a celebration of service, sacrifice, education, commitment and achievement.

He stated that the recognition was an opportunity for the state government to appreciate the retirees for their years of dedication to educating children, administering schools and supporting teaching and learning across the state.

He noted that the retirees had made significant contributions to the development of the education sector, stressing that their years of waking up daily to report to schools and discharge their responsibilities had helped strengthen the state’s education system.

According to him, “The Lagos State government has continued to acknowledge the contributions of public servants and their important roles in the development of the state.”

He said the recognition of the retirees was one of the ways the government demonstrated its appreciation for their loyalty, commitment and dedication to service.

Williams urged the retirees not to regard their retirement from active service as the end of their contributions to society, noting that their knowledge, wisdom and experience remained valuable resources that could continue to benefit the education sector and the wider society.

“For the retiring and retired teaching and non-teaching staff, your service has not ended. Your experience remains valuable. Retirement from active service does not mean retirement from giving knowledge, wisdom and experience,” he said.

He congratulated them on the successful completion of their careers and commended them for their sacrifices and commitment to the education and development of children in Lagos State.

A Board Member in charge of Co-curricular activities, Hon. Adewale Jimoh, advised them to prioritise their health and embrace retirement as a natural phase of life.

He described retirement as an inevitable stage of every worker’s career, noting that employees should recognise from the outset of their appointment that they would eventually leave active service.

He urged the retirees to be grateful to God for the opportunity to serve and contribute to the development of education in the state, stressing that reaching retirement age was itself a reason for thanksgiving.

According to him, “Some of the colleagues who began their careers alongside the retirees had also reached the end of their working years, making the occasion an opportunity to appreciate God for their years of service.”

The Guest Speaker and Managing Director of Meristem Stockbrokers Limited, Saheed Adewale Bashir, urged the retirees to prepare financially, socially and emotionally for life after active service.

Speaking on the topic, ‘Retirement Planning’, he encouraged them to begin preparing for their future early rather than waiting until retirement is imminent.

According to Bashir, who was represented by a wealth management expert at the organisation, Imaobong Asemah, many people are apprehensive about retirement because they associate it with being tired or the end of an active and fulfilling life.

“Retirement is great if you have much to live on and live for,” she stated, urging them to develop a clear vision of what they want their retirement years to look like.

She said individuals should define their retirement vision early so that retirement would not come as a shock or leave them unprepared, adding that retirees and prospective retirees should maintain relationships and communication with people still in active service as social connections could help them remain engaged and productive.

Asemah encouraged retirees to join clubs, societies and other relevant associations where they could interact with people, pursue interests and remain socially active.

On financial preparedness, the expert stressed the importance of making investments that could provide income and cater to daily needs after retirement.

She also emphasised the importance of health insurance, saying adequate healthcare planning should form an integral part of every individual’s retirement strategy.

World.title: Kenya Airways Confirms Death of Nigerian Passenger on Nairobi-Lagos Flight
World.content:
Chinedu Eze

A Nigerian passenger aboard a Kenya Airways flight from Nairobi to Lagos died despite in-flight medical emergency to revive him Tuesday night.

The tragic incident unfolded at approximately 9:20 p.m. local Nigerian time on October 6, 2026, just 20 minutes before the aircraft was scheduled to touch down at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos.

Cabin crew discovered that the traveller had become completely unresponsive while the plane was on its final approach to landing.

The aircraft completed its landing at the Lagos airport around 9:41 p.m., where emergency medical personnel were stationed on the tarmac to immediately board the plane. Despite the prompt arrival of the medical team, the passenger was pronounced dead after an initial on-board examination.

In an official statement released on Wednesday, Kenya Airways confirmed the loss and extended its sympathy to the relatives of the deceased.

The East African airline expressed its deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of the deceased traveler while offering apologies to passengers for any disruption caused by the emergency. The airline also emphasized its commitment to maintaining the dignity and privacy of the passenger and their family.

Kenya Airways noted that it is currently coordinating with local authorities, aviation regulatory bodies, and the deceased’s family to assist with post-incident procedures and provide necessary support during the formal process.

However, THISDAY learnt from inside source that the deceased did not show any sign of ill-health when he boarded the flight but he became restless and despondent while onboard.

This might not be unrelated to the unconfirmed report that he was supposed to disembark in Madagascar, his final destination on the first leg of the flight, which was Lagos-Madagascar via Nairobi, but he was refused entry on arrival in Madagascar by the authorities, prompting Kenya Airways to return him to Nigeria.

Passengers who sat close to him on return flight indicated that he was restless while the flight was airborne, suggesting frustration and anger, which made the cabin crew and passengers to retrain him.

But shortly after the flight was in Nigeria’s airspace, it was noticed he had become motionless and was later pronounced dead.

World.title: Imansuaghon, ADC Candidate, Okonofua Escape Death In Gun Attack
World.content:
The 2027 political battle in Edo State took a dangerous turn as former governorship aspirant, Kenneth Imasuangbon; the party’s Edo Central senatorial candidate, Hon. Herberta Okonofua, and other party leaders on Tuesday reportedly escaped death by a whisker when suspected thugs opened fire on their convoy in Igueben Local Government Area of the state.

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) alleged that the attackers, suspected to be political loyalists of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), were led by the Igueben Local Government Council Chairman, Hon. Endurance Azemegbe, with ADC party supporter, identified as Jerry Oliha, reportedly sustaining gunshot wounds during the attack.

The incident, which allegedly occurred during the ADC leaders’ political engagements in the area, was said to be the third attack on the entourage within the local government, following earlier alleged shootings in Wards 4 and 5.

The development has sparked fresh concerns over the growing political tension in Edo, particularly coming barely a week after APC state Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, was reported to have threatened to deploy AK-47s against perceived opponents in the party’s drive to deliver 2.5 million votes to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

The ADC, in a statement through its state Publicity Secretary, Chris Ojeikere, alleged that the latest attack was part of a wider pattern of violence against opposition members and facilities in the state, citing similar incidents allegedly recorded in Etsako East, Owan West and Owan East.

“The Igueben Local Government Chairman has just led a team of gun tottering assailants to attack the entourage of Kenneth Imasuangbon and the Edo Central ADC Senatorial candidate, Hon. Herbeta Okonofua. The hoodlums shot fatally at a young man, Jerry Oliha, from ADC ward 6, at the premises of the Enogie of Igueben.

“The young man has been rushed to the Irrua Specialist Hospital, where doctors are battling to save his life. This shooting is the third time the entourage was shot at today. First at ward 4, and then, at ward 5, of the Local Government Area”.

“ADC will come out with a comprehensive report on this unfortunate policy of violence of the APC shortly. The DPO of the Igueben Local Government Area has been informed and involved in the unfortunate incident,” the party said.

However, Azemegbe, when contacted denied any involvement in the alleged attack, saying he was not in Igueben when the incident occurred and was only hearing about it from journalists.

“I was not around and I don’t know what happened. I am just hearing this from you. I can assure you that I will investigate the matter. I can’t say anything about what I didn’t know. The thing is strange to me. We are peaceful people and brothers in Igueben,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Edo State Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Eno Ikoedem, said he could not immediately confirm the incident, adding that the command would wade into the matter once it was formally reported.

World.title: Saleng spotted back in Sundowns training ahead of Pirates showdown
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns winger Monnapule Saleng has been spotted training with the first team ahead of Saturday’s MTN8 final against Orlando Pirates at Moses Mabhida Stadium.

The two sides will meet in Durban on Saturday evening, with Sundowns looking to lift the trophy against Saleng’s former club.

Saleng joined Sundowns from Pirates but has endured a difficult spell since making the move. The winger is yet to feature for the Brazilians this season, raising further questions about his future at the club.



Saleng getting ready for #MTN8 Final with other role models. pic.twitter.com/D7JJJBdBcq — Chris Dube (@ChrisMDube) October 7, 2026

Sundowns head coach Miguel Cardoso recently indicated that Saleng’s situation was no longer a coaching matter and had instead been placed in the hands of the club’s management.

The 28-year-old was previously excluded from first-team training after reportedly refusing to travel with Sundowns for last season’s CAF Champions League final.



However, there was a significant development on Wednesday when Saleng was seen training with the Sundowns first team ahead of their highly anticipated clash with Pirates.

His return to training could offer a major clue about his current standing at the club, although it remains unclear whether he will be involved in Saturday’s final.

Saleng’s agent, Karabo Mathang Tshabuse, previously opened up about the difficult situation surrounding her client.



“He is travelling a very difficult path,” she said, while explaining that although she could see there was an issue, she was not in a position to determine exactly what it was.

Saleng could make an appearance for Sundowns in the final

Tshabuse also suggested that Saleng’s reactions during periods of distress could sometimes be difficult to manage and said she had observed similar challenges in different environments.

The agent revealed that she had attempted to secure professional assistance for the player.



“What I can do is I can call for help, I can cry for help, I can walk with my client for that help, but it is up to him to say, let’s take it.”

With Saleng now back in training, attention will turn to whether Cardoso and Sundowns decide to include the former Pirates star in their squad for Saturday’s MTN8 final.

Will Saleng have the last laugh?

World.title: Inside the men’s circles trying to stop femicide before it starts [video]
World.content:
Father A Nation brings men together to talk about ending violence against women. Image: Instagram/@fatheranation and @sydney_madibo

In a Johannesburg informal settlement, a group of men gather in a circle.

They’re not there to watch soccer or share a drink.

They’re there to talk about something many South African men avoid: violence against women.



And the man leading the conversation wants them to see themselves differently.

He’s Itumeleng Stephen Tamaga, known locally as Bra Steve.

He’s the local organiser of Father A Nation (FAN), a non-profit that works with men and boys to promote positive masculinity and help end violence against women.



The BBC recently joined one of his gatherings in Organic Market, an informal settlement in Johannesburg.

WHY THESE CONVERSATIONS MATTER NOW

The talks come at a painful time.



As The South African has previously reported, the discovery of women’s bodies in Ekurhuleni, near Johannesburg, has reignited questions about the scale of violence against women.

By 5 October, the bodies of 12 women had been found in Ekurhuleni since July.

Police have not confirmed that the deaths are linked.



By late September, at least four people were in police custody in connection with some of the killings.

Another victim, Boitumelo Mashita, 23, was allegedly shot by her estranged husband.

Bra Steve’s message to the men was direct.

“You as a man are a powerful force for good,” he told them. He added that women need to be safe.



Some of the men were honest about their own pasts.

Kgomotso Mathekga, 30, admitted that he once grabbed and slapped his girlfriend during an argument.

The couple broke up, and he said he no longer sees his child.



WHO IS FATHER A NATION?

Father A Nation is a non-profit company that addresses gender-based violence (GBV), crime and fatherlessness.

It aims to do this by restoring and equipping men to be nation-builders, fathers and role models.

FAN has been running programmes in communities, schools, colleges and corporates across South Africa since 2010.



Craig Wilkinson founded the organisation and serves as its chief executive officer (CEO).

Wilkinson is also the author of books and courses on fatherhood, positive masculinity and overcoming GBV.

By 2024, FAN said more than 300,000 men had been exposed to its programmes.



WHAT FATHER A NATION DOES

FAN’s work is built on one idea: that “wounded masculinity” is destructive, while healthy masculinity is a gift to society.

It reaches men through events, workshops, camps, mentorship and “mantalks”.

The aim is to teach men to use their strength to love, serve, protect and provide, and to become activists against any form of abuse.



WHY FATHERLESSNESS IS PART OF THE PROBLEM

FAN believes the crisis starts at home.

According to the State of South Africa’s Fathers 2024 report, 64.5% of children in South Africa didn’t live with their biological fathers in 2023.

FAN argues that men who grow up with positive, present father figures are less likely to become perpetrators of violent crime.



Wilkinson has said that modelling healthy masculinity can stop “the cycle of GBV at its roots.”

WHAT FATHER A NATION WANTS TO ACHIEVE

FAN’s mission is to raise the next generation of men to build a safe and prosperous South Africa.

Its long-term goal is to build a lasting movement of men who are outstanding fathers, mentors and role models.



In FAN’s profile on MIT Solve, its founder writes that he started the organisation believing that “if we can heal men, we can heal the world.”

I find it powerful that this work happens in circles of men, not just in courtrooms or on protest marches.

GBV is often discussed as a women’s issue. But women can’t end it on their own.



Watching men hold each other accountable gives me a little hope.

World.title: Thembinkosi Lorch set to leave Libya, could Kaizer Chiefs pounce?
World.content:
Former Orlando Pirates winger Thembinkosi Lorch is reportedly on his way out of Al Ittihad Tripoli after just a few months with the Libyan club.

The 33-year-old South African attacker could be on the move again after joining Al Ittihad in February. His spell in Libya looks set to be short-lived, potentially leaving the former Bafana Bafana international searching for another club.

Lorch joined Al Ittihad after spending a year with Moroccan giants Wydad Casablanca. His time in Morocco included a memorable goal at the FIFA Club World Cup, and he appeared to have settled well before making a surprise move to Libya.



With his future at Al Ittihad uncertain, Lorch could potentially become a free agent.

There has also been speculation that the experienced attacker could attract interest from clubs in the Botola Pro League following his performances for Wydad. A return to Morocco could therefore be an option if he decides against returning to South Africa.

Could Lorch return to the PSL?

A move back to the Premier Soccer League would also be intriguing.



A return to Mamelodi Sundowns appears unlikely, while a reunion with Orlando Pirates may also be difficult to see at this stage. However, Lorch could potentially emerge as an option for Kaizer Chiefs.

Lorch has a strong record against Amakhosi, having scored six goals against Chiefs during his time with Pirates. His experience, versatility and familiarity with the South African game could make him an interesting player should Chiefs decide to explore the market.

For now, Nyoso’s next destination remains uncertain, but his expected departure from Al Ittihad could put the experienced attacker back on the transfer radar.

World.title: R6.4 million Ankole auction: Cyril Ramaphosa’s ‘cattle collection’
World.content:
President Cyril Ramaphosa made history with the sale of his Ankole cow. Image via Instagram @thepresidencyza

President Cyril Ramaphosa’s company Ntaba Nyoni Ankole broke records with the sale of a pregnant Ankole cow named Queen Arusha for a whopping R6.4 million. What other cattle does the President own?

PRESIDENT CYRIL RAMAPHOSA’S COMPANY BREAKS RECORD

Queen Arusha was auctioned off for R6.4 million becoming the most expensive cow, across all breeds in South Africa. The cow was sold by President Cyril Ramaphosa’s cattle breeding company called Ntaba Nyoni Ankole.

Queen Arusha was born in 2023 and is carrying a calf. An anonymous buyer won the auction, which took place at his Phala Phala farm, which is near Bela-Bela, Limpopo.



The sough-after Ankole is the sister of Optimus Prime, the biggest Ankole bull in South Africa. Optimus Prime’s horns span a massive 173cm long, also owned by Ramaphosa. Ntaba Nyoni Ankole also bought two vials of Optimus Prime’s semen for R250 000 each.

THE PRESIDENT’S CATTLE COLLECTION

Ramaphosa is believed to own more than 100 of the unique Ankole breed cattle. This cattle is indigenous to African countries such as Uganda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, and parts of Tanzania. The President reportedly bought the cattle because he was captivated by their majestic appearance, exceptional hardiness. He had a personal fascination with the breed after visiting Uganda in 2004 and seeing the herd of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni.

The Ntaba Nyoni cattle farm was founded in 2004. At the time, he bought 40 Ankole cows and three bulls from Museveni. In addition to the Ankoles, his livestock reportedly include Boran and Bonsmara cattle studs, game farming and feedlot. The exact number of head counts change due to breeding, sales and auctions. Therefore, it is difficult to pin point exactly how much of cattle the President owns.

Ramaphosa is the biggest owner of cattle in South Africa.

Are goals scored and defensive impact the only metrics for success in soccer?

Here’s a look at which PSL players have the most minutes across the season so far.



3 players leading total minutes so far

3 players have recorded the most minutes in the PSL during the 2026/2027 campaign so far:

Bafana Bafana goalkeeper Ronwen Williams has played all 8 games for Mamelodi Sundowns (720 minutes).



Surprisingly, 2 players from newly-promoted and high-flying Milford FC have equalled him.

Defensive midfielder Vusumuzi Mthabela and centre-back Olwethu Cele have also recorded 720 minutes each.

Milford’s Sifiso Mdluli is fourth on the list (706), having been substituted in the 76th minute against Richards Bay in September.



Where others rank for the most minutes this season

The Orlando Pirates goalkeeper is joint-fifth (630 minutes), with the club having only played 7 games so far.

Chaine’s teammate, centre-back Lebone Seema, has also featured in every game in the PSL this term.

Pirates have a rescheduled visit from TS Galaxy on October 13, while Williams should feature for Sundowns against Richards Bay in the concurrent fixture.



Other players who have maximised their minutes represent the likes of AmaZulu FC, who are third on the PSL table.

Interestingly, Kaizer Chiefs ranks lower for players with the most minutes played across the campaign.

Centre-back Inacio Miguel has recorded the most game time with 607 minutes on the park.



Pirates, Sundowns balancing rotation and stability

The Buccaneers and the Brazilians are bracing for a packed October fixture list.

From Saturday, Pirates and Sundowns are back in action across the PSL, CAF Champions League, and Carling Knockout Cup.

Abdeslam Ouaddou and Miguel Cardoso are already feeling the pinch of fixture congestion, with several players on the sidelines.



Meanwhile, Milford’s quieter schedule means they can afford to build more stability and create settled lineups.

The effect of squad rotations on the top clubs will remain an important talking point throughout the season.

World.title: Transfer report: Bafana star gains attention in England, Spain, Germany, France and Italy
World.content:
Reports emerging from Europe reveal that the Rangers FC and Bafana Bafana central defender has inspired scouts in England, Spain, Germany, France and Italy to follow his progress in Scotland.

The 22-year-old from Durban has enjoyed a storming start in Glasgow since joining from Philadephia Union in July.

BAFANA BAFANA STAR OLWETHU MAKHANYA MAKES INSTANT IMPACT IN EUROPE

According to TEAMTalk, as reported by SoccerBeat, Makhanya is being monitored across Europe’s top five leagues.



“Olwethu Makhanya has barely settled at Rangers, but TEAMtalk understands the young defender is already drawing attention from clubs across Europe’s top five leagues,” the report said.

“Clubs in the Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, the Bundesliga and Ligue 1 are understood to be keeping tabs on Makhanya, with the expectation that Rangers would face enquiries next summer should he continue on his present path,” the outlet reported.

Makhanya has started all 6 of his league appearances, playing 540 minutes and helping his side keep 4 clean sheets, while earning an impressive 7.46 match rating.

He has completed 323 passes at an 85.2% accuracy rate. In a 1-0 win over St. Mirren, he recorded a 93% completion rate, completing 62 of 67 passes, while also making 5 of 7 progressive passes and 5 of 7 long balls.

Defensively, he won possession 27 times in his first 5 games, while recording 20 clearances, 4 blocks and 5 interceptions. His total number of clearances has since risen to 24.

He also won 4 of his first 5 tackles and completed 30 duels overall. The defender ranked third in the squad for aerial duels, winning 13 of 24. In possession, he ranked second in the squad for carries, while completing 4 dribbles and creating 4 goal-scoring chances.



Makhanya first emerged in the Marumo Gallants‘ reserve team before signing for Stellenbosch FC. He later moved to the USA to play his football for Philadelphia Union before moving to Rangers.

World.title: Nearly 2,000 Nigerians flee South Africa after anti-migrant protests
World.content:
LAGOS - Nearly 2,000 Nigerians have been evacuated from South Africa since June following a wave of protests against undocumented migrants, Nigeria's foreign ministry said.

Nigeria has been outspoken in its criticism of the South African government's handling of the protests, and has organised the repatriation of citizens who want to leave.

From June 10 to October 2, 14 flights were chartered from South Africa to take a total of 1,926 Nigerians home, the foreign ministry said in a statement issued overnight from Monday to Tuesday.

The Nigerian National Assembly last month banned all official visits by lawmakers to South Africa because of the violence.

As the richest country on the continent, South Africa has long attracted migrants seeking work, but an unemployment rate of over 30 percent and deep inequalities have stoked tensions.

More than 200,000 people have fled South Africa, according to an AFP tally based on figures released by African governments that have repatriated their nationals.

World.title: Cops comb crime scene for abducted child
World.content:
ATTERIDGEVILLE - Police are combing an active crime scene in Atteridgeville, searching for a suspect accused of kidnapping a child and reportedly raping the mother.

The search is currently being conducted at a nearby river, where a pink school bag, believed to be that of the four-month-old child, was found.

A white doek was also found at the scene.

World.title: Ghana to apply to join BRICS, foreign minister says
World.content:
ACCRA - Ghana's cabinet has approved a decision to formally apply to join the BRICS geopolitical and economic bloc, Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa said during a visit by his Indian counterpart.

Ablakwa said Tuesday that Ghana had already sought India's support for its application, describing the move as an effort to diversify the country's economic and diplomatic partnerships.

"The Cabinet of President John Dramani Mahama has decided that Ghana should put in a formal application to join BRICS," Ablakwa told reporters, speaking alongside India's external affairs minister, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar.

The group of emerging economies, founded by Brazil, Russia, India and China, has expanded in recent years, focusing on bringing together countries in the global south.

South Africa joined shortly after its 2009 founding, while countries such as Ethiopia, Iran and Indonesia have joined since 2024.

"Joining India in BRICS will give us economic options, will diversify our base and our partnerships, and will also allow us to have more cooperation within the Global South framework," he said.

Jaishankar said India was supportive of Ghana's aspirations but stressed that membership would require consideration by the wider BRICS grouping.

Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are also members.

World.title: Verstappen revival to be put to the test in steamy Singapore
World.content:
SINGAPORE - Max Verstappen's resurgence in Malaysia will be put to the test just 300 kilometres south at the Singapore Grand Prix this weekend, where the Red Bull driver may need to overcome the elements and his own poor record at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

An imperious Verstappen took his first chequered flag of the year at the wide-open and fast Sepang Circuit at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday.

But it was in a race delayed for an hour and a half after a chaotic formation lap saw cars, including Verstappen's, grind to halt because of a software glitch in the settings for running in wet conditions.

"It was insane," said Verstappen. "At some points, we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn't understand it... I saw eight cars crawling and Lewis (Hamilton) stopped... It's not what you want for the sport."

Rain could again play a part in the tropical city-state, with thunderstorms forecast to affect both Saturday's sprint race and qualifying, and Sunday's night grand prix.

Verstappen has never won at the twisty Marina Bay Street Circuit, where extremes of heat and humidity play a part in the most physically attritional race of the season on a circuit notoriously difficult for overtaking.

Drivers can shed up to three kilogrammes (more than six pounds) during the longest outing on the calendar, where completing the 62 steamy laps often lasts the maximum two hours race time allowed.

A floor upgrade coupled with Verstappen finally working out how to get the best from the new generation car led him to call the result at Sepang four days ago "amazing".

Runaway championship leader Kimi Antonelli was second in the Mercedes and is likely to be challenging for the chequered flag again.

He was the beneficiary of yet more bad luck for his teammate and main title rival George Russell, who was "beyond disappointment" after an agonising power unit failure when running third with five laps to go in Malaysia.

"You've almost got to laugh... it's just so many times this season it's happened," said Russell, who has failed to finish three times in 16 Grands Prix so far in 2026.

Lewis Hamilton has won four times in Singapore in the past and was buoyed by a drive at Sepang where he cut through the field to recover to third after starting on unsuitable dry tyres and dropping to the back.

"To finish on the podium after the way the race began feels really satisfying," said Hamilton.

"It is a great reward for the hard work, determination and resilience everyone showed today."

Russell won the Singapore Grand Prix a year ago, edging Verstappen and the current world champion Lando Norris of McLaren.

World.title: Africa launches own credit agency in bid for cheaper borrowing
World.content:
NAIROBI - Africa will launch its own credit rating agency on Wednesday, aimed at countering what many see as unfair assessments by global institutions that make it more expensive for African nations to borrow money.

The Africa Credit Ratings Agency (AfCRA), backed by the African Union after nearly a decade of talks, will judge the creditworthiness of countries, businesses and institutions.

The Indian Ocean island of Mauritius was chosen as the agency's home, partly due to its established financial services industry.

It aims to offer an alternative viewpoint to the "big three" global credit ratings -- Fitch, Moody's and S&P -- which have been accused in the past of unfairly playing down African economies.

The African Peer Review Mechanism, the institution behind AfCRA, says 23 countries on the continent are not rated at all by the traditional agencies.

They can also overlook Africa's huge informal sectors, which do not easily show up in official data, analysts say.

"Africa is not asking for favourable ratings," Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu wrote on X last month, welcoming AfCRA.

"We are asking for fair ratings, grounded in our fundamentals and in the reforms our economies are actually carrying out."

- Real-world effects -

Low credit ratings have real-world effects as investors charge more interest to lend money.

On average, it cost Africa nine dollars for every $100 borrowed in international markets in 2024, compared to about $4.70 for emerging markets in Asia and $6.50 in Latin America, according to estimates by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, a club of mostly rich nations.

AfCRA is not just a response to "Africa's unhappiness with the incumbent players", Hannah Wanjie Ryder, chief executive of consultancy Development Reimagined, told a recent seminar organised by the Chatham House think tank.

"The theory of change is they would actually be able to look with clearer eyes," she said.

- First test -

It remains to be seen whether AfCRA will be able to persuade investors that its ratings can be trusted over those of the leading agencies.

AfCRA's founders say there will be no government interference.

Analysts say the first test is whether the agency will downgrade an African government. If not, investors risk seeing it as the continent marking its own homework.

"African borrowers have long paid a high-risk premium and standard models can miss the informal economy, domestic savings and reforms," said Jacob Oreki, a management consultant at Kenya's Strathmore University Foundation.

"But a rating agency is judged on independence and accuracy, not where it sits. If it will not downgrade an African sovereign, markets will treat it as advocacy," he told AFP.

Investors will base their decisions on the rating, he added, if "it is credible, not because it is African".

World.title: US, China, EU: three paths to regulating AI
World.content:
WASHINGTON - The United States, China and the European Union are taking different paths to govern artificial intelligence, as calls grow worldwide to rein in its most powerful systems.

Here is how they are going about it:

- United States -

Nearly two years into his second term, President Donald Trump has built his AI policy almost entirely from voluntary industry pledges and executive orders intended to sustain an AI boom that is powering the US economy.

On his first day back in office, Trump scrapped his predecessor Joe Biden's 2023 order requiring developers of the most powerful AI systems to share safety test results with the government.

In July 2025, the White House unveiled an "AI Action Plan" listing more than 90 measures to speed up development.

An accompanying order titled "Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government" requires federal agencies to buy only models deemed ideologically neutral.

Congress, politically divided and heavily lobbied by Big Tech, has yet to pass a federal AI law, and is out of session until after the midterm elections.

Trump has pushed to block state AI laws, but Congress has repeatedly refused to override them, and state laws are taking effect nationwide.

This year, the release of AI models capable of powerful cyberattacks shifted the focus to security. A June order set up a voluntary system for developers to give the government up to 30 days of early access to their most powerful models.

With voter anxiety growing, the heads of major AI companies signed a White House accord on September 29 pledging independent audits and board-level oversight of cutting-edge models.

The pact carries no penalties for companies that fall short, though Trump called it "morally binding."

The same day, Trump ordered federal agencies to replace the term "artificial intelligence" with "super intelligence" in official communications.

- China -

China already has a complex, evolving set of rules on how AI is used, including by children.

Regulations on AI companion bots took effect in July, aiming to curb emotional dependency and banning the creation of digital clones of real people without their consent.

President Xi Jinping said this summer that AI should be "always under human control," calling for more "laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning, and emergency response systems."

Premier Li Qiang has also warned that the world risks "losing control" of frontier technologies such as AI if governments are too slow to regulate them.

However, "a general pause or deliberate slowdown in AI development remains outside the mainstream Chinese policy posture," Oxford China Policy Lab analysts wrote in September.

Some in China see calls to slow progress as hard to justify, "particularly given their perception that US measures such as export controls have already constrained China's AI development for years," they said.

China censors and controls AI-generated content much as it does other online information -- and last month, its spy chief warned that AI could endanger national security.

"Hostile forces" are abusing generative AI to "fabricate political rumours and spread harmful information," Minister of State Security Chen Yixin said.

- Europe -

The European Union rushed to adopt its AI Act in 2024, which Brussels touts as the world's most comprehensive rules on the technology.

But European companies, fearing the rules would stifle innovation as they race to catch up with US and Chinese rivals, later won a delay on rules covering high-risk systems.

Amid growing global calls for control, European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said last month that the AI rules put "Europe in the position to shape global efforts."

She also said she would invite the main frontier labs "for a discussion on how we can support ongoing industry efforts to pace the frontier."

European firms have been more wary of slowing down, fearing it could be an attempt by US giants to lock in their dominance.

The EU has other tools to regulate AI.

In August, ChatGPT became the first AI chatbot added to the EU's list of digital services subject to greater legal scrutiny under its online content rules.

Brussels last month also proposed forcing companies to make AI companions and chatbots safe before children use them.

AI chatbots must not "simulate interpersonal relationships in ways that create emotional dependency," the EU said, following a spate of suicides worldwide linked to children's interactions with such assistants.

World.title: Emmys gala will now stream its premier television awards
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - The Emmy Awards, which celebrate the best in television, are the latest entertainment industry gala to ink a streaming deal and will leave broadcast for Amazon Prime starting next year.

The Television Academy on Tuesday announced the new six-year deal that will make the awards show available for streaming worldwide without a paywall on the Amazon platform.

The 79th edition of the Emmys next September will see it become the first of the major EGOT awards -- Emmys, Grammys, Oscars and Tonys -- to exclusively stream.

The Oscars will move to YouTube starting with the 2029 ceremony, after fulfilling the last two years of its contract with the network ABC.

The Emmys' transition to streaming is a reflection of broader industry trends, with networks vying for continued relevance as streaming proves a dominant force.

But the head of the Television Academy said the decision also offered a way to broaden viewership.

"Television has never been more global, and the Emmys should be a celebration that the world can share," academy chair Cris Abrego said in a statement.

"Now Prime Video audiences in more than 200 countries will be able to experience the Emmys live with no subscription required."

At this year's awards gala, quirky horror series "Widow's Bay" cleaned up, setting a new record for the most Emmys won by a comedy in a single year, as gritty hospital show "The Pitt" won again for best drama.

World.title: 'He talks at every opportunity': Sibiya distances himself from Maumela
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Suspended Deputy National Police Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya has told the court that his associate, Bishop Azwihangwi Maumela, “will talk at every opportunity” he gets.

Arguing for Sibiya’s release on bail at the Randburg Magistrate’s Court on Wednesday, his legal representative, Estelle Killian, said Sibiya had never instructed Maumela to conduct interviews or make contact with witnesses.

This follows a recording presented in court last Thursday in which Maumela was heard asking the father of a 16-year-old girl to drop charges against Sibiya. He was also heard asking the father to persuade an 18-year-old rape complainant to withdraw her complaint against Sibiya.

On the first day of his bail application, Sibiya assured the court that he would not interfere with witnesses. The State has argued that Maumela’s alleged conduct should be viewed in that context.

LIVESTREAM | Sibiya back in court as he seeks bail

Sibiya, through his lawyer, sought to downplay Maumela’s comments, telling the court: “He will talk at every opportunity that he can get, and it is political speak to say, ‘we are going to retaliate’; it does not mean we are going to take up arms and fight.”

In an interview with the media following Sibiya’s arrest in September, Maumela said: “If the president cannot intervene, we’re going to retaliate, because we cannot have law enforcement that has been used to target individuals.”

He later apologised for the remarks.

Relying on the recording, the State has urged the court to closely scrutinise Maumela and his relationship with Sibiya.

Maumela has been vocal in defending his friend. Speaking to eNCA last month, he denied that he and Sibiya had been at a strip club when Sibiya was arrested, saying they had instead been at a restaurant.

READ MORE | Sibiya’s court bid puts disciplinary hearing on ice

He has also criticised Sibiya’s accusers and questioned the circumstances surrounding his friend’s arrest.

Sibiya faces five charges, including rape, human trafficking and three counts of sexual grooming involving a 16-year-old girl.

According to the allegations, Sibiya plied an 18-year-old woman with alcohol before she allegedly lost consciousness and was raped at a hotel in Sandton.

He has denied the rape allegation, maintaining that the encounter was consensual.

The bail application continues.

World.title: Complainant letters cannot be used to initiate judge's removal, court rules
World.content:
Chief Justice Martha Koome. [File]

A letter addressed to the Chief Justice seeking administrative intervention cannot form the basis for removing a judge, the Employment and Labour Relations Court (ELRC) has ruled.

Delivering a unanimous judgment in a case filed by Environment and Land Court Judge Anthony Ombwayo, a three-judge ELRC bench comprising Justices Jemimah Keli, Onesmus Makau, and Dr. Jacob Gikeri ruled that a letter written to the Chief Justice cannot simply be forwarded to the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) and treated as a petition for removal.

World.title: How KNEC plans to stop cheating in 2026 exams
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere. [File]

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) will use smart padlocks to secure all examination storage containers as more than 3.6 million candidates sit the 2026 national examinations and assessments.

KNEC Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere said the council would monitor the containers from its headquarters to prevent anyone from accessing examination papers before the scheduled times.

“Last year KNEC piloted the use of smart padlocks in 250 containers. This year all containers will be secured using the smart padlocks which will be monitored from the KNEC headquarters,” said Dr Njengere.

Under the system, officials will open containers at designated times. Officials will access Kenya Primary School Education Assessment (KPSEA) and Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA) papers at 6 a.m., while centre managers will collect Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) papers at 7 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.

However, Dr Njengere identified mobile phones as the biggest challenge in preventing examination malpractice.

“Mobile phones remain our biggest challenge in administration of KCSE examination,” observed Dr Njengere.

He warned that the council would not allow candidates or examination officials to have mobile phones at examination centres during examination sessions.

“Any contravention of this rule will constitute a malpractice as per the KNEC Act and the Rules and Regulations,” noted Dr Njengere.

The council will deploy 342,005 contracted professionals to administer and manage the examinations and assessments. They include centre managers, supervisors, invigilators, security officers and drivers.

For KCSE, KNEC will deploy 10,765 centre managers, 12,274 supervisors, 57,432 invigilators and 21,388 security officers. Each examination centre will have at least two police officers.

Centre managers will collect KCSE papers twice a day, and KNEC will place morning and afternoon papers in marked cartons to reduce mix-ups and unauthorised access.

KNEC has personalised question papers with candidates’ details, and examiners will receive anonymised scripts with those details removed.

The 2026 examination and assessment season will involve 3,634,846 candidates, a 6.13 per cent increase from the 3,424,836 registered in 2025.

KCSE rehearsals will take place on Friday, October 16. Examinations for papers with low candidature will run from Monday, October 19 to Friday, October 30, while papers with large candidature will run from Monday, November 2 to Friday, November 20.

KPSEA and KJSEA assessments will run from Monday, October 26 to Friday, October 30.

KNEC Chairperson Prof. Julius Nyabundi said the council was preparing for possible disruption from El Nino rains.

“As we start off the 2026 field administration season, one of the risks we contend with are the attempts to cheat in assessments and examination,” said Prof. Nyabundi.

He urged candidates, parents and examination officials to protect the integrity of the examinations, warning that malpractice could undermine public confidence in the education system.

“Cheating in examinations undermines public confidence in the credibility, fairness and quality of the entire education system,” noted Prof. Nyabundi.

KNEC will operate a 24-hour call centre with toll-free numbers for candidates, officials and members of the public to report incidents and seek assistance during the examination period.

The 2026 cycle will continue the implementation of Competency-Based Education assessments, including School-Based Assessments in primary, junior and senior school.

Grade 10 learners are undertaking their first School-Based Assessment, which will contribute 15 marks towards the Kenya Certificate of Basic Education.

World.title: Mbadi hits out at Sifuna, says opposition lacks economic agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Treasury CS John Mbadi after opening new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by the M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency. [James Omoro, Standard]

The National Treasury CS John Mbadi has hit out at Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, saying that criticising President William Ruto should not be an agenda for a presidential candidate.

Speaking when he opened new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency, Mbadi said lack of economic agenda makes the opposition unsuitable to lead the country.

“I have heard of opposition leaders who want the presidency, but they do not have an agenda for the economic transformation of this country,” he said.

The CS claimed that none of the opposition leaders is suitable for the presidency.

“These opposition leaders cannot make any economic change in this country. They should not be elected,” he said.

He told Nyanza residents to shun the new wave of opposition led by Sifuna.

Mbadi claimed that opposition leaders lack political direction.

He said Sifuna had taken too long to unveil a political party that he will use to run for the presidency.

“Do not join the opposition bandwagon. We are just a few months away from the General Election, but Sifuna still doesn’t know a political party he will use to run for the presidency. They are still leaving in confusion,” Mbadi said.

He said Sifuna has not demonstrated how to improve this country’s economy.

“Former President Uhuru Kenyatta left the economy of this country in tatters. We have tried to improve it but we are not yet where we want it to be,” Mbadi said.

He urged Nyanza residents to support Ruto.

The CS said Ruto’s government had improved mega infrastructural projects across the country as part of economic transformation.

He cited the 74 km Mbita- Sindo- Sori road, Lake Victoria ring road and other infrastructure projects as some of the reasons residents should support Ruto.

“I urge you to support Ruto so that we can continue acquiring more development projects in this region,” Mbadi said.

World.title: Kericho Annex Prison under scrutiny over death of remand prisoner
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Brenda Chemutai, 19, who allegedly committed suicide inside the Kericho Annex Prison where she was awaiting trial for an offence of being in possession of bhang that was seized in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer. [Courtesy]

Questions are mounting over security and accountability at Kericho Annex Prison following the death of a 19-year-old remand prisoner in a suspected case of suicide.

Her family is demanding answers about how she obtained a bedsheet and why they were not notified until nearly 10 hours after the incident.

Brenda Chemutai was reportedly found hanging from a double-decker bed at around 9 am when her fellow cellmates were having breakfast on Friday.

The cell had eight inmates, who had gone for breakfast, according to a police report.

However, her relatives state they were not informed until about 7 pm, after her body had already been taken from the prison and transferred to the Kericho County Hospital Mortuary.

The delay has raised serious concerns for the family, which calls for authorities to clarify what happened between the time Chemutai was discovered and when her next of kin were contacted.

Kericho East Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officer, Kennedy Apindi, said police have launched investigations following reports from prison officials that the incident was a suicide.

He mentioned that preliminary information indicated Chemutai allegedly used a bedsheet.

The family, however, insists that investigators determine when she was found, who discovered her, when the incident was reported to police, who authorised her body’s removal, and why her relatives were not notified immediately.

“We had spoken with Brenda. She was expected to be released around December, and by January we would all have been together at home,” said her sister, Phyllis Cherotich.

Cherotich added that the family had seen no signs indicating Chemutai intended to take her own life.

"Her death has shocked us deeply. She never mentioned any plans of this nature. We want to understand how this was possible given the level of security at the facility," she said.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged use of a bedsheet have also raised questions for the family.

Her uncle, Michael Rono, questioned how such an item came into Chemutai's possession while she was in a remand facility.

"I am deeply surprised. When one enters the prison, one is carefully searched. Where did the bedsheet come from? We ask the government to ensure justice is done," Rono said.

Chemutai had been in remand since 2024, with her relatives saying she was arrested while still a minor and had spent nearly two years awaiting the conclusion of her case.

She was being tried for the offence of possession of bhang in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer.

Her death has consequently brought renewed scrutiny to not only what happened inside the prison but also the circumstances that led to her prolonged detention.

Youth activists from the Voice of Youth Organisation, led by Kelvin Kipchichir, have joined the family in demanding investigations into both the death and the case that resulted in Chemutai's detention.

Kipchichir claimed Chemutai was arrested alongside other suspects in a vehicle allegedly linked to an Officer Commanding Station serving in Kakamega.

According to the activists, police recovered 32 rolls of bhang from the vehicle, while some of the suspects allegedly fled, leaving Chemutai behind.

The claims have not been independently established.

Kipchichir questioned why Chemutai remained in custody for such a prolonged period and called for scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the vehicle and its alleged connection to the police officer.

“We are concerned that an OCS in the National Police Service could allow a vehicle to be used by an individual with a known criminal record,” he said.

He called on the Ministry of Interior to establish who owned or controlled the vehicle and under what circumstances it was allegedly being used.

The activists said the vehicle was still at Kericho Police Station.

For the family, the tragedy has been compounded by personal loss. Chemutai's father died while she was in remand, while she leaves behind a young child.

Relatives said detectives had informed them that the person alleged to own the bhang had since been arrested and was being held in Kisumu.

But the immediate question for Chemutai's family is what happened during her final hours.

They want a clear account of the period between the reported discovery of her body at about 9 am and the notification of the family nearly 10 hours later.

They also want investigators to establish how the bedsheet allegedly used in the incident came into her possession and whether prison officers followed all required procedures after she was found.

The activists are calling for the inquiry to extend beyond the death of Chemutai to her arrest, the length of her detention and the handling of the case against her.

The family has demanded a transparent and independent investigation, saying it wants answers on how a teenager who entered the justice system while still a minor ended up dead in remand custody.

The family says it wants those questions answered before proceeding with burial arrangements.

World.title: Pregnant woman found dead by roadside in Kirinyaga with head, hip injuries
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The National Police Service (NPS) has launched investigations after the body of a pregnant woman was found by the roadside in the Itangi area of Mwea East Sub-County, Kirinyaga County.

The woman, identified as Catherine Njeru, was found early Friday morning along the Piai-Itangi Murram Road with visible injuries to her head and hip.

In a statement, NPS said the incident is being investigated as a suspected murder.

"The NPS condoles with the family, relatives, and friends of the deceased and commits to expeditious and conclusive investigations to ensure that any person or persons responsible for this barbaric crime are brought to justice," read the statement.

Police have urged residents of Itangi to remain calm and refrain from speculation as the investigation continues.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation has been asked to report to the nearest police station or a law enforcement officer.

The matter is being investigated by Kirinyaga County Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) officers, local Sub-County police and Central Regional Police Command, led by the Regional Criminal Investigations Officer.

According to NPS, the Inspector General of the National Police Service has also been briefed on the incident and directed the Director of Criminal Investigations to expedite the probe and establish the facts surrounding the woman's death.

World.title: Ruto downplays rivalry over oil refinery in East Africa
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Nigeria President Olesugun Obasanjo, Ali Dangote, President William Ruto and Uganda President Yoweri Museveni during launch of the Lamu Refinery on September 30, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has played down suggestions of rivalry between Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania over competing refinery projects, saying East Africa’s growing demand for petroleum products can support several facilities across the region.

Speaking during a media interview at State House Mombasa, Ruto said Kenya had no objection to Uganda and Tanzania pursuing their own refinery projects, arguing that the different facilities could complement rather than compete with one another.

“There is no bad blood at all. There is no problem,” Ruto said.

His remarks came a day after he presided over the groundbreaking of the Lamu refinery project, which the government is positioning as a major component of a wider industrial complex on the Kenyan coast.

Ruto said he had discussed Uganda’s plans with President Yoweri Museveni and agreed that Kampala could proceed with a smaller refinery without threatening Kenya’s investment in Lamu.

He said Kenya would even be prepared to buy petroleum products from Uganda if they could reach the Kenyan market at competitive prices.

“If it is manufactured there in Uganda and the oil from that place is near Busia, and it can reach Busia at a lower price, we will buy oil from anywhere and bring it to Busia,” Ruto said.

The President argued that the size of the regional petroleum market meant there was room for more than one refinery.

“This one in Lamu cannot serve all of us; it will be necessary to expand,” he said, adding that East Africa had “enough opportunity” for multiple facilities.

Ruto also extended the same approach to Tanzania, saying Kenya could participate in a refinery project in Tanga if it is eventually developed.

“Even if the one in Tanga is built, we as Kenya will go and buy some shares there. There is no problem,” he said.

The comments point to a regional energy market in which petroleum products could move across borders depending on availability, transport costs and prices. Rather than treating refinery projects as competing national investments, Ruto said the facilities could strengthen economic cooperation within the East African Community.

The President said the Lamu refinery would also address some of the challenges Kenya faces from dependence on imported refined petroleum products.

“Lamu will give us an opportunity to have fuel without the fluctuations that we have now,” he said.

He linked the proposed refinery to the need to reduce Kenya’s exposure to international oil price shocks, disruptions caused by instability in oil-producing regions and costs associated with transporting petroleum products over long distances.

Ruto said local refining could reduce expenses related to insurance and transportation while providing Kenya with greater access to locally processed fuel.

However, he said the larger economic opportunity would extend beyond the refinery itself. The government plans to develop industries around the facility, including petrochemical, chemical and plastics manufacturing.

The refinery could also provide raw materials for industries producing fertiliser and bitumen, potentially reducing reliance on imports of some petroleum-based products.

The broader development is expected to create opportunities for employment, investment and trade while strengthening Lamu’s position as an industrial and logistics centre.

Ruto said Kenya’s policy would be guided by competitiveness, allowing businesses and consumers to obtain petroleum products from whichever regional facility can supply them efficiently and at favourable prices.

The President maintained that Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania therefore did not need to view their refinery plans through the lens of rivalry.

Instead, he said, multiple facilities could create a larger and more integrated petroleum market capable of serving the needs of East Africa.

World.title: Outrage as KDF officers detain human rights team along Malindi-Lamu highway
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Activists clashed with police at a Gamba roadblock after being stopped en route to Lamu. [Vocal Africa]

Six members of Muslims for Human Rights (MUHURI), including five staff and a board member, were detained by Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) officers along the Malindi-Lamu highway, prompting condemnation from human rights organisations.

The incident occurred on Monday as the team travelled from Lamu to Mombasa after a field mission. The officers reportedly intercepted them between Gamba and Minjila, detained them for about two hours, then released them.

The Kenya Human Rights Commission (KHRC) and MUHURI said the officers covered their faces and refused to identify themselves when the human rights team challenged them.

The five staff members were identified as Francis Auma, Abdulrahman Mwanga, Fredrick Okado, Lathan Yusuf and Mohamed Abdla, while the board member was identified as Khelef Khalifa.

In a joint statement, the two organisations said the officers' actions violated a High Court ruling by Justice Bahati Mwamuye requiring security personnel to wear clearly visible name tags or identifiable service numbers on their uniforms.

The ruling also prohibits security officers from wearing hoods, balaclavas or face masks to conceal their identities.

"We call on the KDF and other security agencies to comply with the court order. Officers who violate the directive should be held accountable and face legal consequences," the joint statement read in part.

The organisations also demanded immediate compliance with a recent court order lifting the dusk-to-dawn curfew that had been imposed for more than a decade along the Minjila-Lamu highway.

They argued that the curfew had created conditions for arbitrary stops, harassment and detention of travellers using the route, citing the detention of the MUHURI team as an example.

The organisations urged security agencies to respect court orders and protect the rights of travellers using the highway.

However, a senior Anti-Terror Police officer aware of the incident told The Standard that the officers from the Border Police Unit (BPU) manning such roadblocks and tactical borders conceal their faces to protect their identities.

"In high-risk areas prone to insurgent or terrorist retaliation, including Kanyoyo in Kitui heading to Garissa, Moyale and Lamu, anonymity is framed as a matter of personal and operational survival," she stated.

World.title: Kalonzo signals at working with Ruto if 2027 poll is free and fair
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County on September 27, 2026. [Clinton Ambujo, Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has signalled that the Opposition could accept the outcome of the 2027 General Election and consider working with President William Ruto if he wins through a free and fair contest.

Speaking at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County, Kalonzo said the political class must commit itself to democratic competition and be prepared to accept the verdict of voters.

“If you beat us, we will have to consider if you have behaved yourself, and if we beat you, we have to look at all these things,” he said.

The Wiper leader also called for stronger democratic institutions, warning against political confrontation that could deepen divisions in the country.

“We have a nation here. We have to make this country truly democratic. I do not think we have a shortcut,” he said.

Kalonzo used the church service to make a broader appeal for a united and effective Opposition, saying political leaders had a responsibility to work together in the national interest.

“Kenya needs a functional official opposition; one that is united and does not thrive on disunity. As leaders, we have a responsibility to work together and play our part in fixing this nation,” he said.

He said he had remained in the Opposition even when some political allies moved into government.

“I have stood in the opposition all these years. Even when others joined government, my brother Eugene Wamalwa and I remained steadfast, and we will continue to stand firm,” he said.

Kalonzo also turned his attention to Parliament, claiming that the National Assembly had been “captured” and challenging lawmakers in both Houses to exercise their constitutional responsibilities.

“The National Assembly has been captured. Let this message reach every leader in the National Assembly and the Senate: you have the power to change things, not just to complain later,” he said.

He urged legislators to defend the interests of the people who elected them and to put the country ahead of political considerations.

The former Vice President also defended retired President Uhuru Kenyatta against claims that he is financing the Opposition ahead of the 2027 contest.

Kalonzo argued that presidential campaigns have historically relied on networks of political allies and supporters rather than family resources alone.

“But here we are saying, please let Uhuru rest; he is a retired President. Stop saying he is our financier,” he said.

Kalonzo cited previous presidential campaigns involving Uhuru, former President Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga, arguing that major political campaigns require support from friends and associates.

“Even when Uhuru was running for President, or Kibaki and even Raila, no family has enough resources to support a presidential campaign. It is friends who support you,” he said.

He warned that Kenya was at a delicate political moment and urged leaders to avoid actions that could deepen instability.

“We should not allow the country to get to a worse situation than where it is. We are on the edge of a cliff; the country is at a crossroads,” he said.

World.title: Who is Zack Polanski, the ‘eco-populist’ rattling the UK’s establishment?
World.content:
London — The leader of the UK’s Green Party, Zack Polanski, will on Thursday challenge the political establishment by taking on the ruling Labour Party in a special election for the seat held by former prime minister Keir Starmer.

Polanski, with his deep reserve of progressive policies and an active presence on TikTok cuts a markedly different figure to Starmer, who consistently alienated his Labour Party’s left-wing and developed a reputation as a stilted, ineffective communicator.

That contrast helped Polanski and the Greens gain traction as a popular left-wing alternative to the governing, center-left Labour Party, which has been bleeding voters in recent years over its stance on issues like welfare spending, trans rights and the war in Gaza. Polanski even said on more than one occasion that his party “is here to replace Labour.”

But that momentum has largely stalled since Starmer resigned as prime minister in the summer following enormous pressure from his party. He stepped down as a member of parliament (MP) last month, triggering the by-election.

In Starmer’s place, a more formidable opponent has emerged. Andy Burnham, the current prime minister, is widely seen as a better political operator and more capable of appealing to a broad spectrum of voters, including the progressives Polanski has been targeting.

Britain’s new Prime Minister Andy Burnham took office in July. Christopher Furlong/Getty Images

So the outcome of this by-election – in the central London constituency of Holborn and St. Pancras – represents more than just Polanski potentially becoming an MP.

It pits the Greens and Labour directly against each other for the first time since Burnham took office, acting as the first major electoral test for the new government as well as a barometer of the Greens’ ability to compete with a rejuvenated Labour.

If Polanski wins on Thursday, it will be a stern warning for the new prime minister and could be an early indicator that Britain’s left flank has irrevocably split. But if he loses and Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali holds the party’s seat, it will serve as a sign that Burnham has managed to pull progressives back into the Labour Party and slow its electoral decline.

Differing stances over the war in Gaza and antisemitism are central to that split, and to this by-election. Many Muslim voters have said they will not vote Labour because they think the government has not acted strongly enough over Gaza.

This weekend, the Greens adopted a controversial motion classifying Zionism, which Jewish groups sometimes define as a right to Jewish self-determination, as a form of racism, calling it an “ethnonationalist political project.”

Polanski, who is Jewish and changed his name from David Paulden when he was 18 to honor that heritage, did not vote on the motion nor mention it in his speech to the conference. He describes himself as an “anti-Zionist.” Israel responded by banning Polanski from visiting the country.

On Wednesday, a fresh storm broke out in British media over a reported friendship between the Green Party member who proposed the motion and a man convicted in the United States on al Qaeda terrorism charges.

Any split in the left comes at a critical moment in British politics, with Labour (and the Greens) also focused on containing a rising right-wing wave, most clearly signaled by the rapid ascent of the hard-right populist party, Reform UK.

Who is Polanski?

A self-described “eco-populist,” Polanski, 43, was catapulted onto the national stage last fall when he secured a surprise victory in the Greens’ leadership election, beating two of the party’s four MPs to claim the top job. Before that, he was still a little-known local politician, representing the Greens in the London Assembly.

The broad brushstrokes of Polanski’s image go something like this: to his admirers, he is an antidote to the stiff technocratic tendencies of more mainstream politicians; a gifted communicator willing to adopt the bold left-wing policies Labour has largely shied away from.

To his detractors, he is vague and unable to pin down the details of his own policies.

More recently, his social media use sparked controversy after he criticized the police’s response to an antisemitic attack in north London and, in a separate incident, reposted a photo that some interpreted as threatening Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform UK.

Zack Polanski is running to become an MP for the central London constituency of Holborn and St Pancras. Toby Shepheard/AFP/Getty Images

Still, under his leadership, the party has commanded national attention, building on its best general election performance when it secured four parliamentary seats in 2024. By May, the Greens’ rise seemed astronomic – they briefly polled as high as Labour and the center-right Conservatives, the two parties which have dominated British politics for decades, and enjoyed historic gains in spring local elections.

While Polanski has tried to link the climate crisis to other issues, he has largely prioritized immediate everyday concerns, such as the cost of living and suggestions of public ownership of water and other utilities, alongside other progressive initiatives like championing a wealth tax and rent controls, while also adopting a pro-Palestinian stance.

Polanski has claimed credit for pushing Labour further to the left, most recently saying his party was responsible for influencing Labour’s shifting stance on the Middle East, including the government’s recently announced sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Actor turned politician

A former actor, Polanski’s strength lies in his communication. He hosts his own nightclub nights and holds weekly conversations with academics, activists and journalists on his podcast “Bold Politics” on ideas like an extreme wealth line (a proposed globally agreed limit for an individual’s net worth), re-nationalizing water companies and rejoining the European Union.

But he is prone to slip-ups too – in one disastrous interview shortly after becoming leader he seemed to confuse the national debt and deficit. Months later, he more carefully laid out his economic policy at a left-wing think tank event, though it remains “vague,” said Laura Serra, a political scientist at the London School of Economics.

“People don’t really know what they (the Greens) stand for, what they’re going to do,” she added.

While Polanski’s almost constant media presence has given him a far higher profile than previous Green leaders, analysts argue that the party’s increasing popularity has less to do with him and more to do with the shifting political climate in the UK.

A Green Party sign displayed outside a house. Carl Court/Getty Images

And at the same time, Green parties across Europe have become more influential, propelled by growing support among recent graduates and benefiting from “changing societal cleavages,” said James Dennison, a political scientist at the European University in Florence, who has studied the Greens for more than a decade. “The change is more rapid in the UK, and it’s exaggerated partially because of the electoral system, so it takes them longer to break through, and when they do, they go faster.”

Polanski self-consciously forms part of a wider populist trend too; he describes his approach to messaging as “substance with clickbait” and an alternative designed directly to confront the right-wing populism of Reform, and its Trump-supporting leader Nigel Farage.

“Populism is about the 99%, the vast majority… against the very, very wealthy… Trump and Farage come from the 1% and want to protect the interests of the elite,” Polanski told Bloomberg earlier this year.

This simultaneous rise of the Greens and Reform could fracture Britain’s political landscape, in which the first-past-the-post electoral system typically favors two or three major parties.

So, regardless of who wins on Thursday, the Greens even being competitive in a traditional Labour stronghold like this is indicative of how the smaller, more radical parties are increasingly challenging the mainstream.

World.title: What is pneumonic plague and how dangerous is it?
World.content:
A 28-year-old lab researcher at a Russian institute dedicated to studying plague and dangerous pathogens died of pneumonia of an “unknown” origin.

The Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute operates in Siberia, where several other people are quarantined. Rospotrebnadzor, the Russian agency that oversees infectious disease, has downplayed the link between the researcher’s death and her work, but the case has prompted questions about the type of plague that causes pneumonia.

The US State Department and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said they are monitoring the situation closely. The World Health Organization said Monday it’s in contact with Russian health authorities to verify what happened, what testing is underway and any potential international public health implications.

“Based on unofficial information available, the public health risk to the general population appears to be low,” a WHO spokesperson said, adding that its risk assessment would be updated once more information was available.

What is pneumonic plague?

Pneumonic plague is a rare, deadly lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. Scientists consider pneumonic plague the most dangerous form of the infection.

There are other forms of plague stemming from Y. pestis that attack different parts of the body.

The most common form, bubonic plague, often develops after a flea bite or when the bacterium enters through a cut or break in the skin. The infection triggers swollen, painful lymph nodes and can progress to septicemic plague.

Septicemic plague infects the bloodstream, potentially leading to organ failure, it can also come directly from a flea bite.

Pharyngeal plague attacks the throat after someone eats infected meat.

The bacteria Yersinia pestis causes plague, including the most common, bubonic plague, which typically results from the bite of an infected flea. Pneumonic plague is the most serious form of the illness. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Getty Images

How is pneumonic plague transmitted?

Pneumonic plague is the only form of the bacterial infection that passes directly from person to person. Respiratory particles carry it when a person coughs or sneezes. Droplets from infected animals can also transmit it.

The last documented person-to-person transmission of pneumonic plague in the United States dates back to 1924, during an outbreak in Los Angeles.

What are pneumonic plague symptoms?

With pneumonic plague, particles lodge in the lungs and can trigger severe pneumonia, making breathing difficult. Symptoms can begin within 24 hours of infection.

Other symptoms include fever, chills, headache, body aches, dizziness, weakness, fatigue, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.

Without treatment, it is nearly always deadly.

How is pneumonic plague treated?

Doctors can treat plague with at least 10 to 14 days of antibiotics. Most commonly they use ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, gentamicin, and streptomycin. Patients that get antibiotics within the first 24 hours of infection have the best chance of surviving.

Doctors may also support someone with supportive care and provide supplemental oxygen, fluids and encouragement to rest.

Is there a vaccine for plague?
