World.title: Chongwe attributes high number of cholera cases to poor sanitation
World.content:
Chongwe District Health Office has attributed the high number of cholera cases recorded in Ngwerere area to inadequate supply of clean water and poor sanitation practices.

District Director for Health Services, Morton Zuze has stated that residents, especially those residing in Sylvia Masebo Compound have continued drawing unclean water from shallow wells for household use despite efforts by government and some stakeholders to enhance water supply to the area.

Speaking during an epidemic preparedness, prevention, control and management meeting in Chongwe, Dr Zuze noted that poor sanitation practices have also contributed to the spread of the disease in the area.

He indicated that out of the 31 cholera cases that the district has recorded, 21 were recorded from Ngwerere.

Dr Zuze however, added that the District Health Office, with support from various stakeholders have put up some surveillance mechanisms and preventive measures to eradicate the further spread of the disease in the area and other parts of Chongwe.

“We have been disinfecting and testing water from shallow wells, hotspot areas and a number of Public places such as markets, and we are also distributing chlorine in areas where we have recorded cholera cases,” he explained.

He further indicated that residents have been sensitised on the importance of keeping their surroundings clean as well as drinking clean safe water.

Dr Zuze also expressed concern over inadequate sanitation facilities such as toilets in the Meanwood Kwamwena area where four Cholera cases have been recorded.

He noted that most caretakers are residing in unfinished structures which have no water supply and toilets resulting in rampant open defecation.

He stated that his office would soon engage homeowners in the area to find a lasting solution to address the challenge.

Meanwhile, Chongwe District Administration Officer, Evaristo Kayaya, who chaired the meeting, called for concerted efforts from stakeholders in the district to partner with the Government to promote a coordinated response towards the fight against cholera in the District.

Mr Kayaya urged stakeholders in the District to render any relevant assistance to the District Health Office to support the cholera response activities it is undertaking.

“The fight against cholera in Chongwe is not the responsibility of the District Health Office alone, therefore, let us use a coordinated approach by assisting this office in any way we can to prevent any further spread of the disease and save lives,” he said.

World.title: Civil Servants to train through NIPA controller
World.content:
All government employees, including Internal Auditors across the Civil Service, will going forward undergo mandatory training and certification through the National Institute of Public Administration (NIPA), in line with government policy.

Ministry of Finance and National Planning, Controller of Internal Audit, Jamie Mukuwa, says Public Service Management Division Circular No. B4 of 2026, issued on July 16th 2026, directs that NIPA will train all public service employees under the Public Service Competence Development and Certification Strategy.

Ms Mukuwa said Controlling Officers and Heads of Internal Audit Units are expected to plan and budget for the training accordingly, while Human Resource Development Officers are encouraged to factor internal audit training in their annual submissions.

She was speaking when she officially opened the five day Internal Audit training in Lusaka today.

Ms Mukuwa said the audit profession matters in the public sector because weak internal controls do not simply show up on a balance sheet, but in the lives of citizens.

She said a standardised training pathway means every internal auditor in government, whether in a line ministry, a province or an agency, is working from the same standards, the same rigor and the same understanding of what quality assurance looks like.

She explained that such consistency is what will allow Audit Committees, Permanent Secretaries and ultimately the public to trust internal audit findings wherever they originate and will make the profession stronger and more credible.

Ms Mukuwa said his expectation after the training is an internal audit function that produces technically correct reports and acts as a trusted advisor in various institutions.

“What we need is auditors who can identify the risks that genuinely threaten service delivery and value for money, communicate them in a language that compels action, and follow through until recommendations are actually implemented, not merely noted,” she said.

She said Zambia’s development story will be judged not only by the targets it sets, but by how credibly those targets are pursued and reported on, adding that strong, independent internal audit is part of what makes that story believable.

Ms Mukuwa said this is in line with the Grow Zambia Agenda under President Hakainde Hichilema’s second term, urging internal auditors to ensure their mandates align to the 10-10-5-3-3-1-1-1 agenda in their respective work environments.

Public Service Management Division (PSMD) Permanent Secretary Lois Mulube said competence must be built with intent, certified against a clear standard and refreshed continuously.

“A well-written strategy executed by an undertrained workforce delivers disappointing results regardless of how sound the strategy was on paper,” Ms Mulube said.

She said the Competence Development and Certification Strategy is therefore an implementation tool for everything the government is trying to achieve, designed to close the gap between what is planned and what is actually capable of being delivered.

Ms Mulube said under the strategy, mandatory training follows officers throughout their career including pre-deployment training for newly appointed officers, in-service training, preparation for entry into senior management and structured support as officers approach retirement, alongside sector specific Continuous Professional Development for specialised functions such as internal audit.

Meanwhile, Institute of Internal Auditors Zambia (IIA) Zambia President Lubinda Namiluko said economic growth cannot be sustained without strong institutions, sound governance and effective systems of internal control.

Mr Namiluko stated that internal audit has a critical role to play in supporting Government’s Grow Zambia Agenda by strengthening governance, risk management and control environment within both public and private sectors.

World.title: Mbala electoral officer praises political parties
World.content:
Mbala District Electoral Officer, Laura Munkanta has commended political parties in the district for their cooperation ahead of filling in nominations for the Mayoral seat tomorrow.

Ms Munkanta has since encouraged all political parties to ensure that their polling agents are accredited before the end of the day to allow them access to the nomination centre.

The District Electoral Officer said this when she addressed members of the District Liaison Committee during a meeting held at Grasshopper Inn today.

She disclosed that accredited election agents were briefed on Monday to acquaint them with the dos and don’ts of the electoral process.

“I commend all political parties and candidates for maintaining peace during this period, and I urge you to continue adhering to the electoral guidelines as we approach nominations and polling day,” Ms Munkanta said.

“Let us all ensure that our agents are accredited, this will allow them to have access to the nomination centre, and polling stations when that time comes,” she added.

Meanwhile, Ms Munkanta has disclosed that voter education facilitators have been trained and deployed in all the nine wards.

“We are ready for this election, apart from these engagements, i can also confirm that District Voter Education Facilitators have been trained and deployed in all the nine wards,” she said.

The meeting was convened to update key stakeholders, including political party chairpersons, independent candidates and their representatives, on the remaining electoral processes leading up to polling day.

World.title: Mansa Council concerned with underage drinking
World.content:
Mansa Municipal Council has raised concern over the increasing number of underage persons patronising alcohol outlets in the District.

The Local Authority has since advised operators of bars, nightclubs and other liquor-licensed premises to adhere to the Liquor Licensing Act No. 20 of 2018 prohibiting admission of persons under the age of 18 into their premises.

Mansa Municipal Council Public Relations Officer, Joel Kashi warned that the local authority in collaboration with relevant law-enforcement and regulatory stakeholders has intensified inspections and enforcement operations against outlets admitting or employing underage persons.

“The growing trend of underage persons accessing drinking places and nightclubs is a serious concern, not only because it contravenes the law, but also exposes young people to environments and activities that may negatively affect their safety, wellbeing and development,” Mr Kashi said.

Mr Kashi stated that operators are compelled to verify the age of patrons and employees and ensure that their businesses do not expose underage persons to alcohol-related or other illicit activities.

“Bar and nightclub owners who deliberately disregard the law should expect enforcement action, depending on the nature and severity of the offence, offenders may face fines, closure of premises, revocation of liquor licences and imprisonment upon conviction, as provided for under the applicable legal framework,” he said.

The Council has since called on parents and guardians to play their part by monitoring the movements and activities of children, particularly during evening and night hours and to report establishments suspected of allowing underage persons to patronise their premises.

“Mansa Municipal Council remains committed to promoting a safe, orderly and responsible environment for all residents. The Council will not relent in enforcing laws and regulations designed to protect children and maintain public order within the District,” Mr Kashi said.

World.title: FODEP calls for intensified voter education in Mbala
World.content:
The Foundation for Democratic Process (FODEP) in Mbala District has called on voter education facilitators to intensify the voter education activities ahead of the forthcoming Mayoral by-election.

Foundation for Democratic Process Mbala District Chairperson, Bright Sikanyika says it is important that voter education is intensified given the low voter turnout that was recorded during the just-ended general elections in the district.

He has expressed concern that voter apathy may worsen during the by-election if voter education facilitators do not adequately engage the electorate and provide timely information.

He has described voter education facilitators as frontline workers in the electoral process and should ensure that they effectively discharge their duties.

Mr Sikanyika advised that the voter education campaign should focus on the importance of voting as a right of every eligible citizen, while also encouraging voters to correctly mark their ballots to minimise the number of rejected votes.

“Voter education facilitators should reach as many eligible voters as possible and ensure that the electorate is well informed,”

“The just ended general election was characterised by voter apathy, we need to avoid that now and Voter Education facilitators are key as they are frontline people to ensure every voter votes in the by election,” he added.

Meanwhile, a check by the media this morning at the Civic Centre in Mbala found that the deployment of voter education facilitators was underway.

World.title: Mwanakampwe urges civic leaders to curb corruption
World.content:
Central Province Permanent Secretary Milner Mwanakampwe has urged civic leaders to stamp out corruption and other illegalities in local authorities to contribute to the Grow Zambia Agenda.

Dr Mwanakampwe said local authorities have continued to be breeding grounds for corruption and illegal land allocation.

He was speaking during the installation ceremony of Gary Domingo as Kabwe Mayor, at the Civic Centre.

“The Grow Zambia Agenda should be at the centre of the Councils’ operations. There shouldn’t be a party agenda in the councils but development for the benefit of the people,” he said.

Dr Mwanakampwe urged the local authorities to work closely with the Central government in driving the development agenda in line with the Decentralisation Policy.

He called for transparency and accountability in the utilisation of public resources.

The Permanent Secretary emphasised that issues of land distribution should also be done with honesty and in public interest.

“The role of civic leaders is to provide visionary leadership beyond partisan lines,” he said.

Dr Mwanakampwe urged residents of Kabwe to support the Kabwe Municipal Council by keeping their respective areas clean and paying property rates and business levies.

In his acceptance speech, Kabwe Mayor Gary Domingo pledged to anchor his leadership on transparency, unity and service delivery.

“In the next five years, we will focus on delivering a clean environment. A clean town is a productive town. We will work on upgrading the market, issues of sanitation and improving service delivery to the people. We will also make Kabwe attractive private sector investments,” he said.

Meanwhile, Kabwe Town Clerk reaffirmed the council’s commitment to supporting the council.

“As management, we remain committed to providing the necessary technical support to the new mayor and other councillors to advance the government’s development agenda for the benefit of the people of Kabwe,” he said.

World.title: Africa: U.S. Backs Stronger AU-UN Role in Africa Conflicts, Supports UN Financing for AU-Led Missions
World.content:
Nairobi — The United States has backed a stronger African Union-United Nations partnership to address conflicts across the continent, saying a UN framework for financing AU-led peace operations could provide a useful tool in responding to Africa's security crises.

U.S. Representative for UN Management and Reform Ambassador Jeffrey Bartos told the Security Council that closer AU-UN coordination was particularly important in Sudan, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and the Sahel, where conflicts and militant violence continue to threaten regional stability.

"Coordination and partnership between the UN and AU can help achieve peace, security, and prosperity in Africa," Bartos said.

Washington specifically pointed to UN Security Council Resolution 2719, which provides a framework for UN financing of Security Council-authorised, AU-led peace support operations.



Bartos said such missions could strengthen the AU's role in resolving conflicts on the continent while drawing on UN support and resources.

"The deployment of a peace operation under UNSCR 2719 will strengthen the AU-UN partnership and leverage the AU's comparative advantages to addressing conflict in Africa," he said.

The United States, however, said the mechanism should be applied selectively, with any operation kept small, time-bound and focused on clearly defined objectives.

Washington said it would assess on a case-by-case basis where the framework could be most effectively used.

The remarks come as the AU and UN seek closer coordination over some of Africa's most persistent conflicts.

On Sudan, the United States called for an immediate end to the fighting and backed efforts by the AU and UN, alongside other members of the Quintet, to promote an inclusive political dialogue.

Bartos also said the United States was considering measures to support efforts to end the Sudan conflict, including expanding the existing Darfur arms embargo to cover the whole country.

On eastern DRC, he said the AU and UN should continue supporting U.S.- and Qatar-led peace efforts aimed at ending the conflict.

The United States also condemned terrorist attacks, including drone attacks, in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, saying African leadership and AU-UN cooperation were essential to confronting insecurity in the Sahel and West Africa.

World.title: Somalia: Somalia Says Al-Shabab Amniyat Chief Killed in Nisa Operation
World.content:
Mogadishu — Somalia's intelligence agency said a former head of al-Shabab's Amniyat security wing was killed in a planned operation carried out with international partners in the southern town of Jilib.

The National Intelligence and Security Agency, or NISA, identified the man as Bashir Ahmed Haji Nunow and said he was killed during the operation on Oct. 1, 2026.

NISA said Nunow led the militant group's Amniyat unit between 2016 and 2024. The agency said he operated under several aliases, including Geescadde, Fanax, Gardhuub and Ali Dheere.



The agency accused Nunow of playing a senior role in planning and carrying out attacks against Somali civilians. It specifically linked him to several major attacks in Mogadishu, including the Oct. 14, 2017, bombing at the Soobe intersection.

NISA also attributed the Ex-Control Afgooye attack and the attack known as Soobe 2 to Nunow, along with assaults targeting hotels and other locations around Mogadishu's Lido Beach.

The agency said the operation formed part of a wider campaign to pursue senior al-Shabab figures accused of directing attacks and maintaining the networks used to organise militant operations.

NISA said the killing could disrupt al-Shabab's leadership and the networks responsible for planning and executing attacks. It did not provide details on how Nunow was killed or whether other people were killed or wounded in the operation.

Al-Shabab, an al-Qaida-linked militant group, has waged an insurgency in Somalia for more than a decade and continues to carry out attacks despite military operations by Somali forces and their international partners.

The Somali government has increasingly focused on targeting the group's senior leadership and disrupting its command, intelligence and financial networks as part of efforts to weaken the insurgency.

World.title: Africa: How Africa Can Capture More Value From Its Cotton
World.content:
column

As World Cotton Day approaches on 7 October, Africa has an opportunity to consider how its cotton industry can contribute more to agricultural development, employment and economic growth. The opportunity extends far beyond producing and exporting raw cotton.

Africa's cotton industry has significant potential to support agricultural development, employment and economic growth. Yet the opportunity extends far beyond producing and exporting raw cotton.

Building a stronger, more resilient sector requires attention to the entire value chain – from farmers and ginneries through to spinning, textile manufacturing, clothing and, ultimately, consumers.

South Africa's experience offers practical lessons in supporting farmers, promoting sustainable production, protecting fibre quality and strengthening links between growers and downstream users.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

A strong cotton value chain starts with farmers who can produce consistently, sustainably and profitably. Farmer development must therefore go beyond access to seed and markets. Training, mentorship, technical support and knowledge-sharing can strengthen both production and business management.

South African cotton farmer Frans Malela illustrates what can be achieved when these opportunities are combined with determination and a willingness to learn. Malela began farming in 1984 on four hectares while working full-time in Johannesburg. He later moved into commercial cotton production, expanding his operation to more than 200 hectares.

His practices include crop rotation, soil management, integrated pest management, good harvesting practices and field hygiene. His yields increased from approximately 800 kg of seed cotton per hectare to 1.2 tonnes, reaching an exceptional three tonnes per hectare in 2021/22.

Malela also shares his experience through farmers' days, demonstrations and research trials, while his operation provides seasonal employment for approximately 40 people. His story shows how farmer development can improve productivity and fibre quality while spreading knowledge and creating employment within farming communities.

Sustainability and fibre quality go hand in hand

Sustainability is increasingly important throughout global agricultural and textile supply chains. Good agricultural practices are also fundamental to producing consistent, high-quality fibre.

Cotton fibre characteristics such as length, strength and micronaire – a measure reflecting fineness and maturity – directly influence spinning performance and fabric quality. Production, harvesting, storage and ginning practices therefore affect the value of cotton lint.

Cotton SA's South African Cotton Standard (ZACS) provides a practical framework for responsible production, bringing together farm management, environmental stewardship, people and economic viability.

Good agricultural practices support fibre quality from the beginning of the crop cycle. Appropriate land preparation and timely planting encourage uniform development. Locally adapted cultivars, effective weed and pest management, and appropriate nutrient and crop protection programmes support mature, strong fibre.

Quality protection continues during and after harvesting. Clean picking, appropriate storage and careful transport help prevent contamination and moisture damage. Clean ginneries and well-maintained equipment further minimise contamination and mechanical damage.

Sustainability, quality and profitability should therefore be pursued together. Good practices can protect natural resources, improve fibre quality and strengthen the commercial value of the crop.

Making sustainability measurable

ZACS shows how sustainability principles can be translated into a structured, measurable process.

The standard rests on four pillars – Management, Environment, People and Socio-economic – covering continuous improvement, water stewardship, soil health, responsible crop protection, labour practices, worker protection, economic viability and resilience.

Participants complete a self-assessment, followed by an internal review and a farm or ginnery visit. External verification takes place before certification, providing a mechanism to monitor performance and encourage improvement.

The programme is being tested under South African cotton production conditions through a three-year pilot. Malela has joined as a leader farmer, contributing to discussions and sharing his crop rotation system with other smallholder farmers.

For Africa, ZACS offers an example of how locally relevant standards can turn sustainability objectives into practical action at farm level.

Connecting farmers to the textile industry

Another major opportunity lies in strengthening links between cotton production and downstream textile manufacturing.

Producing more cotton does not automatically mean retaining more economic value within a country or the continent. When cotton is exported as lint and processed elsewhere, much of the value generated through spinning, textile production, garment manufacturing and retail is captured outside the producing country.

South Africa has experienced this challenge, highlighting the need to develop capacity beyond the farm gate. Initiatives such as the South Africa Cotton Mark show how locally produced cotton can be connected more visibly to manufacturers, retailers and consumers, supporting efforts to retain more value locally.

The processing gap is particularly pronounced in West and Central Africa. The World Trade Organization reported in March 2026 that around 98% of cotton from the region is exported as raw fibre, highlighting the opportunity to expand regional processing and manufacturing.

Close 

Retaining more value within Africa

Capturing this opportunity requires investment in spinning, weaving, knitting, dyeing, finishing and garment manufacturing, alongside the infrastructure, skills, finance and markets needed to make these industries competitive.

Regional cooperation could allow countries to develop complementary strengths, rather than each establishing every stage of the value chain independently.

Value addition must also benefit farmers. Stronger relationships between growers and downstream users, quality-based incentives, sustainability premiums, traceability and longer-term supply arrangements can help ensure that benefits reach producers.

There is no single solution to strengthening Africa's cotton sector. Farmer development, sustainability, fibre quality, processing capacity, manufacturing and market access are interconnected.

South Africa's experience shows the value of bringing these elements together: supporting farmers, applying practical sustainability standards and connecting local cotton with manufacturers and consumers.

The journey from farm to fashion is an opportunity to strengthen African agriculture, create employment, develop skills and ensure that a greater share of the value generated by Africa's cotton remains within the continent.

Erica Vogel is Senior Quality Control Officer at Cotton SA.

World.title: South Sudan: South Sudan Rejects Claims of Foreigners' Expulsion Order
World.content:
Nairobi — South Sudan has moved to dispel reports that foreigners have been given seven days to leave the country, with Juba County Caretaker Commissioner Kalisto Lado Faustino Nyigilo saying the government remains open to legally resident foreigners but wants them to stay out of small-scale retail businesses.

Lado made the clarification on Tuesday following reports circulating on social media claiming that he had ordered foreign nationals to leave South Sudan.

He said the reports were false and that he did not have the authority to expel foreigners from the country.

"The Commissioner has never said that, and it's even not the mandate of the Commissioner to actually evacuate people or to send people out of South Sudan," Lado said.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said South Sudan welcomes foreigners who enter the country legally for business, residence, humanitarian work and other legitimate activities.

"Our policy is welcoming. We are welcoming everybody from any country who want to come to be with us in South Sudan," he said.

However, Lado maintained his position that foreign nationals should avoid small-scale retail trade in Juba, including boda boda operations and the sale of everyday food items.

He said foreigners should instead invest in wholesale businesses, companies, factories and other ventures capable of creating jobs for South Sudanese.

Lado said his earlier remarks were aimed at protecting economic opportunities for local youth and women rather than discriminating against foreigners.

He questioned the growing involvement of foreign nationals in boda boda operations, asking what opportunities would remain for South Sudanese youth if foreigners dominated the sector.

He similarly raised concern over foreign women engaging in small-scale food vending, including selling chapati, potatoes, onions and tomatoes.

Lado rejected claims that his position amounted to a ban on foreign investment or hostility towards foreigners.

"There is nothing about sending of foreigners out of South Sudan. There is nothing about prohibiting foreigners from business. There is nothing about hating foreigners," he said.

He instead urged foreign investors to bring substantial capital into the country and establish industries and companies that could employ South Sudanese.

Lado also addressed the ongoing removal of roadside businesses and structures in Juba, saying the county was not conducting indiscriminate demolitions.

He said the exercise was intended to clear roads, remove garbage and relocate businesses operating on road reserves to designated areas.

Close 

"We are not demolishing structures. We are organising the road, taking garbage out of the road and sending those who are putting their booths on the road to be in the rightful places," he said.

Lado urged foreigners living in Juba to remain calm, saying those who obey South Sudanese laws had nothing to fear.

"Our foreigners who are here, be peaceful. No fear, no worry, unless if you commit any crime," he said.

World.title: Kenya: The Symbolism Behind Raila Odinga's Pentagon-Shaped Mausoleum
World.content:
Nairobi — The unusual pentagonal shape of the late former Prime Minister Raila Odinga's mausoleum at Kango ka Jaramogi in Bondo was deliberately chosen to reflect a key symbol associated with his political life.

The Kenya Defence Forces officers involved in guiding President William Ruto and other dignitaries through the facility during its handover to the Odinga family have explained the thinking behind the design.

Samson Malaki said the five-sided structure draws inspiration from the raised fist that became one of the most recognisable gestures associated with Odinga.

According to Malaki, the fist was not intended as a gesture of confrontation, but as a symbol of strength and a call for Kenyans to come together.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said the five fingers of the raised hand informed the decision to adopt a pentagonal form for the mausoleum.

"In as much as he was raising that particular fist, he wasn't raising that fist in defiance, but he was raising that fist to call people to unity. It is five, which represents a pentagon, and it's actually what informed the design of this mausoleum," Malaki explained.

The design also establishes a visual connection between Raila's final resting place and that of his father, the late Jaramogi Oginga Odinga.

While Jaramogi's mausoleum has six sides, the structure housing Raila's remains has five. Mr Malaki said the architects deliberately worked with the two geometric forms to create a sense of continuity between the neighbouring structures.

"The Jaramogi Mausoleum is actually hexagonal in shape. The Raila Mausoleum is pentagonal in shape. And for the purposes of that architectural harmony, we tried to play around with the geometry of Jaramogi Mausoleum, which is hexagonal, and we came up with the Raila Mausoleum, which is pentagonal," he said.

The explanation adds a political dimension to what might otherwise appear to be an architectural choice.

The number five has featured at important moments in Odinga's political journey, most notably during the build-up to the 2007 General Election.

'Pentagon'

The term "Pentagon" became synonymous with the Orange Democratic Movement's senior leadership in the run-up to the 2007 presidential nominations.

It referred to a group of five prominent politicians who were positioning themselves for the party's presidential nomination before the contest at Kasarani.

Odinga eventually secured the ODM ticket, with the other members of the group supporting his presidential campaign as the party entered the 2007 General Election.

Close 

Nearly two decades later, the pentagon has acquired a different meaning at his final resting place.

The symbolism of the five-sided mausoleum, according to its designers, links Mr Odinga's familiar raised-fist gesture with the broader theme of unity that defined much of his political messaging.

The structure therefore serves not only as a burial site but also as an architectural representation of elements associated with his public life.

Its pentagonal form stands alongside Jaramogi's hexagonal mausoleum, creating what the KDF officer described as a deliberate architectural relationship between father and son.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 7, 2026
World.content:
press review

Mali Army Retakes Kidal With Russian Support

Mali's army, backed by Russian paramilitary forces, has retaken the northern town of Kidal after Tuareg separatists announced a "strategic and controlled withdrawal" from the area. The Azawad Liberation Front said its forces withdrew without direct fighting, attributing the move to what it described as the disproportionate use of air power by Russia's Africa Corps. Kidal has long been a stronghold of Tuareg separatists seeking an independent state in northern Mali. It was previously seized by the separatists and an al-Qaeda-linked group. The recapture is being viewed as a symbolic victory for Mali's military government, which has increasingly turned to Russia for military support after distancing itself from France. Analysts said, however, that the development is unlikely to be decisive in the broader fight against jihadist and separatist groups. Human rights organisations continue to accuse both Malian and Russian forces of abuses against civilians.

Anti-Immigrant Protesters Harass Asylum Seekers Queuing at South Africa Office

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Asylum seekers queuing at the Home Affairs Refugee Reception Centre in Durban were harassed by a group of about 15 anti-immigrant vigilantes. Some of the protesters wore masks and carried sticks or knobkerries as they entered the centre's parking area, where they shoved people in the queue and shouted xenophobic insults before police intervened and removed them. The group said it wanted to prevent foreigners from applying for asylum. Members linked to the March and March movement questioned why Home Affairs was assisting refugees when many South Africans still lack identity documents. The confrontation came after Home Affairs reopened the asylum system to new applicants following a Constitutional Court ruling, ending a six-year closure. Hundreds of people had arrived from early morning, with some sleeping outside overnight, but only about 20 applications were processed by the end of the day. Many applicants said the lack of documentation has made it difficult to access services, earn a living and secure basic assistance.

Nigeria's Anti-Graft Agency Opposes Diezani's UK Acquittal Evidence

Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has asked a court to reject former Petroleum Minister Diezani Alison-Madueke's attempt to introduce her recent acquittal by a United Kingdom court as evidence in her legal battle to recover assets forfeited in Nigeria. Alison-Madueke was acquitted in June by London's Southwark Crown Court of bribery charges. This came after British prosecutors accused her of accepting lavish benefits from oil and gas interests seeking favourable treatment and contracts. She is now seeking to rely on that judgment in her Nigerian case. She is arguing that it is relevant to questions surrounding her lack of conviction, due process and the forfeiture of her property. The EFCC argued that the UK proceedings are separate from the Nigerian case and have no bearing on the assets at the centre of the dispute, which it says were forfeited and auctioned under Nigerian court orders. The agency has also accused Alison-Madueke of attempting to broaden the scope of her case through new filings. The court has scheduled the matter for hearing on 11 November.

Namibia Intensifies Response to Foot-and-Mouth Disease Outbreak

Namibia is stepping up measures to contain a foot-and-mouth disease outbreak in the //Kharas Region. President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah warned that the crisis threatens farmers, workers and businesses across the livestock industry. As of 5 October, surveillance teams had inspected more than 29,000 animals on 68 farms, with 127 confirmed cases across 15 farms. The government has introduced movement controls, roadblocks, surveillance, testing and tracing, while plans include creating a containment buffer zone and strengthening veterinary fencing along the borders with Botswana and South Africa. The outbreak has also disrupted Namibia's vital beef export industry, with the European Union temporarily suspending imports of fresh meat from cattle, sheep and goats. The European market accounts for more than 80% of Namibia's beef exports, meaning the suspension could affect thousands of jobs and cause significant financial pressure for farmers and businesses. The government said that it is engaging trading partners to limit the impact while maintaining strict disease-control measures and protecting Namibia's reputation as a reliable meat exporter.

Close 

Ebola Outbreak Leaves Thousands of Children Without Caregivers

The Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is having a devastating impact on children. More than 1,900 have lost one or both parents or been separated from their caregivers since the outbreak was declared in May. UNICEF said that at least 2,017 children had been confirmed with Ebola by 29 September, with 1,062 deaths recorded. Children account for just over a quarter of confirmed cases but around a third of deaths, while the fatality rate among children under five has risen to about 70%. UNICEF said that many children are dying before the disease is detected or before they reach treatment centres. The organisation is supporting nurseries near Ebola treatment centres, where babies and young children can receive food, care, monitoring and rapid medical attention while their parents are treated or after losing caregivers. UNICEF is calling for such services to be expanded to all treatment centres. Meanwhile, neighbouring Kenya has confirmed its first Ebola case and death. The World Health Organization believes it was likely imported from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

World.title: Kenya: Nairobi Hospital Says Ebola Patient Was Isolated From Main Facility
World.content:
Travelers being screened for the Ebola virus at the Kenyan border (file photo)

Nairobi — The Nairobi Hospital has moved to reassure patients and staff that its operations remain normal after the death of a patient who tested positive for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease.

The patient died at the hospital on Monday evening, two days after being admitted to its isolation facility, the hospital said in a statement issued Tuesday.

The facility said the patient was managed by a dedicated clinical team in coordination with the Ministry of Health, but declined to disclose further details about the deceased in keeping with patient privacy.

The hospital said its Ebola isolation unit is physically separated from the main hospital and has a dedicated entrance, access route and staff.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"There is no shared clinical space with the main hospital, which has remained fully operational throughout," the hospital said.

It added that emergency services, maternity, theatres, wards and outpatient services were continuing normally.

The hospital said infection prevention and control measures remained in place, with patients presenting an infectious disease risk identified through screening and managed under controlled isolation protocols.

Staff involved in the patient's care worked while wearing full protective equipment and under supervision, the hospital said.

It further said all identified contacts were being monitored in coordination with the Ministry of Health for the required 21-day period.

The hospital said it would continue working with the Ministry of Health and other public health authorities and would implement any additional measures recommended by the government.

The statement comes as health authorities intensify contact tracing following Kenya's confirmation of its first imported Bundibugyo Ebola case.

The patient had travelled into Kenya after spending time in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where the outbreak was first reported, before travelling through Uganda and eventually arriving in Nairobi.

Health authorities are tracing people who may have come into contact with the patient, including healthcare workers and passengers who travelled on the same flight.

The Nairobi Hospital sought to reassure the public that the facility remains safe and operational.

"We want to reassure our patients, families, staff and the wider public that the hospital remains open, safe and fully operational, with appropriate measures in place to protect everyone who comes through our doors," the hospital said.

World.title: Zimbabwe: Mnangagwa Declares State of Disaster As 8,500 Homes Lose Roofs in Masvingo Hailstorm
World.content:
PRESIDENT Emmerson Mnangagwa has declared a State of Disaster following a severe hailstorm that hit Masvingo on Monday, leaving thousands of homes and infrastructure damaged.

The hailstorm caused extensive destruction across residential areas, public utilities, education and health institutions, as well as commercial establishments.

Preliminary assessments indicate that about 8,500 households had their roofs completely blown off, while 90% of the 17,000 households assessed had shattered windowpanes, leaving families exposed at the start of the rainy season.



Several major institutions were severely affected, including Great Zimbabwe University's Mucheke Campus, Masvingo Polytechnic, Masvingo Teachers College, Maud Muzenda Training Centre, the Passport Office, Grain Marketing Board, Chiefs Hall, Veterinary Office, District Development Coordinator's Office, ZIMRE Building, Masvingo Urban VTC, Runyararo Clinic Maternity Ward, Rujeko Hall, 4.1 Brigade, Masvingo Airport and the ZEC Provincial Office.

Business operations in Masvingo City were also disrupted, with major retail and hospitality outlets suffering roof damage, severe leaks and damage to assets.

The storm also extensively damaged electricity infrastructure, with ZESA power lines brought down.

The resulting power outages have affected water pumping systems, municipal drainage and sewer networks, creating an immediate public health risk.

Garwe said government had mobilised all available resources and called on government agencies to assist affected communities.

He also made an urgent appeal to the private sector and development partners to join government in relief efforts.

"The Government remains fully committed to ensuring that no person and no place is left behind as we rebuild and restore normalcy," he said.

Government said assessments were continuing, while relief interventions were being rolled out to affected communities.

World.title: Reddit thread on life cheat codes goes viral with advice on fitness, sleep and compound interest
World.content:
Reddit is popping with an entertaining thread about cheat codes for life.

It's been a minute since we dived into the Reddit bucket here at OutKick. I guess all the geo-political events around the world have been dominating my attention.

For those of you who might not be familiar with Reddit, it's truly one of the final untamed frontiers of the internet. It's a wild place full of a wide variety of content and discussions.

Some are downright bonkers, and others can be more uplifting. The latter is what brings us here today.

DR OZ REVEALS 3 FREE WAYS TO BOOST YOUR HEALTH — NO MEDICATION REQUIRED

Life cheat codes go viral on Reddit

A Reddit thread titled, "What 'cheat code' for life do you wish you'd discovered earlier?" is putting up big numbers on r/AskReddit.

The responses are all over the place, and will be among the most interesting things you read today. Check out some of the top ones below, and let me know your thoughts at David.Hookstead@outkick.com:

Sleep is the one drug that will increase your quality of life most. Kindness is peak human performance and benefits you as much as the recipient of the kindness.

Learning how to say "No" without giving fake excuse.

No one really is paying that much attention. If they are it’s short lived, so do what you want that makes you happy.

Working out 3-5 times a week not only makes you stronger. It helps mentally, prevents injury, makes you feel good, boosts your confidence and so on. It's the best damn thing you can do.

Filling my sock drawer with all the same socks.

The best way to get a raise is to get a job at a different company.

EVERYTHING is easier if you are physically fit and in shape.

Compound interest. I would have started saving for my retirement with my first paycheck if I really understood the benefits of early regular investing and time.

Done is better than perfect.

Stop caring so much about what other people think of you. Invest more in your home—even if you’re only renting. Turn it into a space so comforting, beautiful, and you that you actually want to stay in all the time.

Consistency beats motivation. Small actions repeated every day usually achieve more than occasional bursts of effort when you feel inspired.

Don’t drink your calories

Compound interest/low risk investing.

This is your life and you are living it. Things aren’t going to magically change; no one is coming to save you. If you want changes in your life, you have to do it yourself. Stop waiting.

You can just say "no" when people ask you to do things you don't want to. This even works at work!

Sleep… THE wonder drug that’s free, yet somehow still under-prescribed.

Rest is important as hard work.

No one’s coming to save you.

You can be happy alone and should be able to be happy alone or you're not really happy.

So much of life really comes down to getting enough sleep, getting some exercise, eating health, and interacting with people outside your home or workplace.

Eat healthy, exercise daily.

Knowing which battles are worth fighting and which ones are just causing you (or someone else) stress for no real reason.

Having a positive attitude will improve your life.



Overall, lots of interesting advice. I will tell you the single "cheat code" I use in life that is awesome. I turned on the do not disturb setting on my phone about six months ago, and never turned it off. I also turned on the setting where you can't even get through unless you're in my contacts.

It's amazing. Now, I do have a small list of favorites who can ring through in the event of a critical event, but other than that, I get zero notifications for calls, texts, social media or anything else.

It's honestly nothing short of amazing. One of the best pieces of advice I ever got in life (the person was more successful than me by orders of magnitude) was to limit how accessible you are for people. I was a teenager when I was told that, and I never forgot it.

Unless nukes are in the air, the odds that I need to take any given phone call immediately are hovering barely north of zero percent.

Give it a shot. You might be surprised by how much you enjoy it.

What are your life hacks? Let me know at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

World.title: Holly Madison blasts ‘puppet masters’ for Playboy girlfriends’ feud
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Holly Madison has no problem with reality TV drama – as long as everyone is in on the joke.

The "Girls Next Door" alum told Fox News Digital she would "100%" embrace manufactured conflict on a show like "Real Housewives of Las Vegas," but claimed manipulation by the "puppet masters" behind her former series contributed to lasting rifts among the cast.

For years, Madison had seemingly closed the door on reality television, previously saying she would never return after her experience on "The Girls Next Door." But with time and a different perspective on how manufactured drama could work, she admitted she has reconsidered that hard-line stance.

"You know what, I've changed my thought on that," the Grant a Gift Gala ambassador explained. "I would do manufactured drama if I was in on the joke. I always say that to Bridgette watching 'Girls Next Door,' I'm like, if we knew what the drama was and the three of us were gonna play it out on screen and not take it home with us, so to speak, when the cameras are done rolling, that would have been so much more fun to me than being manipulated from the puppet masters above."

HOLLY MADISON SAYS PLAYBOY MANSION FELT LIKE A 'SAFE HARBOR' AFTER SHE ENCOUNTERED HOLLYWOOD'S DARK SIDE

"Some of us from the cast are still not speaking today because of things like that, so. I would actually do manufactured drama, 100%. I would throw down on like a 'Real Housewives of Las Vegas.' I just don't want to be puppeted again."

The former reality star also pointed to another major difference between the television landscape then and now: the audience.

"Editing's crazy," she noted. "But I also appreciate that viewers are a little more sophisticated now. I mean, back in the 'Girls Next Door' days, they could edit something to be not what it was. And everybody watching was like, 'Nope, that's your character. That's who you are.'"

WATCH: HOLLY MADISON SAYS SHE'D EMBRACE ‘MANUFACTURED DRAMA’ ON REALITY TV UNDER ONE CONDITION

‘DUCK DYNASTY’ STAR SADIE ROBERTSON HUFF ADMITS ‘FEARS’ OVER PUTTING HER KIDS ON REALITY TV

There is one non-negotiable for the former Playboy model.

World.title: Memphis City Council devolves into chaos after data center moratorium vote postponed
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Memphis City Council meeting descended into chaos Tuesday night after lawmakers postponed a vote on a proposed yearlong moratorium on new data centers, as protesters chanted inside City Hall, police cleared the chamber and a fight broke out in the lobby.

The proposal comes as Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI operates its massive Colossus supercomputer facilities in the Memphis area, where some residents have raised concerns about data centers' use of power and water, along with their effects on air quality, noise and nearby neighborhoods.

The council voted 7-5 to delay the moratorium vote until Oct. 20.

ERIC ADAMS BATTLES TENSE CROWD AS WISCONSIN AUDIENCE ERUPTS OVER AI DATA CENTER PROPOSAL

After the vote was postponed, protesters chanted, "This is our city," and, "Show me what democracy looks like," as police moved to clear people from the chamber.

A fight between two women also broke out in the lobby, with video showing punches being thrown, according to Action News 5. A Memphis Police Department spokesperson told the outlet that no one was detained or injured. It was unclear what sparked the fight or whether it was connected to the council meeting.

Council members also clashed during the meeting.

Councilwoman Yolanda Cooper-Sutton exchanged words with protesters before turning her criticism toward Councilman J.B. Smiley Jr., the lead sponsor of the moratorium proposal, according to the outlet.

"That’s all he does; he brings up mess," Cooper-Sutton said of Smiley. "That’s all you do, J.B. Smiley, confuse the people over, over, over and over!"

Smiley had pushed the council to hold the final vote Tuesday, arguing that residents had shown up expecting a decision.

DATA CENTERS COULD BE THE SLEEPER ISSUE OF THE 2026 MIDTERM ELECTIONS

Seven council members voted to postpone the measure, while five opposed the delay. Councilman Edmund Ford Sr. was absent, according to Action News 5.

The proposed ordinance would pause new data center projects for 12 months while the city studies their effects on health and Memphis' power, water and other infrastructure.

Musk's SpaceXAI has established a major computing operation in the Memphis area with its Colossus facilities, raising concerns from some residents about air pollution, noise and the amount of electricity and water needed to run large data centers.

Councilman Jeff Warren, who opposes the moratorium, warned that a year-long pause could push companies to build outside Memphis.

"If we pass a moratorium, there’s no reason for them to think they need to come here," Warren said, according to WREG. "They get the same benefit from going to DeSoto County, Crittenden County, Fayette County, Tipton County."

Memphis Mayor Paul Young has called for more rules governing data centers while also pointing to the tax revenue they generate.

Young said the city should address their water and electricity use, air quality, noise and where the facilities can be built.

"We need to keep the pressure high and make sure that we get the guardrails in place that we need for our community to feel protected," Young told WREG. "There’s a role for all of our agencies to play in ensuring we put the proper guardrails in place. The thing that I want to make sure is that we do it expeditiously."

Smiley said council members should have done more to listen to residents who attended the meeting.

Let’s figure out how we can do what you want, but also what we believe would be in the best interest of the community."

World.content:

FOX News Media CEO Suzanne Scott rang the Closing Bell on Tuesday at Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City as the company celebrates Fox News Channel’s 30th anniversary.

Fox News Channel debuted on Oct. 7, 1996, and original hosts Lauren Green, Trace Gallagher, Steve Doocy and Brit Hume were in attendance, alongside FOX News Media President and Executive Editor Jay Wallace and other 30-year employees who are now at the executive level, to help Scott celebrate three decades since they helped launch the network.

"It's a tremendous honor to be here at Nasdaq as we celebrate a remarkable milestone, 30 years of Fox News," Scott said when delivering remarks before ringing the bell.

LAUREN GREEN: I WAS FOX NEWS CHANNEL'S FIRST ON-AIR HIRE. HERE'S HOW A DREAM BECAME A POWERHOUSE

"Three decades ago, Fox Corporation Chairman Emeritus Rupert Murdoch launched Fox News with an ambitious idea to give audiences another voice in the national conversation and to build a news organization that provided balance to all Americans," Scott continued. "Thirty years later, his vision has grown from one linear network to a multi-platform powerhouse of digital, streaming, audio, books and beyond, made possible by the leadership of Fox Corp Executive Chair and Chief Executive Officer Lachlan Murdoch."

Scott noted that FOX News Media platforms have an enduring connection with the audience and reach over 200 million people on a monthly basis.

"Milestones like this are about recognizing the people behind our success, the journalists, producers, technicians, correspondents, executives, and countless colleagues who show up every day with inspiring skill, energy, determination, and a genuine commitment to their craft," Scott said.

"And they are about the viewers who have welcomed Fox News Channel into their homes, their workplaces, and their daily lives as we meet them wherever they are," Scott added. "So today, as we celebrate 30 years of stories reported and analyzed, and history witnessed at each turn, we also look ahead because the next chapter of media is being shaped right now by new technology, new platforms, and new ways of connecting with audiences."

DANA PERINO: THE UNTOLD STORY OF THE REMARKABLE PEOPLE WHO MAKE FOX NEWS POSSIBLE

Scott, who joined Fox News in its inaugural year of 1996 and was recently inducted into the Broadcasting+Cable Hall of Fame, held several production and creative positions before taking over as CEO in 2018. Under her leadership, Fox News has dominated cable ratings and regularly beats broadcast networks.

"On behalf of everyone at Fox News Media, thank you to all of our viewers and to all of our colleagues who made all of this possible. And now, with great pride and gratitude, we celebrate 30 years of Fox News Channel," Scott said to wrap up her remarks.

'THE FIVE' LEADS CABLE NEWS FOR 20TH STRAIGHT QUARTER AS FOX NEWS OUTDRAWS CNN AND MS NOW COMBINED

Scott was then surrounded by longtime colleagues to officially halt transactions for the day as Fox News-themed red, white and blue confetti rained down.

The iconic Closing Bell, which ends market trading, has been rung by influential figures ranging from Jeff Bezos and Oprah Winfrey to Michael Jordan. Nasdaq Executive Vice President Jeff Thomas presented Scott with a Closing Bell crystal prior to the ceremony, calling FOX News Media "one of the most recognized and influential media brands in the world."

As part of Scott’s ongoing efforts to expand across platforms, Scott launched FOX News Books in 2020 and also spearheaded the brand refresh of FOX News Digital, FOX News Audio and FOX Business. World.title: Rubio to deliver urgent plea to save Western civilization during speech in its birthplace
World.content:

Secretary of State Marco Rubio will deliver a speech in Greece on Wednesday calling for the renewal of Western civilization and urging allies to join the United States in rejecting the decline of the West.

The renewal of the West has been a theme during Rubio's tenure at the helm of the State Department. He has often railed against what he views as an erosion of the values upon which Western civilization was built.

And his speech Wednesday will build on that. The remarks will commence at 11:30 a.m. ET, 6:30 p.m. local time in Greece, and is set in the ancient ruins of the citadel Acropolis.

"Secretary Rubio will deliver an address from the birthplace of Western civilization, where he will call upon Americans and Europeans alike to join together in a great renewal of the Western spirit – an inheritance stretching from Athens and Rome to Christendom to the founding of the American Republic," Dylan Johnson, the State Department's assistant secretary for global public affairs, told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP’S COUNTERTERRORISM STRATEGY SCORES BIG WINS AGAINST GLOBAL TERROR THREATS

"Against the backdrop of the Acropolis, Secretary Rubio will look to the history of ancient Greece as the first full expression of the qualities that would come to define the West: curiosity, courage, ambition, and a restless spirit of exploration and discovery of the unknown," Johnson added.

"He will warn that too much of our civilization has forgotten these essential qualities and urge our allies across the West to join the United States in rejecting decline, defending our shared heritage, and confronting a new era of great-power competition together."

During his visit, Rubio announced a new counterterrorism partnership between the U.S. and Greece.

He emphasized the strategic importance of Greece on Wednesday, calling it a "source of stability in an unstable world."

"As you see a world that faces these destabilizing events, you recognize how important this alliance with Greece is to the United States," Rubio said. "It is a source of stability in an unstable world."

At the Munich Security Conference in Germany in February, Rubio delivered a speech on the topic that earned him a standing ovation from European leaders, and racked up millions of views online. One popular X user described it as "one of the greatest" speeches by a Secretary of State in decades.

Many others insisted the speech upped Rubio's potential 2028 presidential chances.

AS AMERICA MARKS 250 YEARS, OUR GREATEST CHAPTERS ARE STILL AHEAD OF US

Rubio described the five centuries before the end of World War II, a time when the West had expanded across the globe, building "vast empires." But, he said, after the war, Europe was in ruins, and "godless communist revolutions" in Europe caused people to believe that the West's dominance was forever finished.

"Against that backdrop, then, as now, many came to believe that the West's age of dominance had come to an end, and that our future was destined to be a faint and feeble echo of our past. But together, our predecessors recognized that decline was a choice, and it was a choice they refused to make," he said.

AMBASSADOR JEFF BARTOS: UN MUST ABANDON ANTI-AMERICAN, ANTI-WESTERN LEGACY OF DURBAN CONFERENCE

Rubio urged the European leaders to reinvigorate that spirit.

"This is why we do not want out allies to be shackled by guilt and shame," he continued. "We want allies that are proud of our culture and our heritage, and understand that we are heirs to the same great and noble civilization and who together with us, are willing and able to defend it."
