The game promises to be an attractive contest as both the Niners and the Vikings are undefeated through the first four weeks of the season. Tickets range in price from 2,108 pesos (US $177) to 11,656 pesos ($649).

The NFL announced last month that ranchera singer Majo Aguilar and MXKA, an African American singer-songwriter of Mexican descent, will perform the national anthems of Mexico and the United States, respectively.

The halftime entertainment will be supplied by The Warning, a hard rock and alternative rock band formed by three sisters from Monterrey.

With reports from Forbes México, EFE and Aristegui Noticias

World.title: Who Runs South Africa’s Economy, Key Players 2026
World.content:
SOUTH AFRICA · ECONOMY

Key Facts — The country South Africa had 63.5 million people in mid-2026; GDP US$427 billion (2025).

— Who sets the rules Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana; Reserve Bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago.

— What happened The Reserve Bank raised its policy rate to 7.25% from 25 September.

— The players Naspers, Standard Bank, Sasol, Eskom, Transnet; Rupert, Motsepe and Oppenheimer families.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives a 64.6% chance December 2026 inflation exceeds 5.0% (7 October, 8:38 a.m. ET).

— Still open Next rate decision 19 November 2026; local elections on 4 November.

A finance minister, a central banker, two state giants and a few listed companies and families steer South Africa’s money.

The South Africa economy is steered by a small group of players. They are the Treasury, the central bank, two state giants, a handful of listed companies and several wealthy families.

They matter to Americans because the United States bought US$16.5 billion of South African goods in 2025, US Census data show. Several South African companies also list shares in New York.

This guide sets out who controls the money, the mines and the power stations, as of October 2026. Conversions use the Reserve Bank’s rate of R16.61 per US$1 on 7 October 2026.

Treasury and the Reserve Bank Set the Rules

President Cyril Ramaphosa leads the African National Congress (ANC), the party of the anti-apartheid struggle. Since the 2024 election it has governed in a multi-party Government of National Unity.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Kenya confirms first Bundibugyo virus case in Nairobi” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

His record is set out in the Rio Times profile Who Is Cyril Ramaphosa? The coalition’s economic strains are covered in this analysis of unemployment and the November vote.

Enoch Godongwana has been finance minister since 3 July 2024, and held the post from August 2021 to June 2024. He has sat on the ANC’s national executive committee since 1997 and chairs its economic transformation sub-committee.

The National Treasury, which he heads, drafts the budget and manages public debt. His deputies include David Masondo.

The finance minister sets the inflation target in agreement with the Reserve Bank governor. In 2025 the 3% to 6% range used for 25 years gave way to a 3% target, plus or minus one point.

Lesetja Kganyago is governor of the South African Reserve Bank (SARB), whose Monetary Policy Committee sets interest rates. In September 2026 it raised the policy rate by a quarter point to 7.25%, effective 25 September.

The decision was unanimous. The committee pointed to escalating conflict in the Middle East, with little oil getting through the Strait of Hormuz.

It expects headline inflation above 5% in late 2026 and early 2027, then back around 3% towards the end of 2027. The next rate decision is due on 19 November 2026.

Four other ministers matter for business. Kgosientsho Ramokgopa is minister of electricity and energy, and Gwede Mantashe is minister of mineral and petroleum resources.

Parks Tau is minister of trade, industry and competition. Barbara Creecy, the transport minister, oversees policy for railways and ports.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

The Listed Giants on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange

Most of the big private companies below are listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE). How it works is explained in the Rio Times guide to the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

Naspers calls itself a global consumer internet group and one of the largest technology investors and operators in the world. It is the majority owner of Prosus, a separately listed internet group.

Koos Bekker chairs Naspers, and Fabricio Bloisi, formerly head of Brazilian food-delivery firm iFood, has been group chief executive since July 2024. Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa is listed as CEO of Naspers and an executive director.

Two companies holding special A shares, Keerom and Nasbel, together control more than 50% of the votes in Naspers. Naspers calls this its protection structure, meant to keep the group independent.

Sasol calls itself a global chemicals and energy company. Simon Baloyi is president and chief executive, and Muriel Dube chairs the board.

Standard Bank has a presence in 21 sub-Saharan African countries, it says. FirstRand, Absa, Nedbank and Capitec are the other big JSE-listed lenders, all supervised by the SARB’s Prudential Authority.

Mobile operator MTN Group is another heavyweight, explained in the Rio Times guide What Is MTN Group?

Mining From Platinum to Gold

Mining has shaped South Africa’s economy for more than a century. Anglo American was established in 1917 by Ernest Oppenheimer, according to Valterra Platinum’s company history.

Valterra Platinum, the former Anglo American Platinum, was renamed in 2025; its history says its demerger cut Anglo American’s stake to zero. It calls itself one of the world’s leading integrated producers of platinum group metals.

Its mines are in South Africa and Zimbabwe. Craig Miller is chief executive and Norman Mbazima chairs the board.

Sibanye-Stillwater, Gold Fields, Harmony Gold and DRDGold all have shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange, SEC records show.

African Rainbow Minerals (ARM) mines iron ore, manganese ore, chrome ore, platinum group metals, nickel and coal in South Africa. It also makes manganese alloys in Malaysia and holds a stake in Harmony Gold.

Gwede Mantashe’s department oversees mining rights and announces regulated fuel price changes each month. Coal mined in the country also feeds Eskom’s coal-fired power stations.

State Companies Eskom and Transnet

Eskom, the state power utility, is led by group chief executive Dan Marokane, with Mteto Nyati as chair. Ramokgopa has extended Nyati’s term by three years from 1 November 2026, SAnews reported on 25 September.

For years Eskom imposed rolling blackouts, known locally as load-shedding. On 2 October 2026 it said the country had gone 504 consecutive days without them, since 16 May 2025.

Eskom’s energy availability factor, the share of its fleet able to run, was 68.11% from 1 April to 1 October 2026. Diesel spending fell by R4.79 billion (about US$288 million), or 80.49%, on a year earlier.

Its latest annual results are covered in the Rio Times report on Eskom’s profit.

Transnet, the state freight rail and ports company, is led by group chief executive Michelle Phillips, with Andile Sangqu as chair. Its ports include Durban and Richards Bay.

It is opening parts of the network to private operators. In February 2026 it began seeking a private partner for the Richards Bay dry bulk terminal, Mining Weekly reported.

The company’s finances are covered in the Rio Times report on Transnet’s return to profit.

The Families and Tycoons

Johann Rupert, 76, has chaired Remgro since August 2000 and also chairs the luxury group Richemont. Remgro traces its roots to the 1940s, when Anton Rupert founded a tobacco company.

Remgro is now a diversified investment holding company, with interests mainly in healthcare, consumer products, financial services, infrastructure and industry. JJ Durand has been chief executive since May 2012.

Its latest earnings are covered in the Rio Times report on Remgro.

Patrice Motsepe started Future Mining in February 1994, the first step in ARM’s history, the company says. He retired as executive chairman and has been non-executive chairman since 16 February 2026, ARM told the JSE.

Oppenheimer Generations represents the global interests of the Nicky and Jonathan Oppenheimer family. Its ventures include Fireblade Aviation and the Tswalu reserve.

As the Naspers voting structure shows, control often runs through holding companies. That means it is not always visible on share registers.

The South Africa Economy in Numbers

Statistics South Africa estimates the population at 63.52 million in mid-2026. The World Bank puts 2025 gross domestic product at about US$427 billion.

The economy shrank 0.2% in the second quarter of 2026 compared with the first. The SARB still expects a rebound in the second half and growth of 1.2% for the year.

Unemployment stood at 33.6% in the second quarter, so about one in three people in the labour force had no job. Consumer inflation was 4.4% in August 2026.

Food inflation is at its lowest since 2010, thanks to strong harvests and steadier meat prices, the SARB says. Banks’ prime lending rate is 10.75%.

The rand traded at R16.61 per US$1 on 7 October 2026, the SARB’s daily rate shows. The bank called the currency notably resilient throughout the year.

South Africa’s place in the region is covered in South Africa Geopolitics Explained 2026. Daily coverage is collected on the South Africa news page.

What It Means for US Readers

Sasol, Gold Fields, Harmony Gold, Sibanye-Stillwater and DRDGold list shares on the New York Stock Exchange, SEC records show. MTN Group’s US receipts trade over the counter.

The United States imported US$16.5 billion of South African goods in 2025 and exported US$6.3 billion, US Census data show. From January to August 2026, US imports fell to US$7.9 billion, from US$12.5 billion a year earlier.

Since 24 July 2026, most South African goods have faced an extra 12.5% US tariff after a Section 301 trade investigation. The US Trade Representative found South Africa does not effectively ban imports made with forced labour.

Goods already subject to separate US national-security tariffs under Section 232, such as steel and aluminium, are excluded. The 12.5% is charged on top of normal US duties.

For investors, a rate rise and a firm rand cut both ways. Higher rates can draw foreign buyers to government bonds, but they also raise borrowing costs for South African firms.

The government’s 2030 bond yielded 8.18% on 6 October 2026, SARB data show. That is well above the 7.25% policy rate.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a prediction-market platform, runs a market on South Africa’s annual inflation for December 2026. On 7 October at 8:38 a.m. ET, bets priced a 64.6% chance that the rate will exceed 5.0%.

The 4.4% to 4.7% band stood at about 21% on a wide bid-ask spread, the 4.7% to 5.0% band at 13.1%. About US$77,800 had been traded across all bands; at 5:07 a.m. ET, the above-5.0% and 4.7%-to-5.0% bands stood at 65.0% and 17.4%.

The market settles on the Statistics South Africa figure for December, which its rules say is scheduled for 20 January 2027. The SARB’s own forecast also has inflation above 5% around the turn of the year.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the SARB will raise rates again on 19 November. That depends on fuel prices and on how long the supply shock lasts.

The local government elections on 4 November 2026, with special voting from 2 November, could shift the balance inside the coalition. US trade data after August, which would show more of the tariff’s effect, are not yet published.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who runs the South Africa economy?

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana runs fiscal policy under President Cyril Ramaphosa. Reserve Bank Governor Lesetja Kganyago leads the committee that sets interest rates.

What is South Africa’s interest rate?

The Reserve Bank’s policy rate is 7.25%, after a quarter-point rise effective 25 September 2026. Banks’ prime lending rate is 10.75%.

Does South Africa still have power cuts?

Eskom said on 2 October 2026 that the country had gone 504 consecutive days without load-shedding. The run began on 16 May 2025.

Which business families are influential in South Africa?

Johann Rupert chairs Remgro and Richemont, and Patrice Motsepe chairs African Rainbow Minerals. Oppenheimer Generations represents the Nicky and Jonathan Oppenheimer family.

Can Americans invest in South African companies?

Yes, Sasol, Gold Fields, Harmony Gold, Sibanye-Stillwater and DRDGold list shares on the New York Stock Exchange. Most other big firms trade on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

What do prediction markets expect for South African inflation?

On 7 October 2026, Polymarket bets gave a 64.6% chance that December inflation will exceed 5.0%. These are bets, not polls or official forecasts.

Sources: South African Reserve Bank, MPC statement, September 2026; SARB, monetary policy and inflation target; SARB, daily rates of 7 October 2026; Statistics South Africa; National Treasury; South African Government, Enoch Godongwana; SAnews, Eskom board chair; Department of Trade, Industry and Competition; Department of Transport; Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources; Electoral Commission of South Africa; Eskom, 2 October 2026; Eskom, leadership; Transnet, board; Naspers, leadership; Naspers, group structure; Sasol, leadership; Standard Bank Group; Remgro, board; Remgro, history; African Rainbow Minerals; ARM, JSE SENS announcement, 16 February 2026; Valterra Platinum, company profile; Valterra Platinum, leadership; Oppenheimer Generations; US SEC, company tickers and exchanges; USTR Section 301 notice, Federal Register; US Census Bureau, trade with South Africa; World Bank, South Africa; Mining Weekly (all accessed 7 October 2026).

World.title: Mexico Population and Ethnic Groups Explained
World.content:
MEXICO · POPULATION

Key Facts — The country Mexico had 130.9 million residents in October 2025, INEGI estimates.

— The numbers Median age 32; growth 0.7% a year since 2020.

— The groups 18.6% identify as indigenous, 1.6% as Afro-Mexican (2025).

— What happened INEGI published its 2025 Intercensal Survey on 22 September 2026.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives a 3% chance Claudia Sheinbaum leaves office by 31 December (7 October, 8:38 a.m. ET).

— Still open Official CONAPO projections do not yet reflect the new count.

INEGI’s 2025 count shows a Mexico of 130.9 million people that is growing slowly, ageing fast and far from uniform.

The Mexico population reached 130.9 million in October 2025, according to INEGI, the national statistics institute. That is 4.9 million more than the 2020 census found, but growth has slowed to 0.7% a year.

For US readers, Mexico matters as the birthplace of nearly a quarter of US immigrants and as a factory partner. This guide covers size, age, cities, groups, migration and coexistence; daily news is in the Rio Times Mexico section.

How Big Is the Mexico Population in 2026

The latest official count is the 2025 Intercensal Survey, a very large sample rather than a full census. INEGI interviewed a sample of more than 7.3 million homes between 6 October and 14 November 2025.

It estimated 130,911,314 residents as of 15 October 2025. Of these, 130.4 million lived in private homes and just over 517,000 in collective dwellings such as institutions.

Yesterday’s subject line: “Mexico sells record US$60.6bn to the US in August” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

The last full count, the March 2020 census, found 126,014,024 people. INEGI then ranked Mexico the world’s 11th most populous country, below Japan and above Ethiopia.

CONAPO, the government’s National Population Council, still ranked Mexico 11th in July 2026, with almost 133 million people. That projection predates INEGI’s new survey, which points to a somewhat smaller population.

Households are getting smaller. INEGI counted 39.7 million occupied private dwellings in 2025, with an average of 3.3 occupants, down from 3.6 in 2020.

At the 2020 census the most populous state was the State of Mexico, which wraps around the capital, with 16,992,418 people. Colima, on the Pacific coast, was the smallest with 731,391.

In 2025 Mexico City itself had 9.2 million residents and Jalisco, home to Guadalajara, had 8.7 million, INEGI’s state results show.

An Ageing Country With Fewer Births

Half of all Mexicans were 32 or younger in 2025, up from 29 in 2020, 26 in 2010 and 22 in 2000. Women made up 51.9% of residents of private homes.

Older people are a growing share. People aged 60 and over were 12.0% of the population at the 2020 census, against 9.1% in 2010.

The government’s National Population Programme for 2026 to 2030, published in May 2026, makes population ageing a national priority. It also formally recognises the fall in fertility.

Registered births totalled 1,678,532 in 2025, a rate of 47.7 per 1,000 women aged 15 to 49. The rate was unchanged from 2024 but well below the 67.7 recorded in 2016.

Women aged 12 and over had borne 1.9 children on average in 2025, against 2.1 in 2020 and 2.6 in 2000. In July 2026 the interior ministry put the fertility rate at 1.6 children per woman, La Razón reported.

That is below the roughly 2.1 children per woman that keeps a population stable without migration. Regional gaps are wide: Chiapas, in the south, had a median age of 26 in 2025, against 37 in Mexico City.

Cities, States and the Rural South

Mexico is mostly urban. At the 2020 census, 21.4% of people lived in places with fewer than 2,500 inhabitants, the threshold INEGI uses for rural communities.

Almost half, 48.4%, lived in the 145 cities of 100,000 people or more. At the other extreme were 185,243 localities of fewer than 2,500 people.

Mexico City and the surrounding State of Mexico form one continuous metropolitan area, the country’s economic and political centre. Guadalajara and Monterrey are the next big urban poles.

Internal migration is common: 16.8% of residents in 2025 had been born in a different state from the one they lived in. Violence also moves people.

In 2025, 509,900 households included someone who had been forced to move by crime or insecurity, INEGI found. Those households were home to 1.6 million people.

Chiapas had 5.9 million people and Oaxaca 4.2 million in 2025. Both southern states have large indigenous populations.

Indigenous Mexico, From Nahuatl to Maya

Article 2 of the constitution, last reformed in September 2024, describes a pluricultural and multi-ethnic nation originally founded on its indigenous peoples. Awareness of indigenous identity is the fundamental test of who counts as indigenous.

By that test, 24.2 million people considered themselves indigenous in 2025, or 18.6% of the population. Only 29.5% of those aged three and over spoke an indigenous language.

In all, 7,421,285 people aged three and over spoke an indigenous language in 2025, 5.9% of that age group. The share was 6.1% in 2020.

A federal law makes the indigenous languages and Spanish national languages with the same validity. They can be used for any public business or official procedure.

Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs, had 1.6 million speakers in 2025. Maya followed with 778,900, then Tseltal with 663,800, Tsotsil with 596,800 and Mixtec with 505,600.

Those five languages accounted for 56.2% of all speakers. At the 2020 census, Nahuatl was the main indigenous language in 15 states, and Maya in Campeche, Quintana Roo and Yucatán.

Indigenous Mexico is concentrated in the south. In Oaxaca, 66.6% of residents considered themselves indigenous in 2025, in Yucatán 56.5% and in Chiapas 38.8%.

Chiapas and Oaxaca had the highest share of speakers, 29.0% each, followed by Yucatán at 21.4% and Guerrero at 15.4%. Mexico City also had 619,600 residents who identified as indigenous.

Speakers are older than other Mexicans: 35.1% were 50 or over in 2023, against 27.0% of non-speakers. Women aged 15 to 49 who spoke an indigenous language averaged 2.16 children, against 1.42 for other women.

Afro-Mexicans, Mestizos and Religion

The constitution also recognises Afro-Mexican peoples, descendants of people brought from Africa and settled in Mexico since colonial times. In 2025, 2.1 million people identified as Afro-Mexican or Afro-descendant, 1.6% of the population.

The 2020 census had counted 2,576,213, or 2.0%, and the 2025 results do not explain the difference. Their share reached 7.5% in Guerrero and 4.6% in Oaxaca in 2025, both states on the Pacific coast.

Most Mexicans are commonly described as mestizo, of mixed indigenous and European ancestry, but the census does not ask about race. Skin colour still matters, as an INEGI survey of adults aged 25 to 64 found in 2016.

Of those who placed themselves in the darkest skin tones, 20.2% had no schooling, against 10% of those with the lightest. Darker-skinned people were also less likely to hold skilled jobs.

Foreigners are few: people born abroad were 0.9% of residents in 2025. Of those, 57.1% were born in the US, 6.5% in Venezuela and 5.3% in Cuba, and half held Mexican nationality.

Religion data come from the 2020 census, when 77.7% of Mexicans were Catholic, down from 82.7% in 2010. Protestants and evangelicals made up 11.2%, and 8.1% said they had no religion.

Smaller groups included 58,876 Jews and 7,982 Muslims. The Virgin of Guadalupe is central to Mexican Catholicism, and her feast day on 12 December draws huge pilgrimages to Mexico City.

Migration, Remittances and the Diaspora

Emigration continues. INEGI estimates that 1,259,978 residents of Mexico moved abroad between 2020 and 2025, and that 150,752 of them had come back.

The US Census Bureau counted 10.68 million US residents born in Mexico in 2022, 23.1% of all immigrants. That was about one million fewer than in 2010.

Over the same period, the number of US immigrants from South America and the rest of Central America rose by 2.1 million. Mexico’s share of the total fell from 29.3% to 23.1%.

Money flows the other way. Banco de México, the central bank, recorded US$5.45 billion in remittances in August 2026, from about 13.2 million transfers averaging roughly US$412.

Remittances totalled US$41.8 billion from January to August 2026, up 2.2% on a year earlier, Banco de México data show. August alone was 3.6% lower than a year before.

A 1% US tax has applied since January 2026 to remittances paid in cash, money orders or cashier’s checks, the IRS says. Fewer households rely on money from abroad: 4.7% received such support in 2025, against 5.1% in 2020.

Deportations add a return flow. In April 2026 the interior ministry said 203,685 Mexicans had been returned from the US since 20 January 2025, Por Esto reported.

How Mexico’s Groups Live Together

Mexico’s inequalities follow ethnic lines. INEGI’s 2024 poverty measurement found 66.3% of indigenous-language speakers in poverty, against 26.7% of everyone else.

The national poverty rate was 29.6%, and 32.3% among Afro-descendants. Rural poverty, at 45.8%, was almost double the urban rate of 25.0%.

Government cash programmes now reach deep into society. In 2025, 41.4% of households received benefits from a government programme, up from 25.0% in 2020, INEGI found.

Those programmes are central to the politics of the governing Morena party, as Mexico politics explained sets out. Households receiving a retirement pension also rose, from 13.0% to 16.6%.

Identity is fluid. Of the 24.2 million people who identify as indigenous, fewer than a third speak an indigenous language, which shows identity outlasting language.

Some gaps are narrowing. Internet access reached 75.7% of homes in 2025, against 53.9% in 2020, and adult illiteracy fell from 4.8% to 3.7%.

What It Means for US Readers

Mexico’s demographic shift matters to US companies that build plants there, a trend covered in Mexico nearshoring explained. A median age of 32 still means a young workforce, but births have fallen sharply since 2016.

Migration is changing shape. More than 1.2 million people left Mexico between 2020 and 2025, INEGI estimates, while deportations from the US send others back.

The 1% US tax applies when senders pay in cash or with a money order, cashier’s check or a similar physical instrument. Remittances still reach 4.7% of Mexican households.

For investors and consumer brands, Mexico is a market of 130.9 million people, with three in four homes online. The companies that serve it are profiled in who runs Mexico’s economy, with wider context in Mexico explained.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket bettors gave about a 3% chance that President Claudia Sheinbaum leaves office by 31 December 2026 (7 October, 8:38 a.m. ET). That contract had traded about US$35,000, within an event worth about US$288,000.

Sheinbaum, of the left-wing Morena party, has governed since October 2024. For population policy, from pensions and cash transfers to migration talks with Washington, the bets point to continuity through 2026.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

CONAPO has not yet published projections that incorporate the 2025 survey, so official forecasts for 2026 and beyond may come down. The survey is a sample, so its figures carry sampling error.

INEGI’s 2025 release does not explain why the Afro-Mexican share fell from 2.0% to 1.6%, and it does not report religion.

The full effect of US deportations and the remittance tax on migration in 2026 cannot yet be measured. Whether the fertility rate keeps falling below 1.6 is also open.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the population of Mexico in 2026?

INEGI estimated 130.9 million residents as of October 2025 in its Intercensal Survey, published in September 2026. CONAPO projections made before that survey put Mexico at almost 133 million for 2026.

What are the main ethnic groups in Mexico?

Most Mexicans are commonly described as mestizo, of mixed indigenous and European descent, though the census does not count that category. In 2025, 18.6% identified as indigenous and 1.6% as Afro-Mexican.

How many Mexicans speak an indigenous language?

INEGI counted 7.4 million speakers aged three and over in 2025, 5.9% of that age group. Nahuatl is the most widely spoken, with 1.6 million speakers in 2025.

What religion are most Mexicans?

At the 2020 census, 77.7% of Mexicans were Catholic, down from 82.7% in 2010. Protestants and evangelicals made up 11.2%, and 8.1% had no religion.

How many Mexicans live in the United States?

The US Census Bureau counted 10.68 million US residents born in Mexico in 2022, nearly a quarter of all immigrants. Millions more US citizens have Mexican ancestry.

Is Mexico’s population still growing?

Yes, but slowly: about 0.7% a year between 2020 and 2025, down from 1.0% between 2015 and 2020. Registered births were 1.68 million in 2025.

Sources: INEGI, Encuesta Intercensal 2025, press release 54/26; INEGI, Encuesta Intercensal 2025, results report 37/26; INEGI state results for Mexico City, Jalisco, Chiapas, Oaxaca, Guerrero and Yucatán; INEGI, Censo 2020 results; INEGI, Censo 2020 main results; INEGI, registered births 2025; INEGI, indigenous peoples statistics 2022; INEGI, indigenous peoples statistics 2024 (ENADID 2023); INEGI, social mobility module 2016; INEGI, poverty measurement 2024 (presentation); Constitution of Mexico, Article 2; General Law on Linguistic Rights of Indigenous Peoples; Chihuahua State Population Council, CONAPO data, July 2026; Banco de México, remittances (CE81); US Census Bureau, foreign-born population 2022; IRS, remittance transfer tax; La Razón; Por Esto, remittances; Por Esto, repatriations (all accessed 7 October 2026).

World.title: Who Runs Ghana’s Economy, the Key Players in 2026
World.content:
GHANA · ECONOMY

Key Facts — The country Ghana has 34.4 million people and is Africa’s largest gold producer.

— Who decides President John Mahama, Finance Minister Ato Forson, central bank governor Johnson Asiama.

— What happened Growth was 6.0% in the second quarter of 2026; August inflation 5.0%.

— The money Gold earned US$14.9 billion of US$22.4 billion goods exports, January–August 2026.

— For US investors New York-listed Newmont, AngloGold Ashanti and Kosmos Energy operate in Ghana.

— Prediction markets Kalshi bettors give the governing NDC a 61% chance of winning Ghana’s next parliamentary election (7 October, 5:07 a.m. ET).

From the presidency to the cocoa board and the Jubilee oil field, these are the people steering Ghana’s money in 2026.

The Ghana economy is run in 2026 by President John Mahama’s government, the central bank and two state commodity agencies. Foreign oil and mining companies, several of them listed in New York, run major gold mines and the offshore oil fields.

Gold, cocoa and oil earned about US$20 billion of Ghana’s US$22.4 billion goods exports in January–August 2026, central bank data show. More news on the country is collected on the Rio Times Ghana page.

How the Ghana Economy Is Run

John Mahama of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) became president again in January 2025, having first served from 2012 to 2017. The NDC is the centre-left party founded by former leader Jerry Rawlings.

The centre-right New Patriotic Party (NPP), which governed from 2017 to January 2025, is now the main opposition. Under the 1992 constitution, the president appoints ministers with the prior approval of parliament.

These office holders matter most for the economy, according to the presidency’s cabinet list and the ministries’ own websites:

Cassiel Ato Forson , Minister for Finance, who prepares the budget and manages public debt and the IMF relationship.

, Minister for Finance, who prepares the budget and manages public debt and the IMF relationship. Thomas Nyarko Ampem , Deputy Minister for Finance.

, Deputy Minister for Finance. John Abdulai Jinapor , Minister for Energy and Green Transition, responsible for oil, gas and electricity.

, Minister for Energy and Green Transition, responsible for oil, gas and electricity. Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah , Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, whose ministry oversees mining.

, Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, whose ministry oversees mining. Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare , Minister for Trade, Industry and Agribusiness.

, Minister for Trade, Industry and Agribusiness. Eric Opoku , Minister for Food and Agriculture.

, Minister for Food and Agriculture. Alhassan Iddrisu, the Government Statistician, who heads the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) that publishes growth and inflation figures.

GSS projects Ghana’s population at 34.4 million for 2026. The World Bank puts 2025 output at about US$114 billion, or roughly US$3,260 per person.

That is less than 4% of the US figure of about US$90,000. For a fuller country profile, see Ghana explained for newcomers.

The Central Bank, the Cedi and the Banks

The Bank of Ghana (BoG), the central bank, is led by Governor Johnson Pandit Asiama. It sets interest rates, manages reserves and licenses banks.

Its Monetary Policy Committee held the benchmark rate at 14.0% at its meeting of 23–24 September 2026, by a unanimous vote. Inflation was 5.0% in August 2026, below the bank’s target of 8%, plus or minus two points.

Gross reserves were US$12.0 billion on 22 September 2026, enough to pay for 4.5 months of imports. The cedi had lost 9.5% against the dollar in 2026 by 18 September, at GH¢11.55 per US$1.

By 6 October 2026, the BoG interbank mid-rate stood at GH¢11.80 per US$1. Conversions in this article use that rate.

Banking assets reached GH¢500.2 billion (about US$42.4 billion) in August 2026. Non-performing loans fell to 15.7% of the total, from 20.8% a year earlier.

The lenders that matter most include these:

GCB Bank , founded in 1953, which describes itself as Ghana’s largest bank and runs more than 183 branches.

, founded in 1953, which describes itself as Ghana’s largest bank and runs more than 183 branches. Société Générale Ghana , whose French parent is selling its 60.22% stake, subject to approvals in Morocco and Ghana.

, whose French parent is selling its 60.22% stake, subject to approvals in Morocco and Ghana. Attijariwafa bank , the Moroccan lender that agreed on 1 October 2026 to buy 55.22% of it, with the state pension fund SSNIT taking 5%.

, the Moroccan lender that agreed on 1 October 2026 to buy 55.22% of it, with the state pension fund SSNIT taking 5%. Other listed lenders, including Ecobank Ghana, Standard Chartered Bank Ghana, Access Bank Ghana and CalBank.

The details of that sale are in the Rio Times report on Attijariwafa’s purchase of Société Générale Ghana.

Gold, GoldBod and the Big Miners

Ghana is Africa’s largest gold producer, with an estimated 150 tonnes in 2025, according to the US Geological Survey. South Africa mined about 90 tonnes.

Gold brought in US$14.9 billion from January to August 2026, two-thirds of all goods exports, BoG data show. The average price in August was US$4,408 an ounce.

The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), created by Act 1140 of 2025, has exclusive rights to buy and export gold from small-scale miners. Its chief executive is Sammy Gyamfi.

GoldBod says it buys, assays, refines and exports at least 3 tonnes of gold a week. The foreign currency it earns helps rebuild the central bank’s reserves.

Many large mines are run by foreign companies under licences overseen by Minister Buah’s ministry. Two of the best known are listed in New York:

Newmont , the only gold producer in the S&P 500 index, which manages the Ahafo South and Ahafo North mines.

, the only gold producer in the S&P 500 index, which manages the Ahafo South and Ahafo North mines. AngloGold Ashanti, headquartered in Greenwood Village, Colorado, which runs the Obuasi and Iduapriem mines.

How the gold price lifted growth, and what it means for reserves, is covered in Ghana grows 6% as gold lifts exports.

Cocoa, COCOBOD and the Farmgate Price

The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) is the state agency that regulates the crop and sets the price paid to farmers. Its chief executive is Ransford Anertey Abbey.

On Friday, 25 September 2026, COCOBOD set the 2026/27 producer price at GH¢42,400 a tonne (about US$3,590). That is GH¢2,650 (about US$225) per 64-kilogram bag.

The previous price was GH¢41,392 a tonne (about US$3,510). COCOBOD says the new price gives farmers 71.18% of the crop’s gross free-on-board value, the export price at the port.

A new Ghana Cocoa Board Act, 2026, guarantees farmers at least 70% of that value. COCOBOD also says it is fighting cocoa smuggling to neighbouring countries.

To fund purchases, its subsidiary Cocoa Capital PLC announced a GH¢16.3 billion (about US$1.38 billion) note programme on 25 September 2026. It combines GH¢14 billion (about US$1.19 billion) of short-term paper and GH¢2.3 billion (about US$195 million) of bonds for legacy debt.

The Securities and Exchange Commission approved the issue, and repayment is backed by forward cocoa sales. Cocoa exports earned US$2.76 billion from January to August 2026, the second-biggest export after gold.

Oil: Jubilee, Tullow and Kosmos

Ghana’s oil comes from offshore fields in the Gulf of Guinea. Jubilee was discovered in 2007 and began producing in late 2010, according to partner Kosmos Energy.

The partners in Jubilee, according to both Tullow and Kosmos, are these:

Tullow Oil , the London-listed operator, with 38.98%.

, the London-listed operator, with 38.98%. Kosmos Energy , based in Dallas and listed in New York, with 38.61%.

, based in Dallas and listed in New York, with 38.61%. Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) , the state oil company, with 19.69%.

, the state oil company, with 19.69%. PetroSA, South Africa’s state oil company, with 2.72%.

Jubilee pumped 70,800 barrels a day gross in the first half of 2026, Tullow reported on Monday, 28 September. The smaller TEN fields, also run by Tullow, added 14,800 barrels a day.

Tullow, led by chief executive Ian Perks, says Parliament ratified the extension of both licence areas to 31 December 2040. On Wednesday, 30 September 2026, an International Chamber of Commerce tribunal upheld a US$196.5 million Ghana tax assessment against Tullow.

The Ghana Revenue Authority, the national tax agency, puts the total with penalties at about US$393 million, the Ghana News Agency reported. Tullow said it was disappointed; a second Tullow tax case is due to be heard in 2027.

Oil exports earned US$2.42 billion from January to August 2026, BoG data show. Energy Minister Jinapor oversees the sector for the government.

Tullow’s latest figures are in Tullow’s first cash-positive first half since 2021.

The Stock Exchange and MTN Ghana

The Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE) in Accra is small but has rallied in 2026. Its Composite Index stood at 14,221.20 on 6 October 2026, up 62.15% since January.

Listed companies were worth GH¢285.6 billion (about US$24.2 billion) in August 2026, according to BoG data.

MTN Ghana, listed as Scancom PLC, is the local arm of South Africa’s MTN Group, in Ghana for 30 years. It reported service revenue of GH¢14.96 billion (about US$1.27 billion) for January to June 2026.

Profit after tax was GH¢5.13 billion (about US$435 million), with active data users up 17.0%. Chief executive Stephen Blewett credited data and mobile money, MyJoyOnline reported.

On 2 October 2026, MTN Ghana received notice of a spectrum award in the 700 MHz and 3 GHz bands. More on that is in MTN Ghana’s 5G spectrum deal.

Debt, the IMF and the Recovery

Ghana’s 2022 debt crisis led to a 39-month IMF Extended Credit Facility of about US$3 billion, approved in May 2023. The IMF board completed its sixth and final review on Monday, 27 July 2026.

It also approved a 36-month Policy Coordination Instrument, an IMF monitoring arrangement that carries no loan. The Ghana News Agency reported that total disbursements reached about US$3 billion.

Public debt was GH¢733.9 billion (US$62.8 billion), or 45.9% of GDP, at the end of July 2026, central bank data show. The Finance Ministry says it settled a US$700 million Eurobond payment ahead of schedule in July 2026.

Growth reached 6.0% year on year in the second quarter of 2026, according to GSS. The central bank’s policy rate has come down from 28.0% in May 2025 to 14.0%.

What It Means for US Readers

Three New York-listed companies, Newmont, AngloGold Ashanti and Kosmos Energy, have large stakes in Ghana’s gold and oil output. Their results depend partly on Ghanaian tax, licence and currency decisions.

Ghana is a major cocoa supplier, so COCOBOD’s prices and financing can affect bean supply for US chocolate makers. Gold sales through GoldBod also feed a global market priced in dollars.

For visitors and remote workers, a weaker local currency means dollars buy more, though prices rose 5.0% in the year to August. Ghana’s ties with Washington, Beijing and the Gulf are covered in Ghana geopolitics explained.

What Prediction Markets Say

Kalshi is a US betting exchange regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). On its market for Ghana’s next parliamentary election, bettors priced the NDC at 61.0% and the NPP at 36.0%.

Prices were taken at 5:07 a.m. ET on 7 October 2026; trading volume was not available. These are bets on a vote due in 2028, not polls; an NDC win would point to policy continuity.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

GSS was due to publish September 2026 inflation in the second week of October. The date of the 2027 budget statement had not been confirmed.

The IMF said in August 2026 that talks with some external commercial creditors were still under way. Tullow’s next steps after the tax ruling and the approvals for the Attijariwafa deal are also pending.

Gold is now two-thirds of goods exports, so a fall in the gold price would hit export earnings and reserves together. How long the 2026 price boom lasts is unknown.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who controls Ghana’s economic policy?

President John Mahama and Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson set fiscal policy, and parliament approves the budget. The Bank of Ghana under Governor Johnson Asiama sets interest rates.

What is Ghana’s biggest export?

Gold. It earned US$14.9 billion from January to August 2026, about two-thirds of goods exports, ahead of cocoa and oil.

What is the Bank of Ghana’s interest rate?

The policy rate is 14.0%, held at the September 2026 meeting. Inflation was 5.0% in August 2026, below the 8% target.

Who pumps Ghana’s oil?

Tullow Oil operates the offshore Jubilee and TEN fields. Its partners include Kosmos Energy of Dallas, the state firm GNPC and South Africa’s PetroSA.

What does Ghana pay cocoa farmers?

From 25 September 2026, the producer price is about US$3,590 a tonne. COCOBOD says that is 71.18% of the gross export value.

Is Ghana still in an IMF programme?

Its US$3 billion loan programme ended with a final review on 27 July 2026. Ghana now has a Policy Coordination Instrument, an IMF monitoring deal with no loan.

World.title: Nigeria Politics Explained, Who Holds Power in 2026
World.content:
NIGERIA · POLITICS

Key Facts — The country Africa’s most populous nation, with about 237.5 million people in 2025.

— What happened A wave of opposition governors has joined the governing APC since mid-2025.

— The election Presidential and parliamentary vote on Saturday, 16 January 2027; governors 6 February.

— The players President Bola Tinubu faces Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Seyi Makinde.

— Prediction markets Polymarket bettors give Tinubu a 71% chance of winning and Obi 24% (7 October, 7:07 a.m. ET).

— Still open Whether the opposition unites; turnout was about 27% in 2023.

Nigeria has one dominant party, a divided opposition and a president seeking a second term in January 2027.

Nigeria politics in 2026 revolves around President Bola Tinubu and his All Progressives Congress (APC), which governs most of the country’s states. The opposition is split three ways before the presidential election on Saturday, 16 January 2027.

For US readers, the stakes are oil, security cooperation against jihadist groups and the stability of Africa’s most populous country. This guide sets out who holds power as of October 2026, how it is shared and what to watch.

How Nigeria Politics Works

Nigeria is a federal republic built loosely on the US model. A president elected for four years heads both the state and the government, and may serve two terms.

The National Assembly has two chambers: a 109-seat Senate and a 360-seat House of Representatives. Below the federal level sit 36 states, each run by an elected governor, plus the Federal Capital Territory around Abuja.

Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

To win outright, a presidential candidate needs the most votes nationwide. The winner also needs at least a quarter of the votes in two-thirds of the states and the capital territory.

If nobody clears that bar, the 1999 Constitution provides for a second round.

Nigeria spent most of the period from 1966 to 1999 under military rule. The current civilian system dates from 1999, when the generals handed power back to elected leaders.

Politics also runs on unwritten rules, such as balancing the largely Muslim north and the largely Christian south. Many Nigerians expect the presidency to rotate between the two.

Nigeria had about 237.5 million people in 2025, World Bank data show, roughly 70% of the US population. Its economy was worth about US$291 billion that year.

The Presidency and the Inner Circle

Bola Ahmed Tinubu, 74, has been president since 29 May 2023. A former two-term governor of Lagos State, he helped build the APC coalition that first won power in 2015.

He won in 2023 with 8.79 million votes, about 36.6% of the valid vote. The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) declared figures that put Atiku Abubakar at about 29.1% and Peter Obi at about 25.4%.

Vice President Kashim Shettima, a former governor of Borno State in the northeast, is again his running mate. He represented Nigeria at the UN General Assembly in September 2026.

Femi Gbajabiamila, a former Speaker of the House of Representatives, is the president’s chief of staff. George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, coordinates the federal bureaucracy and stood in for Tinubu at events in September.

Bayo Onanuga, special adviser on information and strategy, is the presidency’s main voice. Nuhu Ribadu, the National Security Adviser, co-leads a security working group with his US counterpart.

Tinubu left Nigeria on 30 August 2026 for London and Paris on what the presidency called a working vacation. It said he kept directing the affairs of the nation from abroad.

The presidency also called Atiku’s criticism of his absence from the UN General Assembly irresponsible. He was back in Nigeria by 2 October, when he attended a film premiere.

For a fuller portrait, see the Rio Times profile Who Is Bola Tinubu?, which covers his reforms and the controversies around him.

The Ministers and Officials Who Matter

Nigeria’s cabinet, the Federal Executive Council, has ministers and junior ministers for most portfolios. These are the officials who shape policy most, as of October 2026:

Taiwo Oyedele , Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, a tax specialist who replaced Wale Edun after Edun resigned in April 2026, citing health reasons.

, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, a tax specialist who replaced Wale Edun after Edun resigned in April 2026, citing health reasons. Atiku Bagudu , Minister of Budget and Economic Planning and a former governor of Kebbi State.

, Minister of Budget and Economic Planning and a former governor of Kebbi State. Olayemi Cardoso , Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), which sets interest rates and manages the naira, the national currency.

, Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), which sets interest rates and manages the naira, the national currency. Zacch Adedeji , head of the Nigeria Revenue Service, the federal tax agency created by the 2025 tax reforms.

, head of the Nigeria Revenue Service, the federal tax agency created by the 2025 tax reforms. Christopher Musa , Minister of Defence, a retired general and former Chief of Defence Staff; Bello Matawalle is Minister of State for Defence.

, Minister of Defence, a retired general and former Chief of Defence Staff; Bello Matawalle is Minister of State for Defence. Lateef Fagbemi , Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, the government’s chief lawyer.

, Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, the government’s chief lawyer. Mohammed Idris , Minister of Information and National Orientation, who also coordinates media for Tinubu’s campaign.

, Minister of Information and National Orientation, who also coordinates media for Tinubu’s campaign. Dele Alake, Minister of Solid Minerals Development and one of Tinubu’s longest-serving allies.

Tinubu credits this team and the central bank with stabilising the economy. His 2023 reforms ended the petrol subsidy and let the currency float.

The Rio Times guide Who Runs Nigeria’s Economy covers the business side in detail.

Several ministers left the cabinet in 2026 to pursue political careers. They included the foreign and power ministers, who resigned before May, according to the presidency.

The APC and a Fractured Opposition

The All Progressives Congress, a merger of opposition parties formed in 2013, has held the presidency since 2015. Its national chairman is Nentawe Yilwatda, according to INEC’s register of parties.

Since mid-2025, a wave of opposition governors has joined it. They include Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom, Peter Mbah of Enugu, Caleb Mutfwang of Plateau and Agbu Kefas of Taraba.

Abba Kabir Yusuf of Kano and Dauda Lawal of Zamfara followed in early 2026. Governors matter because they control state budgets, local patronage and much of the election-day machinery.

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), which ruled from 1999 to 2015, has been hollowed out by splits and defections. Its 2027 candidate is Sandy Ojang Onor, 60; Atiku, its nominee in 2023, has left.

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) became the main opposition coalition, chaired by former Senate President David Mark. Its candidate is Atiku Abubakar, 79, vice-president from 1999 to 2007, with former Rivers State governor Rotimi Amaechi as running mate.

Peter Obi, 65, a former governor of Anambra State in the southeast, now runs for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). His running mate is Rabiu Kwankwaso, 69, a former Kano governor who won about 1.5 million votes in 2023.

On 2023 figures, Obi and Kwankwaso together won about 7.6 million votes, against Tinubu’s 8.8 million. Whether those votes transfer to a joint ticket is one of the central questions of the race.

Oyo State governor Seyi Makinde, 58, declared on 14 May 2026 that he would run for the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). A faction of the PDP backs him, and INEC’s final list confirms him as the APM candidate.

The Labour Party, Obi’s vehicle in 2023, now fields Sunday Chibuzo Okereke. The activist Omoyele Sowore runs for the African Action Congress, and former Cross River governor Donald Duke for the Peoples Redemption Party.

INEC recognises 22 political parties in all. A Rio Times profile of Atiku Abubakar, Tinubu’s main challenger, explains the ADC campaign in more depth.

The 2027 Election Race

INEC’s calendar sets the presidential and National Assembly elections for Saturday, 16 January 2027. Governorship and state assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027.

The commission’s final list, published in September 2026, names 18 presidential candidates, two of them women. Tinubu is the APC candidate, again with Shettima as running mate.

The rules changed when Tinubu signed amendments to the 2022 Electoral Act on Wednesday, 18 February 2026. The debate centred on how polling-unit results are transmitted electronically.

INEC is led by Joash Amupitan, a law professor sworn in on 23 October 2025. On 5 October 2026 he said the voter register had passed 103 million names.

A big register does not guarantee a big vote. In 2023 INEC accredited about 25.3 million of 93.5 million registered voters, roughly 27%.

Campaigning began after the parties signed a National Peace Accord in Abuja on Tuesday, 18 August 2026. The accord commits candidates to non-violent, issue-based campaigns.

Tinubu’s campaign is run by former Zamfara governor Abdulaziz Yari as director-general, with Imo State governor Hope Uzodimma as secretary. Senate President Godswill Akpabio and Speaker Tajudeen Abbas serve as deputy directors-general.

The economy is the main battleground. The presidency accuses Atiku of planning to restore the petrol subsidy that Tinubu scrapped, calling the idea retrogressive and fiscally unsound.

Generals, Police and Spy Chiefs

The president is commander-in-chief of the armed forces. The security chiefs, as named in State House statements in 2026, are:

General Olufemi Oluyede , Chief of Defence Staff, the country’s top military officer.

, Chief of Defence Staff, the country’s top military officer. Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu , Chief of Army Staff.

, Chief of Army Staff. Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke , Chief of Air Staff.

, Chief of Air Staff. Vice Admiral Idi Abbas , Chief of Naval Staff.

, Chief of Naval Staff. Tosin Ajayi , Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), the domestic intelligence agency.

, Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), the domestic intelligence agency. Muhammed Muhammed , Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency, the foreign intelligence service.

, Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency, the foreign intelligence service. Olatunji Disu, Inspector-General of Police, confirmed by the Nigeria Police Council on Monday, 2 March 2026.

Threats differ by region: jihadist groups operate in the northeast, and armed gangs known as bandits kidnap for ransom in the northwest. Separatist violence affects parts of the southeast.

The army has grown from eight to 12 divisions to respond faster to attacks, Tinubu said in July 2026. He has also promised state police forces, with safeguards against abuse.

Cooperation with Washington deepened after November 2025, when the two presidents agreed a joint working group on security. The presidency says a coordinated strike on 16 May 2026 killed a senior Islamic State leader near Lake Chad.

Courts, Lawmakers and Governors

The Supreme Court is the final arbiter of disputed presidential elections. Chief Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, sworn in as acting chief justice in August 2024, leads the judiciary as of October 2026.

Presidential election petitions are heard first by the Court of Appeal and then, on appeal, by the Supreme Court. A close outcome in 2027 could end up before her court.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio, a former governor of Akwa Ibom, leads the upper house. Tajudeen Abbas is Speaker of the House of Representatives, and both belong to the APC.

Governors coordinate through the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, chaired by Kwara State governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq. Lagos governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu runs the commercial capital, Tinubu’s home base.

Rising figures to watch include Oyedele, the technocrat now steering the economy, and Makinde, the only sitting governor in the presidential race. Kwankwaso, a former two-term Kano governor, gives Obi’s ticket a base in the populous northwest.

What It Means for US Readers

Nigeria is one of Africa’s largest oil producers and West Africa’s anchor state for security. A smooth or disputed election will shape oil supply, migration and counter-terrorism cooperation with Washington.

President Donald Trump wrote to Tinubu on 6 July 2026 praising his fight against terrorists, the presidency said. The letter singled out violence affecting Christian communities, an issue followed closely in US politics.

The US State Department rates Nigeria Level 3, Reconsider Travel, in an advisory issued on 12 June 2026. It lists large parts of the north and southeast, including Kano, Kaduna and Borno, as Do Not Travel areas.

Investors in Nigerian dollar bonds and Lagos-listed shares should expect election risk to be priced in before January. A disputed result or a runoff would likely weigh on the naira.

Daily coverage of the campaign and the economy is collected on the Rio Times Nigeria page.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, bettors gave Tinubu a 71% chance of winning at 7:07 a.m. ET on Wednesday, 7 October 2026. Peter Obi stood at 24%, and about US$128,800 had been bet on the market in total.

The market lists no contract for Atiku Abubakar or Seyi Makinde, so its prices do not cover the whole field. Contracts on Kwankwaso, Amaechi and Sowore traded below 1%.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The state of Tinubu’s health is not publicly documented, and the presidency has released no medical details. It is also unclear whether the opposition will consolidate behind one candidate before January.

Reliable opinion polls are scarce, so the state of the race is hard to measure. A close three-way contest could force a second round, which has not happened since civilian rule returned in 1999.

The final size of the voter register, after objections and clean-up, has not been published. Nor is it known how many voters will collect the cards they need to vote.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is the president of Nigeria in 2026?

Bola Ahmed Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress has been president since 29 May 2023. His vice-president is Kashim Shettima, a former governor of Borno State.

When is Nigeria’s next presidential election?

The presidential and National Assembly elections are on Saturday, 16 January 2027. Governorship and state assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027.

What are the main political parties in Nigeria?

The governing All Progressives Congress controls the presidency and most states. The main opposition tickets run under the African Democratic Congress, the Nigeria Democratic Congress and the Allied Peoples Movement.

Who is running against Tinubu in 2027?

The electoral commission lists 18 candidates in total. The best known challengers are Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi with Rabiu Kwankwaso as running mate, and Oyo State governor Seyi Makinde.

How does a candidate win Nigeria’s presidency?

A winner needs the most votes and at least 25% in two-thirds of the states and the capital territory. Otherwise the constitution provides for a second round.

Who controls Nigeria’s military?

The president is commander-in-chief, with General Olufemi Oluyede as Chief of Defence Staff. Christopher Musa, a retired general, is the Minister of Defence.

World.title: When Is Mexican Independence Day And Events
World.content:
MEXICO · INDEPENDENCE DAY

Key Facts — The date Mexican Independence Day is 16 September; the Grito is the night before.

— Not 5 May Cinco de Mayo marks an 1862 battle win over France at Puebla.

— Next dates Grito on Wednesday, 15 September 2027; holiday on Thursday, 16 September 2027.

— For US visitors A mandatory paid day off; US Embassy and consulates close.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives President Claudia Sheinbaum a 3% chance of leaving office by 31 December 2026 (7 October, 7:39 a.m. ET).

— Still open The 2027 programme, start times and road closures are not announced.

Mexico’s national day is 16 September, not 5 May, and the celebration starts the night before with the Grito.

When is Mexican Independence Day? It is 16 September, and the celebrations begin late on 15 September with the Grito, a cry first raised in 1810.

It is not Cinco de Mayo, which marks an 1862 battle and is not a statutory day off in Mexico.

When Is Mexican Independence Day, and Why 16 September

Mexico’s flag law lists 16 September as the anniversary of the start of Mexican independence in 1810. The Federal Labour Law makes the same date a mandatory paid day off in its Article 74.

Banco de México, the central bank, says Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla raised the Grito de Dolores on 16 September 1810. That cry started the independence movement, which is why Mexicans call Hidalgo the Father of the Nation.

Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Hidalgo, a Catholic priest, used the bell of Dolores, a town in today’s Guanajuato state, to call people together. The town is now officially Dolores Hidalgo, Cuna de la Independencia Nacional, the cradle of national independence.

The war lasted 11 years, and the flag law marks 27 September 1821 as the day independence was completed. José María Morelos took over the insurgent struggle after Hidalgo’s death, Banco de México notes.

Both September dates are civic anniversaries, but only 16 September is a national day off.

What Happens at the Grito on 15 September

The Grito is the night-time re-enactment of Hidalgo’s call. Mexico’s flag law lists 15 September as the commemoration of the Grito de Independencia, separate from the 16 September anniversary.

The same law requires the president to wear the presidential sash at the Grito on the night of 15 September. It is one of only four occasions on which the sash is mandatory.

In Mexico City, the president leads the ceremony from a balcony of the National Palace, the seat of government. In 2026, Sheinbaum stepped onto its central balcony at 11 p.m. before a packed Zócalo, the capital’s main square, Excélsior reported.

By tradition, the president names heroes of independence and the crowd answers each name with a shout of viva. The cry ends with Viva México, followed by fireworks over the square.

State governments and town halls stage their own ceremonies on the same night. The law fixes the date but not the hour, so start times are announced locally each year.

Where Mexico Celebrates, From Mexico City to Dolores Hidalgo

Mexico City hosts the national ceremony on the night of 15 September. On the morning of 16 September, the armed forces traditionally parade through the centre of the capital.

Presidency photographs from 16 September 2015 show troops and armoured vehicles lined up across the Zócalo for that year’s parade. Expansión listed the 2026 civic-military parade for Wednesday, 16 September.

In Dolores Hidalgo, where the uprising began, the town’s parish church stands on the main square. Nearby San Miguel de Allende carries the name of Ignacio Allende, a rebel leader born in 1769.

State capitals hold their own ceremonies. Rio Times listings for 2026 included a Grito in Mérida’s Plaza Grande and a free concert in central Guadalajara on 15 September.

Under the flag law, Mexico’s embassies and consulates abroad raise the flag at full mast on 15 and 16 September. Check your nearest consulate’s announcements for public events in the United States.

Why 5 May Is a Different Holiday

Cinco de Mayo, 5 May, marks the Mexican army’s victory over French forces at Puebla in 1862, the flag law says. That battle came more than 40 years after independence.

It is a civic anniversary in Mexico but is not a mandatory day off under Article 74 of the Federal Labour Law. The US Embassy and consulates did close on Tuesday, 5 May 2026, listing it as the Battle of Puebla.

So 16 September is the national holiday, 15 September is the night of the Grito and 5 May is a battle anniversary.

Key Dates in Mexico’s Independence Story

Mexico’s flag law doubles as a calendar of the independence story. Public buildings fly the flag at full mast on the birth and event dates, and at half mast on the death anniversaries.

8 May 1753: Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla is born; the law calls him the initiator of Mexican independence.

21 January 1769: Ignacio Allende, a rebel leader, is born.

19 April 1773: Josefa Ortiz, a heroine of independence honoured on the same calendar, is born.

16 September 1810: Hidalgo raises the Grito de Dolores and the independence movement begins.

30 July 1811: Hidalgo dies, and José María Morelos carries on the insurgency.

6 November 1813: the first Congress of Anáhuac, meeting in Chilpancingo, approves a solemn declaration of independence.

22 December 1815: Morelos dies.

27 September 1821: independence is consummated, 11 years after the Grito.

5 May 1862: Mexican forces defeat the French army at Puebla, the origin of Cinco de Mayo.

The sequence explains the confusion. Mexico celebrates the start of the uprising on 16 September, while 5 May belongs to a later war against France.

Mexican Independence Day Dates for 2027 and 2028

2027: the Grito on Wednesday, 15 September 2027; the holiday on Thursday, 16 September 2027.

2028: the Grito on Friday, 15 September 2028; the holiday on Saturday, 16 September 2028.

Consummation of independence, a civic date but not a day off: Monday, 27 September 2027.

Because the law fixes the holiday to 16 September, it does not move to a Monday, unlike three other national holidays. In 2027 it falls on a Thursday, and 15 September remains a normal working day.

Employees who work on 16 September are owed double pay on top of their regular wage, under Article 75. That matters to anyone who employs household staff in Mexico.

How to Celebrate as a Visitor

To see a Grito in person, book a hotel near a main square early. Arrive well before the ceremony to find a spot.

As a mandatory rest day, 16 September closes many offices and businesses. The Rio Times Independence Day expat playbook covers banks, exchange-rate fixing and parade routes.

In Puebla and central Mexico, chiles en nogada are traditionally eaten from July to September, UnoTV reports. The stuffed poblano chile is topped with walnut sauce, pomegranate and parsley, the colours of the flag.

For restaurants, see the Rio Times guide on where to eat chiles en nogada in Querétaro.

For how the 2026 night unfolded, read El Grito 2026 Mexico City Recap and 2027 Guide. Follow the Rio Times Mexico coverage for the 2027 programme.

What It Means for US Readers

Plan mid-September trips around a national holiday. The US Embassy and consulates in Mexico close on 16 September, as they did on Wednesday, 16 September 2026.

The US State Department rates Mexico Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, citing terrorism, crime and kidnapping, with higher risk in some areas. It grades each state separately, so check Guanajuato before a trip to Dolores Hidalgo.

Mexico City keeps Central Standard Time all year, because only the northern border uses seasonal time under Mexico’s time-zone law. In September that puts the capital two hours behind New York.

The green 200-peso note, worth about US$11 at open.er-api.com’s rate of 7 October 2026, shows Hidalgo and the Dolores bell. It is a pocket-sized version of the story.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a platform where traders bet real money on events, asks whether President Claudia Sheinbaum will be out by 31 December 2026. Yes traded at about 3% on 7 October at 7:39 a.m. ET, on volume of about US$35,000.

Sheinbaum has been Mexico’s president since October 2024 and leads the national Grito. See Who Is Claudia Sheinbaum? for her profile; no market prices who will lead the 2027 ceremony.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The 2027 programme in Mexico City, including performers, start times and road closures, has not been announced. Security arrangements and any limits on alcohol sales are set locally each year.

The exact hour of the presidential Grito is not fixed in law and can vary from year to year.

Whether Sheinbaum leads the 2027 Grito depends on her staying in office. The market above covers only the period to 31 December 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Mexican Independence Day on September 15 or 16?

Independence Day is 16 September, the statutory holiday. The Grito, the main ceremony, takes place on the night of 15 September.

Is Cinco de Mayo Mexico’s Independence Day?

No. Cinco de Mayo marks the 1862 victory over French forces at Puebla, while the independence movement began on 16 September 1810.

What is the Grito de Dolores?

It is the cry Miguel Hidalgo raised in Dolores on 16 September 1810 to start the independence movement. Mexico re-enacts it every year on the night of 15 September.

Is 16 September a day off in Mexico?

Yes. Article 74 of the Federal Labour Law makes it a mandatory paid day off, and staff who work it earn double pay.

When is Mexican Independence Day in 2027?

The holiday falls on Thursday, 16 September 2027. The Grito takes place on the night of Wednesday, 15 September 2027.

Where can visitors see the Grito?

The national ceremony is in Mexico City’s Zócalo, led by the president. State capitals and towns such as Dolores Hidalgo, where the uprising began, hold their own.

World.title: When Is The Day Of The Dead In Mexico
World.content:
MEXICO · CULTURE

Key Facts — The country Mexico, where families welcome their dead home at altars and graves.

— The dates Sunday, 1 November, for children; Monday, 2 November, for adults.

— What happened Mexico City’s guide sets the main parade for Saturday, 31 October.

— What closes Banks close Monday, 2 November; it is not a statutory rest day.

— What it means for you Parades are free; ask before photographing graves and never step on them.

— Safety US State Department: Mexico City Level 2, Michoacán “do not travel”.

The exact dates, what each day means, Mexico City’s 2026 parade calendar and the etiquette US visitors need at altars and graves.

When is the Day of the Dead in 2026? In Mexico it falls on Sunday, 1 November, and Monday, 2 November, the Catholic feasts of All Saints and All Souls.

For US visitors, those dates shape flights, bank errands and how to behave at cemetery vigils.

Mexico City’s season starts earlier, with free street events from 17 October. Its Great Day of the Dead Parade is listed for Saturday, 31 October, the same day as Halloween in the United States.

When Is the Day of the Dead in 2026, Day by Day

The heart of the festivity is 1 and 2 November. UNESCO, the UN cultural agency, describes a wider season running from the end of October to the beginning of November.

It notes that the dead are grouped by categories such as age and cause of death. Each group is remembered on its own day.

The business magazine Expansión, citing the Mexican government, set out the common calendar in October 2025. Applied to 2026, it runs like this:

Tuesday, 27 October: pets, a newer family custom that Expansión lists apart from the government dates.

pets, a newer family custom that Expansión lists apart from the government dates. Wednesday, 28 October: people who died in accidents or by violence.

people who died in accidents or by violence. Friday, 30 October, and Saturday, 31 October: children who died before baptism.

children who died before baptism. Sunday, 1 November: All Saints’ Day, devoted to children, often called angelitos, or little angels.

All Saints’ Day, devoted to children, often called angelitos, or little angels. Monday, 2 November: All Souls’ Day, devoted to adults, when families gather at graves.

Practice varies from town to town. San Andrés Mixquic, a village in Mexico City’s Tláhuac borough, follows its own timetable.

There, the city’s official guide says, children’s souls arrive on 31 October and adults on 1 November. The cycle ends on the night of 2 November with La Alumbrada, the Illumination.

That night, thousands of candles are lit on the graves to guide the souls back.

How Mexicans Honour Children and Adults

The central idea is a visit, not a haunting. UNESCO describes the festivity as the temporary return of dead relatives, welcomed by families who prepare for them with care.

Families lay flower petals, candles and offerings along the path from the cemetery to the house, UNESCO says. The dead person’s favourite dishes go on the home altar and the tomb, with flowers and paper cut-outs.

The home altar is the ofrenda, or offering. Its usual elements, as listed by the Mexican news channel ADN40, are these:

personal objects that belonged to the dead;

candles and water;

food the person liked, and fruit;

pan de muerto, a sweet bread made for the season;

cempasúchil, the orange Mexican marigold, and papel picado, cut-paper banners.

Children and adults are welcomed differently. In Mixquic, children’s souls are greeted with white petals and sweets, the city guide says.

Adults are guided home by their favourite dishes and by marigold petals.

The belief carries weight: UNESCO notes the dead are thought able to bring prosperity, such as a good maize harvest, or misfortune. Much depends on how carefully families carry out the rituals.

That is why it is not “Mexican Halloween”. UNESCO describes a fusion of pre-Hispanic rites and Catholic feasts, and the season coincides with the end of the maize-growing cycle.
