World.title: Justice minister vows new gender equality bill will reach vote before elections
World.content:
Justice Minister Liisa Pakosta says the long‑stalled gender equality and equal opportunities bill will be passed during the current Riigikogu term, though she has not yet explained the draft's contents or the timeline for its processing.

"We hope to complete the processing of the equal opportunities bill by the end of this Riigikogu term," Pakosta said.

She is not worried that time may be tight — under normal procedure, the bill should reach the Riigikogu by November at the latest.

"There is nothing unusual about this. It is completely normal that things are in progress and some take a bit longer. That is the case with many bills," she said.

Pakosta said it is not actually a problem that the gender equality and equal opportunities bill has remained unpassed for so long. She said the Constitution already provides protection that covers the bill's provisions.

"This bill changes almost nothing in people's lives because paragraph 12 of the Constitution is directly applicable," she said.

"Courts, the chancellor of justice and everyone else work on the basis of that constitutional paragraph, which guarantees protection for all people across all characteristics in all areas of life. Estonians are very well protected against discrimination because we have a very good Constitution. The changes achieved with this bill are extremely nuanced," Pakosta said.

She did not agree to discuss the content of the bill, including how the current draft differs from the version she withdrew from the process in 2024.

"Once again, the bill is still being drafted," she said.

When Pakosta halted the processing of the gender equality and equal opportunities bill prepared at the Ministry of Economic Affairs in May 2024, the Ministry of Justice commissioned a new perspective from the private sector — from the law firm Sorainen — without informing the NGOs and the office of the equal treatment commissioner who had worked on the earlier draft.

Although Pakosta insisted Sorainen was not commissioned to write a bill, as media reported at the time based on ministry information, but only preparatory materials, she still chose to keep those materials from the public. She also did not show the newly completed analysis to equal treatment commissioner Christian Veske, who requested it, or to the equality policy department at the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

As before, Pakosta justified the secrecy by citing the need to avoid confusion. "There was just a major public confusion over the statute of limitations for sexual crimes against children, which shows how easily confusion can arise. That is exactly why the law states that preparatory materials are not always public. In this case, the Data Protection Inspectorate has confirmed that," Pakosta said.

Gender Equality and Equal Treatment Commissioner Christian Veske. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Commissioner skeptical about timeline

Although Pakosta said Estonians are currently well protected against discrimination, equal opportunities commissioner Christian Veske wrote to the minister in summer with a series of proposals, including a recommendation to complete the processing of the equal opportunities bill and ensure equal legal protection for everyone.

In her autumn response, Pakosta wrote that the ministry considers the issues addressed in the bill very important and added that the bill concerns socially significant and sensitive matters that require thorough consideration of different rights, interests and positions. "We consider it important that these positions be taken into account in shaping equal opportunities policy," she wrote.

Commenting on Pakosta's response to ERR, Veske said it seemed rather vague. Based on it, he finds it hard to believe the bill will be processed during the current Riigikogu term. "Especially considering that none of the relevant parties have received any substantive information about the bill," Veske said.

Because withdrawing the earlier bill angered the NGOs and the equal treatment commissioner's office that had worked on it, Pakosta repeatedly promised at the time that she would definitely submit the new bill for consultation, where all stakeholders could give feedback. "I confirm that we are ready for full cooperation with the relevant state agencies and advocacy organizations," Pakosta said.

Veske, who has had no information about the bill for the past two years, also has no knowledge of any planned stakeholder consultation. He hopes it will still happen. "It would be very poor legislative practice if the ministry wanted to skip the consultation round. There may be some legal obstacles to skipping it, but since this is a Ministry of Justice bill, they likely know that better," Veske said.

In response to ERR's question about whether consultation will take place, Pakosta said it is still planned. She did not say when.

Justice Minister Liisa Pakosta decided at the end of 2024 to halt and not send for official government coordination the gender equality and equal opportunities bill prepared at the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

The bill aimed to merge two existing laws — the Gender Equality Act and the Equal Treatment Act — into one comprehensive legal act. It sought to resolve a long‑standing legal gap in Estonia where protection against discrimination is not equal across all characteristics. Pakosta said she halted the bill because of extensive legal criticism and conflicting feedback.

World.title: Circuit court orders DJ to serve actual prison time in rape sentence
World.content:
A court has overturned a ruling ruling that suspended a three-year rape sentence, imposed on a DJ, ordering him to serve the term in prison.

The Tallinn Circuit Court overturned the earlier county court ruling on Meelis Eskola, known as DJ Cityflash,

He was convicted in April 2025 of raping a young mother at a party venue in Paide in May 2022. Eskola denies the charges.

The circuit court, the second tier of the Estonian court system and which acts as an appeal court, overturned that part of the Pärnu County Court's earlier ruling that left the three-year prison sentence for rape conditionally unenforced.

Under the circuit court's fresh ruling, Eskola must serve real prison time.

The county court had found Eskola guilty of rape and sentenced him to three years in prison with a four-year probation period. He was also ordered to pay €7,000 in non-pecuniary damages to the victim.

Eskola's appeal went through all three court tiers. The Supreme Court upheld his conviction and the civil claim in May of this year, but sent the question of enforcing the sentence back to the circuit court for reconsideration.

Since the conviction and civil claim had already entered into force, the circuit court considered the case solely on the basis of a prosecutor's appeal, which sought Eskola's incarceration.

Under Supreme Court precedent, actual imprisonment is the rule for more serious crimes, and deviation from that — e.g. a suspended sentence — is justified only in exceptional circumstances, which must be apparent both in the act committed and in the offender's personhood, the court found.

The circuit court found that the arguments presented by Eskola's defense — such as the one-off or unintentional nature of the act — did not constitute exceptional circumstances. The court noted that the rape provision itself provides for liability for a single act, and that the county court's assessment of the offense as "average" in fact confirms the absence of exceptional mitigating circumstances.

Given the gravity of the crime — raping the victim in several ways, exploiting another individual's helpless state and using violence — and the absence of mitigating circumstances, the court found no basis for more lenient treatment of Eskola than imprisonment.

The circuit court's ruling can be appealed to the Supreme Court within 30 days.

Eskola stood trial on charges under the Penal Code provision on rape. According to the charge, he had sexual intercourse against the victim's will, at a party venue in the central Estonian town of Paide, on May 7, 2022.

According to the indictment Eskola dragged the victim, a young mother, into a rest room and threw her onto a pool table. The victim attempted to push him away but was unable to, after which the defendant had intercourse with her, causing her pain during the act, pressing a pillow into her face and pulling her hair. An examination found bruises and abrasions on the victim's body, including on her legs, buttocks and genitals.

According to the charge, Eskola committed the rape with violence. He also exploited the fact that the woman was unable to resist due to alcohol intoxication and being physically weaker than him.

In the civil claim, the victim sought non-pecuniary damages from the defendant at the court's discretion.

At the first two court levels — Pärnu County Court and Tallinn Circuit Court — Eskola was acquitted. On November 1, 2024, however, the Supreme Court overturned that acquittal too, finding among other things that the courts had given the defendant's statements preferential treatment to the victim's and had not compellingly justify their positions.

The Pärnu County Court found Eskola guilty on April 8, 2025 and sentenced him to three years in prison, suspended with a four-year probation period, and ordered him to pay €7,000 in non-pecuniary damages.

On November 25, 2025, the Tallinn Circuit Court overturned that sentence and the damages award, imposing one year and six months, suspended with a two-year probation period, and €2,500 in damages.

On May 29 this year, the Supreme Court overturned the circuit court's ruling and reinstated the county court's, except for the part suspending the sentence, and sent the case back to the Tallinn Circuit Court for reconsideration in a different composition.

World.title: Father of 3: The first child benefit should be very generous in Estonia
World.content:
Director Madis Ligema, who recently became a father for the third time, told ETV that while money does not necessarily motivate people to have children, more generous benefits could increase the number of births in Estonia.

"The benefit for the first child in particular should be massive to encourage people to have that first child because once you have the first, then the second and third — and perhaps even a fourth — will follow," Madis Ligema said.

Economist and Family Foundation supervisory board member Raul Eamets, however, stressed the importance of supporting families having a third child.

"When people are planning a third child, it actually means a kind of qualitative change in their living arrangements because it means needing an extra room or a larger car, as three child seats won't fit in every car. Why is the issue of a third child so important? Half of Estonia's children live in families with three or more children," Eamets explained.

Parental benefit and a fixed percentage of GDP

As one way of increasing the birth rate, Eamets suggested extending parental benefits to parents who stay at home: "There are certainly parents, whether fathers or mothers, who do this, but we have taken that option away from them. I, for example, really liked Heido Vitsur and Indrek Neivelt's proposal that if you have decided to raise children full time, you receive the Estonian median wage — their proposal was €500 per child, so if you have three children, that would be €1,500," Eamets said.

Member of the European Parliament Jana Toom (Center Party) said Estonia should make supporting families with children a national priority and allocate a fixed share of the budget to it.

"Our child benefits are shamefully low. We have an extraordinarily high percentage of children living in relative poverty and outright poverty," said Toom, a mother of five. "We need to develop a national policy specifically focused on children and allocate a certain percentage of GDP to it, just as we do with defense," Toom said.

Inconsistent support measures rob people of certainty

According to Elin Järvsaar, editor-in-chief of "Pere ja Kodu," stability in benefits is important to parents, while constant changes to legislation discourage young people from becoming parents.

"More important than the amounts is a sense of security. In recent years, we have made a great many changes to the system of family benefits and allowances. That provides no sense of security whatsoever — up and down, back and forth, the rules keep changing," said Järvsaar, a mother of four. "The system has been made so complicated and it gives me no confidence that I will have support for 18 years. Even if parental benefits or other benefits are extremely generous, I know that four years from now they could be completely different and I don't dare take that step," Järvsaar explained.

Raul Eamets agreed that the demographic problem requires a long-term agreement similar to that on national defense. "Family policy and demographic issues are every bit as important as security, meaning that we need a consensus across society and across party lines. By now, I think all parties have realized that this is a problem, but what we need now are decisions that extend beyond election cycles and strategic decisions. One coalition raises benefits, the next lowers them — I completely understand women wondering how they can dare take those risks under such circumstances. Otherwise, we will simply die out," Eamets said.

A total of 9,240 children were born in Estonia in 2025, a record low. During the discussion, Eamets predicted that the number of births could fall below 9,000 this year.

World.title: Estonia might struggle to fill conscript ranks with men alone in the near future
World.content:
Filling the required number of conscript positions with men alone could soon become difficult as the number of male births declines, Anu Rannaveski, director general of the Defense Resources Agency, said.

Rannaveski said the commander of the Estonian Defense Forces determines the number of conscripts each year. That figure, in turn, is based on the number of reservists needed. In recent years, the number of conscripts has ranged from around 3,600 to 3,800. Starting next year, up to 4,100 conscripts will be called up for military service.

According to Rannaveski, around 50 women enter military service each year. Women have been able to volunteer for military service since 2013 and the figure has generally remained at around 50 since then. "There have been a couple of years when there were 60 women and there have been years when there were 45, but it has remained at around 50," Rannaveski said. She added that women account for 1 to 2 percent of conscripts.

Conscript need must be met

Rannaveski noted that demographic trends show the number of boys being born is declining and the situation will get progressively worse. Rannaveski added that the Defense Forces will nevertheless have to find a way to reach the target of 4,100 conscripts.

In 2025, Estonia's total births came to 9,240, including 4,789 boys.

She explained that more than half of Estonian society currently has little opportunity to contribute to national defense. Rannaveski said women do have the option of entering military service, but they have to find the motivation to do so themselves. By contrast, the state actively reaches out to men, she noted.

Women can currently serve in a variety of units. "The concern that there are specific roles for women is certainly unfounded — women perform very well across the board," Rannaveski said.

Both men and women improve their physical abilities during military service. "When we talk about young men entering military service, only about a third meet the physical requirements that are actually needed," Rannaveski said.

She said that during military service, women want to have access to the same information as the rest of their unit. As a result, they stay in the same barracks and rooms as the men. "They use the lockers there to divide up the room and create some privacy for themselves," Rannaveski said. However, separate hygiene facilities are generally provided for women.

Changes in order

The director said that between 2035 and 2040, it will become difficult to fill the required number of conscript positions with young men alone. She added that in that case, a more compulsory system would have to be introduced.

Rannaveski said Estonia should develop a system that works for the country. She noted that in Norway, Sweden and Denmark, not all women are required to perform military service. "They have criteria: who is the most highly motivated and who has the knowledge, experience and skills that the Defense Forces need," she explained.

She noted she hopes Estonia will adopt a similar approach, adding that making military service mandatory for everyone would also not be a good fit as there would be more people than conscript positions.

World.title: Restaurant spaces in Tallinn do not stay empty for long
World.content:
Many eateries in Tallinn have closed over the past year. Real estate agencies say, however, that there are still plenty of entrepreneurs who want to open new places. Interest from business owners coming from Asia has grown, for example.

This year, restaurants such as Tai Boh, Boheem, Vatikan, Manna La Rosa, Ülo and La Tabla have closed. Even Siili Sahver, a lunch spot that survived the COVID crisis, shut down.

Aira Veelmaa, a commercial real estate broker at Uus Maa, said the situation is not as difficult as media coverage might suggest.

"Looking at the commercial property market, I would say restaurant spaces are among the most sought‑after. There are quite a few people who want to start something new. There is also a more exotic group of clients who have come to Estonia and want to start a business here. Not knowing the Estonian market, they often have more enthusiasm than locals," Veelmaa said.

By "more exotic regions," Veelmaa means people from the Middle East and other parts of Asia.

Popular restaurant spaces often have several interested tenants. Still, some areas are more difficult, such as Narva maantee, where places constantly change. Despite the busy location, restaurants there often do not last long, Veelmaa noted.

The situation is most challenging for eateries located in office buildings because many people work from home. Owners also have to make sure there are not too many food places nearby, since there may not be enough customers for all of them.

But the trend is slightly positive, and more entrepreneurs are looking to open new places, Veelmaa said.

Tanel Tarum of the real estate agency 1Partner also said the situation is not as bad as it may seem from media reports.

"If we look at how many new places are opening, the balance in Tallinn is zero," Tarum said.

He acknowledged that people's movement patterns have changed over time, and areas like Telliskivi and the Volta quarter now see more foot traffic than a few years ago. He added that one reason for closures is insufficient groundwork before opening a restaurant.

World.title: Tallinn Airport sets record for September, but winter traffic expected to fall
World.content:
Tallinn Airport reported it handled nearly 356,000 passengers in September, up 13 percent on the same month last year — the busiest September in the airport's history.

In the first nine months of the year, the airport reported serving a total of 2.89 million passengers, up 12 percent on the same period last year.

Despite the record, the airport expects a decline in numbers over the winter.

Tallinn Airport spokesperson Aet Härmaorg told ERR the past 12 months have all been records on the month, adding the "all-time record was exceeded in four months: May, June, July and August 2026."

Scheduled flights operated from Tallinn to 41 destinations in September. Passenger growth was driven primarily by no-frills carrier Wizz Air, which has expanded significantly in Tallinn over the past year.

In September, the airline carried 16 percent of all Tallinn Airport passengers and offered connections to nine destinations. airBaltic remained the airport's largest airline, with a market share of 27 percent. In total, 22 airlines operated scheduled and charter flights from Tallinn to more than 50 destinations during the month.

Scheduled flights accounted for 90 percent of passengers, while charter flights accounted for 10 percent. Antalya, Turkey, was the main charter destination, with holiday destinations in Greece and Montenegro also proving popular.

While winter is the off-season, there is a winter travel season, starting September, to destinations in Egypt.

Warsaw was the most popular direct destination for scheduled flights in September, followed by Helsinki, Riga, Stockholm and Frankfurt.

The number of aircraft movements also rose, by 5 percent compared with September last year. There were 4,031 landings and take-offs in total, averaging 134 aircraft movements per day.

Eero Pärgmäe, commercial director at Tallinn Airport, said the passenger records show the summer schedule was exceptionally dense. "The growth that Wizz Air started at the end of last year is still carrying us," Pärgmäe told ERR.

Nonetheless, some developments will lead to a fall in numbers over winter. "airBaltic has said it is cutting its schedule due to the restructuring it is currently carrying out. And the second thing is that, since the price of aviation fuel remains exceptionally high, most carriers have said that the high fuel price is hurting them and they will be scaling back their schedules in winter," Pärgmäe went on.

"If we look at next year, we are moving toward last year's level or even a little below," he added.

Passenger numbers also rose at Estonia's regional airports, which fall under the Tallinn Airport umbrella. Together, they served 9,078 passengers in September, compared with 8,191 in September last year. Tartu Airport took in 4,847 passengers, Kuressaare Airport 3,008 and Kärdla Airport 1,111. Pärnu Airport served 104 passengers and Ruhnu Airfield eight.

Tallinn Airport also says it expects higher passenger numbers during the busy school holiday travel period, October 21-November 4. For this reason the airport recommends arriving at the terminal at least two hours before departure time, as check-in, security screening and passport control can take longer than usual. Passengers arriving by car should allow extra time to find a parking space too.

World.title: Cost of new Iisaku school building nearly doubles
World.content:
The cost of building a new school for Iisaku Basic School in Alutaguse municipality has risen far beyond initial plans. The opposition is unhappy with how the process has been handled and intends to file a no‑confidence motion against the mayor.

Originally, most of the funding was to come from the state, which supported the municipality after it closed Iisaku's high school level. During the process, the scope of construction expanded and the price nearly doubled from the initial €6.8 million. For the municipality, this means contributing around €6 million, most of which will be covered by loans. Municipal leaders say they are confident the municipality can manage the debt.

"It was a simple choice: either accept the state support and build, even if our share becomes larger than planned, or not build. I'm glad the council decided to take the support and complete the school building as planned. I think it's a forward‑looking and correct decision for Alutaguse municipality," said Mayor Tauno Võhmar.

The opposition says several mistakes were made in the process.

"We were not shown the new budget strategy, nor was there a supplementary budget. The mayor had no right to enter a procurement with a much larger construction volume without council approval. The opposition will move forward with a no‑confidence motion because we do not trust this mayor and do not approve of this behavior," said opposition representative Annely Oone.

Iisaku Basic School currently has around 100 students. The new school building is expected to be completed next autumn and is designed for 135 students.

World.title: Iraq lowers currency exchange rate to 1,500 dinars per US dollar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved on Tuesday the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) established a multi-tiered exchange framework to facilitate the transition across commercial and banking channels.

An exchange rate of 1,500 Iraqi dinars per US dollar is now used for government purchases from the Finance Ministry, 1,510 Iraqi dinars for official sales to commercial banking institutions, and 1,520 Iraqi dinars for public consumers who buy foreign currency directly from banks.

The forceful monetary policy shift acts as a direct fiscal stabilization mechanism in response to significant macroeconomic shocks.

The regional conflict has severely affected important marine trade routes, including partial closures and interruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Since oil exports account for about 90 percent of Iraq’s national finances, transportation delays reduced real export capacity to around 2.34 million barrels per day compared to 3.6 million.

The Finance Ministry informed the Iraqi parliament that it would be unable to cover the domestic budget for 2026 unless the dinar was revalued.

By demanding more local dinars for every US dollar of incoming oil revenue, the Iraqi government generates artificial liquidity to meet rising public expenditure, local deficits, and civil service salaries.

The depreciation is intended to reduce the disparity between the government’s stated measurements and parallel market realities.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet also prohibited the collection of advance customs duties on foreign imports to reduce unexpected operational disruptions within business supply chains.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China surpass $51 billion in 2025
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, revealed on Tuesday that the trade exchange between Iraq and China exceeded $51 billion in 2025.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), Bo noted that relations between China and Iraq are continually improving. He emphasized that Iraq is a crucial partner for China in the Belt and Road Initiative, which has yielded positive outcomes.

Major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure, according to Bo.

Bo emphasized that the cooperation between the two countries is based on shared interests and is continuously developing.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

The two countries’ strong economic interdependence assures a bright future and enormous possibilities for collaboration, according to Bo.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in various Iraqi provinces.

China’s investments in Iraq are also rapidly rising, notably in infrastructure and energy.

World.title: Iraq advances as Gulf-Europe data hub with iQ Networks, Ooredoo fibre deal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s iQ Networks and OFN, the international connectivity arm of Qatar’s Ooredoo Group, have agreed to build a high-capacity fibre connection across Iraq, furthering ambitions to connect the Gulf and Asia to Turkey and Europe via Iraqi territory.

According to the arrangement, OFN will buy numerous dark fibre pairs from iQ Networks for international transit throughout Iraq.

The terrestrial network will link to Ooredoo’s proposed Fibre in Gulf (FIG) subsea cable infrastructure, creating a single route for international data traffic.

The project might boost Iraq’s position as a regional digital transit center, using the country’s geographical location between the Arabian Gulf, Turkey, and Europe to transport increasing quantities of international data.

FIG is intended to link Qatar, Oman, the UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Iraq with a capacity of up to 720 terabits per second across 24 fibre pairs.

OFN has also struck a landing agreement with the state-owned Iraqi Telecommunications and Post Company (ITPC) to send the undersea cable into Iraq.

From there, iQ Networks’ terrestrial infrastructure will transport connections north across the nation to Turkey and European markets.

According to the firms, the new corridor will serve as an extra route between the Gulf and Europe while also increasing network resilience and capacity.

The need for such infrastructure is fast expanding as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data centers, telecom operators, and big technology businesses require increasing quantities of international bandwidth.

The deal was signed at the Ooredoo Group’s headquarters in Doha by top Iraqi communications authorities as well as executives from Ooredoo, OFN, ITPC, and iQ Networks.

For Iraq, the initiative is part of a larger attempt to transform its position into an economic benefit by attracting international data traffic that would otherwise utilize other regional routes.

The infrastructure might also help Iraq’s developing digital economy and data center industry, as well as provide new possibilities for foreign traffic passing through the country.

Implementation will continue in accordance with the agreed-upon plan, subject to regulatory and government approval.

The initiative is another step toward establishing Iraq as a digital bridge between Asia, the Arabian Gulf, and Europe, broadening the country’s significance beyond conventional energy and commercial channels.

World.title: US dollar surges past 180,000 IQD amid parallel market disruption
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Parallel currency exchanges across Iraq experienced severe disruption and sharp price swings on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, after the federal government abruptly modified the official exchange rate benchmark to 1,500 dinars per dollar for purchases and 1,520 dinars for retail sales to citizens.

The unexpected regulatory shift sent shockwaves through cash trading floors, propelling parallel dollar prices past the 170,000-dinar threshold per $100 and triggering deep regional rate discrepancies across major commercial centers.

Trading data collated across provincial exchanges reflected widespread variance as exchange desks struggled with price discovery. In Baghdad, cash selling rates settled at 170,000 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 168,250 dinars. In Erbil, the commercial hub of the Kurdistan Region, prices surged even higher, with sales touching 180,000 dinars alongside a wide bid-ask spread anchored by buying offers at 166,500 dinars.

In the southern port city of Basra, trading desks quoted selling rates at 179,000 dinars per $100 against buying bids of 178,000 dinars, reflecting intense localized demand for physical greenbacks.

The rapid escalation in currency volatility coincided with growing legislative mobilization inside parliament, where lawmakers have begun organizing appeals for an emergency parliamentary session.

Proponents of the emergency hearing aim to legally compel the executive branch to reverse the sudden exchange rate hike and assess the broader economic and living strains imposed on households, warning that runaway parallel spreads risk amplifying retail inflation and destabilizing domestic supply chains.

World.title: Iraqi MP demands emergency session as official dollar hike paralyzes markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Member of Parliament Miqdad Al-Khafaji called on the Council of Representatives on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, to convene an immediate emergency session to compel the federal government to reverse its decision devaluing the Iraqi dinar against the U.S. dollar.

The legislative push comes as the official adjustment to 1,500 dinars per dollar triggers immediate price shocks, widespread commercial freezes, and severe market gridlock across Iraqi wholesale hubs.

In a formal statement, Al-Khafaji criticized the government’s fiscal priorities, pointing out that political factions continue to expand administrative overhead and create patronized public positions that bloat state expenditures, while forcing ordinary citizens to absorb the financial fallout of structural deficits.

Al-Khafaji warned that devaluing the currency directly erodes the real purchasing power of fixed-income public servants, daily wage laborers, and low-income families, emphasizing that a public already strained by regional tensions cannot endure additional economic shocks.

Currency analysts and market participants anticipate that parallel exchange desks will soon test psychological highs of 180,000 dinars per $100 as greenback liquidity tightens.

The rapid depreciation of the dinar in real terms has triggered public frustration across Iraqi cities, where consumer earnings and local commerce remain heavily denominated in local currency.

On the commercial front, the devaluation has delivered immediate ripple effects to retail and wholesale food supply networks:

Retail Food Surges: Nabhan Al-Ahmad, a commercial market owner in Saladin Governorate, reported that consumer food staples experienced an immediate price hike of roughly 25 percent within hours of the cabinet announcement. A standard sack of rice that previously retailed for 45,000 dinars spiked to 50,000 dinars, with proportional increases hitting sugar, cooking oil, and packaged goods.

Distribution Freezes: Yousef Al-Rubaie, a sales agent for food distributor Altunsa, confirmed that major regional food supply and FMCG distribution firms have suspended shipments and wholesale deliveries until further notice to protect operational capital against volatile replacement costs.

Shorja Commercial Stagnation: In Baghdad’s central commercial district of Al-Shorja, wholesale centers have ground to an effective standstill. Abu Ahmed Al-Asadi, a prominent commercial center owner in Shorja, described the wholesale sector as completely paralyzed. Al-Asadi explained that activity had already begun stalling two weeks earlier amid regional geopolitical tensions and rising exchange rates, adding that the official devaluation has shut down the market entirely, forcing most wholesale merchants to shutter storefronts and suspend trade until currency volatility stabilizes.

As legislative calls grow for parliamentary intervention, commercial friction and consumer uncertainty continue to mount, presenting the administration with significant economic headwinds following its statutory rate revision.

World.title: Iraq Integrity Commission uncovers 2.19B IQD embezzlement in Salah Al-Din
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Federal Commission of Integrity announced on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, the uncovering of a major embezzlement scheme within the Salah Al-Din Traffic Directorate, involving the fraudulent manipulation of more than 56,000 official traffic citation receipts and the misappropriation of over 2.192 billion Iraqi dinars ($1.46 million at the newly adjusted official rate).

Investigators seized original forged accounting records and brought five senior ranking officers—including a brigadier general and four colonels—under active criminal inquiry.

According to an official statement, specialized field teams from the Commission’s Saladin Investigation Office audited financial ledgers and cross-matched serial numbers, exposing two distinct schemes operating within the governorate’s vehicle registration and driver licensing divisions:

The First Operation (1.853 Billion IQD): Investigators identified that the head of the Fines and Thefts Division at the Vehicle Registration and Driver Licensing Complex—a police officer holding the rank of colonel who is currently detained—systematically altered 34,164 traffic violation receipts under his legal custody. He embezzled 1,853,200,000 IQD in cash receipts. Executing a warrant issued by the Saladin Investigation Judge for Integrity Cases, anti-corruption agents raided the directorate and seized the physical originals of all 34,164 manipulated receipts.

The Second Operation (339.135 Million IQD): Further forensic audits revealed a parallel scheme executed by a second detained officer, also holding the rank of colonel. The suspect manipulated on-the-spot traffic citation forms and doctored ledger remittances, embezzling 339,135,000 IQD.The team seized 22,000 altered payment vouchers, specifically official standard revenue forms “Account 38” and “Account 68”.

The Commission confirmed that legal proceedings have expanded to include three additional supervisory officers: a brigadier general and two colonels. The senior officers face prosecution for dereliction of supervisory duty and failing to verify fine remittances, negligence that allowed the multi-billion-dinar fraud to persist undetected.

Formal seizure records, confiscated ledgers, and forensic documentary evidence were submitted to the competent investigating judge.The cases are being prosecuted under Article 315 of the Iraqi Penal Code No. 111 of 1969, which governs the embezzlement of public funds by state officials and carries severe statutory penalties, as judicial authorities continue interrogations to identify all co-conspirators.

World.title: Iraq officially devalues the dinar to 1,500 per USD
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Finance officially enacted a structural adjustment to the national currency on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, resetting the official baseline exchange rate to 1,500 Iraqi dinars per U.S. dollar, while abruptly halting the advance collection of customs tariffs and tax deposits on foreign imports.

The dual decision marks an immediate fiscal and monetary overhaul aimed at realigning official exchange metrics with market realities and easing operational gridlock across the country’s commercial supply chains.

According to a formal ministerial statement, the action implements Iraqi Cabinet Resolution No. 544 of 2026, adopted during the Council of Ministers’ executive session on Tuesday, October 6.

The decision formally alters the central parity framework that had pegged the dinar at 1,310 per dollar since early 2023. Under the updated regulatory mechanics detailed by the General Secretariat of the Council of Ministers, the new pricing ladder establishes:

1,500 IQD per USD: The sovereign purchase rate from the Ministry of Finance.

1,510 IQD per USD: The Central Bank of Iraq’s official wholesale selling rate to licensed commercial banks.

1,520 IQD per USD:The final retail selling ceiling permitted for licensed banks and non-banking financial institutions to end-beneficiaries and private importers.

Simultaneously, the ministry terminated Cabinet Resolution No. 413 of 2026, which had enforced the mandatory advance collection of customs tariffs and estimated income tax deposits prior to outward wire transfers.

The advance-settlement regime, originally passed on August 18 and made operational on October 1, required registered merchants to deposit import funds with commercial banks, forbidding international remittances until all projected customs assessments and duties were calculated and prepaid through the ASYCUDA automated system and certified electronic payment gateways.

The requirement had triggered friction within merchant trade unions and wholesale supply networks, contributing to a severe cash bottleneck as traders turned to the parallel market to bypass advance tax liabilities—a dynamic that pushed cash dollar prices above 160,500 dinars per $100 earlier in the week.

The suspension of advance collections provides relief to commercial importers who have faced overlapping regulatory updates throughout 2026.

These earlier changes included the General Commission of Customs’ rollout of the revised 2026 tariff schedule under Customs Tariff Law No. 22 of 2010—which raised automotive import duties to 15 percent, revoked tax exemptions on hybrid vehicles, and replaced flat container fees with itemized cargo classification under Cabinet Resolution No. 957 of 2025.

By adjusting the statutory peg to 1,500 dinars and suspending upfront tariff deductions, federal authorities aim to stabilize the parallel currency gap, reduce speculative volatility, and restore structured liquidity across Iraq’s foreign trade channels.

World.title: Iraqi policeman killed in terrorist attack near Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two security sources told Reuters that ISIS terrorists assaulted a federal police post near the northern Iraqi city of Kirkuk on Monday, killing at least one Iraqi federal policeman and injuring four others.

The assailants used semi-automatic machine guns and sniper fire on the federal police unit stationed in Hawija, around 70 kilometers (43 miles) southwest of Kirkuk.

No one immediately claimed responsibility. However, security and army officials indicated ISIS militants, who are still active in the area, were responsible for the attack.

The raid is the first documented assault by ISIS terrorists on Iraqi security forces since US troops withdrew from the country on September 30, terminating the military operation in Iraq.

The United States led the international coalition that aided Iraqi forces in their war against terrorism, including measures to keep the extremist organization from reorganizing.

Washington said that it will continue to offer targeted training and intelligence assistance following the departure, but Iraqi forces would be fully responsible for the country’s security and the suppression of remnants of terrorist groups.

Despite the defeat of the terrorist group over a decade ago, Iraqi security officials told Reuters that the organization still has sleeper cells in the country.

The pullout of the US-led international coalition raised concerns that a security vacuum would allow the terrorist group to recover momentum, with some officials warning that Iraqi security forces would now have to hold the group without the coalition’s military presence.

NEW DELHI: The Ministry of External Affairs (Mea) on Wednesday condemned a string of attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea region, including ships carrying Indian seafarers.

India called for an immediate end to attacks that threaten commercial shipping and endanger the lives of seafarers.

Mea spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India was monitoring the situation and assisting Indian nationals affected by the attacks.

âWe have seen a string of attacks in the Black Sea region in the last one or two days. We condemn such attacks that threaten commercial shipping and endanger the lives of our seafaring community,â Jaiswal said at a bi-weekly media briefing.

Jaiswal said the commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov came under attack while sailing in the Black Sea. Three Indian nationals were on board, all of whom were safe, though one was injured and receiving medical treatment.

âWe condemn such attacks that threaten commercial shipping and endanger, first, the commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov came under attack while it was sailing in the Black Sea. There were three Indian nationals on board.





All of them are safe, but one of them got injured and is receiving medical treatment. We thank Romanian authorities for lending a helping hand in this particular incident,â Jaiswal said.

He further mentioned that another vessel, the Palau-flagged MV Able, came under a drone attack, but all 18 crew members, including seven Indian nationals, were rescued.

All 23 crew members on board this particular ship are Indian nationals and all of them have been rescued", Jaiswal said.

Meanwhile, the Indian Embassy in Romania said that a representative of the Embassy met three Indian nationals rescued from the commercial vessel M V Royad Mammadov on Tuesday. World.title: Consensual relation turns sour: Woman cannot use ‘strong-arm tactic’ against man
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has held that a criminal prosecution cannot be reduced to a âstrong-arm tacticâ to force a person to marry by lodging a case of rape after consensual relations did not fructify in nuptial ties.

It quashed criminal proceedings against a man which were initiated by his girlfriend after the relationship turned sour after three years of courtship.

A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said consent allegedly under fear or misconception cannot be loosely inferred to fasten criminal liability on one of the parties when both admittedly had a consensual relationship and the other party willingly permitted a physical relationship.

It said that a consensual relationship spread over three years has eventually ended with a criminal case lodged against the man in this case and it cannot be allowed.

âEven on a bare reading of the complaint, there is no clear assurance or a promise made of marriage, since the specific allegation is that they entered into a physical relationship after courtship, fully knowing the consequences, but alleged to be under the pretext of marriage; clearly an afterthought.





The respondent (the woman) is a well-educated woman, who entered into a consensual relationship and carried it on for three years, allegedly on the pretext of marriage, which never fructified.

She categorically states that she would drop the charge if he marries her. A criminal prosecution cannot be reduced to a strong-arm tactic,â the bench said.

Referring to the apex courtâs earlier order, the bench said there must be adequate evidence to show that at the initial stage itself, the accused had no intention whatsoever of keeping his promise to marry the victim.

It said there may be circumstances when a person having the best of intentions is unable to marry the victim owing to various unavoidable circumstances.

âIn order to come within the meaning of the term âmisconception of factâ, the fact must have an immediate relevance. Section 90 IPC (Consent given under fear or misconception) cannot be called into aid in such a situation, to pardon the act of a girl in entirety, and fasten criminal liability on the other, unless the court is assured of the fact that from the very beginning, the accused had never really intended to marry her,â the bench noted.

In this case, the girl met the accused at an academy, wherein both were enrolled. Admittedly, they fell in love and their family members also talked to each other. On an understanding that they would be married, he used to visit her house, where she lived with her mother and brother. When nobody was at home, they entered into a physical relationship, which continued thereafter for about three years. Admittedly, the physical relationship continued for three years unabated and later they separated.

World.title: Police detain opposition MPs trying to reach Jantar Mantar for anti-CEC protest - top developments
World.content:
Delhi Police detaining Rahul Gandhi

Nitin Nabin slams Rahul Gandhi

Congress workers puncture tyres of bus carrying Rahul Gandhi

Rahul, Priyanka and other protesters taken away in buses

Delhi Police detain protesters

Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lies down on road

Mahua Moitra alleges lathi-charge by Delhi Police

Delhi Police stops opposition MPs' buses

Congress MPs climb atop bus

'Every FIR is medal for me': Rahul Gandhi

Jantar Mantar fortified

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police on Wednesday detained opposition MPs as they tried to protest for a second straight day against Chief Election Commisisoner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Buses carrying opposition MPs were stopped before Jantar Mantar, a day after police stopped the INDIA bloc leaders' march to the Election Commission (EC) office. They tried to stage a sit-in after their buses were halted but were detained and removed after a brief struggle.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge announced the decision to hold an impromptu protest at Jantar Mantar after hosting INDIA bloc leaders for lunch at a restaurant in Janpath, central Delhi.âToday, we will hold a sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar. Until our demands are met, we will continue to stage such protests,â Kharge told reporters outside the restaurant.The Congress-led INDIA bloc is demanding CEC Kumarâs resignation following an Indian Express report that the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had formally raised objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge.However, the EC later said disagreements are normal in a multi-member institution and that all decisions were ultimately taken unanimously by the CEC and the two Election Commissioners.The poll panel is required to take decisions either by consensus among all three members or by a 2-1 majority.The leader of opposition of this country is working with anti-social elements in an atmosphere of anarchy. I would like to tell him clearly that the people of India will never let his motive and intent become a reality. He has only cared about people who snatch away the rights of the public here. He is trying to spread anarchy in Delhi with the help of anti-social elements. I would like to tell the leader of opposition that the people about whom he speaks of getting their rights, people of India will never let such infiltrators be given rights. Who do you care about? Who are you fighting for?...If names of such infiltrators are struck off through SIR and still you are questioning the democracy of the country over it, the biggest question being raised is about you. Such an anarchist mindset will be given a reply to by the people of India: BJP president Nitin NabinCongress workers resisted police attempts to take Rahul Gandhi away from the protest site and punctured the tyres of the bus carrying him and other protesters.Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other protesters taken away in a Delhi Police bus.Delhi Police detained Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other MPs after they tried to stage a sit-in after their buses were stopped before they could reach Jantar Mantar protest against CEC Kumar. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra alleged she was manhandled by police officials.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other female MPs lie down on the road after police stop their buses from reaching Jantar Mantar to protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.You can see the brute force with which Delhi Police is handling peaceful protesters. Gyanesh Kumar has to resign. What is our fault? Why are the workers, the public being brutally manhandled and lathi-charged by the Delhi Police. Why are MPs being blocked from reaching Jantar Mantar? What is going on here? Mahua Moitra, TMC MPThe Delhi Police stopped the buses carrying opposition MPs on Ashoka Road before it could reach Jantar Mantar, saying permission for protests at the venue must be sought at least 10 days in advance."This is Rahul Gandhi's 'sena,' we won't stop," said Congress MP Amarinder Singh Raja Warring.Congress leaders Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, Imran Pratpgarhi and Imran Masood climbed atop the bus carrying the MPs.Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, who was at the centre of Tuesdayâs protest with a nine-hour sit-in at Akashvani Bhavan, the All India Radio headquarters near the EC office, said his goal was to have â100 FIRsâ.The Delhi Police have registered an FIR against Rahul Gandhi and his sister and fellow Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra over their âunauthorisedâ entry into Akashvani Bhavan."I have 45 FIRs against me. My goal is to have 100. I want 100 FIRs to be registered against me. Every FIR is a medal for me," he told reporters.Delhi Police beefed up security in anticipation of a possible opposition protest. The force also cited a Supreme Court directive to justify its decision not to grant permission for a sit-in at Jantar Mantar, Delhiâs designated protest venue.âAs per the order of the Supreme Court in Writ Petition (Civil), Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan vs. Union of India & Others, and the Delhi Police Standing Order issued in compliance with the said order, prior permission of the competent authority is mandatory for organising any meeting, demonstration, sit-in, or protest at Jantar Mantar,â a Delhi Police statement read.âApplications seeking such permission are required to be submitted to the Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi District, at least 10 days prior to the proposed event,â the statement added.

World.title: Tiruppur Kumaran: a sacrifice that defied the British Raj
World.content:
The year 1932 began ominously for satyagrahis of the freedom struggle. The British Raj was no longer in any mood to keep the Congress in good humour. Amid the severe impact of the Great Depression, a “national” government assumed office in London in August, with Ramsay MacDonald of the Labour Party as Prime Minister and Stanley Baldwin of the Conservative Party as the virtual second in command. Liberals were also part of MacDonald’s Cabinet. In a few months, it scored a landslide victory in the general elections. In New Delhi, Willingdon had become the Viceroy, replacing Irwin, who struck a pact with Mahatma Gandhi in March 1931 and adopted a conciliatory approach towards Gandhi and the Congress.

Willingdon was no Irwin. By the time Gandhi returned to Mumbai on December 28 after a four-month visit to England, where he attended the Second Round Table Conference, the Raj had not only abandoned the pact but had also begun repressive measures in many provinces, including Bengal and the United Provinces (now called Uttar Pradesh). The rule by ordinance was in place, with 15 ordinances having been promulgated, under which, as recorded by Tara Chand in History of Freedom Movement in India (Volume 4), “it [the government] was committing harrowing barbarities and ruthless repression.” Two days before Gandhi’s arrival, Jawaharlal Nehru was arrested. A “Civil Martial Law” had been clamped.

Gandhi’s arrest

On January 1, 1932, Gandhi, after holding discussions with members of the Congress Working Committee, informed Willingdon about the resumption of the Civil Disobedience Movement. The response of the government was swift. The Congress was declared illegal. Gandhi was arrested on January 4, followed by Rajendra Prasad the next day. “By January 10, leading Congressmen all over India were behind bars,” wrote D.G. Tendulkar in Mahatma (Volume 3).

It was on that day that in Tiruppur town of the western region of Tamil Nadu, a satyagrahi was beaten to death and his martyrdom propelled him into prominence. He was one of the agitationists who staged, like lakhs of people elsewhere in the country, demonstrations to highlight the Congress’ policy of boycotting foreign cloth and liquor.

While accepting the blows of the police, the Tiruppur satyagrahi upheld the tricolour flag that symbolised the national movement and refused to part with it. He was N. Kumarasami, also known as Tiruppur Kumaran. As he held the flag aloft without letting it touch the ground, he came to be called “Kodi Kaatha Kumaran (Kumaran who protected the flag).” He went on to become a symbol of those who laid down their lives for the sake of the political freedom of their fellow countrymen.

Who was Kumaran?

According to a Tamil biography authored by B.S. Sundaram, a freedom fighter and the leader of the agitation team that led a demonstration in Tiruppur on the fateful day (January 10, 1932), Kumaran was born on October 4 in Chennimalai, now in Erode district, to a modest weaving family belonging to the Senguntha Mudaliar community. He could study up to the fifth standard, after which he took to the traditional occupation. In 1923, the 19-year-old married Ramayee, who was aged 14. He migrated to Tiruppur, where he worked for six years as a clerk at a cotton ginning mill.

The biography, which was published on Independence Day in 1950, states that Kumaran, who wore only khadi clothes when he migrated to Tiruppur, was very eager to participate in the Vedaranayam Salt March of 1930, which was led by C. Rajagopalachari (C.R. or Rajaji) but was prevailed upon by his parents and employer not to take part in the event. However, his interest in the national movement was such that he started getting involved in various stirs. He became a member of the Tiruppur Desabandhu Youth Association. Noticing Kumaran’s growing interest in the freedom struggle, his friends and relatives taunted him for his acts. He continued to engage himself in the activity within a short period of the death of his father, Natchimuthu Mudaliar, in 1931.Yet, he remained unwavering in his focus.

In fact, the biographer Sundaram mentioned that at the time of the fateful agitation, only his mother, Karupayee Ammal, was in town and not his wife, who had gone to Kumarapalayam. “Had she been there, she would have attempted to prevent Kumaran from going ahead with his decision,” the biographer pointed out.

Fateful day

As has happened on many occasions, the person who was supposed to lead the agitationists in Tiruppur had dropped out on the morning of January 10. At about 5 a.m. that day, a couple, who had migrated from Gujarat for livelihood and were enthusiastic participants in the national movement, were picked up by the police and produced before a sub-collector in Pollachi. Eventually, the responsibility of leading the satyagrahis, numbering nine, fell on the shoulders of Sundaram.

Kumaran volunteered to be in the forefront of the processionists, who went around Tiruppur, which was still a small town of Tamil Nadu then. Women at a few places had performed “arati” (traditional way of welcome) and provided their moral support. When the satyagrahis reached the town’s police station on the main road, 30 police personnel and two officers pounced on them without giving any warning, recounted Sundaram.

What followed was a “rain of lathis.” Kumaran, having led the processionists, bore the brunt of the attack. The portion of the brain above the left ear was fractured. Some more blows were given on that spot. Even when he fell on the ground, he held the national flag tightly in his right hand. Another satyagrahi, who also received a lethal blow, was R. Raman Nair. Talking of the other martyr, Sundaram observed that it was on Nair’s suggestion that he agreed to lead the stir. Nair had also participated in the Civil Disobedience movement earlier and had been imprisoned. As Kumaran and Nair lay lifelessly on Tiruppur’s main road, the policemen, using their shoes, trampled on them. As a postmortem was conducted the next day, the government’s records state that the date of Kumaran’s death is January 11, 1932. His funeral was carried out almost in a clandestine manner, with the administration permitting only two persons to carry his body and not allowing other mourners to take it in a procession openly.

Tamil scholar M.P. Sivagnanam, popularly known as Ma.Po.SI, in his seminal work on Tamil Nadu’s role in the freedom struggle – Viduthalipporil Tamizhagam (Volume Two) – pointed out that the circle inspector, Mohammed, who carried out the attack, was transferred out of Tiruppur. “This was not a punishment to him. But it was protection to him from the people of Tiruppur who trembled with rage,” the scholar wrote.

Memorial pillar

In no time, the Congress party had, in Coimbatore, Tiruppur, and many other parts of the State, begun holding events to perpetuate the memory of Kumaran. His birth anniversaries were observed as “Volunteers’ Day” and the death anniversaries as “Kumaran Day.” In January 1948, Cutchery Road, where Kumaran was beaten to death, was named after him and the local body decided to put up a statue too, according to a news item published by The Hindu on February 5, 1948.

On August 18, 1957, a pillar in memory of Kumaran was unveiled by then Chief Minister K. Kamaraj near the Tiruppur railway station. “The stately column is erected near the Tirupur Railway Station at a cost of Rs.[₹] 8,000. It is 25 feet in height with a torch at the top and depicting the picture of a volunteer holding the Congress flag. The pillar is erected in view of the centenary celebrations of the freedom struggle,” reported this daily on August 20. The event was attended by Finance Minister C. Subramaniam, Sundaram, and Kumaran’s nephew, Lakshmanan.

In January 1965, as part of the centenary celebrations of Lala Lajpat Rai, the wives of Kumaran and Vanchinathan, who assassinated, in June 1911, the then Tirunelveli Collector and District Magistrate Robert William D’Escourt Ashe, were honoured at an event at the Rajaji Hall, Chennai. A gold-plated silver medal and a white khadi silk saree were given to each of them. While Vanchinathan’s wife Ponnambal received the award, Ramayee did not make it, but her sister-in-law did.

In October 1979, while participating in a conference of freedom fighters on the Tamukkam grounds in Madurai, then Chief Minister M.G. Ramachandran announced that his government would give a grant of ₹10,000 to Ramayee, besides providing her with a monthly ex gratia grant of ₹300 to ₹500. In April 1991, the State government built a memorial, containing photographs and exhibits concerning Kumaran and freedom fighters of Tiruppur district.

In April 1998, Ramayee died, and her mausoleum is located on the memorial complex. On the occasion of the martyr’s birth centenary in October 2004, the Postal department brought out a stamp on him. In October 2025, the foundation stone was laid in Chennimalai for a Kumaran memorial to be built at a cost of ₹2.5 crore.

Though 95 years have gone by, the legacy of Kumaran lives on.

World.title: CEC row LIVE: Heavy police deployment at Chhatrasal Stadium after Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi detained
World.content:
Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and other Opposition MPs were detained by Delhi Police when they were on their way to Jantar Mantar. The bus carrying the Opposition MPs was stopped at Janpath, following which they decided to march to Jantar Mantar. Heavy police deployment has been put in place at Chhatrasal Stadium, where Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other leaders have been brought after being detained during the protest.

Also read: ECI fact-checks claims on Form 6 following SC observation

A large number of MPs of opposition parties got together for lunch at a restaurant at Janpath in central Delhi hosted by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, after which they boarded buses and headed towards Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site in central Delhi.

Also read: ECI says Opposition MP’s Parliament Annexe meet demand ‘could not be accepted’

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student organisations on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) called for a united mobilisation against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar ahead of their October 10 protest, saying the agitation will continue until the electoral system is overhauled.
