World.title: Kammampalli Government High School in Krishnagiri gets new classrooms
World.content:
Six new classrooms were inaugurated at the Kammampalli Government High School, on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), under the aegis of the Krishnagiri district administration. The classroom building was funded by the Tamil Nadu Firecracker Traders Association and the Parent Teachers’ Association (PTA) of the school.

Kammampalli Govenrment High school has over 457 students pursuing English-medium education. Inaugurating the classrooms, Collector C. Dinesh Kumar said the school’s PTA had long demanded for a new classroom block and also to assign the school as examination centre.

Speaking on the occasion, the Collector said the Tamil Nadu Firecracker Traders Association has consistently contributed through its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative for schools. Earlier, the association funded facilities for the school for the mentally challenged at Bargur.

The new classroom complex was constructed at a cost of ₹59 lakh, of which ₹9 lakh was funded by the school’s PTA. Lauding the participatory approach, the Collector said a shared goal will help accomplish results, and added that measures were being taken to upgrade the school to a higher secondary school.

World.title: Karnataka High Court orders using ‘parenting time’ instead of ‘visitation’ in all child custody cases
World.content:
In a significant move aimed at reforming the language used in cases involving custody of a child between couples in conflict, the High Court of Karnataka has directed all family courts and courts dealing with guardians and wards (G&WC) cases henceforth to use the term “parenting time” instead of “visitation,” observing that no parent should be treated as a mere “visitor” in a child’s life.

Justice Lalitha Kanneganti, who was hearing a child custody case, issued the direction while pointing out that it is time for a small change in the language employed in judicial proceedings.

Pointing out that courts often use the word “visitation” to describe the time the child spends with a parent, who is a non-custodial parent, the court said that the word “visitation” is familiar, but “it carries an unfortunate suggestion that one parent is part of the child’s life while the other merely visits.”

“A child should not be made to understand the relationship through the word visitation, which is used for someone who arrives and leaves as a guest. Children read the conduct of adults and sometimes the words of courts to understand where they belong. Calling it parenting time recognises a simple truth that no parent is a visitor in the life of a child,” the court said.

Though a change in terminology does not decide questions of custody, when a court imposes restrictions on the access to the child, the word “parenting” is more humane, Justice Kanneganti said.

Also, the High Court directed the Registrar of General to issue a circular to all courts in this regard on the use of “parenting time” while also directing that even in the applications for child’s custody the word “parenting time” should be used instead of “visitation.”

World.title: JNNCE in Shivamogga secures eight ranks in VTU exams
World.content:
As many as eight students of the Jawaharlal Nehru New College of Engineering (JNNCE) in Shivamogga, secured top ranks in the Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) examinations for the academic year 2025-26. A majority of the rank holders are from rural backgrounds.

The rank holders, during an interaction with the media in Shivamogga, on Wednesday, dedicated their success to the support of their parents and the guidance of their faculty. They said their parents and the faculty played significant roles in their achievement.

Dhanyashree B.M., a resident of Sirigere village near Ayanur in Shivamogga taluk, secured the first rank in Electrical and Electronics Engineering and won seven gold medals. She said she travelled to the college every day, with the support of her parents, who are engaged in agriculture. She also thanked the college faculty for their guidance. Dhanyashree wishes to work for the Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited (KPTCL).

Six students of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering secured top ranks. Nayyar Fatima Afreen from Tarikere secured the third rank. Her father is an advocate and her mother a teacher. Yashaskara T.G., who secured the fourth rank, is a native of Sringeri, and his father is a priest. Bhumika M., a native of Sagar, secured the fifth rank; she stayed in a hostel for her studies. George T. Paul from N.R. Pura in Chikkamagaluru district, Nithyashree Hegde K.N. from Tirthahalli and Swathi S.G. from Nyamathi in Davanagere district secured the sixth, eighth and tenth ranks, respectively, in the same branch.

Harshika N. secured the fourth rank in the Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Engineering.

P. Narayana, secretary of the National Education Society (NES), said a majority of the rank holders were from rural backgrounds. Their success, he said, proved that the college had been providing quality education and bringing change to the lives of agrarian families. Describing Dhanyashree as a “golden girl”, Mr. Narayana said the NES would honour her with another gold medal in recognition of her achievement.

JNNCE principal Y. Vijay Kumar, Head of the Departments of the colleges, directors of the society and others were present.

World.title: Migrant children in Ernakulam get training in Madhubani painting
World.content:
Thirty-one students enrolled in five schools under the Ernakulam district administration’s ‘Roshni’ project for the educational uplift of migrant children are undergoing a 10-day training programme here in the Madhubani tradition of painting.

The sessions are being led by Madhubani artists, including Chandrakant Kumar Bari and Lalita Dutta from Bihar, at the Government Vocational Higher Secondary School at Kunnumpuram near Edappally. The programme aims to impart vocational skills to the students along with their studies, according to a communication.

Daraksha Parveen, a native of Bihar and one of the early beneficiaries of the Roshni project, is the mentor for the programme. Hrithik Ranjan, Assistant Collector, Ernakulam, inaugurated the programme on Monday. The training sessions will conclude on October 14.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi protesting against ECI out of desperation, says Pralhad Joshi
World.content:
Union Minister for Education, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Pralhad Joshi has alleged that, after successive defeats in Lok Sabha and Assembly elections in various States, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has begun protesting against the Election Commission of India (ECI) out of desperation.

Speaking to presspersons in Hubballi on Wednesday, Mr. Joshi said blaming the ECI for the Congress party’s electoral losses was far from the truth. “The agitation against the ECI is aimed at covering up Rahul Gandhi’s failures,” he said.

He also termed as baseless the allegation that 13 crore voters had been removed from the electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). “Of them, 3 crore have died and officials have not been able to contact 2.80 crore. A total of 6.80 crore voters have shifted to other places. Officials should make efforts to trace the voters they have not been able to contact so far,” he said.

Defending the steps taken by the ECI, Mr. Joshi said voting rights could not be extended to anyone without proper scrutiny. The Congress government in Karnataka should ensure that the SIR process is conducted properly, he said.

World.title: Goods worth lakhs of rupees damaged in fire at coconut fibre mill
World.content:
In a major fire that broke out at a private coconut fiber mill near Singampunari, the produce stored went up in flames.

The private coconut fiber mill situated along Nattarmangalam Road in Singampunari, witnessed a sudden fire on Tuesday night. Upon noticing the flames, workers promptly alerted the fire and rescue service.

Fire tenders from Singampunari and Kottampatti in Madurai district rushed to the spot and battled for hours to bring the blaze under control. Quantities of stored coconut fiber and husks were reduced to ashes in the fire.

Singampunari police have registered a case and are investigating the incident. Preliminary inquiries suggest that an electrical short circuit may have caused the fire.

World.title: CDF Munir reaffirms Pakistan’s commitment to international peace in meeting with UN chief
World.content:
Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Wednesday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to international peace in a meeting with United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres, the military’s media affairs wing said.

The UN secretary general is currently in Islamabad on a two-day official visit.

In a statement on Wednesday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said Guterres called on CDF Munir at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi.

“During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment and the UN’s role in promoting international peace and security were discussed,” it said.

“The two sides exchanged views on regional stability, the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, India’s abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty and terrorism emanating from Afghanistan,” it added.

During the meeting, CDF Munir also reaffirmed “Pakistan’s commitment to international peace and highlighted its contributions to UN peacekeeping missions”. He also lauded the UN’s role in “advancing peace, stability and humanitarian cooperation”.

According to ISPR, the UN secretary general paid tribute to the sacrifices and contributions of Pakistan and its armed forces in the war against terror and in UN peacekeeping missions.

“He also acknowledged Pakistan’s continued commitment to international peace and security,” ISPR said, adding that Guterres specifically appreciated “Pakistan’s efforts towards the peaceful resolution of regional conflicts”.

On the first day of his trip, the UN secretary general held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. During the meeting, Guterres appreciated Pakistan’s “longstanding contribution to the UN, as well as its diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation”.

He also addressed a joint stakeout with Dar, during which he lauded Pakistan’s “pivotal role” in mediating between the United States and Iran as he called on the parties to end the conflict and return to diplomacy.

President Asif Ali Zardari also conferred the Nishan-i-Imtiaz on Guterres in recognition of his “distinguished international service, leadership of the UN and contribution to global peace and development”.

The two also held a separate meeting, where Zardari appreciated Guterres’ principled leadership, his efforts for international peace, dialogue, diplomacy and peaceful settlement of disputes, as well as his constructive engagement with Pakistan and attention to the concerns of developing countries.

World.title: PTI cannot force govt to accept its demands by holding state 'hostage', says Sanaullah
World.content:
The PTI cannot pressure the government into accepting its demands by holding the state “hostage” and creating political instability, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Wednesday.

Speaking to the media in Islamabad, Sanaullah said that the government would not allow the opposition to use talks as a “tool” for making political demands.

“The doors for talks are open,” Sanaullah said, recalling Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s remarks yesterday calling on the PTI leadership to sit down with the government for dialogue and abandon their protest plans.

However, Sanaullah said, negotiations could not be used to strong-arm the government.

The PML-N leader described the PTI as having been “successful” in obstructing peace. He lamented that politics had been transformed into a culture of “below the belt” jabs at one another and a “culture of intolerance”.

On Sunday, hours-long negotiations between the government and the opposition during a second round of talks ended in a deadlock. The meeting at Parliament House began on Saturday afternoon and continued into the wee hours of Sunday, with discussions focusing on the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad.

After the talks collapsed, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accused Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of “sabotaging” the negotiations, saying that he had changed the draft of the agreement despite what had been agreed to earlier.

However, PTI leaders, presenting the opposition’s stance on the failed talks, declared that reconciliation with the government was not possible without including incarcerated party founder Imran Khan in the dialogue process. They said that another reason for the failure of the talks was that the government was not willing to pursue a collective strategy against terrorism.

The prime minister’s adviser on Wednesday contended that the PTI’s stance that it was being left out of decisions concerning the Centre’s counterterrorism policy was “completely wrong” and “misleading”.

He added that the reasons for the deadlock in talks had been misinterpreted.

“The policy on countering terrorism is already being acted upon,” Sanaullah noted, referring to intelligence-based operations (IBOs) being carried out on a daily basis with “huge success”.

He went on to claim that the PTI was against such IBOs.

In June 2024, the government announced a reinvigorated “Operation Azm-i-Istehkam” but, following criticism, clarified soon after that it would only entail intensifying ongoing IBOs and rebranded it as “Vision Azm-i-Istehkam”.

Sanaullah pointed out that the armed forces and law enforcement agencies have been sacrificing their lives to keep the operations going.

He also said it was being falsely claimed that new military operations would be undertaken and more people would be displaced. He clarified that the ongoing IBOs were supposed to continue under the existing counterterrorism policy.

Sanaullah further said that Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir had previously clarified that no one would be internally displaced as a result of the operations.

‘Politics over national interest’

Speaking on the matter of the ongoing rift between Pakistan and Afghanistan, Sanaullah said that Islamabad had been “fair” in demanding that the Afghan government not allow its land to be used for terrorist activities in Pakistan.

He also elaborated on past talks with the Afghan authorities, saying that in the multiple rounds of dialogue, the Afghan interim government had accepted evidence presented by Pakistan for terrorist attacks emanating from Afghanistan as true.

However, he said, the Afghan Taliban had refused to guarantee that their land would not be used for terror attacks against Pakistan.

“Pakistan’s policy is that it has the right to neutralise training camps or any activity on Afghan land that could cause terrorism in Pakistan later on,” Sanaullah stated.

The policy was based on experiences from the past 40 years and more, he added.

The PML-N leader contended that the PTI was the only party opposed to the policy because it wanted to prioritise its politics over national interest.

During his press conference, he also recalled PTI’s past protests in Islamabad, including in 2022 and 2024.

Sanaullah highlighted the recent rise in terrorism incidents, stressing that martyrs included children, civilians and soldiers from KP.

“On one hand, the martyrs’ bodies were lying there, and on the other hand, the entire provincial government was playing the dhol and chanting slogans, urging people to join the march on Islamabad.”

The attitude of the KP government was “unacceptable”, the PML-N leader declared, adding that the people in the province had also condemned it.

“Prioritising personal and political agendas over national interest is not permissible by law, the Constitution or political ethics,” Sanaullah remarked.

He criticised the KP government’s performance, claiming governance and working for the betterment of the people was not on the PTI’s agenda.

World.title: CM Afridi slams Governor Kundi for 'unconstitutional' meetings, claims move intended to provoke KP govt
World.content:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Wednesday slammed Governor Faisal Karim Kundi for holding “unconstitutional” meetings, contending that the move was an “attack on democracy”.

His remarks came a day after Governor Kundi chaired a meeting with the KP chief secretary and inspector general (IG) on the province’s security situation.

Addressing the 60th cabinet meeting in Peshawar, Afridi said that the KP governor, who belonged to the PPP, staged a “drama” yesterday by summoning the meeting and termed the move “unconstitutional”.

“The governor convening such a meeting in the presence of a provincial government with a two-thirds majority is unacceptable,” he said.

“The provincial assembly, cabinet and government are fully functional and intact,” the PTI leader asserted, terming Kundi’s act an “attack on the Constitution and democracy”.

Afridi contended that the purpose of the governor’s “unconstitutional activities” was to “provoke the provincial government and force it to react”.

However, he advised PTI workers to stay peaceful and abide by the law and the Constitution.

Calling on the province’s chief secretary and IG, the chief minister urged them not to comply with any unconstitutional or illegal order from anyone if he does not order them to do so.

He reiterated that KP’s people and administration had made “countless sacrifices” in the fight against terrorism.

“If someone pushes you to follow any unconstitutional order, do not follow it. It can damage our province or the country.”

He also called on the chief secretary to urge the provincial administration not to indulge in any unconstitutional activity and to take action against those who were accused of corrupt practices.

The chief minister then took aim at Kundi’s PPP, blaming ex-president Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, along with General Yahya Khan, for the separation of East Pakistan, now Bangladesh.

He accused President Asif Ali Zardari of “intending to make another East Pakistan here“.

“We will not allow any conspiracy to break up Pakistan to succeed,” he asserted.

“The party that raised the slogan of democracy separated Bangladesh from Pakistan in the past for its personal interests,” he alleged.

“Prioritising personal interests over national interests has been the PPP’s practice,” he further claimed.

Afridi’s remarks come amid heightened tensions between the Centre and the PTI-led opposition, with the latter going ahead with its long march despite warnings from the Centre of action against any such move.

Hours-long talks over the weekend between a joint delegation of the government and PPP, and the opposition alliance ended in a deadlock, with both sides blaming the other for the breakdown.

Political temperatures have also remained high due to speculations of the Centre imposing governor’s rule in the province, with Kundi and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi discussing the move on Sunday.

‘Policy shift is necessary’

The KP CM also reiterated his objection to the Centre’s counterterrorism policy and defended his government’s efforts in supporting the police in the fight against terrorism.

He contended that terrorism had been “imposed on the province again”, asserting that the PTI-led provincial government had always supported the police and the people of KP.

Afridi maintained that he had been making efforts to strengthen the police, the Counter-Terrorism Department and Special Branch since he took the oath on Oct 15, 2025.

“The KP police have the most modern weapons and equipment compared with any other police force in Pakistan,” the chief minister said.

He contended that the federal government had always treated KP like a “stepchild”.

“The tribal districts were merged into KP in 2018, but they have not been fully integrated financially to this day,” CM Afridi claimed, adding that the financial rights of the tribal districts agreed upon at the time of their merger had not been provided yet.

The PTI leader went on to claim that federal governments had “continuously imposed military operations” on KP since 2004.

“People displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies kept crying on the streets, but they have still not received full compensation,” he said, adding that nearly Rs100 billion in compensation were still outstanding.

“Those whose homes were destroyed, families affected and mosques demolished are still wandering from pillar to post for their compensation.”

He highlighted that while a compensation of only Rs400,000 per household had been fixed for tribal families, they had not even been paid the promised amount.

Afridi stressed that a commitment was also made to provide between Rs370million and Rs380m per month to displaced people from North Waziristan at the Baka Khel camp. “The displaced people of Baka Khel are still not being provided the monthly amount as promised.”

“It is the provincial government’s responsibility to stand with people displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies,” the chief minister stated, adding that his government had provided Rs21bn for displaced people.

“The provincial government also has to bear responsibility for losses caused by military operations and collateral damage as a result of drone attacks,” Afridi said.

He also remarked that the individuals making decisions in the federal government had no sense of the difficulties faced by the people as a result of those decisions.

“If the federal government is sincere with KP, it should upgrade the province’s NFC (National Finance Commission) share and pay its outstanding dues of around Rs125bn to the province that has sacrificed 80,000 precious lives,” he demanded.

Afridi reaffirmed that KP had to fight terrorism as well as deal with the situation created by the federal government’s policies.

“The KP government and police are serious about maintaining law and order. Turning the police into personal servants and assigning them other tasks is wrong,” he declared.

“If the policy of KP’s stakeholders is followed, peace can be established within 100 days,” the PTI leader insisted.

He questioned why peace could not be established in the province “despite 14,000 intelligence-based operations and 22 major military operations over 22 years”, terming it a “failure of the federal policy”.

Afridi maintained that if the issue of peace still exists in KP even after 22 years, the federal government should change its policy against terrorism if it was “serious in doing so”.

“The excuse that KP is not cooperating is unacceptable; the same policy is also failing in Balochistan,” he claimed, as both provinces have witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years.

“The Balochistan government is cooperating with the federal government, but peace has still not been established there,” Afridi said, claiming the Centre’s counterterrorism policy was neither effective in KP nor in Balochistan.

“A shift in policy is necessary. KP can establish peace within 100 days,” he reaffirmed.

In his address, Afridi also once again criticised Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s remarks that her province faced no threats from India, despite the state’s narrative of the presence of Indian proxies in Pakistan in the face of Fitna al Hindustan.

Asif says ‘enough is enough’

Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif assailed the PTI-led KP government for continuing its “complete detachment from terrorism in the province and criminal indifference”.

“Enough is enough!!!” he wrote in a post on X.

“The PTI provincial government is roaming the streets for a so-called failed political long march, while its facilitators have unleashed a fresh wave of terrorism against the people of KP during this very time,” he said.

The minister recalled Tuesday’s attacks in Dera Ismail Khan, where customs officials were among five people killed.

He remarked that the entire provincial cabinet, including the chief minister, was “numb to this serious matter and fully engrossed in their politically failed long march”.

“As always, these insensitive and shameless people did not even condemn the innocent murder of these five individuals in DI Khan, offered no condolences to the grieving families, did not attend their funerals or, at the very least, visit their homes to express regret,” Asif regretted.

“This is inexcusable by any standard.”

Instead, the defence minister noted, the KP CM had scheduled a meeting today at his party’s behest to reprimand the IG and chief secretary for attending the governor’s security meeting.

“The chief minister and his cabinet of a province under the scourge of terrorism have completely abandoned the province’s people to the mercy of the terrorists. That is why the people of KP are protesting against the provincial government on the streets in various areas.

“This can no longer be tolerated,” Asif declared.

The defence minister accused the KP government of being in “complete collusion” with terrorists, saying there was evidence available of “its facilitator ecosystem, which every Pakistani has witnessed with their own eyes over the past three years”.

Recalling past arrests of ex-premier Nawaz Sharif and his family members, as well as PML-N leaders, Asif asserted: “Time has proven that the allegations were just allegations and they were imprisoned on Imran Khan’s behest.”

Yet, he stressed, the PML-N fulfilled its parliamentary role responsibly under the Constitution and did not hold the country and institutions “hostage”.

“It fought a legal and constitutional battle in the courts and parliament. It did not ally with the Taliban,” Asif declared.

The defence minister said that the “time has come to make crucial decisions”.

“KP cannot be left any longer to the mercy of incompetent, insensitive rulers and Taliban allies,” he avowed.

Asif further stressed that the unity of the country cannot be put at risk. “An entire province cannot be held hostage. Enough is enough.”

World.title: Marriage can be dissolved on a woman's initiative on grounds of shiqaq even if cruelty is not proven: SC
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that a marriage could be dissolved on grounds of shiqaq (marital discord) under a residuary provision of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 even when cruelty was not proven.

The residuary provision of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 2(ix), explains the grounds on which a woman can obtain a decree for the dissolution of her marriage.

In its judgement, the SC stated: “A marriage may be dissolved by a court, but neither spouse should be judicially deprived of a lawful right, nor judicially burdened with a stigma, without the foundation of law and evidence.”

The judgement was issued by a five-member bench, headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and comprising Justices Naeem Akhter Afghan, Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, Ishtiaq Ibrahim and Miangul Hassan Aurangzeb.

The judges had taken up two connected petitions, filed by Zainab Bibi and Imran Naz Begum, against separate orders of the Peshawar High Court (PHC).

Both cases arose from family suits where wives sought dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty and claimed maintenance, dower and dowry articles. The family court found cruelty unproven in both cases, but dissolved both marriages through khula — a woman’s right to seek release from a marriage.

The family courts also directed the two women to return their dower, while the appellate court and the PHC largely upheld these decrees.

The two women raised two principal grievances before the SC: first, that their marriages could not lawfully be dissolved through khula because they neither sought nor consented to it, as their cases were founded on cruelty; and second, their financial claims should have been allowed in full.

The SC’s 15-page judgement on their please, authored by Justice Waheed, drew a distinction between khula and shiqaq and explained that khula proceeded from a wife’s voluntary election to obtain release from the marriage and ordinarily carried financial consequences.

Shiqaq, by contrast, arose from an objectively established condition of serious matrimonial breach and did not depended on a wife’s surrender of dower or any benefit as consideration for her release, the judgement stated.

The SC held that family courts committed an error in converting the petitioners’ claims for the dissolution of their marriages on the ground of cruelty into decrees of khula without obtaining their clear and voluntary consent or election.

Those decrees, to the extent that they rested upon khula, could not be sustained, the judgement said, though the SC did not set aside the dissolution altogether.

“The matrimonial relationships have undergone a serious and continuing rupture; reconciliation has failed; the evidence does not establish the statutory ground of cruelty; and the record, taken as a whole, establishes a condition of ‘shiqaq’ of the kind contemplated by verse 35 of Surah An-Nisa of the Holy Quran and recognised under Muslim law, thereby bringing the cases within the residuary provision contained in section 2(ix) of the Act of 1939,” the SC explained.

The dissolution could therefore lawfully be sustained, but upon a juridical basis different from that adopted by the family courts, the SC judgement said, adding that marriages of the petitioners were liable to dissolution on the ground of shiqaq falling within section 2(ix) of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, and not on the basis of khula.

However, the directions requiring the petitioners to return, surrender or waive their dower merely as a consequence of khula should consequently stood set aside, the SC ruled. Their entitlement to dower would be determined in accordance with the Act of 1939, it declared.

The SC observed that the Quranic emphasis upon reconciliation in cases of shiqaq was meaningful precisely because it contemplated the possibility that reconciliation may fail. “The law should neither rush towards separation nor prolong a matrimonial relationship which has ceased to serve its lawful purposes,” the judgement held.

Where reconciliation had failed, and the relationship had reached the condition of shiqaq, the judicial task was to bring the matter to a lawful conclusion without unnecessary attribution of blame or deprivation of rights, the judgement explained.

The SC emphasised that courts must distinguish between an unhappy marriage and one in a state of shiqaq.

“Mere incompatibility, occasional disagreement, anger, short separation or the existence of matrimonial litigation cannot, by themselves, satisfy the test. The court must be satisfied that the breach is genuine, serious and continuing; that the matrimonial relationship has ceased to function in accordance with its essential purposes; and that reconciliation has failed despite meaningful judicial effort,” the judgement emphasised.

The wife should not be compelled to surrender dower through an involuntary conversion of her statutory claim into khula, it said, adding that the husband should also not be judicially characterised as cruel or guilty of matrimonial misconduct without the evidentiary foundation required by law.

“Allegations of cruelty, ill-treatment, neglect and misconduct frequently arise in an emotionally charged environment. The courtroom should not become an institution through which matrimonial discord is converted into a permanent injury to the reputation and dignity of either spouse,” it explained.

The judgement further stated: “The law must determine rights; it need not aggravate human conflict. Where the evidence does not establish a particular matrimonial wrong to the standard required by law, the courts should refrain from declaring it proved. Conversely, where the evidence establishes that the matrimonial relationship itself has descended into a state of serious and continuing rupture, the absence of proof of a particular matrimonial wrong does not necessarily require parties to remain bound to one another indefinitely.”

The judgement explained that shiqaq was not established by every quarrel, disagreement, incompatibility or temporary estrangement in a marriage. “It requires a genuine and continuing rupture of such character that the essential purposes of marriage cannot realistically be fulfilled, coupled with failure of reasonable efforts at reconciliation.”

World.title: PPP stalwart Farooq Naek resigns from Judicial Commission of Pakistan
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: PPP stalwart Farooq H. Naek has resigned from the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) — a constitutional body which appoints judges in the superior judiciary.

“Yes, I have resigned from the body [due to] personal commitments,” the senator, who has also served as chairman of the upper house of Parliament, told Dawn.

In a one-page letter addressed to Senate Chairman Yousuf Raza Gilani, as well as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, who is the leader of the house in the Senate, Naek expressed gratitude at being appointed a member of the JCP from the treasury benches.

He said that it was a “great honour and privilege” for him to serve as a member of the JCP.

Naek had participated in a number of JCP proceedings to appoint judges for different high courts as well as the Supreme Court.

As a lawyer, he represented PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari before the SC in the presidential reference moved by the latter’s father, President Asif Ali Zardari, in the murder case of former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

He also appeared in several constitutional petitions before the SC, including cases concerning reserved seats, amendments to the accountability laws, presidential immunities and provincial assembly disputes.

Although he remained associated with the PPP for three decades, he shot to prominence when he defended late former prime minister Benazir Bhutto and Zardari in a number of corruption and criminal cases during former military dictator Pervez Musharraf’s rule.

As a law minister, he also defended the then-federal government in the infamous graft case against Zardari, but eventually dispatched a letter to Swiss Legal authorities in line with SC directions in the National Reconciliation Order case in November 2012 to reopen the case.

Naek has served as a senator from Sindh since 2003. He was appointed the law minister after the 2008 general elections, and reappointed in April 2012 after his three-year term as Senate chairman.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi, Indian opposition lawmakers detained over election chief protest for 2nd day
World.content:
Indian police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several lawmakers for the third time in two days on Wednesday as they launched an unannounced protest demanding the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.

Opposition parties, their student units, and the “cockroach” youth movement have been staging almost daily demonstrations seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, after the Indian Express newspaper last month reported disagreements within the poll panel over updating voter lists, stoking concerns over its neutrality.

Opposition lawmakers led by Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi protested on Tuesday as well, seeking a meeting with Kumar and his deputies, before police broke up their gathering and briefly detained them.

Wednesday’s protest began after a lunch meeting of lawmakers that Congress organised at a restaurant in central Delhi, close to the Jantar Mantar site where authorities permit demonstrations.

“Yesterday … Delhi Police stopped us and said you cannot protest here … so today … we will go to the designated protest site, sit there, and tell the country that, for us, Gyanesh Kumar is not the legitimate commissioner,” Gandhi told reporters, referring to Jantar Mantar.

“The people who have done this (vote theft) are traitors … Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign,” he said, before boarding a bus that was to take the lawmakers to Jantar Mantar.

New political challenge to Modi

Lawmakers in the bus held posters against the windows that said, “no vote theft, no democracy theft”, and “election commission, not BJP commission”, referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party.

Hundreds of Congress members accompanied the bus on foot amid heavy deployment of police and paramilitary personnel in riot gear. Police also closed the road leading to Jantar Mantar, forcing the bus to take a detour.

Gandhi later stepped out of the bus, with a live feed on his party’s YouTube channel showing him standing at the centre of a crowd of protesters and security personnel, while his sister Priyanka Vadra and other lawmakers sprawled out on the road.

India’s Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi (centre, L) scuffles with a policeman during a protest by the opposition alliance INDIA bloc in New Delhi on October 7, 2026 against the country’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, calling for his resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. — AFP

Visuals showed security personnel hauling Gandhi and Vadra into separate vehicles and taking them away.

There was no immediate comment from the police on the detentions.

The demonstrations present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term, just months after similar protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) youth movement forced the resignation of his education minister over exam paper leaks.

Kumar has not commented on the voter lists issue but the election commission and BJP have denied accusations of wrongdoing.

World.title: Pakistan Navy conducts 2 counter-narcotics operations, seizes drugs worth $96m: ISPR
World.content:
The Pakistan Navy seized narcotics worth approximately $96 million during two successful counter-narcotics operations while deployed in the Arabian Sea, the military’s media wing said on Wednesday.

In a press release, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said Pakistan Navy Ship Yarmook conducted the operations “at extended ranges from [the] Pakistani coast, resulting in [the] successful seizure of a large cache of narcotics”.

“During the operations, two dhows were intercepted, and approximately 850 kilogrammes of ice and 2,000kg of hashish/cannabis were recovered from concealed compartments inside the vessels,” it said.

The seized narcotics, valued at approximately $96m, were taken into custody and will subsequently be handed over to the authorities concerned for further disposal and legal proceedings, according to ISPR.

“The successful operations reflect the Pakistan Navy’s sustained presence, vigilance and commitment to regional maritime security and the fight against illicit trafficking at sea,” the statement concluded.

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the Pakistan Navy for its successful counter-narcotics operations in the Arabian Sea.

In a statement, he said that the “navy’s role in preventing illegal activities within the country’s maritime boundaries and safeguarding regional maritime security was commendable”.

He commended the navy’s continuous vigilance, readiness and resolve against illicit drug smuggling at sea.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also paid tribute to Pakistan Navy for its “successful and timely” operations.

In a statement, he said the navy’s role in regional maritime security and in preventing illegal activities at sea was commendable.

Last month, the Pakistan Navy seized narcotics worth approximately $750m during a joint counter-narcotics operation in the Arabian Sea. The operation was conducted by Pakistan Navy ships Hunain and Yarmook under the ambit of maritime security operations.

In June, the navy seized around two tonnes of drugs — 1,500kg of hashish and 500kg of ice — near the coastline of Gwadar. The value of seized drugs was estimated at around $215m in the international market.

World.title: SC dismisses Sindh govt's plea against acquittal of 2 MQM workers in Baldia factory fire case
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court (SC) on Wednesday rejected the Sindh government’s petition seeking to revisit its June 10 decision overturning the convictions of two Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM) workers for their alleged involvement in the deadly 2012 Baldia Town factory fire in Karachi.

Over 260 workers, including 16 who could not be identified, were burnt alive when the multi-storey Ali Enterprises garment factory was set on fire in Baldia Town on Sept 11, 2012, in what became the deadliest industrial blaze in Pakistan’s history.

In June this year, the SC overturned the convictions of Abdul Rehman alias Bhola and Zubair alias Chariya on charges of murder, extortion, arson and terrorism, granting them the benefit of the doubt.

The convicts had challenged a 2023 ruling by the Sindh High Court (SHC) that upheld the death sentences handed to them in September 2020 by an anti-terrorism court for allegedly setting the factory on fire.

On Wednesday, a three-judge SC bench took up the review petition moved by the Sindh government through Sindh Prosecutor General Shabbir Shah, challenging the June 10 acquittal.

The bench was headed by Justice Malik Shahzad Ahmed Khan and also included Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi and Justice Shakeel Ahmed. Sindh Additional Prosecutor General Saleem Akhtar presented arguments before the SC.

Besides rejecting the Sindh government’s appeal to revisit its June 10 decision, the SC also dismissed a separate petition moved for expungement of remarks from the June 10 decision regarding MQM.

The detailed order is expected to be issued later.

Sindh govt’s plea and SC acquittal

In its petition, filed in July, the Sindh government had contended that the June 10 judgment had suffered from “error of facts, circumstances, confessional statement and violation of law of vicarious liability and common object”.

The Sindh government had argued that the SC overlooked the evidence of star witnesses of the prosecution, the factory owner, a judicial magistrate and other key witnesses.

The petition had further contended that the report of the joint investigation team was also overlooked while passing the acquittal as there was sufficient proof against the accused.

In its June 10 judgment, the SC had described the Baldia Town factory fire as one of the most “tragic, painful and heart-rending disasters in Pakistan’s history”, in which 260 workers lost their lives and around 60 others suffered burn injuries.

“The victims were ordinary workers who had entered the factory to earn their livelihood, but many of them never came out alive,” Justice Khan had observed in his detailed 39-page judgement.

The order had noted that the original first information report (FIR) had been registered against the factory owners and management for allegedly failing to implement adequate safety measures.

However, around two-and-a-half years later, the prosecution changed its stance, alleging that the petitioners and their co-accused had deliberately set the factory on fire after its owners refused to pay Rs250 million in extortion money allegedly demanded by the MQM.

The petitioners, however, maintained that they had been made scapegoats to victimise their political party. Given these competing narratives, the judgement had stressed that the court was required to exercise utmost caution before reaching a conclusion.

The SC had also reiterated that it was the prosecution’s duty to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and the court’s responsibility to ensure that no innocent person was convicted on the basis of presumptions or unreliable evidence. At the same time, it had emphasised that offenders should not escape punishment where credible and convincing evidence existed.

Referring to allegations of extortion, murders and arson attributed to MQM, the court had observed that probabilities and presumptions, however strong, could never substitute for conclusive proof required under the criminal justice system.

“We are clear in our minds that if there is no reliable evidence or conclusive proof against the petitioners to establish the alleged motive or other charges, their convictions cannot be sustained merely on the basis of presumptions, probabilities or general allegations,” the judgment had stated.

The court had also made observations regarding the Muhajir community, stating that it formed a cherished and respected part of the Pakistani nation whose members had made immense sacrifices during Partition in 1947.

The judgement noted that MQM had generally been regarded as representing a majority of Muhajirs, but stressed that alleged criminal acts by individuals could not justify attributing guilt to an entire community or its representative political party without tangible and convincing evidence.

Although the prosecution produced around 400 witnesses, the SC had found these statements weak, hearsay or otherwise unreliable.
